column9: Artificial sweetener plus sugar make a bad-tasting cocoa
column10: This hot chocolate is nice and convenient and you can brew it strong or less strong because the VUE lets you customize temperature and volume. But sad to say, I found it too sweet. The reason for it's being sweet is that in addition to sugar, it is sweetened with sucralose (aka Splenda.) This is a new trend in foods-- a mix of natural and artificial sweeteners. (Have you seen chewing gum? Even the non-sugar-free varieties have aspartame?) The reason for using a mix of natural and artificial is interesting but I believe in this case, using sucralose lowers the calorie count of the cocoa and it also allows more sweetener in a smaller cup size, as sucralose takes up less space than granulated sugar. I had to tease out the ingredient info by carefully reading the box, as it doesn't say so on the cup.Here's the good news, if you don't want sucralose, or even if you don't want sugar AND sucralose, you can buy packet cocoas and make a cup of hot water with the VUE, any volume and temp you choose. Just mix it up yourself. The only powdered mix I ever liked was Caotina (from Switzerland) which was not so sweet as American varieties but I can't find it in the US. However, I have guests who adore hot chocolate when they visit my office or home, so I keep Swiss Miss on hand.In any case, for the Cafe Escapes, blech!

Watery and unpleasant.  Like Yoohoo mixed with dirty dish water.  I find it quite odd that Keurig would release a product like this.  I'm sure they can come up with a decent hot chocolate and not this swill.  I had one pod in a sample pack so at least I didn't buy a whole box of them.

Just bought the new keurig vue after having an older model,which I loved and a hot chocolate pod came with the new one. I have to say this is the worst hot chocolate ever! It almost has a plastic taste to it and I don't know why but it's really bad. I think I'll stick to making it in the microwave and using my own mix. Also this doesn't even taste that sweet or "chocolatety".

This cappuccino is delicious when mixed with other coffee - use it instead of sugar and creamer. The price as offered on Amazon is double what one has to pay at Wal-Mart for the same item, hence my three stars. Otherwise I would give it a five star rating.

column4: Writer of Books - Mage - Mom to Two "Writer, ...
column9: The taste is excellent! Can be found cheaper everywhere.
column10: I completely agree with another reviewer, why this is twice the price on Amazon is crazy??!  You can find this from Walmart for just over $3. You can even get it from them online from their website. What is going on with the price here, I don't know.As to the cappuccino  itself, I love it. Because I want it to go further, I add a heaping teaspoon to my coffee, then I add Coffeemate French Vanilla Creamer. I know...that's a lot of flavor. So? It gets me going!!! :DI have made it straight, but you need a lot of it to achieve a rich, full bodied cup of coffee. Then when you do, it is soooo rich, it's more like dessert. If you want that, then totally go for it!! But I like a more coffee flavor, so I mix them.I do love General Foods International Coffees, but you get soooo much less in each can for the same price. If you love flavored coffee, try this from Hills Bros. (Note, currently at Wmart they have two sizes, 16 oz and 12 oz for exactly the same price. Be sure to get the big one!)  It comes in a plastic container similar to the Folger's red container. Nice, because you could reuse it and store rubber bands or post it notes in this.As to a gift? I think adding it to a basket would be wonderful, although the GF International coffees do look a bit nicer in their tins IMO. Flavor-wise, you can't beat this. It comes out creamy and rich but not toooo sweet, like a good cappuccino should be.

column9: Planters is definitely not what they used to be, but then...
column10: Although I seem to be having problems with the quality of some Planter's products, since ever since I was a kid Palnter's was the no. 1 quality product you could get. This has, like many things, changed, but their peanuts are still the best! These lightly salted nuts are the true American peanut with much taste and not too much salt. They are really excellent and STILL better than the competition. Definitely worth buying and above all worth EATING!

column9: Part of an effort to make diet healthier
column10: It's so easy to grab some unhealthy snack foods when one has an urge to eat between meals. Over time, I have tried to discipline myself to better quality snacks. One part of that has been nuts and peanuts. Plasnter's produces a nice decent sized package of peanuts--16 full ounces.The peanuts are nice and crunchy (maybe a bit too much salt). Still, better than candy bars or fried snacks or. . . .

column9: I get a package of these once a month, and they go fast
column10: I like plain peanuts more than mixed nuts. Between my wife and I, we go through these 6 cans easily in a month. They go great with raisins. Lightly salted but still with great flavor. Recommended.

column9: From my dog's snout to peoples' ears
column10: I have a 6 year old chocolate labrador retriever.  Chip has been plagued with a dry itchy coat and profuse shedding for the past 5 yrs.  My vet thought that he was allergic to grains and suggested I try the Nature's Variety GRAIN FREE dog food.  After two months, chip's skin stopped flaking, his shedding reduced exponentailly and his coat was as shiny as when he was a pup. I was a skeptic in the beginning thinking that chip was on the pro plan diet and that was good, right? WRONG!  I highly recommend this food.  Do the research and find what low grade ingredients are in name brand pet foods on the market today.  When all of the dog food poisionings and recalls happened you never seen this brand on the list.  I truly am a believer in this product.

When I met my last rescue pet, Dixie, approximately 6.5 years ago, she was a real mess--both externally and internally.  She exhibited a nervous condition {G.E.R.D.} that my vet said was due to her previous horrendous living conditions; that is to say, that everything that went down her goozle promptly came right back up!  She was painfully emaciated, skeletal almost, and her blood-work was all over the place.  So, after a round of IV fluids and 2 bags of 'Science Diet' chow, Dixie came home with me to recuperate and to learn how to live in a loving home.  The first thing I did was to research which pet foods would address her particular condition; I knew that I didn't want to keep her on the 'Science Diet' regimen--it's too full of ingredients that I feel don't belong in a proper diet for dogs.  Lo' and behold, I stumbled upon the "Nature's Variety Instinct" formula for dogs.  It seemed like a good fit, due to all of the proper ratios {protein/fat} and totally 'GRAIN-FREE".  Viola!  The rest, as they say, is history.... 6.5 years later, Dixie now weighs in at approximately 20 loving, happy pounds of my friendly and well-adjusted best friend.

column9: High quality item - but not for every dog
column10: Please note that I am not questioning the inherent quality of this dog food. Nature's Variety is known to make one of the best commercial grain-free diets out there. Their ingredients are top-notch, and my dogs certainly enjoyed this food. The problem is that it seemed to make their stomach issues worse instead of better. It seems that some dogs simply have problems digesting a totally grain-free diet, because of how rich the food is. My dog ended up having to have simply chicken and rice, which has so far kept his tummy issues under control (fingers crossed). Consult your vet before switching your dogs to a grain-free diet, in case grain isn't the issue causing their problems.

I've been feeding this to my lab for a few months now and it is a great product! I have a 60 lb, 1yr old lab and I feed him 2 cups of this per day.  I recommend this to those dog owners that want a grain-free food and are not yet ready to feed 100% raw.

I have a 1 year old Vizsla who has been plagued with gas and diarrhea since the day I got her.  I had tried other "grain-free" dog foods with no luck.  Many of those foods contained potatoes, which was still too much carbohydrate it seemed.  This food is grain and potato free and seems to have her on the right track finally!

We have a beautiful 2 year old English Bulldog. We started feeding him this dog food when he was 5 months old and he is so much healthier now that we use Nature's Variety Raw Instinct.  He is calmer and less agressive, his digestive system functions well, his allergies are in check and his coat is shiny.  It has saved us a lot of money on vet bills and we would not feed him anything else.

Normally I feed my dogs whole raw chickens, organs, bones, etc, but when I take them on a vacation or I just have the need to feed them a dry food for a while this is the next best thing, arguably the best dry dog food available along with a few other goods ones like EVO. I've tested feeding this to my dogs for months at a time to see the difference between raw BARF feeding and this and there's no difference in weight or healthy appearance or attitude. I still prefer raw feeding and strongly believe that is the healthiest option for my dogs, but this is definitely the next best thing.

column9: Best Dog Food I have found!
column10: Simply the best dog food around, in my opinion.  I am SO glad that Amazon finally is stocking this - it is a lot more expensive on here with the standard price, but with the Subscribe and Save discount, it is the cheapest around.Don't take my word for it, here are some professional reviews of this product:***DogfoodAdvisor.com gives the product 5/5, their highest grade."Above-average protein. Above-average fat. And below carbs when compared to a typical dry dog food.Free of any plant-based protein boosters, this looks like the profile of a kibble containing an abundance of meat.When you also consider its lack of any critical Red Flag items, it becomes obvious we're evaluating an exceptional dry food.Bottom line?Nature's Variety Instinct is a grain-free kibble using an abundance of meat and poultry meals as its main sources of animal protein... thus earning the brand five stars.Enthusiastically recommended."***petfoodratings.net gives the product 5 Stars as well, saying:What's good about this food....Grain-free, very high in quality meat content (first 3 ingredients), pumpkinseeds are great for fiber & skin/coat, herring meal, fruits/veggies.....and what's not so good.Nothing.***dogfoodanalysis.com also lists this as one of their 6 star (best) brands.  The packaging is different, as it was from 2009, but same ingredient list:"The first and fifth ingredients in this food are named meat products, in meal form. Although it is easier to have confidence that there is a good amount of meat in a food when there are multiple meat meal ingredients heading the ingredient list, the supporting macronutrient breakdown of this product lends a high level of confidence in the amount of meat product in the food. The inclusion of fish meal amongst the major incredients provides a good source of omega 3 and 6 OFAs.Tapioca is the starch content with primary purpose as thickener. It is the second ingredient in a food with likely carbohydrate content of around 26% DMB.There are no grains in this food. The major carbohydrate source is tapioca, which may be particularly useful for dogs with sensitivities to potatoes or who suffer arthritis. There is a good range of fruits/vegetables in the food, and a good range of probiotics.We note that chicken fat is the third ingredient in the food and that research at Purdue University has identified fat in the top four ingredients of dry dogs foods as a factor increasing the risk of bloat in large breed dogs. The presence of citric acid as a preservative means that this food should not be pre-moistened prior to feeding (pre-moistening of foods preserved with citirc acid has also been identified as a factor increasing the risk of bloat).This food is outstanding in that it contains no grains whatsoever. Grains are not a natural part of a canine diet and it is pleasing to see dog foods on the market that exclude grains completely from the diet.The only caution we would make on this food is that the high protein and calcium content may make it suitable for adult dogs only, particularly in the case of large breeds."***On the best brands list at[...]
Our dog "Brenda Lee" enjoys this high quality food!  Great food to give to your shorter family members  :o)

Simply put, this is one of the best food that is available, aside from raw. My two yorkies are healthy and happy on this food. We have no issues at all. I will add, though, that the transition from a different brand to this one was tedious, so be patient if your dogs are sensitive.

My dog is allergic to just about everything, and this is one of the only grain-free food's that doesn't contain brewer's yeast. I've noticed his poops are better on this - no more "bad days." I ordered this after that salmonella May 2012 Diamond Dog Food recall. It was a great replacement. The dog didn't seem to notice a different food and he digested it normally.

I switched my 4 year old lab from another holistic brand because she was itching all the time and the vet suspected a food allergy. Two months later the itching has stopped...and there is about half as much loop to pick up. The auto-delivery feature is really convienent as well. No more hauling dog food home from the store or running out at the last minute.

My dog gets tired of dry food so quickly we have to constantly switch from brand to brand, although there aren't many good food to choose from out there. We feed him EVO, blue buffalo wilderness, wellness core, and now we tried Instinct for 3 weeks by now, everything is just fine with him. No diarrhea, no scratching or licking paws, happy as ever. This brand has a very fine list of ingredients and it is top rated on a few dog food review websites, the reason why we tried it in the first place. The vendor is a well-established online distributor, although got our order wrong in the beginning, showed professional customer service and corrected the order immediately.

column9: Best Value for the Money - End of allergies
column10: I have a 10 year old purebred Husky Shepherd mix. Her coat was always dry and itchy, and I followed my vet's advice for Nature's Variety Grain Free dog food. It took some time, but this food was amazing! Shedding subsided substantially, skin itching stopped, and all was well. Simply put, do the research and see how good this food is, and see how well-formulated it is.There is so much junk food in the pet food market today, but Nature's Variety Instinct formula has the proper ratio of protein to fat and is grain free. Similarly, the company doesn't seem to pander to what the average pet owner assumes that dogs need to live well, which, of course, is often wrong. All and all, this is the best made pet food for the best price I have found. Certainly, it is more expensive than the pet market leaders or the big retailers' house brands, but it's a wonderful balance between price and quality. Your pet deserves the extra to live a long healthy life.

I have been feeding my 5 yr. old golden retriever this product since she was a pup. She quickly manifested foot chewing and other allergic reactions when eating kibble with grains. She tolerated this food much better!  She is a very healthy, trim and fit dog, and her check ups are shining testimonies to the good feeding she gets.  My vet is a hostically-oriented accredited and licensed professional who has studied food-therapy for companion animals extensively.  It may seem that this product is more expensive than others, but due to it's high nutrient density she requires less...less than even the package recommends.  I feed her a cup in the morning, "gravied up" with warm water, and feed her home-made raw in the evening.  I highly recommend this product.

column9: Seems great, didn't work for us
column10: I have a 100 lb lab/weim mix who is a little over 2 years old. He has allergies that have progressively gotten worse as he has aged. I haven't had him tested yet but it is clear he cannot eat anything with oats, corn, and even potatoes seem to trigger allergies. His allergies are most commonly seen as stinky, black yeasty ears but he also will get patches on his skin that he chews on continuously, mostly around his feet/legs and dry skin - since he is black it is very obvious when his skin flakes - and hair. Vets haven't helped much besides giving me products to clean his ears - which didn't work! I've tried Dr E's Grain and Potato Free Limited Ingredient Buffalo (cleared his ears up but he hated it and I kept having to put other food in it. Arcana Pacifica - smells just like fish but his ears get worse and his skin flakes more (I think the potato?), Grandma Lucy's Grain Free Chicken - he loves this but his ears get worse; Wells Earthborn Holistic Primitive Natural Grain Free - got bad ears and horrible HORRIBLE dry skin flakes, he looked practically gray.  Prior to this his allergies really flaring up he mostly ate Chicken Soup for the Dog Lover's Soul Chicken.Anywhoo - with this his ears are still runny but not as bad as usual (his right ear gets really bad but his left ear has hardly any stuff in it when I clean them almost daily) and his dry skin flakes have almost gone BUT he's been licking sores into his legs so clearly there is still something in this he is reacting to. I've started adding in Dr E's potato and grain free duck formula and his ears have gotten better but since his legs look worse so we won't continue on this. The only thing I can think is the alfalfa meal? because the Dr E's has tapioca and he never had a problem with that though I do know some dogs are allergic to that. Or perhaps the chicken? so frustrating and sad for my dog with trying to figure this out. He eats less of this then he had other foods and he isn't getting underweight (as he seemed to when he ate the Buffalo he hated) but his breath really smells on this. badly! so we won't be re-purchasing and the search continues.otherwise it came in a timely manner and was as described. if it had worked I would have continued with the subscribe and save, it is a nice savings. the local independent pet store here carries it but for a much higher price point.

My dog has allergies that create skin problems.  Tried a lot of foods and other methods to help it.New vet recommended no grain dog food and gave me a few names of manufacturers that are trustworthy (ie ingredients listed are true).  Chose the least expensive one (which was comprable to the other "premium" dogfoods I was feeding him)around $50-$60 for 25 lb.  He likes it (he's picky).  His coat is shinier now.  His skin allergies are minor irritations when they used to be awful and turn into staph infections.  I am really happy I found this vet and tried this food.

column9: Buy small bags before getting this food
column10: Dog got very sick from this food even though he was already on a grain-free diet.  Not sure if it was an allergy(ingredients were almost identical to his old food) or some kind of bacteria but make sure before you buy this food for the first time, you get a small bag to feed your dog for a week to make sure they can handle it as it seems to be pretty rich.

I have 3 dogs. After giving them cheap Walmart dry food and stepping in doggie diarrhea throughout the house, a high quality dry food was necessary. I like Natures Variety Instinct because it's grain- free, good fat content, high animal protein and the kibble size is good. Expense is offset by quality over quantity of useless fillers used in cheaper food and who knows what other toxins. Plus the Subscribe and Save helps in cost, time  and back breaking lugging of packages. Digestion is good. Poop looks good. Fur is fine.And I can walk without fear through the house.
these sucked and were not worth the cash. I was shocked at how small the can was and the almonds tasted stale!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

It's more than $10. And the can contains only 30grams. Height of can is about the same as your middle finger! Taste was ok, but the price for this extemely small quantity is a fraud! It shouldn't cost more than $2-3 if you pick up in the shop.Definately take a pass of this.
Simply the best tomato soup to be had, why it's not easily available in the states I don't know.

column9: Tomato Soup the way you remember it
column10: For some reason, the good people at Heinz see fit to market a number of delectable items that Americans might like but are reserved for the Brits. One of them is baked beans (the kind you serve on toast, not the kind you serve with barbecue.) Another is this tomato soup.The soup comes in a pull-tab can, with two moderate servings (not quite a full soup mug.) You do not dilute this soup. The flavor is rich with tomatoes. The "cream" is some skim milk and a little bit of cream; this is not a bisque. The other chief attraction is that the soup has no wheat flour.Ingredients:Tomatoes (84%), water, vegetable oil, sugar, modified cornflour, salt, dried skimmed milk, whey protein, cream, citric acid, spice extracts, herb extractCompare this with Campbells:tomato puree (water, tomato paste), water, wheat, flour, high fructose corn syrup, contains less than 2% of the following : salt, ascorbic acid (added to help retain color), flavoring, citric acid.Look, Campbells has that nasty HFCS! That cloying, sweet taste that is not good for you!  No wonder Heinz tastes like a tomato.

I know - this is not exactly a review of the soup.  Sorry.  There's no other place to put this.  If you're not celiac, skip this warning and disregard the single star.The product description does not mention gluten free but a search for gluten free tomato soup always brings it up.  I accidentally ordered it.  Yes, mea culpa - I'm not blaming Heinz or Amazon. I've learned my lesson but I also hope to warn anyone else who might be as as hasty as I was.

column9: Heinz Cream of Tomato Soup is Available in the U.S.!
column10: F.Y.I. - To all the people who wrote a review of this product, Heinz Cream of Tomato Soup, yes, you can get it at the grocery store.  I just found it not in your ordinary "Campbell soup" isle, but in the foreign foods isle, tacos, taco shells,asian food, Japanese Udon noodles, Heinz Cream of Tomato Soup, etc.  It sells for $3.49 a can at Shaw's Supermarket in Manchester, NH.  So, next time you're at Shaw's or maybe your favorite food market, don't check the "Campbell's soup isle, check the foreign foods isle.

column9: Please don't discontinue this product. I love it!!!!
column10: I grew up with Heinz tomato soup in England and since I came here 34 yrs ago I have had difficulty getting a good supplier. I am so disappointed that Amazon is disHeinz Soup, Cream of Tomato, 14.1-Ounce Cans (Pack of 8)continuing supplying it. There is no tomato soup that even comes close to the flavor and creaminess of Heinz tomato soup.

Soup was delicious. No complaints at all except for the price.  Which unfortunatly is to be expected with gluten free food.  Why Heinz doesn't sell it more over hear is baffling.  Just as good as cambells minus the gluten.
Heinze tomato soup is a great source fo celiac disease patients or gluten sensitive patients to enjoy ready made soup. Campbells is not gluten free. The soup is fast, easy and tastes great.
For those who haven't tried it this is the best canned tomato soup you can get.

Being from Pittsburgh, I grew up on Heinz pickles, ketchup, tomato soup, etc. We lived just a couple miles from the company headquarters and factory. They are still the best. I found this in specialty section of a large grocery store under the "British" foods! I just cracked the can and it is exactly the way I remember it! Got to get a case! I haven't had it many, many years. It is soooo good!
I have already ordered more of this soup. No high fructose corn syrup. The cans were shrink wrapped and arrived in perfect shape.
This is THE BEST Gluten Free Tomato Soup ever! I cannot get it in local grocery stores and was thrilled to find it on Amazon! Thank you, you have a repeat customer with me!!!

i think this soup is just fabulous.  i have ordered it a few times now.  once i get it, i eat it up so quick, i can hardly wait for my next order to come.  it is very creamy and so good.  i'm thrilled that i can have a wonderful gluten free soup.  i just ordered 8 more cans.  i'm sure they will not last me long.  it's delicious, very very tasty.

This is a great staple to have in your pantry for those cold fall/winter evenings. It doesn't have that cloying sweet flavor that Campbell's and others have. Just put some fresh basil on top and serve with some crusty french bread! Yum!
This is the best Cream of Tomato soup that I have found that is Gluten Free.

I had never tried this soup but bought it primarily because it was gluten free.  I made an easy Stuffed pepper soup with it. Can of soup, small can of tomato sauce, added browned ground turkey, onions and bell peppers and some cooked rice.  Awesome on a cold winter day!

This is my favorite soup and I really wish Heinz would make their soups available here in their homeland in the US.  This is staple part of the British diet, along with Heinz Baked Beans and Heinz Vegetable soup among others.  They are all delicious and it gives me a taste of home every so often when I can afford to buy them here.  Thanks Amazon, for making them available.  Try them and you will find they are delicious.

The soup is delicious.......the price is not!I purchased an 8 pack of this soup for under twenty dollars delivered about 6 months ago direct from Amazon. Unfortunately it looks like we now have to go through a reseller to obtain this product and pay an inflated price, hence the one star rating. I'm down to my last can but I cannot bring myself to pay this much for soup!

I bought these at a store and they were really good.  they are toasted, so they taste a little like Rice Crispies and I tried them because I needed a cracker that didn't have corn in it.  Actually, i also like the buckwheat, but sometimes I just want a mild flavor.

The greatest invention ever for sodium restricted folks who like to cook and make dip.  Try mixing 3 packets with 1 cup mayo, and one cup sour cream, and dehydrated onion to taste.  Then dip salt free potato chips.  You won't believe you're sodium restricted.  Great for cooking, gravies, etc.  As good or better than any other boullion I've ever had.  Salt or no salt.

Okay so they taste yummy or so my mut tells me...but the box this replaces was dated Jan. 29, 2012.  The "new" box is dated to expire on September 29, 2011...I suppose it's OK for the dog, but I bought 2 boxes, each one will last about a month. If I were a dog food manufacturer my thought process might go something like this: "Amazon sure would be a good place to dump our outdated dog stuff;  who would object?"  ... sure feels like rip off time and I'm too old and my poor dog is too old to go through the hassle of returning and replacing just dog food...the principle of dumping old stuff surely makes my blood pressure go up.  Fool me once, shame on you.  Fool me twice, shame on me..but again there won't be a second purchase.  Amazon should be showing expiration dates for perishables of any kind...Good luck in maintaining customers in your Grocery/Food stuffs.  And please, review drones, spare me the whine that this is not a product review.  This is a review of the process whereby Amazon takes your money and provides a product worthy of your investment.  When the system doesn't work to the buyer's satisfaction, I want to know about it so as to avoid a costly transaction.  Blow it out your pie hole if you don't like it.
The raspberry white tea is the best.  All the white teas are wonderful, but this one is my favorite.  Thank you Amazon for carrying the Bentley products at a great price.

I had purchased this tea some time ago at a store in another state. When I ran out I began looking and could not find any in my area. I looked online, found it at Amazon and ordered enough to last awhile. It is a wonderful tea and I would recommend it to anyone. Some teas make me feel jittery, but this tea is calming and smooth.

Delicate scent, light amber color, not bitter, no aftertaste, delicious with a touch of sweetner, white tea has more antioxidents and less caffiene than black and green teas. It is always so nice to sit down with a cup of this lovely raspberry scented tea. It is my current favorite and I have trouble finding it locally so I am glad I can order it here.
The raspberry taste is so crisp and light.  It doesn't taste artificial at all (but probably is).  Never bitter if you steep 90 seconds or less, as they recommend.  It is great hot or as iced tea.
There's really nothing like it. It's not so easy to find in the states, sadly.
Wan Ja Shan Organic Soy Sauce has a pure, bright, tangy, not-overly-salty flavor.  It's thin and pricey, but it goes farther on less than, for example, a dark mushroom soy sauce, in my opinion.

This is the third stevia sweetener I have tried so I will compare it to those.  I have used NOW Stevia, and Truvia.This tastes the same as Truvia, which you can buy in the grocery store.  It is less bitter than NOW Stevia.What bugs me is this - it is labeled as "stevia" but the first ingredient is agave inulin, which is a fiber product.  Second ingredient listed is stevia extract.  And the last ingredient is silica.  I looked up silica - it is that grainy stuff in little packets they package with electronics - the packets labeled DO NOT EAT.  I read that silica is not actually toxic but that doesn't mean I want to eat it.  Stevia by itself is prone to caking, so I guess the silica is to prevent that from happening.If you are ok with eating silica, this is a tasty sugar substitute.  If you are trying to be healthy and keep weird things out of your diet, I'd suggest you pass.

column9: THIS IS A GOOD STEVIA PRODUCT
column10: I have tried a few STEVIA products over the last few years.They were okay for my usage in cold drinks , coffee and teas.This STEVIA is better than the others. The sweetness is more  on the corrrect levels ...and I only needed one packet to sweeten my cold drinks instead of the two ,three or so of the other brands.Must be that the plants they are using are more controlled and of a better standard.What ever it is--this is a STEVIA product that I can finally suggest that others try.This one really tastes good and sweet.

I like using low calorie sweeteners and prefer stevia.  However, the problem with stevia is that the taste varies so much from brand to brand.  Some are downright bitter.  This stevia has a great taste.  All sweetness with no aftertaste.  Highly recommended if you're a stevia fan looking for one with great flavor.  Highly recommended.

I have been using stevia for the last several years. It's got zero calories and does not act like sugar in your system. At the same time, it is natural and harmless. The only things you have to look out for are: 1) some brands have a bitter aftertaste, and 2) supermarket brands often have sugar alcohols added (sorbitol, e.g.) which is not good for you. This brand has neither, just a pleasant sweet taste, equivalent to 2 tsp of sugar per packet. I make my iced tea with it and it's delicious. Recommended for anyone watching their sugar intake.

Barb: I have before me three different brands of alternative sweetners to sample and decide which I like best(pre-diabetic).  Splenda, Pure Via(Stevia), and Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Stevia.  Splenda tastes like sugar: is a chemically altered malt and cane product,(been using it in cooking).  Pure Via has a very intense strange supersweet/bitter taste, leaving an aftertaste,(stuck with a big box): is a Stevia extract, cellulose, etc.  Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Stevia tastes like sugar with honey undertones, smooth and mild: is an organic Agave inulin (inulin is good stuff produced from many different plants), organic Stevia extract, silica.  Of the three products, "THE WHOLESOME SWEETENERS ORGANIC STEVIA TASTES THE BEST", says my tastebuds!  The product may cost a bit more, but the benefits seem to be worth it.  The company has a nice website.

column9: Great sugar replacement, and organic too!
column10: First off, the great point of stevia as a sweetener:  it is a natural product.  Love that.  And throw in the fact that it has no calories, zero glycemic index, no artifical ingredients.  This Wholesome Sweeteners product has an advantage in that it is organic, while not all stevia products are.  I'm very sensitive to pesticides in our food products, so I really appreciate organics.  This stevia is packaged much like the thin packages of artificial sweetener, and it is processed into a fine powder.  The individual packets are sealed well with an airtight paper.  The box says that each packet has the equivalent taste of 2 teaspoons of sugar.  That's probably about right, as I drink my coffee without creamer, so I like it just a tad sweet.  When opening the package, the stevia powder flows right out when poured, no clumping, and it dissolves quickly.  I've heard some people say that stevia is an acquired taste, but I've loved the taste of stevia in my coffee since the first time I tried it.  My only reservation about the Wholesome Sweeteners product, and this won't affect 99% of all consumers out there, but as a gluten-intolerant, I am very aware if any product has a disclaimer saying that this product is processed in shared facilities where wheat products are processed.  It does also list a handful of other common allergans that are processed at the same facility.  Now, chances are there isn't any cross-contamination of the allergans in the stevia product.  However, it's something that causes me to have to make a decision whether I want to take a chance on the potential for cross-contamination.  Anyway, that's my issue.  For everyone else, this is a great tasting product, it's organic, no calorie, I strongly recommend it for those reasons.  Would be 5 stars, if not for the cross-contamination potential.

I've used a few different brands of Stevia including Stevita Supreme and Sun Crystals (stevia mixed with sugar).I honestly don't find a huge difference between stevia of any brand.  It's a bit like asking which sugar tastes best.  On the other hand, I do find the Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Stevia slightly better tasting than some other brands.  It's also a little more expensive than some other brands, but not overly so.One reviewer commented on the fact that this product contains "silica" and that silica is used when electronics are packaged.  What you find packaged with electronics is not the same as silica for food service use. Just like oil you put in your car is not the same kind of oil you use for cooking.Fine particle size silica, or its chemical cousin sodium silicoaluminate are used in a lot of food products. Especially, powdered food products. A primary use of the silica is to act as a flow agent, anti-packing agent, and water scavenger. Common table salt is a common example. Dissolve a teaspoon of table salt in a glass of water and you will observe that the solution is cloudy, not clear. This cloudiness is not undissolved salt, it is the silica-type mineral added to keep the salt flowing in humid conditions.

There is one key noticeable distinction between stevia and sugar: taste. I personally think you get ove it quickly, but I know people who never get used to it and prefer sugar.It's less noticeable than the taste of honey and much less so than molasses. But it's there, so don't expect something sweetened by stevia to taste the same as something that uses sugar.That said, stevia doesn't have the side effects of sugar. It's not as processed, naturally low calories, lower glycemic index, etc.This particular packet is ok, it has conveniently wrapped individual packages, and a recyclable light cardboard container. Though I prefer bulk and less useof packages, this keeps the stevia in good condition for longer time. To top it off, this stevia is organically grown.If the pricepoint was a little lower I would probably give it 5 stars.

column9: High in agave which I'm trying to drink less of, but the taste is good.
column10: I like the taste of this sweetener and I am a huge fan of stevia, but my problem with it is that agave is the first ingredient. Now, contrary to popular myth, as someone in the food biz I can say that that does NOT mean it's mostly agave. As you can verify on the FDA website, ingredients are not listed in the order of what they contain most of as most people believe, but they are listed in order of weight...which means if there are 2 ounces of agave in a pack and one ounce of stevia, (I just made that weight up for explanation) then agave will be read first...even is there is a tablespoon of agave and 2 tablespoons of stevia in a packed (again, that amount is used just for explanation...doesn't contain near that much in a packet.). Since stevia weighs next to nothing, it still may very well be the main ingredient, but we do know there is a good deal of agave... and that's my issue.I actually switched to stevia from using agave as a sweetener (although I still use it occasionally.) because of the controversy and studies showing that it may very well have the same weight-gain effects as high fructose corn syrup due to how your body processes it. There are some very well respected doctors such as Dr Mercola who say this. I scoffed at first, until more reports said the same. I haven't made up my mind yet, but in the meantime I cut back on agave so when I bought stevia I didn't expect to find it there. But it's listed first in these packets.Why do they add another sweetener? Stevia is SO sweet that you have to. It takes a few grains to sweeten a drink...there would be nothing in the packet otherwise. However, I perfer to find it cut with erithritol as this does not spike your blood sure, is all natural, and zero calories.I now simply buy straight stevia in order to sweeten my coffee...in liquid form. It's not mixed with anything and is very economical. One drop sweetens an entire cup of coffee and the liquid form means it mixes perfectly.This isn't a bad sweetener...it could be a bit sweeter if I had my say...but my main gripe is I believe they'd have better marketing if they cut it with another natural zero calorie sweetener with less current controversy.  For agave lovers, however, it would be the best pick. For me, I'm lukewarm.Now, add to that it has silica...this is not in any other stevia products I've bought. Look, I just want stevia...or a stevia and eriythritol blend...but not a mix of stevia and stuff I don't want.Anyone consuming stevia is likely a label reader so I think this product would do well to tigthen its' belt in order to compete...and by that, I mean stick with cleaner ingredients.

We've been dedicated Stevia users for almost 10 years and have tried pretty much every product on the market.We thought we had found the best-tasting one out there--until we sampled Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Stevia.It comes in a foil packet which contains the equivalent of two teaspoons of sugar, but, with stevia, a little goes a long way.  I find half a packet plenty sweet for a mug of tea.And, while first-time Stevia users might detect a slight bitter after-kick, I personally don't notice it.  It tastes closer to sugar than any Stevia product I've previously used.  Maybe because it's organic, or maybe because it's blended with organic blue agave inulin, which also aids in digestion, but I'm really liking it, especially in hot liquids, where it dissolves very quickly.I also like that fact that, unlike my previous fave, it doesn't produce a little cloud of "powder" when you tear open the packet.  I enjoy stevia in may beverages--up my nostrils, not so much.

Always on the lookout for a good non-sugar substitute (or high fructose corn syrup) not necessarily because of calories but sugar has never appealed to me. And, I can't stand HFCS.Stevia tastes very sweet and can easily be the next big thing in sweeteners. As the price continues to drop, keep an eye on this product. This is still a bit pricey and stevia proves worthwhile as a beverage sweeter with limited use in foods.When the price comes down a bit more I'll be switching to stevia for good.

I've been a stevia fan for a few years now.  Usually I buy it in 1.3 oz or 3oz bottles.  Almost always organic, and almost always 100% stevia.What I Like About This Product: These packets of stevia travel easy, and the taste is good.What I Don't Like:  It's not 100% stevia. However, the only other ingredient is organic agave inulin. In fact, the inulin is the main ingredient.  I didn't know what inulin was, so I had to look it up.  It's "a polysaccharide based on fructose present in the roots of various plants."A little more research into inulin found that it has widespread use in the food industry. That's always raises a yellow flag for me, but digging deeper I found it didn't have any reported side effects.  With that, I felt comfortable with this inulin / stevia combination, especially since the inulin comes from organic agave.To elaborate on the taste factor, I've noticed that different brands of stevia have distinctly different tastes (due to many factors).  So while some stevia I love, others are "eh" and some qualify as all out "blech."  This brand has a good taste (to me, anyway - your mileage may vary).It's a fine product that I have no problem recommending. I want to give it four and half stars (only because stevia is not the main ingredient), but I'll round it up to five.

column9: Changed my mind about stevia .. a little....
column10: I last used Stevia about a decade ago; I always found it to be too bitter and just not something I enjoyed. My husband liked it in his coffee and tea, but he seems to be oblivious to off flavors.I have to admit being very surprised when I tried one of these Wholesome stevia packets; I braced myself for that distinctive biting off-placed stevia taste, but it did not come. I would actually use these! I put some in my purse so that we can have them the next time we are at a restaurant that has iced tea. (Restaurants don't stock stevia or anything other than the usual sugar or artificial sweeteners, that I have found)I noted the word 'agave' on the front of the box and I have to admit a negative feeling towards agave; it is not the natural wonder sweetener some people think it is. Hey I used to believe it too!! But then I found how it's processed, and it is no different than corn syrup, it just has a pretty story attached to it. *SO* just by the fact that the word agave was on the front of the box, I would have assumed it was a stevia/agave sweetener and I would never have touched this product. My lip curls at the Agave marketing hype. However it has agave INULIN, a fiber, as a sweetener. This is no different than any other type of inulin you find in other products (like chicory inulin), it just happens to come from agave. So if you have a dislike of agave, don't let the source of the inulin put you off. In this case, inulin is inulin and the source of it does not matter glycemically as it would if we were talking 'agave syrup'.These packets have 1 carbohydrate each, the same as Splenda.My husband of course, liked these packets. He liked them better than the glycerite (liquid reduction of stevia) he's been using. I would buy these for him.

Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Stevia with Organic Blue Agave InulinIf the sweetener boasts of being zero calorie, zero artificial ingredients, can be used with hot or cold food or beverages, comes in an  individual (take anywhere) serving convenience -- into my shopping cart it goes! :)I currently use Splenda No Calorie Sweetener for my bit of sweetness, and am satisfied with it -- but, have always wanted to try Stevia, as an alternative.Compared to Splenda, Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Stevia with Organic Blue Agave Inulin is a wonderful, finely ground, white crystal sort of product, which looks and has the same texture as cane or beet sugar, or Splenda.Dissolves super fast in hot or cold liquid -- and on my daily oat bran or grapefruit half.  I like that! :)I found that Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Stevia with Organic Blue Agave Inulin does not taste as super sweet as Splenda (using one-to-one, individual serving, packet for comparison).  But, that is okay, as taste is subjective to the user!  To Me, it has a mellow, smooth, honey, sort of sweetness.No funky aftertaste.I'm glad I finally tried Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Stevia, and am off to order more!Does Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Stevia sound like what you may be looking for, in a sweetener? :)  Highly Recommended!  --Katharena Eiermann, 2012

column9: sweet enough for me but is not all stevia
column10: I feel it is sweet enough for me but I am trying to tame my sweet tooth and cutting back on sweets. I don't like that it has the agave in it, It is not something I am interested in using on a regular basis. There is some controversy it seems over how good agave really is for your body. I am looking for a natural sweetener that is good for you and tastes good. I am not completely convinced that this is what I want. Everyone has there own tastes and can make their own decisions. This is just my opinion.

I've tried a lot of stevia - not sure why this has agave or silica but then again, the last stevia I bought had lactose listed first, then stevia leaf.The taste is good and it dissovles fast, but I wish it was just pure stevia.

column9: Alternative to sugar, but not very competitive to other Stevias
column10: As I continue to try to decrease sugar intake, I like to test out the different brands of Stevia sweeteners. The Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Stevia comes in a box of 35 individually sealed packets. Each packet contains 1 gram. Most of that weight is in dietary fiber according to the box - 0.8 grams. The individual packets are large enough (6.5 by 4cm) that you can fold over if you only plan to consume a portion of each packet instead of the one packet.I compared this to my current favorite Stevia, the Stevita Supreme - 50pkts - 1.8 oz / Packet and here is what I found: Stevita is more white, while this one (Wholesome Sweeteners) is more off-white/creamy. Stevita is more crystalized while this one is more on the flour side of things. Stevita tastes better on a direct taste test, but when I mix them in a drink (tea, water, etc), there's no big difference. Stevita does not have dietary fiber. Both are 1 gram per packet, and the packets are about the same dimensions. Prices can change over time, but based on current prices, Stevita is a better value.The inside back of the container includes a $2 off coupon pre-printed on the actual container.

column9: Good but not the stevia I prefer
column10: I like stevia but through my journey's thru different types I prefer the liquid best because you don't have to wait for it to dissolve and I would rather have a pure stevia product not any additives which this has. I don't know why they call it stevia anyway because it's a hybrid of two different sweeteners. This isn't bad but for me it's not the best.

I think I'd only give five stars to sugar so four is probably as good as its going to get for a zero calorie experience. The little packets are nice to carry; they are a bit heavier than most artifical sweeteners which are in fragile packets. You can carry it in your purse without being afraid that it would end up on the bottom.

column4: ROBERT W. SAINTJOHN "I am The Pumpkin King"
column9: An addition, but not an alternative to sugar or Splenda
column10: Our family has gone out of our way for years to reduce sugar as much as possible in this modern lifestyle. For the past few years, that has mostly involved switching to products using Splenda (sucralose-based) as a sweetner, and a sugar/Splenda mix for tasks like baking.We've never used a Stevia based product until now, partly because we've been happy with Splenda, and partly because I'd heard so many complaints about bitterness. Wholesome Sweeteners seems to have resolved this problem with their Stevia packets. We've used it in tea and coffee and it's great, no after-taste or bitterness. We have not used it directly on anything like cereal yet, but our friend did and she likes it as well. Will definitely be purchasing some more.

column9: A half packet in a cup of tea provides a smooth sweetness
column10: When I first received this product, I was concerned to see that organic agave inulin was the first ingredient. I was expecting the ingredients to contain only stevia. However, after researching it, I found that this is common among the stevia products I've used.I tried it first using one packet in a cup of tea and found it too strong. But half a packet is perfect.  It dissolves quickly and provides a smooth and enjoyable sweetness.  I usually use liquid stevia, so I'm used to the stevia taste (which is slightly different than sugar).  I was impressed to notice little difference betwen this powder and the liquid form.This is a good product that I would purchase again.

This product was a happy addition to my usual afternoon tea, and indeed has a nice flavour, without any after-taste or bitterness. I only withheld the fifth star because, since I have never experienced any bad effects from other, less expensive artificial sweeteners, Stevia is relatively more expensive.

column9: It's ok, but not my favorite artificial sweetener.
column10: I liked the idea of an organic sweetener, so I was prepared to make Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Stevia my preferred product, but after trying it for a month, I think I shall stay with my old favorite, Splenda.  Stevia is "OK", but I found it to be not as sweet, when used in some instances.  My breakfast Cheerios needed at least two packets, and still didn't seem to pack the sweet flavor.  Plus I found the individual packets rather difficult to open sometimes.  They are kind of a foil/plastic type packet, and occasionally they fight back when I try to open them.  Plus sometimes the product is lumpy inside, despite the packaging.  If you are truly wary of side effects of other sweeteners, than this should work for you.  But I'm not going to give up my old brand.
This is a natural sweetener which does the job. Similar to other brands.My impression is that their sweetness is not quite as potent as another brand we use.But that is being a bit picky.Recommended.

I've been using this in my coffee for the last few mornings and I like it. It's certainly not as good as real sugar.... and most definitely not as bad as artificial sweeteners. I appreciate that it's healthier than those nasty chemicals, and I also like that it has a very minimal aftertaste. It's also great that it doesn't have the calories of sugar. Great for coffee, I'll continue to use it!

Sure, nothing tastes quite as good as sugar, but this product is just as tasty as the other Stevia based sweeteners on the market. And unlike so many of the other sweeteners on the shelves, it won't have a negative glycemic impact. Thumbs up.

column4: Julie A. Dawson "Bards and Sages Publishing"
column10: At over $4 for a box of 35 packets, this is a pricey sweetener, organic or not. The quality is very good. There is no weird aftertaste and it has a pleasant taste. But I can't say it is so much superior to other sweeteners to justify the price. Seems to be common with all stevia-based products. If you can catch it on sale at your local supermarket, pick it up. But Amazon isn't really offering any deal on the price here and there are less expensive alternatives at your local supermarket.

column9: Better Tasting Than Other Brands I Have Tried
column10: I have Diabetes II and I have tried various sweeteners over the years, but have yet to find a product that I really like.  I don't drink coffee, mainly hot and iced tea. so I use these 'sugar substitutes' daily.  I also use it on cereal and again, I like the taste, it doesn't have a metallic taste as some other products have.  I can actually enjoy the taste of the cereal.Organic Stevia does not have the bitter taste that I have found in similar products.some  I am starting to enjoy using it, which surprised me.  I love sugar and honey :-) but since they are a no no, it is nice to finally find a product that  I actually like.UPDATE -10/1/12.  Still using and enjoying this product, but it is pretty expensive, for the little packets.  Other brands sell it in larger packages like sugar and it really lowers the cost and the waste if you don't use a whole packet and have to save the rest for later.  I called the company and they told me that they were hoping to put it out in a larger package in the Spring, one you could spoon out like sugar.  They have no exact date or price yet.I love margaritas, but rarely make them at home or drink them in restaurants because of all of the sugar.  Last night I made some at home in my Vitamix, using their whole fruit recipe (orange, lemon, lime) and substituted 4 packets for the 3 tablespoons of sugar that the recipe called for.  It was excellent with no after taste and no guilt. I halved their recipe and the two of use got l.5 glasses each.  Now if I could figure out how to use it in chips .. I would be way ahead of the game :-).

column9: One of the better Stevia products on the market
column10: I recently ditched sugar and artificial sweeteners and discovered Stevia since it's a healthier alternative and plant-based. However, not all Stevia products are the same and it's a good idea to check out the ingredients since the stevia products you now see on the shelves are not pure stevia. Many contain a corn-based sweetener called erythritol or Stevia in the Raw contains dextrose.I regularly use Sweet Leaf and Kal Stevia as they're both the purest forms of Stevia and would highly recommend those over all others. However, Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Stevia is a great choice over many other brands of Stevia. The ingredients are Organic Agave Inulin, Organic Stevia Extract (Stevia rebaudiana), and Silica and it's certified organic. Agave Inulin is a natural dietary fiber and Silica is a common additive in food products, which is also sold as a mineral supplement. It's something we already have in our bodies and it's essential for increasing bone strength.Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Stevia has no bitter after taste and I find that one packet sweetens my coffee just as well as two teaspoonfuls of sugar. If you're looking to make the switch from sugar and artificial sweeteners, this is definitely a smarter choice.

I used this in a few different teas and found it added sweetness, but not the clean taste of sugar.Actually, I prefer my tea plain, but wanted a vehicle that would allow the Stevia flavor to come through.Like others who have reviewed this product, I have found differences in bitterness in different brands. This one was not bitter, per se, but it still had that echo of "not sugar."That said, if I had to stay away from real maple syrup (my sweetener of choice), I would probably buy this brand.The fact it's organic is a plus, though with the tiny amount you eat, I am not sure how crucial that is.

column9: Comparable in taste to other powdered stevia brands
column10: This powdered stevia is comparable in quality to other brands I have tried. Like other no- or low-calorie sweeteners, stevia is extremely concentrated, so the envelope contains other substances as well, in this case organic agave inulin and silica. Each envelope contains a little over a half teaspoon of powder in all.Each packet claims to sweeten "like 2 tsp. of sugar." However, I found it to be comparable to one teaspoon of sugar.While the agave inulin and stevia are organic and this may attract some buyers, in my opinion, Truvia Natural Sweetener, 300-Count Package has a more sugar-like taste. That being said, I strongly prefer SweetLeaf SteviaClear Liquid Stevia, 4-Ounce Bottles (Pack of 2). This form of stevia is more economical and a more palatable sweetener than any powdered stevia brand.For any buyers who are new to stevia, I recommend using this in foods, but not in drinks. Stevia always tastes odd to me in beverages, though it may be that one can become accustomed to its unusual taste/aftertaste in time.

I have used Sweetleaf brand stevia off and on for years and find this  Wholesome Sweetness to be the same as far as taste.  The only way I can enjoy the no-calorie sweetness of stevia is in tart or acidic foods.  For instance using stevia in lemonade or to make a warm apple cider vinegar quaff.  Also it is excellent sprinkled over grapefruit.  Stevia just does not taste good to me in coffee, tea, or cocoa.  Or in baked goods unless they happen to be lemon squares.  I do feel that the silica in this stevia is unnecessary because it's sealed in single use packets.  The only time I've had caking issues with stevia was when I bought a small jar of it and it turned rock hard after a while.  I've never had that problem with stevia sealed up in single use packets.

column9: Works OK Price is a Little High
column10: This Stevia has less of an aftertaste than the original Stevia.  It is very sweet but it does contains other ingredients.  Instead of repeating I recommend you read K. Franklin's review on ingredients.  It is also a little pricey.  Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Stevia, 35-Count Package (Pack of 6) for 32.52.  That is 5.42 for a box of 35.  Even though it is organic I though that was  a little high.  All of that said it does sweeten very well so it just depends on how much you want to pay for organic and how you feel about the addition ingredients.

I've only used one other Stevia product which was very good. This is just as good and does not leave any bitter aftertaste in my opinion. I only use it in my morning coffee- two packets for a 16oz cup. I'd definitely buy this product if I wanted to stick with something organic. However, I personally still prefer Splenda- whether it's good for me or not.

I just did not care for this.  Put it on a bowl of cereal and tasted the sweetness an hour later.  I think it is too sweet for table sugar use but may work fine in cooking.  It is really really fine, does not look or taste like sugar.  I am always looking for a natural replacement but so far Aspertame seems to be the one I choose.  Like I said, I am always ready to find a better one, but this isn't it in my opinion.

column9: Okay tasting, expensive, not into the hype of agave
column10: When agave first came on the scene I thought it sounded great.  But after a lot more research I don't think it's the wonder sweetener that many people think it is.  It is VERY high in (processed) fructose, not the same as fructose found in natural fruit.  Fructose is metabolized directly by the liver, which is different from other sugars, and can lead to fatty liver deposits. High fructose intake has also been linked to weight gain, insulin resistance, and heart disease risk in animal studies.Also, at the Amazon price this is extremely expensive.  My favorite is a 2 oz. bottle of NuNaturals No Alcohol Liquid Stevia--it mixes instantly in beverages, is not bitter, and lasts forever.

I tried Stevia many years ago but abandoned it because at that time it was only available from health food stores and was very expensive.  It's great that you can now purchase it online or in any major grocery store.  In the past 6 months I've had fun sampling the many new varieties of low-calorie and/or artifical sweeteners that have come to market.  This morning I did a side-by-side comparison of Splenda Nectresse and this Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Stevia.  I had actually tried the Splenda Nectresse about a month ago and couldn't decide if I liked it or not, so the side-by-side with the stevia seemed like a good experiment.  So...first I simply dipped a damp pinkie into each packet and tried them straight-up. BIG difference in taste.  The stevia shocks your tongue with how sweet it is.  The Nectresse on the other hand doesn't convey much sweetness at all and also has a unique taste that is hard to describe.  Next test...half a packet of each in a hot, regular coffee with half-and-half creamer.  Side-by-side tasting yielded a clear winner for me:  the stevia would be my first choice every time in a cup of coffee.  The Nectress adds a funky little taste that I don't enjoy in coffee.  Now, it's possible that the Nectresse would be fine to sweeeten a cold glass of a fruity iced tea.  In general tho' I don't want my sweeteners to have any taste of their own - other than just plain old SWEET.  This stevia answers that call nicely and I would certainly buy it again.

column9: pretty much what you'd expect it to do
column10: Compared to other stevia packets from other competing manufacturers, this doesn't taste all that different.  The only question I have is that one of their ingredients is silica.  Curious as to what that is doing in there.  I see it in my whey as well.  Supposedly silica is a component of our bones and is available in foods like celery, which can strengthen bones.  But not sure why they would add it here.  As a filler agent?The packet dissolves pretty well.  Even a bit better than another stevia packet that I have from another company.

This is the first stevia I have tried. (I'm a Splenda fan, currently.) The flavor was very good, though I was not prepared for just how sweet it is. Blam! Perhaps a half packet is the right amount for, say, an iced tea. I rather prefer the mildness of Splenda, which is not organic.The packaging is very convenient, and it dissolves quickly.

First off, stevia is my favorite natural sweetener.  I was, however, curious to see how Wholesome Sweeteners handled the "fillers" aspect.  The deal is that every packet of low-/no-calorie sweetener (that I've ever run across) is packed in some agent, typically maltodextrin.  In this case, it is agave inulin.  The 1 gram of agave inulin contains 0.8g of fiber, so it's really closer to 1 calorie, whereas typical zero-calorie packets actually contain 4 calories.  Due to a technicality, they get to round down to zero if under 5.  This loop-hole is pervasive in the USA.  Anyway, this 1 calorie is pretty good.  I don't like, however, that they say it's zero calories and you don't need to count them, but it's close.The calories of carbs can creep in if you are on a very strict diet and drink a lot of coffee or tea.  This is especially true if you are on an extremely strict diet like an Atkins or other ketogenic diet. But, for both the price and for true zero calories, you are much better off just buying liquid stevia in a water base.  I do like packets since they are portable.  For that, I give it a some stars, but I will be sticking with liquid stevia where I can, though.

My favorite sweeteners are stevia and agave.  This Organic stevia has a bit of taste of both.  The main ingredient is agave inulin and then the second one is stevia.  This makes it really sweet with no aftertaste.  In fact, you can say that it almost has a hint of honey (must be the agave inulin)  It dissolves quickly too.A packet equals 2 tsp of sugar.  I like 1 tsp in my cup of coffe so I use only half a packet at a time.  It is very good though.  Considering that it is organic and natural, the price is slightly above what I would pay, but I think it's ok if you're used to buying other products with stevia.  Truvia costs about 50 cents less than this organic stevia at about the same number of packets, but truvia is not organic.  So it depends on what you're looking for.

This is a great sweetener. I found each packet sweeter than say Sweet N Low or similar products but at close to five times the price it's a luxury item.As a Vine reviewer I might have given it a higher rating but after checking the price I can't recommend it.

The package says that one packet of this sweetener is like using 2 tsp. of sugar, and I would agree with that.  I definitely like my coffee on the sweet side and one whole packet was just right for me.  There is no bitterness or any kind of chemical taste.The Wholesome Sweeteners brand has a very nice website with all kinds of information on their various products, information about their company, a blog and recipes.  I really don't know that much about the safety of Stevia or anything like that, but if you are interested in checking it out before purchasing, you can find plenty of information there.

column9: My choice for natural no calorie sweetener.
column10: Had not tried this brand before but like the handy packs I can take with me when going out. Stevia is a natural and not processed with a lot of chemical that are harmful to our bodies especially the liver. One I will not name uses formaldehyde,yuck we know other uses for that,Stevia to me has no unpleasant after taste. It is just like using sugar. The fact this brand is organic is all the more reason to buy this brand. I make a lemon water that takes just a pinch and it is a great for that and the combo seem to be acting as an appetite suppressant for me. I know they are making no such claim just passing along something I personally have noticed.If you use other non sugar sweeteners you should give this a try I do believe it is the best tasting and best for your body. Enjoy.

Ok but not as good tasting or as sweetening for me as the NuNaturals stevia - my favorite being the NuNaturals Nustevia Pure White Stevia Extract.The main ingredient is Organic Agave Inulin. I usually avoid agave ( and fructose) as it has to metabolize in the liver.It took 4 packets to sweeten a glass of light lemonade to my taste, twice as many as some other sweetners.

This is my first time to consciously use Stevia. It does sweeten but you'd have to put a heap of it in your cup/bowl for it to match the sweetness you'd get from Splenda. I had a glass of peppermint tea and I used 6 packets before I gave up (the packets are stiff) and the tea was not sweet.Further, the taste is rather earthy although that could be because it's organic.In short, if you like your food/beverage to be really sweet without the calories of real sugar, you may do better with Splenda unless you want to spend 10 minutes opening packet after packet of this Stevia.

column9: great, but these come in a box without a liner...
column10: great candy, just as you would get in the store, however they came shipped in a corrugated cardboard carton direct from jelly belly without a liner ( literally, the candy was just in the box with nothing else- no plastic bag, etc), which was a bit off-putting. However, I assume that if this is how I get it, this is how most retailers get it, meaning I've been eating jelly beans direct from a cardboard box my entire life. I ordered four different flavors of jelly bellies and they all came this way. No one got sick, so I assume this was sanitary.
I ordered these jelly beans to fill wedding favors for my daughters wedding.  They arrived on time,are the perfect color and they taste great!
The jelly beans were verrry yummmy...I can't wait to have them at my daughter's wedding in July...thanks again

I looked all around to find a good price on Blue jelly beans for a baby shower. The price was right and they were GREAT tasting. I did not care about the taste, i just needed blue jelly beans. I was pleasantly surprised.They are great tasting. The shipping was fast and I was happy that I did not spend a fortune. I was very happy with my purchase
I guess I should have read the description more carefully.  Box contains 24 small boxes, each of which contains less than 15 pieces.  I paid way too much for this.

column9: Finest green tea ever and beautifully packaged
column10: This is a remarkable product in every way - beautifully packaged with the bags unbleached, nice cube fort a box, paper of the highest quality, and extraordinary tea - perfectly balanced in every way in terms of taste, which is light but somehow full bodied, smooth, and is pure in feel at every phase of drinking from the first sip to the aftermath of the last sip.  The price is worth it, especially if you remember how even the Mayo Clinic has done recent research confirming green tea's anti cancer properties, so you are adding a few years to your life as well as enjoyment of this extra years!  The only thing that raises any doubt is that it seems impossible to find any information about the company and its location on the Internet.  But the standards of the packaging and the whole spectrum of taste argues that this is as high quality as you'll ever get in green tea.
I have been drinking this tea for years.  I cannot get enough. Really great tasting and perfect with chocolate! I go through these boxes so fast I'm happy they sell these in a 4 pack.
Delicious sweet taste.. Never have I had any green tea as great as this one! My family always enjoys this tea at relative gatherings.

column9: Love these!  I have eaten 3 in one sitting!  But why all the packaging?
column10: I really really like these brownies - they are 75% organic (at least that is what the package says).  I just received my second shipment of 2 boxes yesterday.Question for the manufacture:  why all the waste and individually wrapping these?  Not only are they individually wrapped but there is also a plastic holder for the brownie inside - this just seems to add to the landfills needlessly! Even my husband commented to me about the waste.

column9: Only 2 Weight Watchers Points Per Brownie!
column10: These are great for diets.  Only 2 Weight Watchers points per entire (not huge, but not tiny) brownie.  They are moist, chewy, and yummy.  Low (100) calorie and high fiber, plus 75% organic.  Definitely a great find.

Let's face it, most of us love a good brownie but we don't like all the calories that come with these tasty treats.  Glenny's 100 Calorie Brownie is really good and satisfying.  Frankly, for an organic, low calorie brownie, I was surprised at how rich and full chocolate flavored it taste.  In fact, I'm ordering another box as my friends enjoyed them as much as my family.I also like their packaging.  For one thing, it's easy to toss them into your lunch bag without having them get squashed.  They are also a great  take along treat and because they are so moist, the package keeps them from sticking together.Glenny's has a real winner with this product.  You won't be disappointed by adding it to your shopping cart.

These brownies are pretty darn good.  It depends on what you're used to eating. If you routinely make Betty Crocker or heaven forbid (not really, I love them too) Ghiardelli brownies, you probably won't love these.  But if you eat Kashi and breakfast cookies, you'll find these a really decent substitute, and at only 100 calories, its a bargain.  Not a bad chocolate fix/sweet tooth satisfier for taste buds accustomed to organic and natural foods.

column9: Love, love, love these brownies (soft, chewy and delish) - but too much packaging!
column10: Love, love, love these brownies (soft, chewy and delish) - but too much packaging!These are best 100 calorie brownies I've ever eaten (I think they may be the only ones too)...but they taste like a 200-300 calorie brownie and are very moist, deep chocolately flavor...loves 'em! column9: These are good tasting but not too satisfying.
column10: I am comparing these to Vitalicious and they are not as filling for the calories.They do have the moistness of a real brownie and taste like the fudgie brownie but they are smaller and the packaging is too much for what you get.I like them but I am staying with Vitalicious.There is one important item that these do NOT have which is very important for people who do NOT want iron added to their diet. This does not have iron listed on it.Vitalicious has 50% of the RDA of iron in each piece. I have tried to get them to get it out but they do not listen.Glenny's Brownies are much better for having NO iron added.

column9: Weak taste but priced like gold
column10: I love cinnamon sticks and have bought from many different venders. I boil or pressure cook them to make a big batch of tea. Some give up amazing flavor: sweet, spicy and oh so good. These were weak and woody and were among the worse I have ever bought. I don't mind spending the big bucks but it had better be the best quality. These sticks sucked.
