The sticks are unevenly sized (some very thin, some very thick, some tall, some short) and smell awful, even through the sealed plastic bag!  When my dogs chew them, we can't stand to be in the same room, because the whole room stinks.  I don't know why the sticks from the bag I sampled were evenly sized and smelled fine and this order was so different.  I will look elsewhere for bully sticks from now on as I need to be able to depend on the quality of the product.  My friend also ordered a bag with the same poor results and won't be buying from this company again either.

These bully sticks are super cheap (for bully stick standards) and they last pretty long. I typically buy these instead of the 6" variety and cut them in half for my Cairn Terriers as they last a lot longer. They're pretty tough to cut, but a good hacksaw does a good job in short order. Once cut in half, the additional thickness means they still last about twice as long as the 6" ones.Still wish they were cheaper though!

column9: Bull sticks now much thinner/don't last
column10: My dog LOVES this product and it does help keep her teeth tartar-free, BUT the stick is much thinner than in the past and my dog can now chew through one in less than 1/2 hour as compared to 2-3 days in the past.  Too expensive and too dangerous as she will swallow the stick when at 4".  Company called and they had no explanation for why the sticks are thinner, so will buy the thicker braided 12" sticks through another company on Amazon (1/2 price vs. store pricing).

I'm editing my review. Since then these bullysticks have gone from $19.99 to $24.99 to now $27.99 in just over a 3 month period. I also noticed that when the price was $19.99, there were 12 sticks in each pack. At $24.99, there was only 8. Very disappointed in the raise in price of $8.00 a pack. So, back to shopping around.

column9: Love it, my pooch is ADDICTED
column10: My brother's Siberian Husky loves this item so much he will do ANYTHING for them...When I received them, I was dubious, I wondered how could a great dane possibly chew something so thin and enjoy it "for hours"...It doesn't last long (I'd say 2-3 hours, if they play with it) if the pet is a big Chewer (like my brothers pooch)BUT....it is worth it..in the long run....As I said, he'll do a-n-y-t-h-i-n-g for a stick, and so far, I've trained him pretty well just by using this.I intend to stock up.

column9: Very stinky but apparently taste good
column10: Dog loves them, they last a long time (some almost a week, which is great for a terrier) but they are so stinky I have to open the bag outdoors while holding my breath - I store them double wrapped!

I've ordered several packages of these and the dogs always love them. They can be somewhat smelly but never overpowering that I've found. They all tend to be fairly large with a decent sized diameter. Fantastic value for the price when you compare to Brick and Mortar stores!
Our Rottweiler just love these.  We get a package a month for her.  Never any problem. They also don't stink that bad. She chews them non-stop her favorite treat.

column9: They WERE great bully sticks, now they are just average.
column10: Great bully sticks.  No real bad odor, although there is a little of it.  Quality is good with no pieces looking horribly inedible (for a dog anyway :).UPDATE 5/19/2011:  I've stopped ordering these bully sticks as the quality seems to have gone down.  Not only are they are little smellier, the quality of the sticks has gone down.  They are odd shapes and sizes, and some have loose particles that fall out of the sticks...I don't even want to know what it is.
We have been using these for a couple of years.  Consistent quality and the dog loves them.  However, our 70 lb German Sheppard goes through one quickly and they are relativley expensive.

I usually order 2 packages of these every couple of months for my Labrador who loves them. They have always been a great buy. But they price just went up $5 per package. I'll definitely order them much less often now.

I buy about 5 lbs a month of the 12" Bull Sticks.  They arrive almost immediately.  They keep our Brit occupied so he doesn't chew our shoes, cell phones, or other mouth sized human necessary morsels.

My dog (a labX) loves these!!  She will chew on one for hours, and these larger bull sticks last throughout the day because she takes time out from the chewing.  I will definitely be buying more of these.
good product although not as good as the one purchased at Costco, same company, but just a better quality, smoked, no smell to them, and larger, thicker sticks, for the same price, also more of them
Half of the bully sticks received were practically hollow and my dog tore through them in minutes. There was one quality one in the pack and the rest were junk. Do not purchase these

My sister and brother-in-law rescued a beautiful black labrabull. They had no intentions of adopting a pit bull - quite the opposite, that was the one breed they wanted nothing to do with. But there at the Northshore Animal League their dog Rosie chose them, and they went for it. She's a mellow, friendly, loving, playful, athletic family member. As my sis has two boys - 9 & 10 - they've got the energy to burn exercising their lovable muttigree.One teeny-weeny issue - she chews. She's only 4 months old so teething may be part of it, but based on her lineage, the chewing part will last a lifetime. I read up on bull pizzles. Supposed to last a long time, and give a digestible, safe alternative to typical rawhide bones. I ordered a pack of these. From the reaction from the dog I'll be ordering again and again. Rosie gnawed her very first one is about 15 minutes, wagging her tail the entire time.Yeah, they do smell a bit - but you have to put your nose right inside the bag, or get in the dog's face while chewing (not advisable - my sister said that really stinks.) She solved the problem with Ziplock freezer bags.

column9: caused my dogs to have allergies
column10: both of my dogs got allergies from these bully sticks. Both dogs are itching like crazy, first started with the shaking of the ear then scratching all over. Took them to the vets and finally got it narrowed down to these. Not good at all.

column9: Gross for us, great for dogs!
column10: Yes, bully sticks smell horrible... And if you think about what they are made from you just may gag (or eat yourself up with guilt if you are an animal activist).  However, my dogs go absolutely crazy for these! NOTHING can distract them from their chewing with one of these in their possession!  They are supposed to be much better/safer for dogs than regular rawhides and I have noticed that my dogs don't seem to choke after eating them the way they sometimes did with rawhides.  We have 1 small and 1 medium sized dog, both very aggressive chewers and these keep them occupied for over an hour (depending on the size of the stick).  I think the larger sticks are a better deal and if you have a small saw you can saw them in half for the smaller pups.  Yes they are pricey, but if you have ever bought these at any pet store you will quickly realize that this is a great deal!  One large bully stick at Petsmart or Petco will cost you about $8 and you usually get about 10 per package with these...well worth the cost.  So if you can get past the smell and the source of these nasty lil things, your pups will thank you!

column9: My dog enjoys a little bull
column10: Bully sticks are a great help for keeping my dog busy for a few hours.  This product is a good value if you are to compare it to getting them individually at the store.

My adolescent golden retriever just loves these! As soon as she sees me holding one, she is on her best behavior with the hopes I will give it to her. These are great for when my family and I want to eat dinner with peace and quiet. She will not leave the bully stick alone until it is all done. She chews one up in about 30-45 minutes. I'm pretty sure she is going through a teething phase right now so these are perfect for that as well. She hasn't had any intestinal problems (i.e. diarrhea, vomiting) from these either, which is nice.The only complaints I have is the price and I've noticed a small odor. However, I find the benefits of giving this product to my pup FAR out weigh any costs.

column9: My dog loves these and after one Stick, her teeth look better already !
column10: My dog loves these Pizzle Sticks.  I wish I would have found them or had them recommened to me sooner.  My Pittie can and will chew any type of chew practically within seconds.  I needed to find something that would last longer because I wanted something that would help keep the tartar off her teeth.  She is going to be 6 years old this year, and the tartar is starting.  Even though I brush her teeth, and give her a couple different types of Dentel Chews, this was not helping.  Then a friend of mine whose dog will also be six years old this year, and is the same breed, has the most sparkling, white teeth.  I needed to know what she gives him to help keep his teeth so nice.  She told me about the Pizzle Sticks.  I read up on them, and although I found what they are made of a strange item for a dog to chew on, I gave it a try.  And yes, she had her first one today and she chewed on it, for about 35 minutes.  I was delighted that I found something that she can actually chew on for more than a couple of minutes.  She finished her Pizzle Stick and was so happy.  I looked at her teeth later, and I was amazed that the tartar is almost gone.  Really it is.  So these will be the Dental Chew of choice from now on.  Pizzle Sticks are expensive, but so are all the other Dental chews that I have found available.  And, the Pizzle Sticks from Amazon is one of the best buys of them than anywhere else I have checked.  I highly recommend these Pizzle Sticks.

column9: If only my dogs didn't love them so much...
column10: ...but they do. These are by far my dogs' favorite chew treat. Unfortunately, these are not the "no smell" bully sticks Cadet also makes. That said, the price here is REALLY good and the smell is a small price to pay for something that keeps my dogs from getting into trouble on rainy days when they can't go out.

I ordered from this company a few months ago and was happy, but I just ordered again and the bully sticks were so stinky that we threw away the entire package.  In fact I tried to give them away to a friend with a dog and she wouldn't take them.  They smelled up my entire house during a party which was a bummer for me and my guests.  Now I'm looking for an odor-free alternative.

This is a great outlet for dogs or puppies who like to chew, and chew safely.  While a puppy, one bully stick would keep her entertained for about 2 days, and she never ever went to chew chair or table legs.  Priceless.  Now that she's older (9 months) they don't last longer than 1/2 hour, but it's still a great diversion when she needs something to do on a rainy day.  I limit her to 1 per day as they're not cheap.  If buying bully sticks elsewhere, read the ingredients list.  You want something that's 100% bull pizzle (which these are).  Anything cheaper tends to have something like potato flour in it which has made my dog sick.  My dog loves these.

These bully sticks work wonders for those of you who have a puppy or a dog who likes to chew. To this day my older dog and our young lab love them.The down side is they stick pretty bad so make it an outside treat!!!
Dogs love them, No bugs no problems.  I don't care for the smell, open a window and all is good.

column9: Bull Sticks, dog chews, not as smelly as Costco's same brand
column10: Although slightly more expensive per pound than the same brand from Costco (approximately a 1.2 pound pack vs. 1 pound for same price), these have very little odor, while same brand at Costco are very "aromatic".  Our golden retriever likes both about equally.  The chews seem to clean her teeth.I cut the sticks in half on my band saw, so a 6" piece is about right for a good days chewing.

"Great quality product, good value, I took the advice from other reviews and cut them (easily with garden clippers) into thirds for my 2 Jack Russells. It didn't make much difference to me that they varied in size-some quite large, yes others quite skinny but it evens out and I won't complain about the price when I was paying upwards of 5.00/bully stick."

column9: It's tough to find good long last bully sticks
column10: I was buying sticks from my local high-end pet store.  $6 a whack for a 12" stick.  EXPENSIVE!  But, those sticks last FOREVER.  Like everyone else, I wanted to buy in bulk for cheaper.  This seemed like the best reviewed product on Amazon.  The sticks are OK, but are really like 1-time use sticks.  My small dog can kill one in an hour.  It's probably an equal trade off since the price is so much better, but it's a little frustrating to see similar looking sticks disappear so quick.  Anyway, I'll probably buy the product again because it's so cheap, and it has taught me to be more sparing with the dogs and use the sticks more like treats.  Probably a good thing for them.  It's just a weird change going from leaving a stick on the floor for about a week of chewing activity.

column9: Smaller Than They Used to Be
column10: My five dogs, Mastiff, 2 Labradoodles, 2 Blue Heeler puppies, all under 2 years of age, love Bully Sticks. I started purchasing them at Costco. When they stopped carrying them, for a several months, I purchased these from Amazon. Recently they have been thinner than the first ones I purchased. We go through several pounds a month. Costco has recently stared carrying them again. This batch at Costco, are mostly thick, some even Mastiff sized. In fact the 10 packages I purchased a month ago didn't have many, Doodle sized, only huge. So I cut them in half for the Doodles and Blue heelers, now 5.5 mos old. But never mind, they switch them all out amongst themselves so I've stopped cutting them in half. I use a big tree branch hopper.I was going to order a few packages of the smaller diameter for the "smaller" dogs, here, but the last few packages we purchased at Costco had a few smaller diameter.My 1.5 year old Mastiff finishes one of these smaller ones in a few minutes, if he doesn't get distracted. I then have to give him another and then another. I would rather give them all one large one. When the smaller dogs tire of chewing they will leave the stick, and sooner or later, another finds it for an extra treat. Thank goodness they get along well enough that there is no fighting when only one has a stick; otherwise I would be handing them out throughout the evening and next morning. They get the Bully Sticks when we are home to supervise.I will continue to purchase from Costco as long as they carry them and only purchase these when I have to. I've ordered the "premium" sticks but they cost quite a bit more.

My 20 lb Border Terrier loves bully sticks!  I buy them at Costco when I can, but these are excellent...just a few dollars more.I cut them into three pieces so he can hold them easily.  Great prodouct and fast shippp8ing!  Thanks!

Our Golden loves to chew pretty much anything we give him, but these bullies are far and away his favorite. When we ask him if wants a bullie, he jumps up, runs to the cupboard where we keep them and hops up and down excitedly. One of these last about an hour for him. He usually doesn't leave anything for a second go-round.As for the vendor, Rawhide Depot is outstanding. My order usually arrives in two days tops. Even if I could find these local - which I can't - I'd still use Rawhide Depot because of its customer service.

After buying some Bull Sticks at the local store, my new puppy loved them.  This was the cheapest place I could find to buy them on the internet.  The quality is high and identical to what I had found in the store.  And, my puppy still loves them!!!

For such a little dog, my bichon is a powerful chewer and like all dogs, he HAS to chew! He rips through most man-made chew products made for dogs or just plain ignores them. This product may smell bad to humans, but it is smells wonderful to my dog and my dog loves it! He does not chew up any of my things because he has his bully sticks (as well as carrots and yams).

product was as advertised, merchant shipped product out very fast.my dog just loved these bully sticks.This was the 2nd time that I ordered from this Vendor and I will nothesitate to order from them again.

The price was great- so I had to order some for my dog to try.  He loves them. Some of the brands you can buy at the local pet store smell foul when chewed, but these are not as strong.  I would buy these again.

column9: MY DOG LOVES LOVES LOVES THESE
column10: THESE BULLY STICKS ARE GREAT. I WILL ORDER THEM AGAIN. GREAT DEAL WITH NO SHIPPING CHARGES. MY DOG LOVED THE FREE SAMPLE THAT WAS GIVEN WITH THE STICKS. NOW I HAVE SOMETHING NEW I CAN ORDER FOR HIM.

I was very disappointed with these bully sticks. They were incredibly skinny. I have been ordering these bully sticks from Rawhide Depot for quite some time and have never been disappointed before. There is usually one in the package that could be better but on the whole they have aways been an acceptable size.  These are priced very well.  I cannot afford to buy them anywhere else. My doggies may have to do without. I may take a chance again in the future but if I receive the same incredibly skinny ones I will never buy them again. The shipping was fast and there were no other glitches. I love that Rawhide Depot offers free shipping on this item if the minium purchase is met and it isn't very high - I think about $30 just off the top of my head. I always shop Rawhide Depot for dog treats and will continue to do so.

column9: No comparison with " 12" Best Bully Sticks" made by BBS
column10: Don't waste your dogs time with these skinny minnie ones. My bulldog puppy shreds any one of these in about 10 minutes.I ordered a pack of these only because Amazon discontinued the prime shipping on 12" Best Bully sticks (by BBS).Absolutely no comparison. These guys dish the sticks out by the pound,not like BestBullySticks by the count, and the sticks by BBS are much thicker and keep my dog happily busy for a long time. Do yourselves a favor and get the good stuff from BBS.

column9: Would have rated 5 stars a couple of months ago, but...
column10: When I got my keeshond puppy about a year ago, I had trouble finding something that he would like to chew (that he was supposed to chew) until I discovered the wonderful world of "Bully Sticks".  My vet advised against nylabone (which didn't interest him at all anyway) and rawhide for puppies, so I let my pup browse the pet store shelves and his nose lead him to the Bully Sticks (any nose from afar could smell these out.)  I handed one to him and it was love at first bite.  They are quite expensive at the pet store, so I was thrilled to see them here on Amazon for such a bargain (compared to pet store prices.)  With all the hype about pets getting sick from products made in China, I was also happy to see that these Cadet Bull Sticks are made in Brazil... (though I know USA would be best.)On average, I've been buying 2 packages of these "Large 1 lb. Bull Sticks" a month for about a year.  At first, my puppy would take at least a whole day to consume one, and it was my sanity saver.  Any time I needed my pup to just chill out for a while, I'd give him one of these long Bully Sticks and he wouldn't want to do anything else until it was finished.  Yes, they do smell.  When you first open the package and if your dog is chewing it by your feet, you will definitely be surrounded by the fresh "pizzle" aroma.  Remember what these things are made of, though.  (It's what makes a bull, a bull. ;)  You also may not want your furry best friend to give you kisses while he's chewing it, but the smell does go away quickly and having my dog content and occupied is worth more to me than a brief "pizzle smell."  Because of their shape, they have not posed a choking hazard to my dog nor do they upset his tummy like many other things do.Now, if I had thought about writing a review on these Large Bull Sticks months ago, I would have given this product 5 stars.  I'm rating it 4 stars now because the last couple of recent batches I've gotten, have been very inconsistent in size...  most of them pieces around 6 - 8" long instead of 12" long, however, they do package them to equal out to be 1 lb. worth of bull sticks, albeit some are short and very thin, some are very short and thick, some are long and thick.  (Resisting inappropriate joke...;)  My other disappointment with these latest batches is that the price has gone up about $5 from earlier in the year, but it's still a nice value compared to the pet stores.  Like someone else has mentioned, they also don't seem to grab the attention of my now 14 month old, 45 lb. keeshond like they used to.  The last 2 batches, he'll leave it lying around awhile, but will finish it in about an hour when he does feel like chewing it.  I wonder if/what they changed at the manufacturer?  Though it's still a must-have for me in my arsenal of items to keep the dog busy.

column9: My dog gives these five stars.
column10: My dog gives these five stars.  They stink. When the dog chews on them they really stink. Maybe that's why the dog loves them. At least she doesn't roll on them like she does dead animal parts she finds outside. Even if she did, I don't think the stink would end up smeared on her fur.These are easily $10 cheaper here than at the local pet store. I have them on speed order. Did I say my dog likes them?

was looking for the best value without spending $100.  my 3 dogs are so happy chewing these!  i don't buy rawhide.  the package had mostly large sticks, which is what i was looking for.  the few small ones in the package only lasted a few minutes with each dog, but they will take what they can get.  very low odor considering reviews of other brands.

I dont think a lot of pet owners realize that the reason raw hides are cheaper is because your pets can choke on them.  They can rip chunks of the stuff off while chewing and it will expand after they swallow and choke.  There have also been many cases of raw hides being contaminated with Salmonella especially those imported from China.  I have a friend whose little Maltese got Salmonella from a little raw hide stick off those cute Christmas gift bags.  She got lucky and got better but it took a couple of months and was on lots of anti-bionics.Most shelters & Rescue Groups will not accept raw hides as donations. So although Bully sticks and tripe are pricier, they have better nutrition as well as safety for your pet.  As a precaution, make sure they are not imported from China.
Hoped they were still 12" long.  Not so, 9" and my Golden goes through them much faster.  Almost bite size for her.

column9: Good value, but the smell is horrendous
column10: My bulldog loves bully sticks more than anything. These sticks are a good value, and last quite a long time, but I must say these are probably the worst smelling bully sticks I've ever purchased. My dog sits beside me in the evenings while I watch TV or read, and I gag at the smell of these when she's near me. Will be looking for "odorless" sticks next time around.

Have been buying 1 bully stick at a time in Pet store.  Product from this seller was about half price per stick by buying in a 1 pound package (about 10 sticks).  Ordered and found quality of product to equal that of the higher priced pet store sticks.  Puppy loves them.  Would order again.

column9: My dog loves these bully sticks.
column10: My 11 lb. puppy loves these sticks and they keep him busy while I'm away at work during the day.  The smell goes away and is something I'll put up with as it makes him so happy.
they are like crack for dogs! we use them for special occasions and they always last a good twenty minutes time

This package contains about a dozen bull sticks, ranging from 12 inches to as short as 6 inches long. I have ordered those before and the length of previous orders is about 12 inches. This shipment contains more shorter sticks than longer one. I am disappointed at the shorter sticks as my dog is a large breed.

My dog really loves these bull sticks!  The smell is not so bad when opening for the first time, and definitely goes away completely after a few days.I recommend this product to other potential buyers.

column9: Stinky, But My Dog Loves Them!
column10: This is one of the only "treats" that last longer than 5 minutes with our Golden Retriever.  They smell horrible but he likes them, and that's what matters!

I've gotten these from my local pet store, and am very picky about getting the tallest, fattest one I can locate. Recently the price for one jumped from $2.99 to $4.99, which is ridiculous for a chew stick that lasts no longer than 24 hours, on a good day. I learned of this "economy package" and though there's many, many negative reviews, I thought I'd give them a whirl. Well, I am now in the market for new bull dicks altogether. Exactly half of them were 6" tall and the 12" tall ones were completely anemic. I myself, if this was my business, would be embarrassed to sell this product. There's clearly no quality control. I cannot speak to odor, as I've not opened the package yet, so I cannot comment on that. Maybe that would knock off the last star possible.

Maggie loved the bully sticks, but we could not tolerate the smell in the house. The pack we got smelled like rotting garbage after sitting in the sun for hours. We froze them to help with the smell, but once she starts eating them the odor permeates the room. After eating the bully sticks, we have to give her dental treats to get rid of her awful breath.

You would think that a bull pizzle is created the same, right?  Right?! I have been procuring bull pizzle for my puppy for the past 6mos.  I have bought odor free [read: less odor than full stink] bullies, regular odor bullies [read: first and last 5min is barf-inducing], and then these Cadet bullies [read: ability to make a human pass out while sealed in the bag]. Apparently, not all bullies are created alike and these bullies are not for my lil miss pittie mix.  She'll chew on them for a few minutes and leave them.  With other bullies, she would chew forever.  Maybe it was just this batch.In the bag that I got, there were about 9-11 bullies of different lengths and thicknesses.  There were about 5-6 6" fairly thick bullies; 2 or 3 thin (like a reed) bullies; and some others.  I am sure each bag has a different variety, but they were definitely not all large.  Unless large has multiple meanings, such as small, short, thin. They somewhat do the job for now, but I will go back to other vendors.

column9: Not as good as it used to be
column10: My dog used to love these and would chew through an entire piece in less than an hour. With the new one, it's been over a week and there's still 3 inches left. They seem to be thinner, but they don't stink as much. However, if that's what my dog wants and I am buying it for him then I rather it be something he wants to chew even if it stinks.

column9: Great for our pit bull and our wallet
column10: Our 75 pound pit bull loves bully sticks, but they're horrifically expensive at our local pet store.  These are larger than the ones at the pet store, but less than half the cost.  Our dog is an aggressive chewer and will rip through just about any other treat.  These bully sticks will keep him occupied for 5-10 minutes, which doesn't sound like much, but it is for our dog.Like most other bully sticks, the smell is a bit, um, pungent.  It helps if you open the bag in the garage and let them air out for a few days.  Also, your dog's breath will reek, but he'll reek happily.

column9: Not the long lasting chew I hoped for
column10: Purcahsed these for my 62lb, 14 month old, Shepherd/Boxer mix.  One stick lasted maybe 30 minutes.  My dog enjoyed it, but it just didn't last long enough.

column9: Longest lasting chew toy I've found
column10: I've finally found a chew toy that can keep my hyperactive dog entertained and distracted for more than 10 minutes. I've tried everything - she had no interest in hooves, pigs ears rarely lasted more than a few minutes and synthetic toys couldn't get even the slightest bit of attention from her. These are absolutely great! She has finally stopped chewing on my childrens' toys! They do smell rather horrible while she chews on them but they get the job done.

Costco doesn't always carry this large sack of bully sticks, and pet stores charge $9 for one or two, so for our dog's chewing bliss and us not having to keep our own dinner down when we walk by, this is a great buy.  Usually no odor, arrived quickly, and the dog is content.

My chihuahua has loved bully sticks ever since I brought him home.  They keep him busy for long periods of time and I guess overtime has prevented him from chewing on "no no"  items in my home since I've never had those issues with him.  My chihuahua runs through these so quickly so continuing to purchase locally no longer made financial sense. I feel the large bull sticks are a great value as previously I was paying $7-$10 per bull stick - purchasing Large Bull Sticks, 1 Lb comes to around $2 per bull stick so I will definitely be a repeat buyer. The smell is intense but I'm used to it.  These 12inch sticks last about 3 days with my little one.The only reason I gave this 4 stars was the packaging, it comes in a thick plastic that is tightly sealed but I prefer something that snaps shut because of the smell.

My 3 dogs absolutely love bully sticks. Head to your local pet supply store and you will be horrified to find out that these can cost as much as $12 a piece! This 1lb package is a great deal especially if you get the free shipping. In my last package I received eleven, 12" bully sticks that were all quite thick.As some other reviewers have mentioned they do smell. It's a gross smell but guess what dogs love gross stuff! It's not the type of odor that permeates your house, lingers or makes you gag (at least not me). It usually takes my slowest chewer 20-30 minutes to finish one and my most voracious chewer about 15 so that's not as long as some might hope but really for my adult german shepherd dogs and one cattle dog this seems to sate their need to chew and they really love them. When they were pups they lasted even longer.A very nice treat!Edit: Some reviewers have said these bully sticks are yet another product "made in China" but that is not the case. I check every package I get and they all say "Made in Brazil".

column9: My dog enjoys them, but not very long lasting
column10: I have a medium-sized 60 lb dog who is not an aggressive chewer. He can go through one of these in under 10 minutes, however. He seems to enjoy them quite a bit, so I keep buying them. I've bought several packages so far and I've noticed that in every package, there is a stick or two that smells absolutely AWFUL. The smell for most of the sticks is usually pretty unoffensive but occasionally you get one that stinks to the high heavens. The stinky ones don't seem to give him digestive issues so I guess they're fine, but it is a little weird....Can someone please comment and tell me why bully sticks are so expensive? Is there a reason or is it because pet companies know owners will pay through the nose for their dogs' enjoyment? Bully sticks are just cow penises after all!

column9: Very Smelly Bully - The dog likes them but I don't
column10: My dogs have had many different types of bully sticks over the years.  Some have a funky smell.  These are the worst smelling bully sticks I have ever smelled.  With other bully sticks, the funny smell goes away after the bag has been open for a few minutes.  These bully sticks really stink.  They have a very strong smell that you can actually smell from many feet away. And it does not go away even after the stick is gone. Not only in the bag but hours later and the smell goes wherever they go.  My puppy now has stinky breath.  My family room where he has been chewing reeks of funky bully.  But dogs being dogs really love bad smelling things.  I am not returning them but I will never buy these again.  We will be sending them to the kennel next time my dog has an overnight stay and letting them keep the leftovers.  We have had better luck with 12" Free Range Bully Sticks Thick Select Odor Free 25 pieces Sealed with UPC  Even though they are not Prime eligible.

I was turned onto these bully sticks by a dog forum I belong to. I have a 12 month old female Labrador that LOVES to chew! She will chew walls, carpet, toys, shoes, wood, ANYTHING! You know, I feel so guilty that I had been feeding this crap to my dog for 3+ years and I admit the only reason I did was because I didn't know any better and it was affordable. Why did I not put 2 and 2 together when he stared getting very dry, flaky skin, itchy paws, hot spots, red crusty sores and on top of all that - ear infections? When I started learning about the ingredients in dog food it really opened up my eyes. This food is a sham. They want you to believe it's chock full of beef and vegetables but it's not - it is full of corn (which is a an allergen), flours, fillers, artificial ingredients, fats and sugar with a little bit of beef and veg thrown in at the end. No wonder my dog was having so many problems with his health! I have since switched to higher quality foods with chicken, lamb or fish meal as it's first ingredient. I highly recommend these brands if you want your dog to thrive on healthy whole foods full of nutrients and flavor: California Natural, Innova, Canidae (the old formula), Merrick and Wellness Core. See http://www.dogfoodanalysis.com/ to research all brands of dog food.

column9: Healthy as a box of chocolates for your dog.
column10: You would think such a large brand should be trusted; that they made money by making a healthy product for dogs. Well, let me not even say what effects this dog food had on my dog--let me just show the beginning of the ingredients list from the [...] website as of the date of this review (Check there yourself if you don't trust me):Ground yellow corn, chicken by-product meal, corn gluten meal, whole wheat flour, animal fat preserved with mixed-tocopherols (form of Vitamin E), rice flour, beef, soy flour, sugar, sorbitolCorn and corn gluten and rice flour are not exactly wonderful, but--SUGAR and SORBITOL! Sorbitol, that nasty stuff in gum that gives people gas and loose stools! Can you wonder why your dog stinks up the house if it's eating this crap? And sugar! Need I even say why that is bad, or what health problems that can lead to? My vet sure got on a soapbox over the dangers of sugar, and rightly so. And even the "healthy weight" stuff has sugar and sorbitol in it!Don't buy Beneful for your dog. Pay careful attention to the entire ingredients list of the dog food you DO buy, as a lot of brands sure don't think you care about whether your dog lives many years or has expensive vet bills as long as it scarfs down their corner-cutting product. And if you must buy Beneful, at least send the company a few angry letters telling them to take the sugar and fake sweeteners out so you no longer have to feel you're killing your dog. I mean, come on, they could use apple juice if they wanted a sweetener. This is incredibly unhealthy and reprehensible, if you ask me. I sure won't buy this dog food ever again, and I would think twice before trusting Purina.

column9: not going to kill your dog but definitely not healthy
column10: I fed Beneful to my last dog for 13 years and he lived to be almost 14 years old so it obviously isn't going to kill your dog.  But my current dog has really bad skin allergies and the vet said to try switching food first. That was the first time I looked at the ingredients in Beneful and was shocked! Even with water normally too hot for green teas, the result is a smooth, low tannin flavor.  There are a few downfalls, however...Although each tin has a generous amount of tea bags, there is NO air tight seal.  You rely on whatever reduction in air exchange through the tight fitting aluminum lid.  Once you open this 60-bag pack, therefore, try to drink it quickly.  If you drink a lot of tea, this may not be a problem.  Oxygen in the air catalyzes rapid degradation!That being said, the tea, so far, is still wonderful after a couple month of usage (down to 1 tin!).Another issue, I like my tea to have a little stronger flavor than these bags allow.  It may be a product of the amount of tea in the bags, but even steeping in boiling water for over 10 minutes does not extract a ton of flavor.  If you're looking for a VERY light tea, this will not be a problem for you.I've adjusted my drink schedule and switched to my strongly caffeinated, stoutly flavored coffee for workday mornings and this delightfully light tea for weekends.In summary, this tea is quite fresh and tasty with almost no bitter tannin flavor, though comes with no airtight seals and brews a little weak for me.  A great buy if you consume a lot of tea, or have two friends who would benefit from your generosity.

column9: Use in place of  garlic oil...
column10: Truffles remind me of garlic with an added dimension of aromatic appeal. In fact, I'm convinced that you can use truffle oil in many recipes that are compatible with garlic oil. While black truffles are highly prized, you may prefer the white truffle oil in a rice recipe."Risotto with Red Bell Peppers and Truffle Oil" is a good example of a recipe using truffle oil. I actually created this recipe using the URBANI truffle oil and it is superior in flavor!The chicken base gives excellent flavor and is less salty than most bouillon cubes which are less flavorful.1 T. Urbani "white" truffle oil1 T. salted butter1 chicken liver, chopped, this is optional1 T. chopped yellow onion1 T. chopped fresh parsley1/4 c. chopped celery stalks1/4 c. chopped red bell pepper1/4 tsp. ground black pepper1 tsp. garlic salt1 c. uncooked Arborio rice1 T. chicken base4 c. boiling waterHeat the oil (some have told me to add it later, but I don't think it makes much of a difference in this recipe) and butter in a 6-quart Dutch oven over medium heat. Fry chicken livers, then add onion, parsley, celery and bell pepper. Cook 5 minutes. Add pepper, garlic salt and rice. Stir until rice absorbs the butter and looks transparent on both ends of the grain. This actually takes 2 minutes. Stir in 1/2 cup of the water with chicken base. Stir until most of the water is absorbed. Continue to add water in 1/2 cup additions for the next 30 minutes. This dish must be continually stirred and is completely done when water is almost completely absorbed and there is a creamy sauce coating the rice. Serve immediately or the creamy sauce will be absorbed into the rice and you will have a drier, but still delicious, dish.Makes 6 servings.Recipe Note: This creamy dish is perfect as an accompaniment to Roast Chicken. Red bell pepper has a dramatic effect on any dish it touches, any remaining bell pepper may be chopped and frozen to be used later for decorating a cream soup.~The Rebecca Review

column9: Do not use this in your cooking
column10: I used to use white truffle oil in my cooking a lot. I had it on a dish at French Laundry and figured it was a great way to up my game and make myself a "fancy chef."  That was before I figured out how to actually cook.  For some background: truffle oil is not an oil made from truffles. There are no truffles in it.  It is olive oil combined with 2,4-dithiapentane, which gives the oil a truffle aroma.  Although 2,4-dithiapentane is not a chemical and is organic, it's still not truffle.  If you see a dish in in a restaurant that uses truffle oil, it is usually because the chef is trying to jump on the "truffle craze" without resorting to the expense of using actual truffles.That being said, I won't lambast the product completely. You can make a successful dish with it if you know what you're doing and use it sparingly (better to cook with it than to use it in the raw form as a dressing to anything).  I've had several truffle oils and Urbani's is one of the worst, because of how pungent it is. The truffle smell is overpowering, and I don't believe they use a good olive oil base, because the stuff goes bad after a couple months.My advice is to stay away from all white truffle oil, but if you have to use it, try to find a better brand than this.

I try to buy it in bulk when I can to ease the sting of the price a bit.

column9: Many great evenings over Asian fumes
column10: Perfectly proportioned and very generously bagged. The strongest tea on the market. Powerful, tasty, energizing.The most addictive chai tea ;)

column9: Great alternative to daily Starbucks trips
column10: My wife and I are big fans of hot morning drinks (with caffeine), especially in the winter. We realized this to be a great way for us to get our morning fix more affordably from home. It's been about a year now and somehow this "flavor" tea hasn't gotten old yet!

I love this tee. I steep two bags for about 6 minutes in the boiling water, and add local honey. After i steep it, I add soy milk. Or I pour it over a tall glass of ice, and the soy milk. It taste so good hot or cold.

I have to agree with most of the other reviewers, this is the best black tea spice blend you can find.My problem is with Amazon pricing it very close to retail price even if you are buying in bulk. I would rather pay little more and pick up a fresh box every month. I have even found them on discount in mid town nyc store. So I am not too eager to stock it from Amazon.
I love hazelnut coffee and Coffee Master delivers on it's promise. Rich, flavor-full, with a great aroma. Far above what you can get in a local market. Good job Coffee Masters.

I'm a big fan of Hazelnut, but there was something seriously wrong with our shipment. All 4 bags tasted like soap, or perhaps some kind of rancid oil on the beans. I see that many other Coffee Masters products have gotten decent reviews, so perhaps this was an aberration, but I know I will be avoiding them in the future.

column9: the best main lobster bake through the mail ever
column10: I had food ordered through the mail before and I never had such a delicious meal in my life.  I will order from you again with no doubts.  I was a little afraid in the begining but Im so happy that I went throught with the order.  If you want an romantic dinner for two this is the way to go.  follow the instructions to the tee and you will not be sorry.

Easy to prepare, this was a nice meal. The potatoes were excellent and the clams and mussels were tender and delicious, but the shrimp and lobster were somewhat disappointing, being tougher and less flavorful than I anticipated. The lemon-butter sauce was a bit lemony for my taste.I could prepare a slightly better quality meal for less money from fresh ingredients if they were easily available, but the convenience and quality of this package are certainly worthwhile. I would buy it again, and probably will.

column9: Excellent Balsamic! Well Worth the Money
column10: Like most Americans, I'm used to the same balsamic taste that remains pretty much the same across all major grocery store brands. This is not that at all. An incredibly intense flavor, this balsamic is a thick, sweet syrup to be used sparingly. It's great drizzled over salad! I bought mine in Florence at 20 euros, so this is a bit more expensive for the exact same thing, but even with this, I highly recommend if you love great tasting balsamic.

I eat these once every day! They are low in sugar, high in fiber and protein. I have been on weight watchers and lost 30 plus pounds...these are only 3 points a bar! They are delicious and nutritious and fill you up.

column9: Healthy and Tasty Snack Cherry-Dark Chocolate Bars
column10: A nutritionist recommended Kashi products and bars to me.  When you want a little bit of chocolate, these don't quite replace a Snickers Candy Bar or Chocolate Chip Cookie, but they come close enough for me.  They're a non-guilty pleasure.Dark chocolate is good for you, say health experts.  These also pack 5g protein and 4g(15%) of fiber.  Only 8g of sugar (a Snickers candy bar has 28.8 g of sugar by comparison or almost 4X the sugar of these Kashi bars--nutritionists say your body burns sugar BEFORE fat as it's easier to burn so your body will keep the fat.) These are only 120 calories per bar vs. 280 calories in a Snickers bar--not to pick on Snickers but it demonstrates why these are healthier than most candy bars.  I like to take them in the car when I'm running errands and need something to tide me over, or they're a tasty after-meal treat.A confession: I grabbed this box by accident at the grocery store thinking I was buying this Kashi bar: Kashi TLC Chewy Granola Bar, Dark Mocha Almond, 6-Count Bars (Pack of 6) which is my absolute favorite.  I generally like my chocolate straight-up and not mixed with fruit.  However, as an alternative, the cherry taste is refreshing although I think the dark chocolate taste, which I love, is stronger in the other bar with the almonds.  Family members may prefer this one, however.  So, it's great to have two healthy treats in the house that are better nutrition than a candy bar or cookie.If you like the taste of cherry with chocolate, you may want to try these bars.
These are my absolute all-time favorite!  Delicious, filling and so good -- what a kick that they're healthy food, too.

column9: Someone Please Hand Me a Glass of Water
column10: I'm not sure if I'll be buying these again. They are only 120 calories per bar and contain 5 grams of protein, but wow are they dry. The occasional tart cherry taste is nice. I'd like even more. I also could not taste the dark chocolate - at all. Maybe I'll eat the remaining bars with my morning coffee.Be sure to have water on hand when eating these.

column9: Tastes Good, not the best quality of bean
column10: I'm a home roaster, and I really enjoy coffee. This blend does taste good when roasted. My reason for 4 stars is the quality of bean is not the best. I had to sort through it to find rocks and bad beans before roasting. This was the first time I had to do that with this company. Not a big problem, I paid less than the fancier ones. The beans roast well, but turn out less attractive than the higher quality beans. If I was stretched for money I would purchase this product again, but I would probably pony up for some higher quality beans next time.

column9: great green coffee from coffee direct
column10: this blend roasts to a medium color and has a great flavor and aftertaste. it becomes somewhat bitter if roasted to french roast.

I have bought this before direct from the site and let me tell you it keeps your eyes wide open. I instantly noticed how much caffeine was in it after one drink. Kept me wired to the point of jittering for hours after 3 cups.The taste was fairly decent; better than most commercial blends.
I've roasted this twice now. it's OK. I use a whirlypop popper and have roasted it at about a City + roast. Not bad, nice and smooth, but not my favorite. I will probably not order it again.

Been home roasting for two years now. I use an I-Roast II, but stop by sound, sight and smell. I would not recommend the light roast that the company claims it is blended for. The mixture of bean types and sizes just do not really allow all of the beans to roast to same level. This is true of a darker roast as well, but at least all the beans make it to/through first crack. Not the best blend I've experienced, but satisfactory. I roast at FC+, with some beans falling into the french roast catagory. Tough to beat the price and the beans were dry. I'll buy again, but not too soon. May give some of their others a try. Arrived very quickly. That impressed me. I usually buy from Sweet Maria's but their arrival is usually about a week or so. My decision to buy was more out of a need to get some beans quickly, as I was down to my last couple of roasts of the beans I had left. Give this one a try. It may be to your taste. It will still certainly taste better than folger's, no matter how melange the roast.

I've been roasting coffee beans for over ten years, couple times a week, and the Eyes Wide Open Blend is a winner, particularly in its price range.  Normally I don't buy blends since they tend to be "whatever we got too much of" propositions, but this combo, as of 4/12/12, has the desired balance one looks for in a fresh-ground cup.

column9: It's ok, but there is better
column10: I'm a relatively new home coffee roaster using an air popper.  I've only bought beans on Amazon from Coffee Bean Direct and this blend isn't as good as others I've purchased.The beans are very small, very un-uniform and yes it looks like rocks from time to time.  The best roast for me was right after first crack, let it go to long and it just tastes burnt.I won't buy these again.  They have many fine other beans thought.
There was so much chaff in my roaster after roasting these beans that I had to run it in two cycles; the flavor was fine, but the process was messy.
sucks thought was a brand name the beans aren't eveb roasted what a rip off ordered some more that were actually roasted 1st

column9: A Tasty, Less Sugary Granola from Kashi
column10: I actually like Kashi's new commercials about how healthy ingredients need to taste good to be in their cereals, and then they show a somewhat overweight guy as a food researcher going into various third world situations to find them, Indiana Jones-style. I had an opportunity to try Kashi's GoLean Crunch! Cereal in a sample packet as part of a promotional package Amazon sent me of their non-perishable groceries. Full of their Seven Whole Grains and Sesame cereal, it is indeed tasty without the overwhelming clusters of sweeter granola cereals. There is some of the sawdust taste of barley and soybean in there, but the whole oats and brown rice manage to dominate with honey, cinnamon, evaporated cane juice and brown rice syrup adding a dash of sweetness. A cup is 190 calories, which is higher than my favorite, Kashi's Heart to Heart cereal, but it does have only 95 mg of sodium and 8 grams of fiber. It's definitely a worthwhile entry in the granola category.

This is a tasty, relatively healthy cereal which probably goes well with milk.  I don't know as I don't drink milk, but it works for me as a snack.  Better to nibble on this than sugar-laden or fat-laden commercial "snack foods" IMHO.  It does have some rye & wheat so if you are very sensitive to gluten, this might be a downer.  I'm somewhat sensitive, but it didn't seem to have much effect on me.  Fortunately, the main ingredients are oats & rice.  Enjoy!

This is one of my favorite "healthy" cereals.  It's high in protein and fiber, and doesn't contain artificial ingredients or sweeteners that I can't pronounce.  This cereal also fills me up for most of the morning (unlike many high carb, oversweetened cereals). And, most importantly, it actually tastes good!  The flavor sort of reminds me of Cracker Jack - crunchy and slightly caramel-ly.  I like to add blueberries or dried cranberries to it for a little extra sweetness.  It's also great in yogurt.  My only complaint is that some of the clusters in the cereal are really large, so much so that I have to break them up before eating.  A minor complaint, really.  Overall, I highly recommend Go Lean Crunch!
I LIKE MIXING OTHER CEREALS TOGETHER FOR BREAKFAST  THIS IS PRETTY GOOD ALL ALONE. TRY IT !  ANOTHER KASHI GOODY!!!

column9: This stuff is just downright nasty
column10: Tried this stuff for the first time, and to put it bluntly, the taste is just down right nasty.As for the crunch, I will give them that, but say goodbye to your teeth, it is like chewing on rocks.Avoid this stuff, our black lab finished the box.

As someone with blood sugar issues, I had given up on cereal years ago because they just didn't have enough protein to prevent a "crash." The Kashi cereals with 9 or more grams of protein sustain me all morning! I'm thrilled to be able to eat something besides peanut butter toast for a quick breakfast!! The berry crunch is yummy.

column9: Great Meal At Any Time of the Day!
column10: I love Kashi Golean.  It is filling and high fiber and protein.  I have been able to lose weight eating this cereal and sensible low calorie meals.  I buy it in bulk to save money.
This is very filling and good cereal... kind of guiltless as there is so much fiber in it. We eat it daily, and the brand overall seems to have gone down a bit in price.

I am very disappointed in my last shipment of Kashi Go Lean Crunch.  It was very dry in large lumps--not at all the even distribution of cereal I had expected and have always found in Kashi's boxes for the last several years.  I don't know if this was a shipping problem or a product problem.

I love crunchy cereal or anything that does not turn to mush in 60 seconds. However, this cereal is just way to hard. Mid way through my jaw started to ache and I was seriously concerned about one of my teeth since it only has a temporary on at the moment.I hate to rate a cereal with lots of other good attributes only 2 stars, but I just would not buy this again.

I ate the last bowl today of 7 whole grain Kashi and the last shake of the box which had an experation date of October 2008 exposed the insect, not sure what kind of bug it was, but I know its not whole grain anything!

column9: GOLEAN - the name is a lie
column10: There is no way that one gets lean by eating a food that has 13 grams of sugar per serving (a cup). The product name seems to have been clearly chosen to deceive the buyer. Trust the manufacturer?? Get serious! But, America, just keep on eating it and getting fatter.

I recently went on a new diet without any preservatives and chemicals.  So I switched to Kashi cereal.  And this is my absolute favorite.  The price is much better (with Subscribe and Save) than in the stores too.

column9: Watch out for stale products from Amazon
column10: I bought a case of Kashi GoLEAN cereal from Amazon in December 2007, and opened it only to find an expiration date of March 2008.  According to the manufacturer the cereal has a shelf life of one year and therefore has been sitting on the shelf for the past nine months.  Amazon offered only a partial refund for the stale product.

Delicious cereal but the intense intestinal gas and cramping I will not be buying this one anymore. I am actually in a slight amount of pain. I tried a second box to make sure its not just me, but if you google kashi golean and gas, there are millions of hits.Also, the protein comes from Soy, a no no for certain types of Thyroid conditions.

Tastes great, has lots of fiber, lots of protein, and ....is extremely crunchy, tends to be formed in huge lumps. When I tried to chew it, one of my veneers broke in half. WTF? Seriously I ate  different foods for over a year and 1 stupid cereal  did that!EAT AT YOUR OWN RISK!

They call it "Crunchy". This is much more than crunchy.The taste is actually good, not to sweet. nice honey and nut flavor.BUTThe clusters are big and very hard. Like rockswhen i eat this i have to pour a bowl, add milk and let it sit for at least 10 minutes before i can eat itI much prefer Kashi Heart to Heart Honey Toasted Oat Cereal,

This is a great cereal from Kashi. It has clusters of grains and nuts, and does NOT have high-fructose corn syrup nor sugar, yet it tastes sweet (they use cane syrup, which I assume is not processed like sugar). At times, I have made a meal on it by eating it straight from the box, like a snack. But is very tasty with milk, and doesn't get soggy very fast. My only complaint is that the picture on the box shows it with blueberries, but there are no blueberries in the cereal. This product is one we have bought many times and introduced to others.

Tastes great, has lots of fiber, lots of protein, and stays crunchy all the way through the bowl.  BUT, it stays a bit too crunchy.  This morning, I found a marble-sized, tightly-packed, super-hard piece of "crunch" in my bowl and removed it right away.  Unfortunately, my next spoonful had more of this hard cereal in it.  And, when I tried to chew it, my tooth broke in half.  OUCH!  Sorry, but no cereal should break your tooth, ever!  It's very unfortunate because I ate a bowl of this every day, it's good for me, and I actually liked it.  But, I need my teeth for a few more years.  EAT AT YOUR OWN RISK!

I love Kashi products. I think they taste great and the health stats are sublime. It is with great pain (literal and figurative) that I rate this a 2-star product. I must be in the minority, but about 2 hours after eating any of the Go-Lean cereals I experience pain inducing intestinal gas (farts). Google it if you don't believe me. If this didn't turn my stomach into a pressurized cannon, I would easily rate it 5-stars. It's healthy, tastes great, can be found on sale for the price of regular cereal, and Amazon has it for subscribe and save. Unfortunately, I am one of the seeming minority who will have to stop eating this after making the connection to it's terrible gas inducing powers.

This cereal is extremely crunchy and tends to be formed in huge lumps unsuitable for eating.  "Sweetened cardboard" is what always comes to mind when I try to describe the taste.  It is extremely low in calories compared to other cereals and granolas, but I found it practically inedible.
It does not taste as good as back to nature Granolas, not even Post's pecan cereal. I bought 2 packs, unfortunately, and finished only 1 box in 2 months. I just don't like it.

column9: KASHI GO LEAN JUST NOT CUTTING IT!
column10: I love granola cereal and since I'm watching my weight, I decided to try the Kashi GO LEAN Crunch. Well, needless to say, it is not satisying my granola cereal craving at all. It is totally lacking in flavor and texture. I guess some things you just can't mess with and one of them is granola. IMO, LIGHT granola is just that, "light"-weight. I'm going back to the Quaker Oats 100% Natural Granola Cereal, which by the way, does include raisins and almonds so I don't have to add my own.
Beware, this product is not vitamin fortified. It is probably best utilized for its fiber content.

If you are looking for a healthy, good tasting cereal you should try Kashi's GOLEAN Crunch.  Compared to most healthy (particularly high protein and high fiber) cereals, it has a higher protein and fiber content per serving.  As important, it tastes good.  Its taste obviously cannot compare to some sugar filled normal cereal, but as health cereals go, this one is a keeper.  I eat it 3-4 days a week and have done so for over a year and I still like it!  Just note that you may want to buy one box from your local grocery store before buying a six pack from amazon.com just to make sure you like it.

Kashi GoLean Crunch! is really good. Seriously, truly tasty. It's got a real "crunch!" to it, as the name makes clear -- but after the initial crunch, it's got this understated sweetness about it, a mixture of cinnamon and maybe a little honey. Mmmm. A bowl is very filling, and here's the amazing part: it actually KEEPS me full. For hours. As for the "clumps" that some people are complaining about, those are my favorite part! It's just a characteristic of the cereal -- kind of like how, sometimes, pizza will have a bubble of dough in it. Mmmm. Love the bubble, love the clumps.HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

column9: Great to eat right out of the box
column10: I've been eating GOLEAN Crunch! cereal for over a year now and the exclamation mark after crunch is fitting.  There are huge round clusters at the top of the box perfect as finger food, but after you get half way or so into the contents most of the rest is small and harder to eat right out of the box.  Still tasty and crunchy, however.Despite the great taste without milk, or in concert as a granola topper of sorts, I find that this cereal causes an inordinate amount of gas buildup in my system.  Hence the rating of 4.  It may be just me, or one of the seven grains is the culprit.  And, despite this realization, I'll continue to eat it primarily because of its great taste and good all-around nutrition.

I love this cereal so when I saw a big sale on the 4.3oz boxes of it I bought 48 boxes!  Halfway through our first breakfast my wife realized that the little black seed looking things in the cereal were actually little dead bugs!!!  Once she said that I started looking in my bowl and realized it was full of them!  I'm a big fan of the cereal but will NEVER purchase any from Amazon or probably off the internet for that matter.  Grocery store is fine with me!  Buyer beware!

With so many other glowing reviews, I feel a little ashamed to put my own lukewarm review in.  Kashi GoLean Crunch! has 7 whole grains in it, which means puffed rice is mixed with oats and rye and other grains to make clusters.  It's naturally sweetened, which is a plus, and it definitely stays crunchy in milk.  Really, really crunchy.  It has sort of a sweet, oat-slightly-nutty flavor to it, and it's not bad.However, as I said, I'm not really addicted to it.  I prefer Back to Nature Granolas, and as I wrote this review, I became curious as to their nutrition facts.  So here is the Kashi measured up against the Back to Nature All-Natural Granola, Apple Blueberry, 15-Ounce Packages (Pack of 6) - measured by 1/2 cup servings.  There are definitely more calories in BTN (200 vs. 95), but there's fruit too, which the Kashi GoLean lacks.  BTN has slightly less sugar (6 g to Kashi's 6.5g), less salt (20 mg to 47.5 mg) and there's more protein in it (6 g to Kashi's 4.5g). They are equal in the following categories: dietary fiber (4g) and calcium (2%); there's more fat in BTN (2.5g=4% BTN, 1.5g=2.5% Kashi).  So there is not a lot of difference between the two.But as for the taste and the texture?  I'd readily take granola any day over the Kashi.  I don't like overly crunchy cereals (why buy a cereal specifically named, "Crunch!" right?) and the granola is crisp enough for me.  There are fewer sharp edges to stab me in the gums.

column4: Sherrill St Germain "The Career Change Financ...
column9: More like Go Lean Chew! instead of usual Crunch! despite current "Use by" date
column10: While I eat Go Lean Crunch! often -- not least because of the incomparable crunch -- I have been very disappointed with this particular shipment, which has been more chewy than crunchy right from the beginning.  Kind of like it had been opened and then subjected to humidity for too long.  This despite a "Use by" date of 6/2013.  Edible in milk, but otherwise, blech.  Was hoping it was a fluke w/the first box of the 3, but no such luck.  At this point, I can't return it, but if this happens again, I'll have to reconsider where I buy it.
Kashi GOLEAN Crunch! Cereal ..  this cereal is a little sweet for my taste.  I will not buy this Kashi again

Good product at a high and increasing price and the size of the container keeps shrinking.  Will soon be single serving container at a very high price.  Need to start looking for other breakfast options.

This cereal is nutritionally fortified gravel. But that's not necessarily a bad thing. It takes a suspiciously long time to get soggy in milk and it isn't too sweet. Think of it, philosophically, as a less extreme Grape-Nuts.  With some freeze-dried strawberry slices on top it's actually even kind of good. If you are especially into eating healthy cereals or small rocks you would probably like it. I'm going to finish what I have but not go out of my way to purchase this again, because I can only consume so much gravel in a given year.
I love Kashi, but this product has been less fresh than what I buy at my local grocery. Maybe I have been eating it less frequently? In any event, I won't be reordering!

column9: Great cereal, maybe a bit TOO crunchy
column10: This serial is awesome. I pretty much exclusively eat cereal as a grad student with very little time, and this has to be among my favorite cereals. The crunch can be a bit too hard sometimes (I didn't think such a thing could happen), so I usually let it soak in the milk for little, making sure I get every cluster.I've had a hard inedible bit here and there, but very rarely. In the whole year+ I've been getting these in the mail from Amazon, I've had maybe two or three boxes that showed the anomalous hard bits.Also, its great with soy milk (are there things that arent?).As always, check the expiration date!! I haven't had a spoiled box yet, but you can never be too careful!
My husband is on a diet and enjoys this cereal mixed with Cheerios every morning.  Kashi is filled with protein goodness.
This week Just finished a box of this cereal. Taste great...more filling ...before you use this product you should be aware of its high test gas production.

We love this cereal and found that the value offered by Amazon's Subscribe and Save deal was great. Only problem is that quality may be hit or miss - one out of the three boxes we received was stale and tasted pretty bad.

This cereal is amazing.  Tasty, filling, nutritionally balanced, and cheaper than a lot of other premium "healthy" cereals.  I love eating this cereal in the morning for breakfast or after work as a snack.  Really, as far as taste and nutrition, this cereal cannot be beat.However,There is some ingredient in this cereal that causes HORRENDOUS gas in some people.  I am one of them.  Forget beans, peppers, whole grain...all the things that usually cause gas.  This is the worst gas imaginable.  In fact, I am still in awe of how much gas one bowl of this cereal causes.  It is not just the fiber.  I eat a high fiber diet anyway and have never had problems like this...there is some specific ingredient that causes this problem.I would recommend trying this cereal from a store before buying a bunch to see how you react to it.

Enjoy twice the crunch: Kashi go-lean crunch is an intestinal wrecking ball. Fun to eat, tastes great and then.... generates the most amount of farts imaginable from a breakfast food. Really, no exaggeration, this cereal should be a registered weapon.

Trying out Golean Crunch for the first time and really like it.But for being a healthy cereal -why does it have more sugar than Kellogs Frosted Flakes!  13g of sugar in Golean Crunch and 11g in Frosted flakes.

column9: Delicious! But not as healthy as expected
column10: I'm a type 1 diabetic and am supposed to avoid "bad" foods. Kashi sort of has a reputation for healthier fare, which initially attracted me to this cereal.What a taste! I enjoy the cereal very much; it's crunchy, sweet, and filling. It doesn't taste as processed as lots of common sweet cereals, and isn't bland at all like typical "healthy" cereals.For those without my specific health issues, I'd highly recommend this cereal as it's pretty darn good and relatively healthy. However, it has a pretty high glycemic index and really gives me sugar spikes, so unfortunately after this case I'm done with the product. Farewell Kashi, you sweet seductress of the cereal isle.

column9: Love it, but should be called Colon Go Clean
column10: Love, love, love this cereal. Great taste, good for you and high in fiber. But my god does it wreck havoc with my intestines.  Wow!

If you are looking for a cereal that is good for you; one that is sweetened with natural ingridents such as honey and cinnamon and has seven whole grains and sesame this is it.  Golean Crunch has twice the protein and fiber of the average cereal, it's crunchy and really quite tasty.It will not go limp in milk and if you are looking for a fiber cereal that works, this little number is certainly it.This cereal makes a great topping on yogurt giving you a double dose of health in every bite. Give it a try...enjoy!

First let me say that I eat a healthy, balanced variety of foods, and am not prone to hardly any bodily disorders.I eat lots of bread and cereal, so this seemed a good choice for supposed good benefits.I noticed after only one bowl, some stomach discomfort and bloating - something I never get save after the massive Thanksgiving dinner.  It lasted 1 full day, and made me wonder...  I ate another bowl 2 days later, and sure enough it happened again.  After checking online I found a vast amount of space already dedicated to the potent side effects of eating Kashi (noxious gas, bloating, diarrhea...)So, a word to the wise - see if any of these symptoms develop coincidentally with the eating of this cereal.  Otherwise it has good flavor - but is overly dry and reminds one of chewing styrophoam...  I guess I'll pass and keep eating my Triscuits and Raisin Bran :)

column9: Very tasty and filling, but save for solitary days.
column10: AS others have said, this cereal is pretty tasty. I like the flavor, although the cereal is pretty crunchy (hard).Despite the good flavor and other positives, BE WARNED!Do not eat this cereal for breakfast if later that day you are:-going on a hot date-having a business meeting-meeting the in-laws for the first time-giving a presentation in front of any number of people-going on a long road trip with other peopleThis cereal is better saved for days when you plan on being a solitary hermit....or are spending the day with someone that doesn't mind (or is highly amused by) explosive flatulence! Holy cow! I bought the 4-pack of these cereal from Amazon several months ago, and I could NOT for the life of me figure out why I've been having such tremendous farts! My long-term boyfriend was initially amused by the frequency and volume of my trumpeting (farts that literally lasted 30 seconds or more), but it's since just become something for him to grimace at. Notably, I ate this for breakfast the morning on the day he proposed to me....Let me just say that our hotel stay that day was less than romantic. Hilariously awful, but not romantic.So, this cereal has its purposes. Despite being a 26 year old woman, fart humor is still a blast (pun!) to me. I might buy it again (I just finished the last box), but I'll just be selective on when to eat it. A Google search for "Kashi gas" reveals that I'm not alone in this.

100% of the soy used in Kashi products is Genetically Modified, and when the USDA tested the grains used there were found to be pesticides that are known carcinogens and hormone disruptors. It's true, most Kashi and Kellogg's products are contaminated with GMOs. If you write Kellogg's to complain, they will try to tell you how great GMOs are. We know better! Tell Kellogg's you're boycotting Kashi until they stop using Monsanto's GMOs.
This is one of the best morning items you can have, Kashi GOlean Crunch cereal is great and the price point beats going to any store.

This is certainly not the worst tasting cereal in the world, not the greatest, but for a health food not bad at all.  The main problem with eating it is that it is a bit too crunchy, and it leaves a very stubborn residue if left in the cereal bowl for an hour.  HOWEVER, the main problem doesn't come when you eat the cereal; it comes about 3 hours after you eat the cereal.  You will be haunted by the most unrelenting gas that you are likely to have ever experienced.  I am positive that GoLEan crunch is responsible because for the last two days that and milk were the only two things I ate and both days I experienced the same tortuous flatulence (I have never had a problem with my milk [Horizon Organic whole]).  The gas isn't particularly smelly but it is frighteningly voluminous.  If you were to consume this product along with a serving of egg curry, you could vanquish your most powerful enemies.

For those with clumping problems: I have encountered this too.  It happens when the cereal soaks up too much moisture from the air!  Seal the bag carefully, and if the air where you live is especially moist, you might even consider transferring the cereal to another container that can be sealed airtight.I've been eating this stuff for YEARS and I still love it just as much as I did when I started.  While I think the Honey Almond Flax variant is somewhat tastier, this one does take significantly longer to develop any rancidity.  This may be due to the omission of the flaxseed which contains polyunsaturated linolenic oils which, though healthy, are highly prone to oxidation (I am extremely sensitive to this; my friends and family can't tell and think I'm crazy).  This may be a consideration for you if you are similarly sensitive and take a while to finish the six boxes in this multipack!I share an apartment with two other college-aged guys.  Kashi is really expensive in the grocery stores nearby, so we get monthly subscribe-and-save deliveries of the following:Kashi GOLEAN Cereal, 14.1-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)Kashi GOLEAN Crunch! Cereal, 15-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)Kashi GOLEAN Crunch! Cereal, Honey Almond Flax, 15-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 4)Kashi GOLEAN Crisp! Toasted Berry Crumble, 15-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 4)Kashi Heart To Heart Honey Toasted Oat Cereal, 12.4-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)We save quite a bit of money this way, and we always have a stock available.  I eat it for breakfast every morning and often for a snack as well - it really is tasty and filling, has lots of healthy protein and fiber, and doesn't leave you feeling sugar-shocked like kid's cereals overloaded with high fructose corn syrup and cane sugar.  I rotate between the five cereals listed above to keep things interesting.

This might be an excellent cereal, but the boxes that I bought had large pieces stuck together that were hard as a rock and dangerous to the fillings in your teeth.  They can be manually broken apart, but that is a lot of extra trouble.  Other than that, the flavor is good.  It does have a significant amount of fiber, and a reasonable amount of protein.  There is a potential problem with sodium deficiency if you eat too many foods low in sodium (that can cause muscle cramps, especially in your legs).
This stuff is the most delicious healthy cereal. It's not too sweet and maintains its "crunch" throughout the entire bowl.

column9: Yummy and super cruncholicious--but needs less "sugar"
column10: I find the crunch and texture of this is very satisfying when you want to get your teeth into a granola-like cereal. The flavor is a melange of grains and of sweetness. It's reminiscent of sugar smacks--but richer and more healthful. :)I do wish they'd dial down the sweetness. Kashi has some very nice granola medleys and cereal products, but on some cereals--like this one and the Cocoa Beach granola--its sooooooooooooooooo sweet. Too sweet. I'm assuming most of the consumers of Kashi cereals are grown-ups, not kids. Well, grown-ups just don't need cereal to have this much SUGAR...er...let's call it "evaporated cane juice". (same diff, really)I'll give it five stars the day they ease up on the sweet stuff.But I'll still buy it. I just dilute with a bit of unsweetened wheat puffs or more milk or Almond Breeze.

i tried golean crunch as part of kashi's free sample gimmick--i'll assume that the quality is the same as the store-bought!... anyway, i rate it highly on taste, as it reminds me a little bit of the honey smacks i used to eat, only not so overly sweet. and its health factor is pretty fantastic too (for me, some things taste better when you know they're good for you, although usually it's the opposite!) but the texture, well, they don't call it crunch for nothing--it was a little too crunchy for me. in some bites, the crystallized honey or whatever was like rock candy, and rock solid. still, it's good stuff, but i'll take one of kashi's crunch bars over this any day.
This cereal is good, but...  make sure you have dental insurance. I am guessing it is a crown breaker.
A great price for this delicious cereal, making my family's stomachs AND my wallet happy :)  I will definitely buy again in the future.

column9: Wonderful cereal if you can tolerate it
column10: The nutritional profile of this cereal is excellent.  It's high in fiber, high in protein, yet has low fat and only moderate sugar.  The clusters are very crunchy if eaten straight, or shortly after put in milk.  In fact, they may be too hard for some people with sensitive teeth or gums.  They do soften after a couple minutes in milk, which is the best time to eat them in my opinion.  The taste is moderately sweet with mild, grainy undertones.For a such a healthy cereal, this is really one you could eat every day and not get tired of for a while.  One thing to note is that due to the chicory root extract in this cereal, some folks will experience very bad indigestion with this cereal.  I would advise trying a box from the store before buying a pack of 6 online.  If it plays nice with your stomach, then it's fantastic.
Great taste and healthy, too. Subscription price brings monthly delivery directly to my door at lowest $/oz. cost, including big box stores. Good value!

column9: Tastes good and keeps you full
column10: I'm a big cereal person. I can spend about ten minutes in the cereal aisle, comparing nutritional information, trying to choose between different flavors and brands (yeah, I'm super indecisive :/). However, I often come back to Kashi GoLean. Good old dependable, trusty Kashi. It tastes good and it keeps me full for much longer than any other cereal (I usually feel hungry again about an hour after eating, but Kashi can hold me off for a couple hours at least).My only complaint about this cereal is its hard texture. I don't like having to bite and chew so hard to eat my breakfast, especially when it's early in the morning and I'm only half awake and incredibly grouchy. But the high fiber and protein make it a good breakfast otherwise.

I bought a few cases of this cereal when I found it on sale. It is normally quite a bit more expensive in the grocery store. It arrived in good condition and I probably worked through 12 boxes in 2 months, which is a lot of cereal. I lost a bit of weight from it. I'm not sure if it makes you lean because it is healthy or because it is so crunchy that it takes twice as long to eat so you probably end up eating less. I like the taste and feel good for hours after I eat it. I'm not sure if this is exactly the same as what is sold in the stores. I felt like there were maybe more defects like the super-hard balls of honey, etc in the boxes I bought. This could just be paranoia on my part. Overall I love how it tastes and was very satisfied. I highly recommend this cereal if you are trying to lose weight.

column9: Best Cereal to beat mid morning hunger!!
column10: I have been eating this cereal for a month now and I must say it is very feeling and satisfying! The crunchy texture is actually the best part! I think because it takes so long to actually eat, that is the reason why it is so satisfying as well: It digests slower!You can't beat the 9 grams of protein and 8 grams of fiber for under 200 calories per cup, astonishing!I would recommend this cereal to anyone who is watching their weight or would like to lose weight! Usually I add a half cup of fruit or half a banana to the cereal and one or two pieces of turkey bacon! With that I'm usually full for 4-5 hours!
Best price for this cereal I've seen in years! And with free shipping it's a no brainer.

column9: Great crunch, not too sweet or "stick-like"
