column10: Before I begin let me just explain where I am coming from. Though I am by no means a coffee expert I have become a little more sophisticated just in the regard that I own a french press as well as a chemex cofffee maker and grind my own beans as well. Though I like some of the standard coffees out there (especially Peets), I am trying to broaden my horizons and try new coffees. I decided to give this brand a try just because I saw it was a top coffee seller on amazon and had received mostly postive reviews.When I received the bag I opened it up and it smelled wonderful. as many coffee drinkers know,opening and smelling a new bag of coffee beans is almost as good as drinking the coffee itself. As for the coffee though, it was superb. I think the best way I can describe it is to say not too strong, but not too weak so it's perfect for someone looking for the best of both worlds. also, it is not as acidic as other coffees (which I understand is a common chracteristic of Sumatran coffee in general) so that was a positive for someone like me who loves coffee, but is always popping antacids.There are a few things to keep in mind though. This is a huge bag! It's like 3 standard supermarket bags in one. so if you drink a ton of coffee a day or have a big family of coffee drinkers, that might not be a problem. However, for someone like me who is single and drinks one or two cups a day, it prevents a bit of a challenge. The instructions tell you to put the bag in a ziplock bag and refrigerate for prolonged storage, which is what I did. Two weeks later the coffee still tastes good, but not as fresh as when I first bought it and there is still over half the bag left! If anyone out there has any suggestions on how I should store this coffee other than refrigeration, please shoot me an email.But other then that the coffee is great. Just make sure you realize you are going to get a lot of it unless there is a smaller bag for sale on amazon, which I do not think there is.

I have been buying another variety of Cafe Altura for a couple of years. My sister recommended the Sumatran dark roast, and it's the best! I will continue to subscribe and save to this product, as long as amazon has it available!

This is by far one of the best coffees I've tried!  As a complete coffee addict, I've searched a long time for a good coffee at a reasonable price.  This coffee exceeded my expectations!  After receiving a coffee grind & maker all-in-one for Christmas, I figured I'd start ordering a few different coffees through Amazon until I found the right one....this was the first one I chose & I have no intention of trying any others!  Luckily, my first choice happened to be fantastic.  Highly recommended dark bean!!  I would buy this coffee whether it was $18/ bag or $30/bag!!

column9: Great coffee at a great price
column10: This is one of the best coffees I've ever tried at home, and better than most that I can find out and about. When I first opened the bag and put a few ounces in my grinder, the kitchen was filled by by the savory, smoky fragrance of this exceptional coffee. The roast is dark, but not too dark. The coffee doesn't taste burned or bitter and it doesn't smell "skunky" when it's brewing the way Starbucks roasts do. It's smooth up front without any acidic sharpness, and the finish is, well it's fantastic. I can't describe all the flavors in the finish (nutty, smoky?), but after each sip things just keep getting better and better.Be forewarned, this is not a small bag of coffee. Typical bags are in the 8-10 ounce range. This one is 32 ounces. I filled the hopper of my grinder, and put the rest of the coffee in a big zipper bag stored in a dark cupboard. The coffee kept that way for a couple of weeks with no noticeable loss of flavor. You can do the arithmetic to see how inexpensive this coffee is compared to other whole bean coffees, but by my reckoning it's about 2/3 the price for a vastly superior product.This was my first taste of Cafe Altura coffee, and I'm thoroughly sold on it. I had to go digging through my email to find the right brand for a re-order, but it was worth it. I've tried two Cafe Altura coffees thus far, Sumatran Dark and Peruvian Dark, and both were delicious. I'm re-ordering the Sumatran Dark and another Cafe Altura coffee I've not tried (haven't decided which). I expect to try them all by the end of the year.

I'm not a writer enough to detail the tastes, flavors, bouquets, etc., but this coffee is GREAT!  I like it so much, I'll wait for it.  I'll wait to get home to brew a freshly ground pot in a french press, rather than stop for a to-go cup at a brand name coffee shop.  I drink more coffee now, this coffee, than I ever have.  Probably not a good thing, but not all bad either, and a testament to the coffee.  A fresh pot for guests always elicits "..what kind of coffee is this? It's delicious." comments.I've tried three of the Cafe Altura organic coffees, this is my favorite.  It prompted my to try the others.  The French Roast would be my second favorite, and then the Peruvian.It's a Subscribe & Save item for me.

I really wanted to like this coffee and based on the other reviewers' ratings I was eagerly awaiting my shipment.  Unfortunately, for me this coffee although obviously super high quality is just too bitter in the brew for my taste.  I ordered this on subscription for repeat delivery certain that I would like it as I am a Sumatran coffee drinker but after trying several different grinds and methods of brewing this I just do not like the bitterness in these beans.

column9: huge differences in between lots, used to be great, now horrible
column10: I ordered this coffee the first time about a year ago, and it was amongst the best beans that ever passed through my Jura espresso maker. At the time the packaging also looked like the one shown on this picture (black).However, I since reordered twice, and in both cases the coffee has a horrible, burned aftertaste, probably from getting burned in the roasting process. This coincided with a change in the packaging style (which is now green). As a matter of fact, I am having a cup of it as I write this, and I can't wait for the beans to be finished so I can put something else into my machine again.NOT recommended as it is now! If you ask me, go with the "Biodynamic" (whatever that means...) French Roast instead, I just had that and is was GREAT!

My nephew and his family recently returned from Hawaii and brought my Mom a pound of very expensive Kona beans for Christmas.  I had a cup of the Kona this morning instead of my Cafe Altura organic dark sumatra.  I'll have sumatra in my mega-mug come morning!!

We are complete coffee addicts, we've searched a long time for a good quality coffee at an affordable price to make at home. Thanks to all the Amazon Customer Reviews, we were so happy to have found it! This organic coffees' flavor and strength exceeded our expectations! It's so delicious! We were Dunkin Donut Coffee Junkies and wouldn't go to work until we had some. LOL  I am more experimental than my husband and tried every type, flavor, grind, whole bean, etc. This coffee is a real eye opener and has an amazing flavor.  Now we are proud fans of this organic coffee and will continue to buy it and I can't wait to taste all of their other selections!Thank You Cafe Altura for making a quality product at an affordable price! Try it People!  One smell of that open bag and you will be in coffee heaven! Enjoy!

I was looking for organically grown, whole bean coffee for my percolator.  I'm very happy with this purchase.  The coffee is dark and rich, and is very affordable.  I will definitely buy this brand again.

column9: Strong, complex taste without the smoky after taste
column10: This is my second try into Cafe Altura coffee and I must say I am again impressed.  I have tried the Peruvian, which is very good.  However, the Sumatran is just a bit better.  Is stronger than Peruvian and has a very complex taste that makes a cup of coffee something to appreciate for more than just Splenda and creamer.  This coffee is not for the faint of heart.  If you have acid indigestion issues, I would not recommend this.  This is definitely something that could cause some acid reflux.  For those without that problem, the strength makes this coffee that much better!
This has become our first choice for coffee. We have a Bed and Breakfast and the guest always comment on how good the coffee is. Great taste with a fantastic price.

There's not really a whole lot more to say, this is simply a great coffee.  Due to its balance of top quality beans at a reasonable price point, it has become the daily staple coffee in our house.  I haven't tried their other varieties, but if the dark, earthy and herbal notes of Sumatra suit your taste, than Cafe Altura's Sumatra is a great option.

I like my coffee really strong, and with this coffee I can go from unleaded to jet fuel mode depending on how I feel. A lot of coffee can get very bitter and can even give you an upset stomach if you grind the beans too fine. Not this stuff.With the average price of coffee going insanely higher, I think that given the quality and quantity, you get more than you pay for with this.  I have had every kind of Starbucks coffee, and none even come close to this ..oh... and this is ORGANIC TOO! Why buy overpriced, average coffee, when you can get something like this?
Love this coffee, its robust and full bodied but not bitter and the organic factor is a plus for me as the beans are not covered in chemicals and other potential harmful issues Savour and enjoy!!

This organic, fair trade, shade grown coffee is excellent, and it improves mornings a great deal.  Ordering it got a little confusing, and I can only hope that my next automatic order still stands, but that's a separate issue.  The coffee itself is really good.

column9: By far the best for the price
column10: I was looking for a dark roast, organic, fair trade Sumatran. I was pleasantly surprised to find something so specific. We had tried brands from Trader Joes, Sprouts, and a couple of online vendors but we found nothing this consistently good and for such an excellent price. We go through about 6 pounds a month, so it was important to us to find a good price. It is full-bodied and complex and is the first coffee I've ever been able to drink black due to its smooth, rich flavor. We buy it through the subscribe & save program, so it comes right on time just as we are finishing up the last of the previous purchase, and we receive a 15% discount on its already excellent price. Especially since we are living rural now, we don't have to make a frantic run to the store or buy something of less quality until we have time to make it to the city.

column9: This has become my morning grind!
column10: Dark, earthy, smooth, sometimes velvety....this coffee is hard to beat at any price...but on Amazon with free shipping...it is the real deal! Oh, and its "green" ...you know organic, small farms, shade-grown,,,,etc.

Great coffee.  SWMBO (She Who Must Be Obeyed) bought a variety of Altura whole bean coffees from Amazon and loved every one of the.  This coffee has a rich, full flavor but is "lighter" than their San Francisco beans which are my personal favorite.

column9: Not your typical cup of coffee
column10: Forget what you hear about the military running on it's stomach, it's coffee. Back then my only experience had been with the standard production line coffees until I was deployed in Europe. I got spoiled to say the least. Over the years I've developed a taste for the Indonesian coffees. The deep rich earthy undertones have always caught my taste and as a result become one of my favorites. If you like a deep rich full bodied cup of coffee then Cafe Altura Sumatran Dark Roast is an outstanding choice. Rich,smooth,full bodied all describe this coffee. If this is indicative off the other coffees in this line then I've found something special. Try this, you won't be disappointed.

Compared to Starbucks Sumatra. This is pretty close. However there is some bitter taste to it. So in summary  Cafe Altura  vs  Starbucks SumatraFlavor : SameRichness : Sameno Bitterness : Starbuck wins

column9: Surprisingly good coffee for the money
column10: I have been a Starbucks fan (of sumatra coffee)for the past several months, but it isn't cheap.  I opted to try this coffee as the price was right, and it was organic.  I was  pleasantly surprised at how good this coffee is.  I think I actually like it better than Starbucks (I know, heresy for true Starbuck fans) as it is a little more mellow in flavor but yet still full (a paradox?).  For those of you who look at color and quality of beans, these are a beautiful dark brown, large, clean, and shiny (but that doesn't mean diddly in taste).  Hey, want to try something new?  Try this, I don't think you will be disappointed. One minor thing is it does come in a rather large quantity (32 ounces)which means you have an opened package for a while (assuming you grind your beans as necessary) but you can put it in an air sealed container or bag (the company recommends that and then refrigerate, but I have read a bunch on that best way to keep coffee and theories abound--some say freeze it--to me the verdict is still out as to what way you go).  Just keep in mind, if you only use a little bit each day, the coffee will go stale after a while, I don't care what method you use to extend freshness, but that's only my opinion.  I am following their advice and keeping it around refrigerator temp in a sealed container.

If you want organic coffee, this is probably one of the cheapest you'll find.  However, in this case you get what you pay for.  The coffee was fresh and oily, and has an ok, but not great flavor.  BUT the beans had a strong urine smell that was off-putting.  The coffee did not smell like urine once brewed, but the smell of the unground beans was truly awful.

column9: Good Coffee just not great coffee
column10: I drink Sumatran almost daily and this coffee while good lacks richness, depth and body.  I like the organic, small batch roasting qualities and for the price it is a very good buy.

column9: A great big bag of good coffee...ahhh
column10: Got the new coffee maker and grinder and have been experimenting with different types of coffees.  I've tried some of the expensive types but I have to say this really is a great coffee.  The beans are fresh and the coffee is a nice dark roast without that "acid shudder" finish.  And you really get alot for the money.  Definitely a coffee I'd recommend and will purchase again.

I like my coffee strong, bold, dark, and am often disappointed by bland coffees.  We use this for espresso (lattes etc) and it's wonderful - we go through it quickly so even signed up for regular delivery.  Great stuff.

column9: Coffee Novice - New to Grind & Brew
column10: I just purchased a new Capresso Grind & Brew machine and this coffee was my first choice based on the reviews and reasonable price.I'm very impressed by the freshness and SMELL of these beans.  Heavenly!The end result is also very good...although for me lacks just a bit of complexity.  It is rich and smooth, but somewhat mellow in personality.Don't get me wrong...I'm going to enjoy every cup of these beans as my Capresso gently grinds the beans just before brewing.  I have the machine set to grind at largest/coarsest setting.  It is a conical burr grinder...so it is not burning the beans as it grinds.  I don't think I could improve the process used to experience this coffee.Would definitely re-order...but will also try other styles from Cafe Altura to inject some variety.

column9: Not as smooth as I had hoped it would be
column10: Now that First Colony has gone out of business,I needed to find another supplier for French Roast whole coffee beans and based on reviews on Amazon, decided to try this brand.  It is just OK and not as smooth a taste as I had hoped for so I'll continue to search.
I have been buying this coffee on the subscription plan for several years.  It is one of my favorite dark roasts and it is organic as well.

I love a bold, strong coffee.  Some dark coffees are too bitter to enjoy, but this one has a nice balance of bold and smooth.  My husband and I prefer drinking 1/2 decaf in our morning coffee, so we blend this bean with Jeremiah's Pick Coffee Mocha Java Decaf Whole Bean Coffee (also purchased here on Amazon).  Together, they make an excellent robust morning coffee.Five stars for this relatively inexpensive bean!
this is some of the best coffee I have ever drank. I like dark roast coffee, and this is very dark.
this coffee is smooth as silk, with a nice rich taste,great aroma, but not real bold or bitter,just a great cup of coffee!!!

column9: Beats out Dark Roast Illy for me in my Jura Capresso Superautomatic.
column10: I have been using a Jura Capresso Superautomatic for years (best superautomatic espresso machines IMHO)--After trying many different beans,  Illy Dark Roast was our favorite, then we discovered Cafe Altura Organic Coffee's Sumatran Dark Roast.  We are now going through four bags of Sumatran Dark Roast a month.  Smooth dark rich flavor without bitter tones, a great pressure brew with rich crema and flavor.

column9: Good cofee, I am enjoying it
column10: First time I tried Sumatran Dark Roast. I really like it. I love coffee at leasttwo cups a day, thanks for a good product.
this is a nice dark roast coffee  no bitter tastebrewed up easily  packaged well  will definately buy again

column9: Great coffee, a regular delivery at work
column10: I have had this coffee on monthly delivery at work for quite some time.  It is convenient to not have to leave to buy coffee, and the consensus at the shop (with several coffee snobs) is that this is great coffee, and it is a good price for organic, fair trade coffee. I have purchased Cafe Altura coffee off and on for several years and have always been happy with the quality of the product.
I have been really fond of my morning coffee since I purchased this product and will be stocking up on it. Fair trade and organic and great taste. What more could a person want?!

I have tried a lot of different coffee from Amazon.com, but nothing can really compare to this. The fragrant taste stays with you long after the last drip of coffee. I will continue to buy this as long as it is available here.
This is a good, basic coffee. I will continue to try other brands and would have no problem re-ordering this brand.
I find this product to have an excellent flavor and aroma. That it's organic is a fringe benefit.
It was great to find an organic, fair trade coffee at this price. But at least for me, and based on the bag I received, the flavor just wasn't there. I'll keep looking.
I love this coffee. I also love having it sent once a month to my front door for a reduced price. It's organic and fair trade.
The Cafe Altura Organic Sumatra Dark Roast Whole Coffee Beans in 32-ounce bag is a worth combination of price and quality.
This was an excellent coffee. I have had Starbucks Sumatran coffee, but I think the Cafe Altura is much smoother. Great choice.

column9: sumatra coffee at a great price
column10: A GREAT COFFEE AT A GREAT PRICE; JUST AS GOOD (IF NOT BETTER THAN) THE 3 LOCALES IN OUR AREA WHERE I CAN PURCHASE SUMATRA BEANS,

I just received the coffee yesterday.  Brewed a cup of coffee in my french press this morning and what beautiful cup of coffee.  The beans smell super fresh.  When I opened the bag the smell of freshly roasted beans filled my entire kitchen.  These have a great rich taste and not a burnt or over roasted taste.  I love the Starbucks Sumatran blend bean and this just blows them out the water.  I can't wait to try the other blends the Cafe Altura has to offer.  I am very pleased with the purchase.  If you enjoy the rich and complex dark roasted bean buy this and you will be in love.

I bought this based on other reviews. Wow, I'm disappointed. Maybe, (let's give them the benefit of the doubt), I got a bad batch. I knew something was up when I opened the bag and smelled how skunky it was. Thought, hmm, that doesn't smell much like coffee. Not fresh roasted anyhow. Brewing in my Bialetti was a big disappointment. Tasted like it smelled, old socks. Weird aftertastes. I drink my coffee black so it is of course less forgiving. Perhaps one can get by with crutches to mask the flavor but it shouldn't be necessary. I'm going to cut this with espresso beans to mask the flavor somewhat and try not to feel to bad about my wasted purchase. Will not buy any of their products again.

column4: Carole Feist "Carole in Big Sky Country"
column10: Love this coffee!  Doesn't take me long to go through a bag.  Seems to be priced very competitively.

I'm not disgusted by this coffee which is often the case.  It's not burnt and I'd say that goes a long way towards the rating I'd give anything in this Starbucks flooded market..but what I'm used to is the Backcountry Roasters that you can also find here on Amazon and I'll still attest that that coffee puts all others thus far to shame.  do yourself a favor and check them out first.

What's with the rave reviews? This stuff is tasteless. In addition, it is very weak. We had to add an extra 2 scoops to get the same strength as other coffees. As far as Sumatran coffees go, Starbucks blows this out of the water. Keep in mind that I hate everything about Starbucks, but until I find a better coffee I have to give in.

column9: It's okay but not that great
column10: I made a purchase because of the rave reviews of others. After few tried out I found it lacks the typical full body aroma of sumatra grown coffee beans  which I'm so used to it. May be because it is organic therefore not so full of flavor.

column9: This makes you appreciate your local roaster
column10: How shall I put this...  Yuck.  I guess I'm spoiled by my local roaster.  I thought I'd give this a try, at almost half the price of my local guy.  In this case, you get what you pay for.  Back to what I know, support the small and local. :~{

We drink only organic coffee because of the high amount of pestisides used on the beans. This coffee however is wretched!! It has an awful burnt taste! I couldnt even drink it! To give it 1 star is being to nice to it!

I brew espresso on great equipment at work. I normally use Peet's Espresso Forte, which is better, but much more expensive. My bag had shiny, dark beans with a pleasant aroma. The espresso isn't as strong as I'm used to, but isn't offensive. It will take me a while to use 2 pounds; I expect that I'll go back to buying 1/4 lb weekly instead.
After all the rave reviews, I was a bit disappointed in this coffee.  I'm cancelling after my second order.

Good coffee but nothing great.  Price is good though and I can't justify spending a lot of $$$ on other beans.  Better then any Folgers ground coffee.  I am still looking for a better, stronger coffee bean though.

One of the great things in life is the aroma of a newly opened bag of coffee.  This bag doesnt smell like coffee, it smells burnt.  Fortunately it doesnt taste burnt, but it doesnt taste that great either.

I got this as a Christmas gift and wow, what a disappointment!  If you enjoy a strong, full-bodied coffee, for heaven's sake, get yourself to Starbucks and buy one of their expressos instead of this. The script on the bag was full of hype, none of which added up to high-quality coffee. I'm donating most of the bag to my church, where they will eat anything.

column9: delicious low-cal comfort on winter days... or any day!
column10: This fantastic chai is the real deal. Even my Indian friends love it and asked me for the brand name! It has a rich, soothing taste that is perfect in times of stress or on cold winter days. I keep a box at work and several boxes at home, so I'm never without it.Try it with a high quality french vanilla creamer, such as Hershey's (made with real whole cream). Only 35 calories per serving.

As an avid milky tea drinker, I find a tea I like, drink it 3 -5 times a day for years then tire of it suddenly and change.I can only review flavor.For years, I varied between Earl Gray, Lady Jane Grey and Constant Comment.  Then I fell in love with Chai, but found some chais too strong.This chai was a good introduction for me.One benefit of chai is less sugar is required.  The vanilla helps to soften the cinammon flavor.

I was looking for a decaf chai tea and found this Decaf Vanilla Chai Tea which was even better. The addition of vanilla really enhances all the other spices and makes this tea sort of soothing. The ingredients include: decaffeinated black tea, natural flavors, chicory root, cardamom, ginger root, nutmeg, black pepper, star anise, cloves, panax ginseng leaves and vanilla extract. I like that I can drink this in the evening and not be awake all night. I think it is perfect with two tablespoons of dry milk and a packet of stevia. You could also use milk or cream to make a more authentic chai tea.~The Rebecca Review
This is my favorite chai - and I love that it's available in decaf.  I grew up in Good Earth's neighborhood in CA and it can be harder to find in places such as Ohio and Tennessee.

column9: This tea is delicious but is it gluten free
column10: This tea is delicious and I put honey and lactaid milk in it. I am intolerant to gluten so before I continue drinking this I have to know if this is gluten free. Most tea companies are now putting gluten content on their packages because there are so many people with this problem.I recommend that Good Earth do the same.

I've been drinking different types of Chai Tea for a long time and this Vanilla Chai Tea is very pleasing great tasting tea. This particular blend in Decalf is kind of hard to find in our local supermarket and I'm glad amazon has it for sale. I will continue to purchase this Vanilla Chai Decalf for as long as it is available. Many good comments from family and friends on this tea.

Okay, you know this tea has to be good to look at buying it online!  So, if you like the flavors of chai & vanilla, then this is a no-brainer... your only surprise will be the smooth robust taste... equally good by itself or with milk and honey.  If you're new to chai teas and are looking for a calm, delicious (I can't believe it's tea!) experience than again... this is the winner! Bonus story: over the holidays I wound up with a terrible head cold, this is the only food (if you can call it that?) that I LOOKED FORWARD to ingesting. Even with infirmed taste buds I could still taste these comforting flavors and knew I was at least able to "treat" myself to something enjoyable to keep hydrated. So, TRY IT... YOU'LL LOVE IT TOO! P.s It's decaf-good-for-you-too! Enjoy!
Every item in this jar is delicious! Its one of my favorite products on the market.

I received this Aloe plant just a few days of ordering it.  It was already a healthy and happy looking plant.  The product details say 4" tall; mine was 7-5/8" from base to tip.  4 of the stems 3" above the base were 3/4" & 7/8" wide.  I placed it in a planter I built especially for aloe plants with organic soil for the cactus family plants.  This plant is kept inside on a East facing window and gets a shot glass of water every Saturday at the base of the plant so the root system becomes deeper.  Now 4 1/2 months  later I now have 5 Aloe pups growing like crazy.  The smallest one has 3 stems 3-5/8" tall.  Obviously you can tell I am very pleased with this purchase & the high quality of this Aloe Vera Plant.  When it comes time to purchase plants I will be going to Angel's Garden of Eden.  I've seen there quality and care.Happy Growing.Oh Yeah!  The box it was shipped in was really cool.  You could tell it was designed for shipping plants.  UPS, FED-EX or UsPs couldn't hurt this puppy without driving over it several times.  Jim Cary - The Pet Detective couldn't destroy this package.

I bought this at my local Safeway and the Thyme is so good and fresh and just extraordinarily special, that I am here looking for a better price so I can buy more.  Most dried herbs from the grocery store and even our local health food, organic store where you can buy in bulk,  have an off flavor that only faintly resembles the fresh.  This, on the other hand, is just superb.  It has a lovely fragrance and gives an incredible fresh thyme flavor to soups and other foods.I am going to spend the money and start buying Morton and Bassett herbs and spices.  I already love their peppercorns and now the thyme is just exceptional.  I have to try more of them.Buy this.  You will not be sorry.

If chips are your downfall you have some help coming!  The Great Plains Multi-grain toasted chips from Wheat Thins are now our favorite chip, and there are other flavors to try, however the multi-grain are the ones we like best.  They come in a bag like regular potato chips... an 8.1 oz bag.  They are made with 100% whole grain, no high fructose syrup or high sodium content. They are toasted, not fried. Calories are 130 p/s and only 5 grams total fat.Best of all is the TASTE -- wonderful!  Just right in saltiness, crisp and satisfying.  It will be easier than you think to give up fattening and greasy potato chips for these. Highly recommended.  Put some in a baggie for your kids lunches and help train them to make healthy choices in snack foods.Love 'em!

These candy bars are hard to find in our area.  I use them in trifle bowl recipes for the holidays and the recipe calls for 8 of the bars.  It's easiest to order them this way, although I notice someone is sneaking in the kitchen and eating them!!
Product was fresh and arrived fast.  Packed w/ice tightly to prevent crushing during transportation. I was quite surprised at how when I received the package.  THANK YOU!!!
I recieved this Cheese in 2 days, it was cold and wrapped in double foil. It is wonderfull for pasta and lots of other great receipes.I am very satisfied with Amazon, And my CHEESE!!

Family have difficulty getting Greek products in their city. It arrived twice -- apparently it did not ship prior to the w/e when promised and they shipped another one on that Monday. Both arrived in great condition and family have been enjoying Greek spaghetti with browned butter. They are thrilled. Thanks!

column9: Tastes good, not quite a lb however
column10: I ordered from this company another mizithra cheese that was not good. This one tastes good but is not a pound...states on the wrapper .89 so just be aware.
I love this cheese.  However, it is far to expensive.  I found I can have my local store get Mizithra Cheese for me at about a quarter of the cost of ordering it here.

Ive tried seemingly all protein bars on the market and this one is my favorite purely in terms of taste.  Its like a super heavy reese's candy.  Another reason I love it is the high calories.  Alot may be from fat, but I have a ridiculous metabolism and lift weights, mountain bike and hike 6 or 7 days a week so the more the better.  For those exercising and dieting, I'd steer clear because of the fat and sugar content but for skinny people like me, chow down!

column9: Tasty dessert or workout recovery bar
column10: Honey Stinger's "Peanut Buttah Pro" bar is 2 things: full of protein, and tasty! (Those 2 don't always go together.) It's a bit sweet (high in sugar) for general consumption, but I love it for after a hard workout or as a dessert alternative after lunch or dinner. It's an easy way to squeeze in another 20g protein, and my muscles thank me.The slight drawbacks are the high sugar, and some unnecessary ingredients in the chocolate coating (probably added for texture). I prefer a very pure chocolate w/no modified oils in it! That said, the whole thing still tastes great, and the coating is a small percentage of the bar.

column9: Almost a Meal Replacement at 300 plus Calories
column10: Warning! Do not eat these without working out ;-)!They taste great, they have 20 grams of whey only protein.  The sugar count is high and I would not recommend using them as a meal replacement.They are great as a pre or post workout treat.  If pre, make sure to also drink 16 oz of water to help quickly process the food.The other versions of the bar taste too sweet, and have a few more calories.

This simply is delicious. If you've ever enjoyed a Reese's Peanut Butter Cup you'll love this, it tastes the same. I've got my own theory of why it tastes so good, and I suspect it's the Chocolate Liquor used to make the milk chocolate! This bar is also Gluten Free if that's a concern to you

I have sampled, tasted and stayed with many different types of protein bars until I found Honey Stinger Peanut Butta Pro Bars...Now, I will eat no other bar.  These are quite simply the BEST tasting...as another reviewer said, "like Reese's Peanut Butter Cups" only not as sweet, thankfully, and they satisfy my craving for chocolate.  I find that tasting real chocolate candy bars now are revolting. I will go a step further to say that I actually almost live on these bars...probably not the best idea, but at this time in my life, when real food from grocery stores, except for fruits, veggies, yogurt, soy milk, and a few other things, does not have a satisying or appealing taste for me, these bars are my sole source for protein.  I eat at least 2-3 a day, never get tired of the flavor, will drive out of my way to find them if I run out of my shipment before the next one arrives.  I feed these to my grandkids and they open their little mouths like birdies waiting for the next bite...great for a substitute for candy, plus it is nutritious, and as I said, my grandkids think they are the best, pure and simple.  As for the sugar content, I am not worried about it...mostly oganic honey and evaporated cane juice...better than sucrose in my book.  All I can say is, I believe in this product, will continue to use it every day and hope they NEVER change the formula...I don't think I could live without them.

column9: Holy Cow - these are really...too good
column10: The Peanut Butta Protein bar is incredibly good tasting... packs a whalloping 350 calories and a hefty amount of saturated fat...but, I will eat them for two reasons - because I'm hungry for a tasty snack and pumping up the protein (20g per bar).  I also eat PowerBar Protein bars which have fewer calories but don't taste nearly as good as this one.  The chocolate is of amazingly good quality, and..watch out - it will melt in your hands.  You must love Peanut Butter (which I do) and it has nice taste of honey (of course) in every bite.  Very filling....thankfully, or I'd probably eat another right after!

These don't taste like oreos at all. They have a single oreo cookie, on top of that is the creamy peautbutter and then they are covered in a fudge type covering. The peanut butter over-shadows the other flavors, I can't really taste the chocolate or the oreo. While these are good, it is not something I would buy often, they just aren't habit forming like some cookies are. They are almost too sweet. I think they would be better with w reeces type of peanut butter instead of the creamy. Don't buy a lot of these until you try them. We got tired of them before the package was empty.

column9: Okay but not too much like oreos
column10: The cookie in these is thinner than a regular Oreo and more crunchy. The amount of peanut butter and fudge substance is more than the amount of cookie, which makes the overall product a little too gooey for my taste.

column9: A delectable, if slightly imperfect, treat
column10: This is actually a review for the Peanut Butter Fudge Cremes, NOT the Golden Oreo Fudge Cremes.I love peanut butter and chocolate together, so was delighted to find out I actually got to taste test these instead of the Golden Oreo Fudge Cremes. I set out experimenting the best way to devour these sweet treats: room temperature, refrigerated, and frozen. At room temperature, they're good but left a weird aftertaste, and I was surprised by how creamy the peanut butter was inside. Eaten this way, they remind me of those Girl Scout cookies, Tagalongs. Next up was refrigeration, which made the cookies even better tasting, with less of that aftertaste I mentioned before. I like that the peanut butter is more solidified, which fits better with the crunch of the cookie inside. So the last experiment left was freezing, which has been my favorite way to eat these cookies. They are simply delectable this way! Of course, that doesn't mean I don't have some faults with the product. Mainly the peanut butter and chocolate could both have a stronger flavor; the peanut butter doesn't taste as peanutty as it could be and the fudge doesn't taste too chocolate-y to me. Then there's the fact they are a bit sweet, but I usually find most dessert-types too sweet, so that's just a preference. Those are really minor nitpicks and I would get these again, but prefer the regular peanut butter Oreos to the cremes.As far as calorie count, it's not bad for a sweet treat: 170 calories, 80 from fat, for three cookies (of which there are 28 in the package), but I do fine with only two cookies. The sugar and saturated fat are rather high, 17g and 4.5 grams respectively, but I doubt anyone eats Oreos for their health benefits, the first ingredient is sugar afterall. I'd say give them a try if you're interested, they make a good alternative to Tagalongs and are available year-round at a cheaper price.

column9: If you're a fan of fudge & peanut butter, this one's for you
column10: There are things that undoubtedly go great together... for example, chocolate & coffee, chips & salsa, cinnamon with pretty much anything :) Fudge and Peanut Butter are another such example. If you're a fan of other fudge (or chocolate) & peanut butter snacks, chances are that you'll enjoy these new Oreos.  It is exactly what you'd expect and tastes pretty much exactly the way you'd think it'd taste too.  I found these to be very delicious and will probably buy more of these soon at my supermarket.  As with anything though, I think these are definitely "good" but not "amazing".  One thing that I thought would've made it more delicious is if they had used semi-sweet (let's say about 60% Cacao :) chocolate instead of the low content chocolate fudge that was used.  This can be verified by checking the ingredients... chocolate is near the bottom of the list.  I'm a big fan of dark chocolate, and this fudge covered peanut butter Oreo just didn't have enough chocolate taste to motivate me to give it 5 Stars.  If you're more into 'milk chocolate' than the 'dark' variety, you may disagree with me.All in all, I think it's a delicious concept... and one that I hope they will keep.

I have to admit I didn't look carefully at the picture on the package of these cookies, and expected regular oreo cookies covered in peanut butter and chocolate.  Well, not so but that's ok, these cookies are delicious! I also was happy when I first noticed that 3 cookies had only 170 calories, only to find out that they are three very little cookies!  But they are so full of flavor that I was happy after nipping at these as slowly as possible.  They left a very nice taste in my mouth, and were fresh tasting, with a crisp cookie and soft coating.  I loved them!

column9: Pretty Good Cookie but Not Great
column10: This is a review for the Oreo Peanut Butter Fudge Creams. The cookies are pretty good, a little waxy in taste. They remind me of the peanut butter Girl Scout cookies.The peanut butter filling could be a little more nutty. It seems to be a lot of filler and not as much flavor. I like the crunchy cookie in the middle.I have a close-up in customer images to show you how it looks cut in half.

This might sound weird, but if these cookies were marketed without the Oreo name, they might taste better. Or, if they were called "Oreo Crisps," I wouldn't have been hoping for that classic Oreo taste.My first impression was that these are "weak-sauce Tagalongs" (Girl Scout cookies). They're thinner, and don't taste super peanut buttery. The package clearly says "Peanut Butter" with "Creme" in small letters next to it, so I've theorized that the "creme" part means it's the familiar Oreo creme that has *some* peanut butter flavor added.The cookie texture is nice. Very crisp and tasty. It's just when everything is put together that it's kind of disappointing. I have hope for the original flavor, Oreo Fudge Cremes, 8.5-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 4), but have yet to try them.That said, I do keep eating them. They kind of grow on you, but they're not as amazingly delicious as I like my snacks to be. I think I'll stick with regular sandwich Oreos.

column9: Girl Scouts everywhere should be nervous
column10: These cookies are phenomenal. I was a Girl Scout for five years in my younger days, and I used to tear apart Tagalongs. I got to the point where I stopped eating them because I was eating them so much and needed a break, but I still enjoyed them. This is the first time I've ever tasted a cookie that compared to those. The peanut butter is soft. The fudge is moist. The cookie is just the right texture for crunchy. I'd strongly recommend getting a handful and hiding the cookies from yourself. Otherwise, you'll end up with a plate of cookies, a glass of (soy) milk and a big smile on your face, feeling guilty about how you now need to exercise these things off.

column9: My favorite style of Oreo, I bet you can't just eat one!
column10: I have always liked Oreo cookies and I love chocolate and peanut butter. So I was excited to try this new style of Oreo that includes all three.These cookies are a bit more expensive than regular Oreo cookies and the package contains less as well. However I think these taste a lot better and are worth the extra cost.These aren't your typical Oreo cookies. They start with an Oreo cookie wafer, add some peanut butter filling and then dip it in chocolate. If you like chocolate and peanut butter then I think you will love these. I love the taste of normal Oreo cookies but I normally dip them in milk because they are rather dry. That is not the case with these cookies, they are moist and creamy. I have a weakness for chocolate and I find these addictive and difficult to stop eating them. I have also tried the Oreo Mint Fudge Cremes, 11.3 oz. (Pack of 3) and they are very good as well.

I was expecting another flavor and recd these by mistake.  I don't think I would have made an effort to buy these, but since I received them I gave them a try.  I doubt I would ever purchase them.  They are very similar to the Girl Scout Peanut Butter Patties except they have a lot less peanut butter.  The fudge topping and cookie wafer crust are so sweet & rich, that when combined with the peanut butter, the cookie has an extremely sweet, sugary taste to it.  One cookie was more than enough (no way I could ever eat more than two at one sitting).  I think Oreo should stick to what they do best - chocolate cookies with creamy centers.  These just taste like imitations of other brands, and not very good ones at that.

Oreo makes these Fudge Cremes in a few different flavors.  Mint (which I loved), Regular, Golden Oreo and these Peanut Butter Creme ones.The Peanut Butter Creme Oreo Fudge Cremes are really good.  Take a chocolate oreo flavored wafer cookie and put a thin layer of peanut butter on it and then dip it in a yummy chocolate fudge.  That's what these cookies are.  They are a bit on the thin side but you can eat the serving size of 3 of them for 170 calories.I'm not a huge Oreo fan but I absolutely loved the Mint Fudge Cremes.  I'm a big fan of peanut butter and chocolate so I thought I would love these more but to me they aren't as flavorful as the Mint ones.  I wish the peanut butter flavor would've been a bit stronger than it is.  That's my only complaint.Overall these cookies are really good and I'd recommend them.

I like Oreos, but I didn't care for this incarnation.  The Peanut Butter Fudge Creme Oreo has only one very thin cookie, not the sandwich we associate with traditional Oreos.  On top of that is peanut butter and the whole thing is dipped in chocolate.  Peanut butter and chocolate usually blend well for me, but this was just too sweet and I needed more of that cookie bite.  I shared it with a large playgroup yesterday and got some positive comments but no wows.  My husband says he'll eat them if they're there, but he wouldn't go out of his way to buy them.

column4: Wandrwoman "Wise as Aphrodite, Beautiful as A...
column9: More Candy Than Cookie and Oh So Sweet!
column10: If these Oreo fudge coated, peanut butter crème cookies were a building they would be the Fontainebleau Hotel in Miami Beach. Ostentatious and overblown, they leave nothing to the imagination. The first taste is gooey chocolate, then rich peanut butter, a little crispy something and then just full-on sugar explosion.What happened to the good old Oreo? Did it really need improving?The original Oreo would be Thomas Jefferson's Monticello, rational and balanced with clear tastes of crispy chocolate wafers sandwiching sugar crème filling. A classic, Oreos are always appropriate, satisfying and never let you down.I ate two Fudge Peanut Butter Crème cookies and was overcome by intense sweetness and the slight headachy feel of a sugar rush. Three of these little things are 170 calories! Yuk! I quickly locked the package of cookies in the closet, afraid of easily losing a battle with sugar addiction.These cookies are mean beasts! Beware!PS. My family liked them a lot.

column9: In Search of The Peanut Butter Oreo...
column10: I used to eat snack foods like this all the time, constantly trying new snacks that I would munch on whilst playing board games and watching sci-fi with my teen friends. Alas, I am almost 30 years old now, and I have...different sensibilities.Take half an Oreo, add peanut butter, dip in chocolate, and that's what this is. Does it taste good? Yes. If you like Oreos or just crave a novelty occasionally in your snack food this ought to do the trick. It tastes like a typical Nabisco chocolate-covered snack, but with a peanut butter taste that tastes a lot like a Butterfinger (alas, it does NOT taste like a Reese's).If you are even READING the nutritional information you are eating the wrong snack-food. This cookie contains RAPESEED oil (brain damage, loss of memory, headaches) CORN-SYRUP (diabetes, kidney problems), and enough artificial and highly processed things devised to be filler and poison your innards to probably get it banned in enlightened countries.If you eat this junk occasionally (as I do), and KNOW that eating it even in moderation is going to drastically shorten your lifespan, be my guest, it tastes great. I would mention however, that OBVIOUSLY you don't want to eat it on an empty stomach because...it isn't really food and will make you sick. Now and then won't kill you....immediately.The cookies get four stars for taste ect (not five because they still don't leave you feeling so hot afterwards unless you have like...one, due to all the garbage ingredients).The subtracted star is because in this day and age...Nabisco has no excuses not to TRY to eliminate at least THE MOST HARMFUL ingredients. Rapeseed. RAPESEED? REALLY? As a 12-year-old that stuff made me start to act like I had Alzheimer's. I wouldn't even THINK about feeding it to kids. And why can't they at least use real sugar and eliminate the toxic oils? Hey, it's their product and people still buy it, but when you can buy kettle-cooked Lay's and 7up has no artificial ingredients, there are no more excuses.As it is, I would buy these...just not often.

column9: Taste is fine, mouth feel is gross
column10: I only ate a couple of these, but I didn't like how it left my mouth with a greasy feeling after eating it.  The taste was fine, but not something I would go to a great deal of effort to obtain.  I liked that there was only 1 cookie--the 2 cookie "classic" Oreo design is a little hard to eat without making lots of crumbs, but this was pretty much mess free.  The cream filling was spiked with peanut butter and the whole thing is dipped in chocolate.  DISCLAIMER: I'm not a big store-bought-cookie fan, so take my review for what it's worth.

column4: Agatha Kristy "•The secret of getting a...
column10: My kids loved this cookie. It is a graham cracker covered in Oreo cream, peanut butter and chocolate. All aspects of this cookie are things that make most taste buds go yum! And it did for my kids, however I found the chocolate to be a bit waxy and not chocolaty enough for my taste buds.

I am a big peanut butter fan.  In fact, if I were ever deserted on a island I would want a couple of cases of peanut butter with me and I'd be content.  So when I saw these new peanut butter fudge cookies from Oreao my first thought was "The goodness of Oreos with peanut butter - score!"  However, my excitement was short-lived.  To put it nicely, any resemblance in taste between peanut butter and these cookies is purely coincidental.Don't get me wrong, they are decent cookies - I'd say they rank up there with generic grocery store brand cookies.  However, there isn't anything WOW about them - and there certainly isn't any of that peanut butter goodness.  In fact, there really wasn't any taste of Oreos either.  The fudge chocolate coating drowns out any taste of cookie that may be there.  The peanut butter filling is so thin, and so bland, it's really hard to tell it is even there.If you are looking for a peanut butter treat, steer clear of these guys.  If you want a cookie to give the kids or snack on then these are decent - but honestly, you could find much better and probably for a lower cost.

My original review for this product was deleted as it appeared under the wrong category due to having received the wrong product.  If I had seen the list of ingredients prior to ordering, I would not have (but understand that Amazon will be listing more nutritional information soon).To start, 2 cookies, less than one ounce contain 23% of the fat (max) recommended as the usrda, all of it saturated.  It contains hydrogenated fat (though stating 0 grams of trifat, it is higher on the list of ingredients than anything but sugars).  It also contains palm oil, once considered suitable only as lamp oil and now frequently used in cosmetics (but seldom in food).I found some irony in the warning regards peanuts and wheat (the only real food in here) though I do understand that it is for people with allergies.  I do not understand how the comanpy: kraft/ nabisco can even sell these with the hydrogenated fat ban in NY and California.  Do they have a separate line which they produce for those states, or do they just not sell them there?This is a product which I would actually go out of my way to avoid.  it is not as though there are not other good cookies out there (and these were not that good... unless you really like overwhelming amounts of artifical fat and sugar).  Really they should add a he4art failure warning to the label in addition to the peanut & wheat warning, and maybe deny health insurance to people who eat these.  They are bad enough that they could be considered a pre-existing condition.It looks like Amazon may have stopped carrying these, in my opinion a wise choice.

I am outraged that in these hard economic times, companies think they can succeed by offering products that contain hydrogenated vegetable oil, as this one does. I will not eat products that contain such things. Companies that do this are the ones that should go bankrupt!

column9: No one in my household wants them.
column10: Three people in my household, two of them chocolate junkies, all three of us unimpressed and no one over a period of days wanted more than a couple, and these are tiny cookies. Comments include: "Blah," "bland," "Too much chocolate, not enough peanut butter," "You know I like a good cookie, but I don't want any more of those." My husband who maintains he literally needs sweets every night, and has eaten some pretty dubious desserts out of the belief that if it's sweet then it's better than nothing, has stated he won't eat these. I just put them in a big baggie and told him to take them to work and let his co-workers finish them.I tasted them a couple days ago and felt I needed to try them again a little while before reviewing and there was no real pleasure to it. They were neither revolting nor delicious. I can't call them three stars because that would indicate okay, and since no one in my household wants to eat them and we all spent time trying to pin down why no one likes them, I think three would be too high. Three, to me, would be: "I'm not crazy about these, but I'll eat them, just not gobble them down," but the reaction is more a universal, "I won't eat those." Therefore, I have to call them 2 stars, maybe 2 1/4.

column9: The peanut butter version of thin mints
column10: The product retains the chocolate wafer of an Oreo cookie, but other than that hasn't much to do with the original.  It's better thought of as a peanut butter version of the classic thin mint and just as good.

column9: Oreo's answer to the Girl Scout Tagalong.
column10: Length:: 3:43 MinsThere's nothing quite like a glass of milk and an Oreo cookie.Enjoy!

column9: Think nutter butter with less cookie and covered in chocolate
column10: I have to say, when I first saw the package, I cringed a little. These didn't look too tasty, and I expected them to be overly sweet. I opened the package to find the chocolate a little melted, which made me even more hesitant.When I popped one in my mouth, I was very pleasantly surprised. There's a lot of peanut butter in this cookie - a perfect amount in my opinion. The chocolate coating isn't overwhelming, and there's just enough cookie to give it some texture. They're not as sweet as I expected, but still pretty sweet, and they're pretty filling. They taste nothing like Oreos, so don't expect an Oreo sandwich with peanut butter instead of creme. The best way to describe them is like a Nutter Butter with less cookie and covered in chocolate. If you like crunchy with creamy, chocolate, and peanut butter, you'll likely enjoy these.

column9: The chocolate and the peanut butter don't mesh.
column10: I decided to try these because I love, love, love the original, regular Oreo cremes. These are essentially the same cookie with peanut butter cream instead of the regular cream. However, I did not like the taste of these. The chocolate and peanut butter don't really mesh well together. I thought the peanut butter overpowered the chocolate. And, I didn't really like the taste of the peanut butter. It just didn't have a good taste.

column9: Good, but not as good as you might think from the description
column10: I like Oreos. OK, I love Oreos. I am one of those people who need to hide them from myself because it is way too easy to go through a whole bunch of them before I realize that I've just surpassed my weekly caloric intake. I also love peanut butter, and am definitely not impartial towards fudge. So when I read the ingredients of these little cookies I was really excited. When I got my package in the mail form Amazon, I couldn't wait to try them. Overall, I like the way they taste, but they didn't live up to my expectations.The cookies are much thinner than the regular Oreos. They are essentially "half of an Oreo" covered with fudge, although the crispy part may be even thinner than that. The peanut-butter crème filling is tasty, but it doesn't have as much of the peanut-butter flavor as I had expected. It is certainly not on par with Reese's Peanut Butter Cups. The fudge covering is very tasty as well, but again nothing spectacular.When it comes to nutritional content, these cookies are definitely inferior to the regular Oreos. They contain 9 g of fat, 4.5 g of saturated fat, and 17 g of sugar as opposed to 7 g, 2 g, and 14 g respectively in regular Oreos.These cookies are very tasty, but not as tasty as you would have suspected based on the list of ingredients. I certainly prefer the regular Oreos taste, and when it comes to similar fudge-covered cookies I think they are better alternatives out there.

column9: Suprisingly good but bet you can't eat just one!
column10: My wife and I were shopping in our favorite supermarket last week, and we found ourselves strolling down an aisle we usually avoid: the packaged-cookie aisle. (No way you can avoid all the fresh stuff in the bakery section, which is always conveniently placed in one of the first walk-through areas when you get in the store!) I pointed out all the space being taken up by all different varieties of Oreo cookies. We grew up knowing just one Oreo, the original, but we were aware that new varieties had come to market because our kids sometimes asked for them when they were growing up: double-stuff, especially.The next day I was here on Amazon and saw the opportunity to try this new variety, the Oreo Fudge Cremes, Peanut Butter creme style, and I just had to have it. It got here quickly, and I just couldn't wait to have a good old Oreo snack. I ripped open the pinched end of the outside wrap, pulled out the tray, and saw chocolate. Nice milk chocolate coating. I popped one of these new Oreos in my mouth and was very pleasantly surprised. I don't usually love peanut butter in anything except sandwiches--not even in Reece's Peanut Butter Cups or even Reece's Pieces--but this was a very delicate peanut flavor with a good amount of milk chocolate around it and, of course, one thin Oreo wafer to give it the crunch (and the justification to label it an Oreo brand!).Hmm. Mmm. I popped another. Then another. And another. I had to reach into the bag, because the cookies were in a plastic rack to keep them in place, or so they wouldn't melt into each other in transit, but the bag is a bit oversized for the tray and so many of the cookies flipped over and back further into the bag. (Wait, more on this later.)Anyway, four quick cookies, small and light, but tasty. Just over 200 calories--not so great for people watching their weight. But tasty.I worked through the bag over the next few days, always having to reach in over the rack to get to the cookies piled up in the back, but then yesterday I suddenly realized that there was a lift-back, "easy open pull tab" right across the top of the package that exposed the whole tray and that you could easily bring back down to seal the package with a lightly glued seal--very lightly, I might add. Think Post-It Note kind of stickiness. But very convenient and good thinking!!Duh!I peeled it back, and it works great to allow easy access to the cookies wherever they happen to have fallen inside the tray/wrapper.I recommend these for a convenient taste treat, but be aware that they pack a lot of calories and saturated fat.Serving size: 3 cookies (each a fairly small coated wafer)Per serving:170 calories9g total fat, of which:4.5 g saturated1 g polyunsaturated2.5 g monounsaturated100mg sodiumHave a couple, but then lock them up for at least 24 hours and then dip in again!

column9: A melted mass of mouth-watering munchies
column10: Let me start this by saying I live in Florida.So when I joyfully opened my OPBFCs I was greatly disappointed to find them melted and tossed about in their package like some kind of fudgey massacre had taken place in transit.In an effort to save my demolished delicacies I hurriedly rushed them to the refrigerator where they sat, for the most part untouched, for a number of hours. Hoping against hope that my tortured treats might recover some semblance of edibility I opened the package once again.Too my horror, what had previously been cookies had coalesced into a semi-anthropomorphic mass of cold-hardened fudge.But that didn't stop me from eating the entire package in 2 or 3 days. Good stuff. If you've ever tried peanut butter twix then you know what these taste like.

column9: OREO NOT JUST FOR SPLITTING AND FUSING WHITE CREMEY FILLING ANYMORE
column10: now in peanut butter.Ok. So I admit it. I submitted this package to an elite board of taste testing, not my own taste buds. I am far beyond the age of reason.The Board gave her approval, and how!Oreo. Not just melt in your mouth white filling anymore. Not even the monster super-thick filling variation anymore. Now, in peanut butter fudge.Can you really keep your hands off of these?Get a bag, and see!Passed the board.

column9: Peanut butter and chocolate oh my!
column10: What can be wrong with a peanut butter and chocolate cookie? Nothing. The Oreo cookies are much like their mint flavored cousins except your taste buds will be enjoying a yummy peanut butter filling. The cookies will remind you of a favorite candy made famous for the peanut butter chocolate flavor or perhaps a chocolatized version of a famous girl's organization cookie. Either way you will find these cookies absolutely delightful in taste, especially when washed down with a tall glass of cold milk.THIS REVIEW WAS WRITTEN AS PART OF THE VINE PROGRAM. I RECEIVED A FREE BOX OF COOKIES TO TASTE AND REVIEW.

Our fudge covered, peanut butter Oreo cookies arrived today so we were eager to crack open the package.My husband LOVED them, and said that they reminded him or Reese peanut butter cups. I, on the other hand, thought they were just okay; (2) were perfect (3) were too too sweet for me. I disagreed with my husband, and felt that there was no comparison to Reeses Peanut Butter cups, which we both love. Too sweet for my taste, and (3) cookies were 170 calories (and they are very thin; about the thickness of the Girl Scout Thin Mint cookie). Personally, I would not buy these in the future.My rating 3 stars; Husband's rating 5 stars, so we gave the product a 4 star rating.

This cookie is basically a single Oreo wafer topped with a thin layer of peanut butter creme and dipped in fudge. Not your typical Oreo, but a good idea!The entire thing is thinner than the original Oreo cookie and a little chocolatier. My little sister is an Oreo fanatic and I am the type of person who likes the Oreo flavor, but not the cookies by themselves. We both agreed that these cookies were a good addition to the Oreo family. I personally thought that the peanut flavor was a little bit strong, but I tend to prefer a weaker peanut flavor.I really like the design for these cookies and am looking forward to trying the Mint version!

column9: They taste like Diet Girl Scout Tagalongs but sweeter
column10: When I saw these Golden Fudge Creme Peanut Butter oreos, I was very glad to try them.Sadly, I can't say they were that good. Don't get me wrong, they weren't terrible but They basically tasted like n over-sweetened Girl Scout Tagalongs with a diet soda/aspartame after tasteAnd When I read the nutrition facts, I see why they taste so swet. 3 cookies have 170 calories. That's 56 and 1/3rds calorie per cookie.The Fudge part was fine. It's just the peanut butter. That's where the bitter aftertaste comes from because I tasted it in the original original Oreo peanut butter (Double stuff) many years ago. I could swear a few years ago those came out as 'new and improved'.just stick to nutter butters. If you want fudge, just dip them in a fudge ice cream topping sauce. at least you won't get the after taste.These would probably be much better with different peanut butter

There is no denying that these cookies are delicious, incredibly rich, and wonderfully creamy.  That said, they taste more like Girl Scout Cookies, specifically Tagalongs for the peanut butter flavor I received, more than Oreo cookies.  This is not a criticism, and I suspect that this peanut butter flavor will help satisfy yearround cravings for Girl Scout Cookie fans.On the downside, they are higher in both calories and fat than regular Oreos, and an entire bag could easily blow someone's diet.  There are 4.5 grams of saturated fat for just three cookies, but fortunately, due to the richness of the product, the recommended serving size of three cookies feels just about right.  Any more would be chocolate overload, at least for me.  Secondly, they are very messy.  Each cookie comes in its own slot in a plastic tray larger than regular Oreo bags, but if left at room temperature more than an hour or so, the fudge coating starts to melt a little.  Prepare for very sticky fingers, and you'd best have some napkins around!

column9: An interesting take on Oreo Cookies
column10: I've always been a fan of Oreo cookies and these new Fudge Cremes are intriguing updates on an old classic. However, having peanut butter mixed with Oreo cookie crusts and drenched in milk chocolate isn't quite what I had hoped when I tried these. The peanut butter flavor tends to be so overwhelming that I thought I was eating a Reese's Peanut Butter Cup, not an Oreo cookie. I wished that Oreo had created a cookie with more of a chocolate flavor than what I tasted. However, this is just my conceit and others may believe, with ample passion, that Oreo has stumbled upon a winning combination. Unfortunately, I am not one of these.

Both my 4 1/2 year daughter and I really enjoyed these cookies. I love the combination of chocolate and peanut butter. You are not dominated by one or the other. I think they are the perfect match.My daughter really enjoyed them, she keep asking for more.

column9: Not bad, but not what I expected
column10: I had thought these were going to be the Golden Oreo version, but I got the Peanut Butter Version. Oddly, although I love chocolate and I love peanut butter, I don't much care for the combo in one product. So, perhaps I wasn't the best judge. Anyway, I tried them myself and had a number of friends, at least one of whom is a chocolate professional try these.The overall verdict is= not bad at all. Several mentioned they were quite a bit like a product sold by a certain non-profit org around this time of year. So, if you really like those, and want them year around, this seems to be a excellent choice.If you do like the combo of chocolate & peanut butter, you should give these a try. Myself, I am going to try to find the Golden Oreo version. I used to love the Mint version of these.

I was in the mood for a peanut butter and chocolate treat, but not a peanut butter cup. Being hungry for sweets, I hurried in the store and down the cookie aisle and noticed "New" Oreo Peanut Butter Fudge Cremes; just what the doctored ordered!  When arriving home, I tore into the package and tried a couple and, to my surprise, they were quite good!  They kind of remind me of the Girl Scout Peanut Butter Tagalongs. When first biting into the cookie, there is a very sweet peanut butter taste and then the chocolate seems to over-power it is some.  More peanut butter taste would be nice, but they did the trick for my sweet tooth.  A friend of mine tried one and didn't really care for the cookie, but we all have different taste.  :)

What a treat! It's like eating candy, peanut butter and an Oreo cookie all rolled into one.They are the same Oreo cookie bottom but with creamy rich peanut butter in the middle and a great tasting chocolate covering. It's amost a "candy" instead of a cookie.I'm very impressed with the favor of the milk chocolate. I love my chocolate and feel I know good tasting chocolate. Some chocolate leaves an almost bitter after-taste - this is a sweet pleasant taste that has you reaching for the next cookie.If you are looking for a treat that will satisfy your craving for a piece of candy combined with a good peanut butter cookie - put the Peanut Butter Oreo Fudge Creme Cookie on your grocery list.A caveat: You must like peanut butter.

column9: All Sugared Up With Noplace To Go
column10: I tried the Peanut Butter variety of Oreo Fudge Cremes, and they are definitely delicious- and RICH! When I first opened the pack, I was a little disappointed by what looked like a very meager number of cookies in the 11.3-ounce package.  The recommended serving size is 3 cookies.  Now, with a regular Oreo, I laugh at the regular serving size and proceed to obliterate an entire package in one or two sittings sometimes.  So I was ready to yell "What a rip-off, Oreo!" and be done with it.Then I tried a cookie.  I expected the fudge on the outside to be a little waxy and not very flavorful.  That's not the case with the Oreo Fudge Creme.  That fudge flavor was almost overpowering as I popped the whole cookie in my mouth - they're small enough to do that!  Then came the crunch of the thin Oreo, and the distinctive Oreo creme texture but VERY potent peanut butter flavor of the filling.  Imagine a piece of peanut butter creme pie with an Oreo crust exploding in your mouth, and that's close to the experience of these cookies.Back to my initial impression that Oreo's ripping us all off, putting so few of these cookies in a package.  People, it's a public service that they don't put more in.  At first I'd scoffed at the serving size, and while I had to try two of these cookies in pretty rapid succession (a conditioned response to an open package that says "Oreo" on it), I admit as I ate the third, I was slowed down considerably, more to a civilized three-bite per cookie pace.  That's when the richness and sugariness of the first two started hitting me.  I poured a glass of milk and enjoyed the rest of the third cookie, and had a fourth out of obligation to the remainder of my milk, and have decided that's the way to enjoy the Fudge Cremes- at least the Peanut Butter flavor- with a glass of milk.  I'd still rather have a package of original Oreo Cookies, or Double-Stufs, but I do like that the Peanut Butter Oreo Fudge Cremes encourage drinking a glass of milk, and I do think that three of them is quite a generous serving if you're enjoying a glass of milk and taking the time to enjoy each bite, instead of wolfing down a handful.  They're a fun treat I think even Cookie Monster would approve of... in moderation.

Note:  I received my package of Oreo Peanut Butter Fudge Creme cookies for free as part of Amazon's Vine program.The cookie portion is thinner and more delicate than a regular Oreo, and it is only on the bottom (it's not a sandwich cookie).  On top of that, there is a surprisingly skimpy layer of peanut butter-flavored "crème" (much thinner than it appears in the picture on the package), then the whole thing is covered with "fudge."  I'm not a fan of Oreos, and I like these even less, though these are really nothing like an Oreo.  The filling is much creamier than Oreo filling, which sounds good, but it's not.  The texture is reminiscent of a mouthful of grease.  The "fudge," too, has a soft, greasy feel.  Don't get these for eating in the car . . . they melt quickly on your fingers.I'm a cookie (and candy) hound, so a product has to be pretty bad for me to not like it.  I didn't dislike these enough to not eat them (being a hound and all that), but I'd never buy them or accept an offer of one again (and that's saying a lot).  However, a lot of people seem to like these, so if my description didn't put you off, you might be one of them.

column9: Lots of calories and sweetness (not a proper Oreo)
column10: As you can expect when eating an Oreo Peanut Butter Fudge Crème, you get lots and lots of calories per bite, and you get a lot of sweetness. Great if you have a sweet tooth, but unless you have an iron will or a timer-controlled food dispenser, it is hard to eat just one cookie at a time. There is peanut butter in the taste, and chocolate too, which is what they promised.On the other hand, if you are an Oreo purist, this is not a "proper" Oreo cookie! It's like Oreo - the Next Generation :)

This is a review for the Peanut Butter Creme, Oreo Fudge Cremes, Fudge Covered Chocolate Cookies.New from Nabisco is this peanut better creme, fudge covered chocolate cookie. Otherwise know as Oreo Fudge Cremes, this is a tasty little cookie with what I would describe as a mild peanut butter creme. The peanut butter taste was not overwhelming and the combination of crunchy oreo bottom along with the soft creme and fudge resulted in nice sensation in the mouth.They go down real easy and before you know it, you've eaten more than you probably should have. Oh well, the perils of cookies.I like the easy-open package. It is easy to keep the cookies sealed when you're done munching.I'd buy these again but I'd shop around as you can find these cheaper elsewhere.

column9: Peanut Butter Lovers--This Cookie is for You!
column10: Don't expect an oreo covered in chocolate--This is a different cookie altogether. It consists of a thin chocolate wafer topped with a layer of creamy peanut butter. Then the whole cookie is covered in a layer of chocolate fudge.I enjoyed the cookie. Even though it was rich and delicious, the cookie itself seemed like a lighter snack than the typical heavy Oreo sandwich cookie. (Plus not as crumbly). It had the perfect combination of softness and crunch. The taste was similar to a peanut butter cup candy with an added crunch.Next time I'll try the Mint Fudge Creme. It sounds divine!These are great for an indoor snack; however, I'd be cautious taking them to an outdoor picnic. I haven't tried it, but they may just turn into a melted mess!When I opened the box, a few of the cookies had shifted and broken in transit, but it was just a few in the middle row. Not enough to bother me, but just be aware of this when ordering online.

The quote is from a friend, who while saying this, still ate several in quick succession.I started the bag going before taking the rest to work (I don't need a lot of cookies sitting around in the house). Upon getting them to work, I told everyone they had to give me an honest assessment if they ate one. The consensus was:"Excellent!"  "Mmmm, Girl Scout cookies."  "Can I have more?"The final word on them came the next morning, when one of my co-workers came in, made a beeline for where the cookies had been the night before, and expressed much regret upon finding they had been completely consumed.I will try the fudge-covered Oreos next. The peanut-butter Oreos were universally enjoyed, and are tasty and addictive. Four-star; I'm glad I brought them to work to spread the calories.

At first taste they remind me of the Girl Scout peanut butter cookies, Tagalongs I think they're called.  They have a sort of fakey peanut butter taste and the Oreo is so thin that you can't really taste it at all.  Maybe if it had two oreos with the PB in the middle it might have been better, but it just really didn't grab me.  If you want chocolate and PB there are better options and if you want Oreos, just go with the orignal (or double stuffed which are my fav!) because you won't get much Oreo taste here.

column9: Different but not as good as just-plain Oreoes
column10: These are a variation of the basic Oreo cookie, basically they are a single cookie with peanut butter creme and then covered in chocolate. While I love the easy open package that can be resealed to keep them fresh, these cookies are in a different type of tray than the basic Oreo that keeps each cookie separate. As such there are fewer cookies than you would expect in the package.As to the taste, I would say the chocolate and peanut butter overwhelm the Oreo cookie. I still like them, but when you are buying Oreos, you should be able to taste the Oreo cookie.Also, they don't ship to well. Mine were almost all out of their tray slots and several were broken.

These were surprisingly good. I don't usually like fudge or chocolate Oreo cookies. And I definitely don't care for peanut butter in my desserts. These didn't have a strong peanut butter flavor though. The Oreo cookie on the bottom was very thin and crispy. I really liked them. My only complaint is that the cookies are the same color as the tray they come in. I almost threw away a cookie because I couldn't see it the package. And as good as these are, that would have been a crime.No stars deduced for fat, calories, etc. They're cookies. It's expected.

column9: Tasty, but probably not something to order via Amazon
column10: I received a box with a package of these tasty Oreos - they are chocolate-like coated, with a peanut butter creme filling, and the usual Oreo cookie for the bottom. When I pulled the package of Oreos out of the box, it looked strange. Unfortunately through delivery, sitting in a hot UPS truck/ other, these things melt and change position in their little plastic slots. I immediately put the Oreos in the refrigerator, just on a hunch. It's not even hot yet here in South Texas, it was maybe 80 degrees yesterday. After these cookies had been in the fridge for a few hours, I pulled back the front of the package and saw what happened to my treats! All of them were melted and stuck to other cookies, etc., it was a mess. I shudder to think of what these cookies would look like if it were the usual temperature around here.As far as how these cookies taste, yes they are yummy. They are also very messy, even if they weren't all melted and re-solidified.  I am not a huge fan of Black Oreo crumbs all over my flooring.  I felt like I had eaten something similar to it before, but still can't quite put my finger on it. These things are way too easy to eat, kinda like Girl Scout Thin Mints. Before you know it, half the package will be gone. Definitely not good at this time of year if you are trying to figure out how to shed some of those extra winter pounds.I stopped by Walmart today and saw these very cookies on the shelf there for under $3. My advice has to be to get them at a brick & mortar store if you want your cookies to be in any kind of condition to eat.

First, if you don't like chocolate and peanut butter, just stop reading right here. Second, there are cookies, and then there are Cookies. There are three layers: the bottom is the chocolate cookie that defines Oreo, the middle is a creamy peanut butter, and the top is creamy chocolate, with the entire cookie being covered in chocolate. This cookie blurs the line between cookies and candy. Oreo has done a great job of balancing the chocolate and peanut butter tastes, somewhat reminiscent of Reese's Peanut Butter Cups.They are about 55 calories each. My husband and I have been trying to lose weight but not give up everything good tasting in the process. He is addicted to a late evening snack after dinner; after 20 years, I've given up on trying to break this habit. What I have done is replace the ice cream or pie with two of these cookies and half of a sliced granny apple. He's going for it. Also, I never thought I would ever say that I would offer an Oreo cookie to company; these cookies are that good.Cost wise, it works out to about $4.77 a package on Amazon, including the super saver shipping option. In my opinion, they are worth it but frankly, I'm going to look for them in the grocery store and update this review later.

column9: Another Girl Scouts rip-off? But delicious!
column10: Just like the Mint Fudge Creme Oreos are a doppelganger for the much-loved mint Girl Scout cookies, so too are these peanut-butter variants.  And, like those mint versions, they are excellent, if small.  Soft chocolate coats a small portion of peanut butter and a very crunchy cookie reminiscent of the original Oreo but obviously thinner and lighter.  If you are like me, you will eat too many too quickly.
