It is far too easy to overindulge with these.The only real disappointments here comes only in that these cookies are *small* for the current Amazon price - very thin and not very large in diameter for something that costs so relatively much - and the fudge is so soft that they had to be kept in the fridge at our house lest they melt right onto your fingers, making for a tremendous mess.  Upside: they are excellent cold.

These cookies are pretty good. A little too sweet and I'd have liked a bit more actual peanut butter taste. The cookie part was nicely crisp and crunchy and the chocolate was flavored well.My main concern is melting during shipment. I received these cookies in Central Florida via US Postal mail at the end of March. The package was brought to the door so it spent no time heating in the mailbox. Just the few days in transit caused every single cookie to melt to some degree and stick quite badly in the plastic dividers they rest in. It took several hours in the 'fridge to cool them down and even then a not insignificant portion of the chocolate coating was left behind on the packaging.I would hate to see what these would have looked like or the mess that they would have made in July or August. I like these cookies and will probably buy them again but I'll do so at the local grocery store. Think before you order. Chocolate melts!

If you're a fan of chocolate and peanut butter, you'll love these cookies! They have just the right blend of both, and go super with milk or coffee.I took some in my lunchbag to work, and they accidentally became a little melty. No problem - it's possible they taste even better this way.One thing, however, is that they may be a little rich for some people. This, of course, depends on your individual palate.

column9: A big hit with the kids
column10: We received the chocolate version with the Peanut butter creme.my older 2 kids really enjoyed these. The 3 year old not as much but he does not eat much peanut butter.I also thought these were a nice chocolatey snack. The peanut butter creme filling had a nice light flavor that complimented the chocolate well.The cookie crunch inside was also a mix. Overall definately a treat the kids will want to have again.

Disclaimer: I received these cookies as part of Amazon Vine, which means I received them for free. I review everything I receive through Amazon Vine as if I actually paid for them.These cookies just arrived at my doorstep, so let's start there. Once I opened the box, which was well packed as is typical for Amazon, I opened the package of cookies. As other reviewers have stated, I don't believe even 1/3 of the cookies were still in their individual slots. To give an idea of what this looks like, the package is the typical Oreo style "peel to open" package. Inside is a tray that has slots in it in which to hold the cookies. Have you ever heard the saying "some settling may occur during shipping?" Well, in this case it was a LOT of settling. Had I received a four pack perhaps they would have been in better condition? I don't know.As for the cookie, it is a thin Oreo chocolate cookie wafer, much thinner than a typical Oreo cookie wafer (one side of an Oreo I mean), covered in rich chocolate. Between the chocolate layer and the wafer is a small smudge of peanut butter.My first idea was dipping. I am one of those people that likes Oreos, but only if they are dipped in milk. Given the Oreo wafer is encased in chocolate, none of the milk would get to the wafer, so dipping it would have proven pointless. Instead I started chewing one of the cookies and drank a little milk. That didn't really do much either as it seems the cookie is immune to milk. The flavor of the cookie was pretty much the same, whether in a mouthful of milk or not.The flavor itself is over powered by the chocolate coating. The flavor of the wafer, let alone the peanut butter, was all but blotted out by the chocolate. You could taste hints of the wafer and the peanut butter, but over all the impression was one of chocolate with a little distraction included.I don't know. The cookies aren't bad, but at the end of the day, if given the option between one of the Oreo Fudge Creme cookies and say, a standard Oreo, so long as milk was an option, I'd take the Oreo in an instant.3 stars because quite simply there are many, many other cookies I would rather have than one of these. And I won't be spending my own money to purchase a package of these cookies, so that probably says something as well.

column9: Awesome cookie, but could have been much better
column10: Unfortunately a previous reviewer stole my thunder, but the Oreo Peanut Butter Fudge Creme is basically a knockoff on the Girl Scouts' "Tagalongs" since both have a hard cookie base and peanut butter center, all dipped in fudge.When you have perfection, a copy usually pales in comparison and Oreo's Peanut Butter Fudge Creme does pale in comparison to the Tagalong - namely they skimped on the peanut butter. Also I think they'd taste even better if they had had a double layer of cookie - rather than just the single. Both together leave the cookie rather thin - thinner than your standard Oreo cookie and obviously much thinner than the fat, double-stuffed, variety. Also the packaging does not include very many cookies. Open it up and there are 5 rows of seven cookies with packaging making up maybe 50% of the area - very unlike your typical Oreo package where you have wall to wall cookies. I know that prices are going up and manufacturers are cutting portions in order to keep prices down, but this seems like a colossal waste to have this huge package and only 35 cookies... I'd also like to say that they are cheaper than Tagalongs, but at $8.66 a package (at Amazon's market price of 3 for $25.99) these are pretty expensive as well.That said, knockoffs are not always bad, as my wife and I basically ate the entire bag in one sitting. However, as an honest reviewer, I had to weigh the positive with the negative and when you are left wondering about "What If's", then it can't be 5-stars. Still pretty darn good...

column9: Didn't think I was eating an Oreo
column10: These barely taste like Oreos.  The peanut butter didn't taste very good.  The Oreo part of the cookie is a thin wafer, probably about a little less than half the thickness of a regular Oreo wafer. It should really be the same thickness as an Oreo cookie so the peanut butter and chocolate is not overbearing.  The chocolate tastes good.The serving size of 3 cookies is about 25% of saturated fat. All that for 3 mediocre cookies is not worth it.  The cookies are individually held in the dispenser, and there's 28 cookies total. Rating: 3 out of 5.

column9: Yes But Is It Still An Oreo?
column10: Oreo Peanut Butter Fuge is a nice little snack cookie very reminiscent to Girl Scout Cookies. They take one side of a traditional Oreo, add peanut butter and then coat in chocolate.  The result is tasty and less filling than a standard oreo. But as I ate them I had to ask "Is This Still an Oreo".  In a world of brand extension, I understand why Oreo wants to have a wide variety of products and options. But to me an Oreo is iconic. It's two dark chocolate cookies with a creamy center.Had they stuck to this formula, changed out the cream center for peanut butter cream and dipped the whole thing in chocolate, I think you'd still have an Oreo. But by splitting the cookies and having no real "Center", you lose the essence of what an Oreo is.On its own merit, the cookie isn't all that bad.  The idea of chocolate and peanut butter isn't new and it's pretty proven. I thought the peanut butter could have been more peanuty and the chocolate coating better.  All in all it's OK but I'd rather go for a good old fashioned Oreo over this variation.

Whoever came up with the idea to take an Oreo wafer, put tasty peanut butter on top, and cover the whole thing with creamy fudge is a genius.These tasty cookies are a nice addition to the Oreo family!Writing this review has given me the craving for more of these cookies...  Guess I've got to order some.

I admit it. I just love snack foods. And amongst my favorite snacks to eat are cookies. I can't think of a year that I haven't ordered Girl Scout cookies and Oreos are amongst my favorite cookies (especially double stuff Oreos).So I was excited to have the opportunity to try the new "Peanut Butter Creme Oreo Fudge Cremes". While I think that they could shorten the name of these cookies a bit, the bottom line is that they are yummy.The only description on the bag is "fudge covered chocolate cookies" so they could probably expand on that a bit. But basically, it tastes like a single cookie wafer with peanut butter creme stuck to the side and then the whole thing covered in a soft fudge.The bag I received was 11.3 ounces, which is a generous size. It is also resealable, so not only is it very easy to get at the cookies without a knife, scissors or your teeth, but it's also easy to reseal the bag and keep the cookies fresh. Of course they probably won't be around long anyway, because you're going to gobble them up. At least, that's what I expect to do.I really like these cookies. If this was a Girl Scout cookie, I'm sure they'd sell very well. I definitely do recommend them. Just try not to eat the whole bag at once!

column9: Great Cookies But Not What I Expected From Oreo
column10: I have always loved Oreo cookies, splitting them in half and doubling up on the insides (way before Double Stuff Oreo cookies).  Dunking them in milk is also a favorite thing to do.  So when I heard there was a new Oreo product out I decided to give it a try.First of all the packaging is great it is a thin plastic / metallic wrapping that pulls open and than self sticks when you close which keeps the cookies closed.  All though the bag is dark and it is hard to see the cookies inside so I almost threw out the last two.  You don't get as many cookies as a normal Oreo package.  I believe my bag had 27 cookies with a serving being 3 cookies (really 5 is closer to what you will eat at a time).Taste wise they taste like the peanut butter cookies from the Girl Scouts perhaps a tad bit thinner.  The cookies are great but if you gave me a blind taste test and asked if I felt there was any Oreo in the cookie I would say no.  I tried to dunk one in milk and it was not tasty at all so be warned.  Once again a great cookie but it just did not have the Oreo taste to it in any way.

Customer review from the Amazon Vine(tm) Program (What's this?)I loved these Oreo Peanut Butter Fudge Crème, 11.3-Ounce (Pack of 3). They aren't your typical Oreo cookie, these are very similar to the Girl Scouts "Tagalog" I believe.This is a thin crispy chocolate cookie topped with peanut butter cream dipped in more chocolate. If you like the traditional Nabisco Oreo Cookies-America Favorite Cookie, 3 lb 4.5 oz. Box, you will be disappointed in this cookie. It's much thinner and crispier. But personally I'm not a fan of the Oreo sandwich filling, so I like this cookie much better.So if you think that peanut butter and chocolate is the perfect taste combination, definitely buy these cookies. You'll love them. If you are looking for the traditional Oreo cookie, this is probably not the cookie for you.I recommend this cookie to anyone who likes the combination of peanut butter and chocolate with a crispy cookie. It's very good.

column9: Where Have You Been All My Life?
column10: These were fantastic. My wife and kids loved them and we quickly polished off the package--within a few days. What is nice is that they are not too heavy. You can eat a few for enjoyment, but don't find yourself too stuffy or full. And it seems there is a perfect blend of fudge and peanut butter, where neither overwhelms the other. My wife and daughter are chocolate lovers, but they enjoyed the nice blend with peanut butter. I'm more of a PB guy, but I enjoyed the mix with chocolate. We love these and will continue to purchase them.

column9: Good, but a bit too "civilized" for me...
column10: I pulled a package of these out last night during a movie night when we had family over, and my kids and the nieces and nephews snarfed them right down. There were universal sounds of delight and praise. I was, luckily, able to get my mitts on a couple of these before they disappeared, so I can tell you about them.First of all, the cookies come in packaging that seems to me to be over the top. The plastic liner had individual slots for each cookie - that keeps individual cookies from partially melting and re-solidifying into a large Oreo-chocolate-peanut butter mass, I suppose, but it still seemed like over-packaging to me.The cookies themselves have one thin Oreo cookie layer that is covered with a layer of peanut butter filling one one side, and the cookie with peanut butter filling on top was dipped in chocolate. it was a tasty treat. There was a much higher filling and chocolate covering to cookie ratio than I've had in any other Oreo product. This is not however, an Oreo version of Hershey Reeses Peanut Butter Cup, 1.5 ounces Boxes (Pack of 36).This combo of less cookie and more other stuff made for a non-traditional Oreo cookie experience. When it comes to Oreos I'm used to having a cookie-rich and filling-poor experience. These cookies were the opposite. The cookie barely crunched in my mouth before the cookie texture and flavor was swallowed up in chocolate covering and peanut butter filling. That's not bad, just different.I do not recommend serving these to little children. The chocolate covering will melt and they will get chocolate on their hands and then it will end up on everything.I have to say that I will probably not be buying these again. I mean, they are good and all, but I prefer a more traditional Oreo experience. I still like twisting the cookies apart, eating the cookies, scraping a couple of cookie's worth of filling on one side of an Oreo and eating that. This cookie option seemed a bit too, um civilized for me :-)So, all in all, I liked these cookies, but the combination of over packaging and not quite enough cookie to other stuff in the treat lead me to award a 4 star rating. Good, but not great.

column9: Girl Scouts "Tagalong" by a different name.
column10: The title says it all.  The Peanut Butter variety of this cookie is pretty much the same cookie as the "Tagalong" offered by the Girl Scouts in a "lighter" variety.  The peanut butter flavor is not as strong as in the "Tagalong".  Chocolate is the predominate flavor with a mild peanut butter flavor (not nearly as strong a PB flavor as in a REESE'S Peanut Butter Cup *or* the "Tagalong"). The base cookie is a thin chocolate cookie which is nicely crisp.  It's roughly half as thin as a single Oreo wafer.  The whole cookie is about half the height of the "Tagalong".  I'm not a big fan of the "Tagalong" and as such do not much care for these either.  In all fairness my wife and daughter love them as they are huge "Tagalong" fans.  Their comments were pretty much: "Like a Tagalong with less peanut butter and more chocolate, but good".

column9: Do NOT think "Girl Scout Cookie" before you try.
column10: Overall, it's a good cookie. It's really hard to mess up chocolate and peanut butter.  Unfortunately, I thought it would be MORE like a Girl Scout cookie and it is nowhere near that. That does not make this a bad cookie, it's just different. It has a thin layer of peanut butter with a thin cookie which is dipped in chocolate.  Goes great with milk!

Oreo Fudge Cremes come in several different flavors: peanut butter, mint, vanilla, regular. I've only tried the peanut butter variety, but they're great. Since these are Oreos, I was expecting a sandwich cookie, but these are not sandwich cookies. Rather, there is one thin cookie layer topped by a thin layer of flavored cream (e.g., peanut butter), and the whole thing is covered with a thin layer of chocolate. The peanut butter variety reminds me very much of the Girl Scout cookie named Peanut Butter Patties or Tagalongs.

column9: Not Quite as Good As I Dreamed
column10: Previously, I had tried the mint Oreo Fudge Cookies and they gave the Girl Scout's brand a run for their money.(especially at $3.50 for two tiers.) But, I can't say the same about Oreo Thin cookie filled with peanut butter and coated with fudge. These would be so much tastier if the filling was peanut butter and there were two normal size Oreo cookies surrounding them. The thin cookie is a bit harsh, the peanut filler bland, and the fudge topping fine. It just wasn't something I would buy again as the flavors don't blend well.Maybe Oreo will take my idea and run with it. I am sure that would sell better than these.

These are not your regular Oreos in that there is no sandwiching of the cream. There is one cracker, topped with peanut butter, and the whole thing is covered with rich chocolate. Very delicious. It is possible to eat just one Oreo and be satisfied.Tastes almost like Reeses, but with a crispy base.Outer chocolate layer could become soft under warm conditions. They were soft and sticky when we first opened the box, but storing in the fridge for just 10 minutes solved the problem.Serving size: 3 cookiesServings per container: 9 (there are actually 28 cookies)Calories: 170Calories from fat: 80Total fat: 9gSodium: 100mgSugars: 17gOuter plastic bag is resealable - just like the regular Oreo bag.Tastes great, but I think it is too rich. Children enjoyed the cookies and I think they will consume most of them.

column9: OREO PEANUT BUTTER FUDGE CREME - Supremely creamy
column10: Put it in a wrapper and call it a new and improved, premium, and supremely-creamy chocolate-fudge peanut-butter cup "candy." It's that good. It's sinfully good. This ain't your childhood Oreo cookie. This "cookie" has a rich peanut-butter center that is covered with a smooth and creamy fudge. But just like those childhood delights, these treats are great with milk. Lots of milk. A bag of these bad boys doesn't last long in our household, and neither does the milk. Comment | Permalink

Both Oreos and Nutter Butters are available for purchase at my workplace. You get 6 Oreos or 4 Nutter Butters for $1. Every day I AGONIZE unable to decide. But that's all over now.These Peanut Creme Oreos solve my dilemma. They taste more like a Nutter Butter or Peanut Butter Cup than they do like an Oreo, but have enough chocolate to sate me.Each cookie is one Oreo wafer that actually seems thinner than a regular Oreo wafer, spread with a thin layer of peanut butter creme, then the whole thing is covered in chocolate. I do wish the wafer were a little thicker, or that there were a second wafer like a regular Oreo, but it's still good as it is.Of note is that the package depicted on this product is NOT the same as what I received. I didn't think I was getting the peanut butter kind, was dismayed when I did, but then thrilled once I tried them.I often receive Vine products and think, well, that's nice, but I'd never actually buy it for myself. But I might start buying these for myself. Obsessively.

I got the Peanut Butter version of these things. I like how they call it "Crème" - like it's some sort of fancy parisian pastry. C'mon guys, this is America! CREAM. "Crème" is not something I wanna see in my kitchen cabinet!-Let's get down to business. So, what are these things? Well, they are like 1/2 of an Oreo cookie dipped in chocolate. And by half, I mean literally, half. They are composed of three elements: 1) A thin cookie - this is about half the thickness of the standard oreo cookie layer. 2) A thin layer of "Crème". Can I call it cream? No? Well it's literally 1/2 the thickness of the filling inside a normal oreo. 3) Chocolate covering.-I love peanut butter and chocolate. It is like the perfect gluttonous combination. These come close to hitting the mark.These things are thin, overall, so you think "Boy I am not getting too fat eating these" but in reality you at half the box standing there with your milk - so really who are you kidding? But I do like that they are thin. If you posess the willpower, you can have one or two and not feel like you ate a brick.-Taste: I like them well enough. I do personally feel the peanut butter flavoring could be stronger. BUT, they still have that addictive quality we have all come to know and love with Oreo products.Texture: I gotta tell you, I found these things to be slightly greasy. I did not mind it so much, but still they felt a little weird. But this is such a minor point because they are still awesome with milk.-So overall, I did really like them. Addictive, a little greasy, but still a bona-fide Oreo product.

column9: Love peanut butter and chocolate - with a little Oreo crisp
column10: Our family loved these cookies.  A nice Oreo crisp layer with peanut butter cream and a chocolate coating.  The cookie has a great flavor.  Chocolate coating is smooth.  If you love the classic peanut butter & chocolate combo, give these cookies a try.

column9: Peanut butter cream worthy of Oreo
column10: You'll need a glass of milk with this rich cookie, ideal for those who love both chocolate and peanut butter. This is not a sandwich cookie: An Oreo chocolate cookie -- like one segment from a typical Oreo cookie with vanilla cream inside -- is topped with a dollop of peanut butter cream, then the whole shebang is covered in chocolate. The resulting cookie is thinner than a regular Oreo, but just as rich. The peanut butter cream is very smooth with lots of peanut flavor.

column9: Half cookie, Half Peanut Butter Creme, Half Fudge.....Huh?
column10: How can a product be greater than the sum of it's parts? When it's the newest member of the Oreo Family, the Peanut Butter Oreo Fudge Creme. Oreo has done it right for chocolate lovers for many years and this new cookie-like product is no exception.It tastes like it's half cookie, half peanut butter creme, half rich chocolate fudge and completely delicious. If this cookie can't satisfy the craving for chocolate nothing can. The taste is too good for kids, although I'm sure they will enjoy it, but give them the regular Oreos and save these for yourself. This cookie would be equally good when relaxing with a good cup of coffee or letting the kid in you come out and having a couple of them with a ice cold glass of milk. Stay away from them if you can, but after one bite you won't want to.

These remind me of the Girl Scout cookies, only better because they have a chocolate cookie. I don't buy a lot of cookies, but I'm a sucker for the chocolate/peanut butter combination and I found these totally addictive. I kept the bag in my desk at work. I also liked the re-sealable package.

I got the Oreo Peanut Butter Fudge Creme flavor through Vine and I was not impressed. The Peanut butter flavor seems very muted to me, while the fudge was overbearing. The fudge-y taste was waxy and cloying to me, for the peanut butter all I could do was faintly smell the aroma - I can't say there was much of a peanut taste at all. I had my friend (who's a big peanut butter dessert fiend) try them and he really liked them so I guess it's all up to personal preference.The ingredients list hydrongenated soy or rapeseed or cottonseed listed in the ingredients and according to the Mayo Health Clinic, if the ingredients does not say "fully or completely hydrogenated oil," it is possible that there are some transfats. The nutrition facts do not list transfats but nor does the package have the "zero transfats" advertised - so it's really up in the air.What I can say is that it was about 80 degrees outside at the height of the day and the cookies were partially melted and stuck together by the time I opened the package. So if you're in a hot area, that might be a point of concern. I think what it comes down to is that I highly suggest trying these out in the store before buying a pack of 4 - just saying it's "Oreos with a peanut butter filling" doesn't really describe it in my eyes.

column9: It isn't Reese's Peanut Butter Cups, but I don't think it was meant to be!
column10: (Note: This product was sent from Amazon for the Amazon Vine program.)Note: This review is for the Peanut Butter flavor of the new Oreo Fudge Cremes.  (The product image is of the Golden Oreo package.)The 'oreo' in this cookie comes from the fact that at the center there's a chocolate cookie wafer identical to the ones that frame an Oreo.  A peanut-butter creme center is placed on top of it, and then the whole thing is dunked in chocolate.  Sounds yummy, right?When you bite into the cookie, it has a satisfying crunch.  The peanut butter flavor is strong, but doesn't taste pure...it's definitely mixed with something creamier, maybe the 'normal' Oreo filling?  Each layer - fudge, peanut butter, cookie - is about the same thickness, so they blend together pretty well.  Unlike Girl Scout Tagalongs, the most similar cookie I can think of, there isn't a little 'mound' of peanut butter - the cookie is pretty flat.I'm not a huge peanut butter fan, but I like the flavor well enough.  I thought this was a good blend of chocolate and peanut butter,  although not the best attempt at the combination I've ever had.  I would buy these again, though, and I'm really intrigued now about the mint flavor.

column9: If I'm going to pay this much for a cookie I'm going to buy it from a little girl in uniform
column10: Well, it's a certain time of cookie season and little girls are sitting at a table in the entrance of my favorite grocery store. I love these cookies, especially a certain chocolate covered peanut butter cookie. I'm trying to save money. Trying to save calories. What do I do? I sneak in the opposite entrance like a coward.Enter Oreo Peanut Butter Fudge Creme cookie. Now, subtract a bit of peanut butter and this cookie and it tastes like a thinner version of the Girl Scout cookie I've loved since childhood. The downside is that the price is higher than those from my favorite annual cookie peddlers.My final verdict. Semi-Delicious cookie. Bad price. Next year I'll go with the Girl Scout version.

These are scrumptious and easy to snack, a hold me over to the Girl Scouts have their tag a longs again next year.  (This review is for the Peanut Butter Oreo Fudge Cream).  These were super yummy.  Peanut Butter, Fudge, Cookie a little milk and a slight sugar shock later I was totally at peace with the world and a-okay that my day had been brutal. These are a little chewy so not that crisp snap of a tag a long, but hits all the right flavor receptors.  Thank you oreo!

column4: Michelle L. Beck "Always the Devourer of Good...
column9: Interesting concept, but the peanut butter was a little overwhelming! 2.5
column10: It's nothing like a handful of chocolate covered oreos (they come out around the holidays) or a reeses peanut butter cup, or even a tagalong girl scout cookie, with a tall glass of milk or a cup of coffee. So, when the opportunity came to try the new the "Peanut Butter Fudge Crème" I jumped all over it. Now, I am thinking I jumped on it a little tooooooo quick. What I was expecting is a "combination oreo holiday cookie with a little peanut butter added for good measure. What I received on the other hand was something very different.First, if you are expecting something similar to those "chocolate (milk or white) covered oreos" that come out around the holidays, with a tab bit of peanut butter you will be GREATLY disappointed. [I envisioned a plain 2 cookie cookie with peanut butter in the middle, dipped in milk chocolate. Meaning a variation on the old, well loved theme of their holiday cookie.] However, this cookie contained a really  slim wafer like oreo cookie, with a layer (perhaps too thick) of smooth peanut butter, covered in dark or fudge chocolate. What makes the holiday cookie (in my mind) a success (it is perfection), is what made this one new oreo cookie fall short. Don't get me wrong, this was not marketed in any form or fashion as the holiday cookie, but that is what I was thinking when I read the description. The main difference is that the holiday oreo (and maybe I shouldn't compare it to that) is a whole oreo dipped in white or milk chocolate. Maybe a better comparison (instead of the holiday oreo) would be maybe the Girl Scout Tagalongs (whose cookie is definitely thicker than this wafer) but closer to the taste. And while I enjoy peanut butter in a Reese's peanut butter cup or a GS Tagalong, I thought this had a little too much peanut butter, almost to the point of being overpowering. You should know that the flavor that lingers the longest in your mouth is the peanut butter, while I think it should have been the chocolate flavor. Maybe it could have been because the cookie is wafer thin, but while a thicker cookie would have masked (or toned down) the flavor of the peanut butter, it probably wouldn't have completely muted it. I also think that a sweeter milk chocolate, versus whatever kind this was....which seemed more of a dark chocolate/fudge, would have made complemented the cookie better. Overall, I guess I was just a little disappointed because I was looking so forward to a tasty treat. This is definitely not that little something that I would reach for to complete my meal (although the last thing I need is a cookie). But my 9 and 12 year olds gobbled them up.

column9: For when the girl scouts (and your stash) are gone...
column10: When the girl scouts are gone and your thin mints are just a memory, you may be able to find a bit of solace here with these new oreos.  I tried the peanut butter ones.  You get a thin oreo bottom, creamy peanut butter center enrobed in chocolate.  They are basically the same size as a thin mint cookie but with a delicious filling.  I can't speak for all the flavors (yet), but the look of joy when I ate this cookie made my hubby grab the box to make me share.....We agree....this one is a keeper, especially if you love chocolate and peanutbutter flavors together.  Not that you would be looking, but the calorie count on these are 170 for 3 cookies.  I would definitely buy these and would consider trying other flavors, perhaps hubby's favorite flavor....mint.

column9: average - not as good as expected
column10: package is easy to open. that is probably the best thing about these cookies. they taste more like wafers than cookies. the cookie is too thin and the p-nut butter flavor is too weak for my taste. i expected more from oreo.

column9: OK, but not the best buy
column10: My son loves peanut butter cups, so I thought he would like these in his lunch. He ate a few and the rest are languishing. Only one Oreo piece (not double), so there's not much to these things. And the chocolate just tastes like wax.AND... the packaging is irresponsible. Each cookie is in an individual molded well in the cookie tray. So, not only is there way more plastic than needed, there's only 28 cookies in the package. That makes these things way overpriced. Not on my shopping list.

column4: Chris Swanson "I'm just this guy, you know?"
column10: Oh, dear lord... merely looking at these was almost enough to send me into a diabetic coma. They are so incredibly rich it's insane. I was able to eat about three before I was willing to say "Yep, I'm done!" These really aren't as good as regular Double Stuff Oreos and you don't get very many. I counted, and you get 28 cookies. That's all. For the price you're paying you can find better. Heck, you can do what I suggested with the mint creme Oreos and buy normal ones and dip them into bark chocolate.Overall these aren't bad, but I didn't like them as much as the mint ones. They were way too rich for my tates.

I love Oreos. I mean I really love them. They're my favorite commercially produced cookie and I could probably inhale a whole package in a day or two along with a gallon of milk and a good movie. So when I saw the Peanut Butter Fudge Creme Oreos, I thought "Can't be bad. Must try."Well they're just okay. The best thing about them is the oreo chocolate cookie. (This isn't the golden variety I'm talking about in spite of the photo and the name; this is where the Vine link brought me.) The fudge coating is way too sweet and the pb cream doesn't have a lot of flavor and even has a bit of a bitter after-taste. They come in a large tray with individual compartments which may be to prevent the cookies from sticking together or breaking, but which also is rather misleading since it looks as if there are twice as many cookies in the package as there really are. The package itself is resealable, and that's handy.Mostly I think these cookies can be summed up with a "meh." Don't mess with an iconic cookie.

column9: If you like tag-a-longs, you will like these
column10: I must confess that I love Girl Scout tag-a-long cookies.  The only thing I don't like is that they are not available all year.  These cookies, while not replacing them, will hold me in between.The bottom of the cookie is a chocolate oreo cookie.  This is covered in a thin layer of peanut butter.  They entire cookie is then covered in chocolate.If the cookie had a slightly thicker layer of peanut butter, I would have given it five stars.  But they are very yummy and I will have a hard time passing them by at the supermarket.  I have a feeling some may be coming home with me, especially on one of those "I need chocolate" stressful days.

I like peanut butter cups so i liked these as well. 7 of us in the family tried these and we all liked it. We were a little hesitant at first, not knowing how "oreo" would taste with peanut butter. But we all though it was great. 5 of us preferred regular oreos to these--with the traditional cream. The other 2 preferred the peanut butter. In reality, though, the two don't really compare as they are completely different tasting from each other.These are thinner than regular oreos with just 1 oreo wafer, peanut butter "filling" and covered in chocolate. A better comparison for these would be to peanut butter cups, but even that isn't a good comparison. It is like eating a peanut butter cup with an oreo wafer--which adds a slightly crunchy texture.If you like peanut butter cups, i highly suggest you try these. If you don't like peanut butter cups at all, the chances of you liking this are probably zero.Hope this is helpful.

But then, they're not meant to be, are they?  They're meant to be irresistibly yummy, and on this score, they succeed, brilliantly.This is a new variation on the Oreo cookie.  The cookie portion of the Oreo is flattened out to about half the thickness of a usual Oreo, topped with a thin layer of peanut butter and then dipped in yummy chocolate.  It's very sweet, almost teeth-achingly so, and filled with ingredients that will please your fat and sweet loving tastebuds.  Unfortunately, this kind of lip-smacking tastiness comes at a price: the ingredients list is a like a rogue's gallery of bad-for-you stuff, like hydrogenated fats.  These cookies are great for a once in a while treat, and because there are only 21 in a bag, they're more limited in quantity than regular Oreos.  If you are inclined, enjoy in moderation.  Or just go whole hog...you know you want to.

First of all I thought these were going to be Oreo sandwich cremes with peanut butter filling, covered in a fudge coating. Well, the inside is not a 'sandwich' creme - it's one Oreo disc with some kind of processed (to the point of no-peanut-flavor) cream inside, and the whole thing is then coated in fudge (which Oreo loosely uses to mean 'chocolate,' but I knew it wasn't really going to be real fudge). Because there's only one cookie inside each unit, the proportions are pretty gross - you get the medium firm texture of the outer chocolate layer, which is fine, but a single interior cookie is not enough crunch to set off the sort of lardy faux-peanut-butter layer. My son (age 10) ate a bunch and probably would have eaten more, but I'm more of a discerning customer when it comes to both chocolate and peanut butter, so I stopped after my 2 experimental ones. I do like plain Oreos, and the plain Oreos covered in the 'fudge' - but this combo just doesn't do it for me. It seems like it's just a typical processed sweet snack food with no real flavor.

At our house, we were split down the middle. My 13 year old son thinks these Peanut Butter Fudge Creme Oreos are great, and I was underwhelmed. They were very thin - about the size of a GS Thin Mint cookie. The peanut butter has an extra-sweet processed taste that I thought was too much, but as I said, my son really liked them. If you are looking for something extra-sweet, these are for you.

column9: Good, but not enough 'Cookie" in the cookie for me...,
column10: This review is for the Peanut Butter Fudge Cremes. I love sweets! Chocolates , cakes , pie, ice cream and COOKIES! I was looking forward to trying these. It's a nice package with delicious looking artwork depicting the chocolate covered, peanut butter stuffed specialty Oreo in all it's glory. YUM! I couldn't wait to get it open and chow down on a few! (OK, MORE than a few but who's counting?)Right away I was disappointed by the fact the cookie itself is maybe HALF as thick as a Ritz cracker, maybe even smaller. Not much crunch going on at all and nothing much to chew either. Also, the 'fudge' to me had very little chocolate taste. The 'peanut butter' stuff on the inside was OK, much like the inside of a peanut butter flavored M and M.Overall, I just didn't like this cookie much. It's a fine product but just not my cup of tea. (or cookie)NOW THE REBUTTAL: My father happened to be sitting there watching me "TEST" (yeah testing!) the cookie out and wanted to sample same. HIS opinion was much different than mine and said he LOVED this cookie and it was just right and then he grabbed my bag and made off with them. So as you can see, a good cookie is in the mouth of the beholder, or the muncher as the case may be.

These Oreos begin with a single, chocolate-flavored Oreo cookie. That is topped with a peanut butter creme and the whole treat is then enrobed in chocolate 'fudge' coating. My one-word analysis would be "addictive". Oh, these cookies are good. Oreo uses real peanut butter in the creme. This is sweeter than your typical out-of-the-jar peanut butter, but it is still very tasty. These are the same chocolate-flavored cookies Oreo has been using for years in their sandwich cremes that everyone knows and loves.Oreo has come out with another winner. Just watch the price. Some outlets are charging a fortune for these cookies.

The product ain't bad, not bad at all; crispy cookie, peanut butter layer (that same highly-processed and not-really-peanut-buttery stuff one finds in Reese's and peanut-butter-esque cookies), covered in fudge. With a hint of mint, mostly in aftertaste, which you wouldn't for a second think would go with peanut butter, but it actually works. What I question is the brand association. And I admit, this is probably a personal thing and you can switch me off right now, but come on. If it's an Oreo, it's got two cookies with stuff sandwiched in the middle, not one cookie with stuff piled on top. Yes, I admit that's a petty reason to dock it a star, but come on, is it an Oreo if you can't do the Oreo Twist(TM)?I think these guys are good enough to break from the brand association and go it on their own. Would be a good idea, IMO.

Although this is not the Golden Oreo, this addition to the Oreo family is certainly tasty if not healthy. What we have here is what appears to be an original Oreo cookie topped with a layer of peanut butter covered with chocolate. While this little delight is not as peanut-buttery as say a Reese's Peanut Butter Cup, it has a great texture and flavor. It is perfectly fine to like this latest sweetie and still remain loyal to the original Oreo that we have all come to love with a glass of cold milk, in a pie crust or nestled inside a cheesecake. It is not wonder that the original is considered-- I believe-- the world's favorite cookie.If you are avoiding fat and sugar, however, beware as this cookie is high in both.

First off these are really nothing like regular Oreos except for the thin cookie. The cookie is thinner and crunchier than regular Oreos and, along with the cookie, the peanut butter cream and chocolate covering mix to make a delicious combination. The only problem is that the thin chocolate covering seems to melt very easily even at mild temperatures and all over your fingers while eating them so I have been keeping them in the freezer (along with my Girl Scout Thin Mints), like this they are just as tasty and not as messy.

column9: Not a fan. Can't distinguish one flavor from the other, and the creme, and fudge coating, just taste cheap.
column10: All it took for me was one cookie to decide that these just weren't going to do it for me. I love Girl Scout Cookie Thin Mints, and Grasshopper cookies, as well as Keebler Fudge Grahams, so I don't take issue with the fudgy coatings on those cookies. I love peanut butter. Like, LOVE, LOVE, LOVE peanut butter. When I make homemade peanut butter cookies, I DOUBLE the peanut butter the recipe calls for. I LOVE Oreo cookies (even though I'm one of those weirdos that removes the creme half of the time, 'cuz the chocolate wafers are just so daggone good on their own, too)!But I don't love these.The peanut butter creme doesn't have anywhere near enough peanut flavor, and it just tastes cheap. Or, the fudge coating tastes cheap, and it masks the peanut butter flavor. Or, both of them taste cheap, and they totally mask the chocolate Oreo wafer flavor. Honestly, I really can't tell; what I DO know is that I just didn't like these cookies in the Oreo line of creations.Really, growing up, I didn't eat a vast amount of Oreos. Heck, I didn't even KNOW about the whole dunk-'em-in-milk thing until college, and when I DID find out about that, I swear, the Heavens opened up and angels began to sing. I don't even keep Oreos in the house, 'cuz it's WAY too easy for me to go through a whole bag of 'em in two sittings. But these? I think I'll be giving them away to someone else whose taste buds are less selective than mine. Like maybe my First Grade students...Not a win with this product, Nabisco...

column9: Ok - sweet, but lacking in a distinctive flavor, March 24, 2011
column10: Customer review from the Amazon Vine(tm) ProgramNote: This review is for the Peanut Butter Oreo Fudge Creme's. Amazon's Vine program seems to have mixed up the this product with the Golden Oreo Fudge Cremes.If you're interested, I've uploaded some pictures of these cookies side by side with the Girl Scout Do-Si-Do's.These are good, but the main reason I gave them 3 stars is that they simply have no "signature" flavor. There's not a whole lot of peanut butter in them, so they really don't give you that peanut butter fix. Likewise, to me, they're not even as rich as a regular Oreo, and therefore really don't give much from the chocolate side, either.When you eat a regular Oreo, you know it. The cookie part is rich and has a distinct chocolate flavor different from other chocolate cookies. Unfortunately, with these Fudge Creme's the wafer is slightly different, and the fudge covering more or less masks the chocolate flavor with sweetness. It's kind of like eating a hot pepper where all you taste is hot, not the pepper. Imagine that, but subsitute sweet for hot and chocolate for pepper and you'll know what I mean.I tried them side by side with the Girl Scout's Do-Si-Do's (or Peanut Butter Patties). The girl scout cookies definitely have more peanut butter in them and it has a better flavor. The Oreo is more chocolaty, but the fudge is more waxy and doesn't melt as readily in your mouth.I'll take a regular Oreo, a nutter butter, or a Do-Si-Do over these anyday, but if none of those are available, these would do.On a separate note, my kids loved them. I didn't find them too sweet, just lacking in the ability to represent a signature flavor that sets them apart.

Like the Oreo Fudge Mint Cremes 8.5 Oz. (Pack of 3), these have a THIN and wonderful layer of peanut butter (rather than mint), with a chocolate cookie, covered with luscious fudge coating.Unlike the "girl scout" peanut butter cookies, these have JUST the right amount of peanut butter for my taste.  But, I have to confess - I am on a DIET. Only 1200 calories a day. That's just about one package of these wonderful cookies (57 calories per cookie), and when I say wonderful, I really mean it. I finally passed them out to a group of kids I was teaching, just to get them out of my kitchen and out of temptation's way.Since Amazon is having problems with the Vine badge on these, I do want you to know that I received this package to try through the Vine program.Wonderful, WAY too wonderful ...

I love Oreos. I love peanut butter. I love chocolate. Seems like a no-brainer that I should like these cookies, but I didn't. They were ok at best. I thought maybe it was just me, so I had my kids give them a try. One of my sons didn't like them at all. The other son (who has more of a sweet-tooth) liked them a little. He liked them enough that he's going to eat more, but told me not to bring home any more. He'd rather have the original Oreos. If he was in the mood for PB & chocolate, he'd just rather have a Reese's.The other thing I'd like to point out is that I wouldn't really even consider these "cookies". They contain more PB & chocolate than cookie. The cookie wafer is really thin and is just overpowered by the other 2 ingredients. And the peanut butter part had too soft a consistency and not enough of a peanut flavor..

column9: Oreo Versus the Girl Scouts of America
column10: If you are like me, chances are that you've eaten a lot of Girl Scout cookies over the years, and if you are like most GSA cookie buyers, your favorites are the famous Girl Scout Thin Mint Cookies.  If this is true, chances are you have found the occasional thin mint cookie that equaled them but not a thin mint cookie that bettered them,...until now.These Oreo Peanut Butter Fudge Crèmes, also available in Oreo Regular Fudge Crèmes, Oreo Mint Fudge Crèmes, and Oreo Golden Oreo Fudge Crèmes, are IMHO BETTER tasting than the Girl Scout Thin Mint Cookies so while I might in future be persuaded to purchase fund raising thin mint cookies, they will be for other people.I'll be eating these!Note: As other reviewers have noted, this is not an entirely new concept for Oreo, which has offered limited editions of chocolate dipped whole sandwich cookies: Oreo Mint Fudge Covered Chocolate Sandwich Cookies, Oreo Pure Milk Chocolate Covered Mint Sandwich Cookies, and Oreo White Fudge Covered Chocolate Sandwich Cookies.  The trouble is that these are by definition limited editions that may not be available when you want to purchase them while the new fudge covered half cookies look to be a regular stock item available year round.

column9: more of candy treat vs a cookie- MESSY !
column10: love peanut and chocolate and was pleased to try these cookies... Well they are very similar to Thin Mint Girl Scout cookies with peanut butter filling vs mint.That said I would consider these more of candy treat vs a cookie.. Very thin wafer cookie topped with sm amt of lightly flavored peanut butter and the whole thing encased in very chocolaty coating.Just 1-2 is more than enough and I wouldn't serve these as a after dinner cookie but perhaps a mid meal light treat with large glass of milk but only occasionally. Not as peanutty as I expected but very clearly peanut flavored.I wasn't thrilled with the packaging. it has a new type of pull tab opening that flips open the whole top of the cookie package exposing all of the cookies at once.. when opened more than 1/3 of the cookies had flipped out of their slots in the cookie holder and some were smashed against each other and had to be pulled apart. Can't imagine this would survive in the heat of summer if it can't make it through this mild spring weather.. Looks like they might be a melty mess in warm weather..I enjoyed these but not sure would be a repeat order for us. Due to the candy-like nature of the treat. and we live in a warm climate and this just looks like a mess in the making for our climate..

column9: Not much Oreo flavor, slight artificial aftertaste
column10: I love love LOVE regular Oreos, the Oreo Mint Fudge Covered Limited Edition Chocolate Sandwich Cookies are to die for, and I love peanut butter...so I wanted to love these...but I didn't.If I didn't know it was an Oreo cookie piece, I'd never be able to tell it's an Oreo. The thin peanut butter layer is smooth and creamy, but leaves a faintly artificial aftertaste. They reminded me slightly of the old school Girl Scout cookies called Hoedowns (now called Tagalongs) but not nearly as thick or as rich tasting. Maybe if it had a thicker cookie layer it would taste more like an Oreo.So overall, three stars for a "meh" rating. I'm not going to toss the package I have, but I wouldn't likely buy them again.

There is a certain aesthetic appeal to eating an Oreo cookie.  The twisting apart.  The dunking first one half or the other in a glass of milk.  Unless, of course, you prefer to keep the cookie whole and dunk it in like that.  They have made an entire industry on the concept with so many commercials reminding us about the rituals of eating Oreo cookies.So why would they create this cookie?  Okay.  It has an Oreo bit to it, only one cookie.  No twisting apart.  The filling is there, except this time it's peanut butter and not that snowy white filling one typically associates with a classic Oreo cookie.  Then this mutation-one-sided cookie with flavored filling-is covered in chocolate.  This doesn't exactly inspire one to dip it in a glass of milk because the cookie would go untouched, covered as it is in chocolate.  If the cookie can't soak up the milk, there's really no point in dunking.Three different people tried this new variation on a theme and all three of us shrugged.  It's a good cookie but we've all had better.  And one of us is an Oreo cookie fan.  He said he wouldn't buy these.  He'd rather not have his Oreo covered in chocolate and he definitely wanted both cookies with the cream filling sandwiched in between.None of us, truth be told, would buy these cookies.This was a disappointment.  An overly sweet one.  And for those Oreo cookie eaters who take delight in the ritual of eating an Oreo, this cookie simply will not suffice.
These cookies have a similar Reese hard shell candy flavor, with a crunch from the cookie.I think I prefer original Oreo myself.

Blindfold someone, and they may not be able to tell the difference between this cookie and a girl scout tagalong. I guess if you are deathly seriously about your cookies, you'll notice some small difference. Not me. I don't know what this has to do with Oreos. No cream stuffing. Big deal, if you like chocolate and peanut butter you'll like this.

column9: Tastes good to me but probably not great for health
column10: It does taste fine to me. It has a good peanut butter flavor yet at the same time tastes like Oreo. However, look at the ingredient list. The top ingredient is sugar, followed by oil (the third ingredient is flour). Eat/buy with moderation. I like the packaging, which allows you to seal the package after taking out some cookies - great idea. This helps keeps the cookies fresher longer.

This is a review for the Oreo Peanut Butter Fudge Creme cookies:These cookies invite the obvious comparison to Girlscout Tagalongs.  I'll detail the differences so my fellow Tagalong junkies will know what to expect.1.  The cookie in the Oreo offering is a single chocolate wafer.  If memory serves, a Tagalog cookie is not chocolate2.  The peanut butter in the Oreo is more a peanut butter flavored creme than straight peanut butter.  Personally I'd rather have more peanut butter and less creme.3.  The Oreo cookie is quite a bit thinner than a Tagalong-less cookie and peanut butter both.4.  The Oreo has a faint aftertaste that is reminiscent of Crisco.In summation- these were yummy but not "to die for".  I really expected a traditional two-layer peanut butter filled Oreo dipped in Chocolate.  That would have been great and more in keeping with the Oreo brand.  Don't get me wrong though, we had no problem polishing off the box in lightning speed!

When I first opened up the packages, I was kind of disappointed because they weren't as big as I thought they would be, I think the packaging is a bit misleading. It is like one of those burger king commercials where they show a mouth watering thick hamburger and when you go to order it you get a thin soggy looking thing. That is how I felt.It is a thin oreo wafer, then a thin layer of peanut butter wrapped in fudge. The oreo is not a regular size oreo, and the peanut butter isn't even the thickness of the regular white creme in an oreo. Because the peanut butter and fudge is so sweet the oreo almost tastes a bit salty to me. It does kind of taste like those girl scout cookies the Tagalong, but I am pretty sure you get more peanut in those.Overall taste I do like, maybe a tad bit sweet. But if you have a craving for chocolate and peanut butter this will sure do the trick!

column9: Not that great.  Shouldn't be labeled oreos as they really aren't.
column10: This review is for the peanut butter fudge oreos. Evidently they may have the same code as the fudge cremes as this is the link I was given to review them from the Vine program. The peanut butter fudge oreos are not really oreos in my opinion. They really shouldn't use the name Oreo as I personally think it implies that they have an oreo taste somewhere in them. Yes there is a VERY thin oreo crust cookie in them but that taste is overwhelmed by the peanut butter and fudge. It hardly has any taste of oreo at all. Also, these cookies are very thin and there aren't as many as I expected in the package. Nobody in my household likes these cookies. Everyone who has tried them says they are nothing special and are a very forgettable cookie. I'm sure there are some people who like them, just not us.

Good clam broth. This is the very best source of Vitamin B-12, a vitamin essential to health. Without it, death always ensues; it is called pernicious anemia. B-12 is absolutely necessary for one to live with enough oxygen and stamina.  I am pleased.Iris

These are our puggle's favorite treat!  We discovered the cheese snacks at a small boutique pet store and the dog fell in love with them -- he loves anything made of cheese.  I was thrilled to find them at Amazon in the two pack at a savings!  The treats themselves are small -- about the size of a nickel -- so they are better for smaller dogs.  They even smell good!  Only drawback is that there seems to be a lot of broken pieces and cheese "dust" at the bottom of the bag.
My dog has a wheat allergy and these are the best treats I have found! He loves them! He is an 80lb boxer and boxes still seem to last a long time!

The packages are very small but it is a nice variety! It is a good way to sample some of the different flavors. However, it is a bit pricey. I think I will go for a bigger bag now that I know how tasty they are!
All of these fruit snacks are large and tasty. Muscat was a little gross, but all in all, a great product.

column9: My super picky puppy LOVES it!
column10: I have a super picky Cavalier King Charles puppy who refuses to eat dry food, and even some wet food. Generally she has to be coaxed to eat her meals. We had her on an expensive brand of canned food, which she mostly liked, but in an effort to save some money, I switched her to Merrick Whole Earth Farms Puppy canned food. SHE LOVES IT. I do not have to even try to get her to eat- she devours it the minute I put the bowl down. It is still a very "healthy" food, and it saves me $15 every time I order! Highly recommend, super, super happy!!

column9: My puppy loves & great score on dogfoodadvisor
column10: My puppy loves this food, and it's very healthy (5 stars out of 5) according to dogfoodadvisor. It's the best quality food I have been able to find for this price. We recently had to switch her to another brand since Amazon is out of stock and I can't find it locally, and she's been throwing up on the new food.

column9: Quality Puppy Food at Reasonable Price
column10: We have two new additions to our family and started feeding both girls a mixture of this puppy food mixed with 2nd Step Puppy Weaning Food.  The puppies were just over 5 wks old about 2 wks ago.  Now we just feed Merrick Whole Earth Puppy Food.  For the cost, you can't beat it!  The girls are developing wonderfully and are happy and healthy.  Cheers!  And, American made.

These are my favorite type of Jelly Bellies. I had been eyeing this product for some time. After a few glasses of wine, I decided that this was a must buy because its price per pound was much lower than a single pound of this flavor. The price is still pretty high, but it is about the same price as buying 5 single pounds. I have been snacking on these for a few months. They are still around, and I still love them.The product arrived in a cardboard box with the jelly beans directly in the box. No plastic bag or anything, just the shipping box filled with jelly beans. I am not a huge germaphobe, but would have preferred a better container than the shipping box. This was the only reason why I docked it a star.
I purchased this for a friend of mine from Canada, since they're not available in the US.  He was so excited to receive his favorite flavor of Spitz!
Spitz seeds blow away David's and Biggs by a longshot!!!! Give these a try,very mild taste and not too salty.

Got these at Rite-aid last night.Came across them from the cashier. He said they where on sale 4 bags for a dollar. I was skeptical and thought they would not be good tasting but am happily surprised that they are not too salty and I can taste the seed unlike all the other salty brands and that makes my mouth happier cause I can eat the whole bag in one day. I am going back to buy the whole lot now.....Yummmm!

column9: Nice Light Seasoning - Not To Salty - Lets Natural Flavors Shine
column10: Lightly Seasoned - Not To Salty.  Good Size Seeds - Poly bag - not that usual stiffer plastic. (IE quiet bag but more likely to rip) Very good seed indeed!

I have ordered over 6 boxes of these spitz sunflower seeds with great success but I just opened my second box on this order and I will never order these from Amazon again. They are small, stall, no taste, and cannot be eaten. The first box of 12 was ok but the second box was terrible.Please note that who ever is sending these is not doing a great job. Very disappointed and will look elsewhere for this product.

Great texture, much more like regular left over meat. Makes very good homemade hash. Very different from the canned corned beef I grew up with, the fine textured kind, like Libbys or Hormel.But, you must shop around for price. Prices vary considerably. Also, if you live in an area with good Asian grocery stores you can often find it there and avoid paying for shipping.Cooking tip. The meat has a fair amount of moisture and fat. I heat it gently in a sauce pan until the fat & moisture separate, dump it into a wire strainer & then back in the pan. Makes for a much leaner and tastier result.

This is the kind of corn beef I remember from childhood - shredded, not ground.  It's delicious!  Just heat with some chopped onion.  Terrific meal along with stewed cabbage, pork & beans and cornbread.

Great price and shipped a lot faster than expected which is always a plus! While definitely be buying more in the future. Not sure if Amazon reads these reviews but subscribe and save discount would be awesome!

We have been purchasing this catfood ever since we got our kittens last October.  They love #2,3, and 4.  The ingredients seem fresh and there are no fillers...just natural protein.  Our kitties have a ton of energy and seem very happy with it.

I have never once come across a cat eating a fruit salad or a bell pepper in the wild. This is because cats eat meat. This food is mostly meat, ergo, this food is for cats.As for taste, my cat isn't the most picky, but he has rejected a fair number of foods. He loves this stuff.

This is by far the best caramel popcorn. The best part is the packages are small keeping you under control portion wise. I pack this for my kids for their snack and they love it. The taste is not over powering by sugar.A perfect snack when you are tired of eating tasteless stuff.

I have to say I enjoyed eating this snack. I never had chocolate with popcorn and I will definitely have to try it again. The dominant flavor is still the caramel, but every now and then you get a popcorn that has more chocolate on it. I wish there was more of those, but it's still good. If you like caramel popcorn you should like this.

I'm a lover of popcorn, caramel and chocolate, though not always together.I also like indulging in an occasional extra sweet treat and that's what SnackWells delivers.Most of my 'sweet' snacking consists of fruit and dark chocolate which makes these taste like a sugar explosion. After one bag I was definitely not interested in more (at the time), but was satisfied with the over-the-top sweetness it delivered.Overall, if you like the flavor combination this snack provides then you'll probably enjoy enjoy it. Do be warned that it's on the 'dry' side as far as caramelly snacks go.

I didn't like these, but then I don't care for many of Snackwell's products, most of which seem bland to me. This was especially bad because it had the feel of packing peanuts instead of real popcorn.

I got this snack, not knowing quite what to expect, as I had never tried a Snackwell's product before. I was surprised at how delicious they were! Each pack carried just enough to quell my hunger for something quick and sweet. Even though these are marketed as a low fat snack, they don't taste like it at all. This is something I would definitely buy again, and it makes me want to try other Snackwell products as well. The only thing I thought of is that you could probably save money by making these yourself as all you need is caramel popcorn and chocolate!

column9: A Little Goes a LONG Way!
column10: I didn't expect to like this as well as I do. It's crispy, with a salty-sweetness that I sometimes just CRAVE. The pouches are the perfect amount and you get a lot of flavor for 130 calories. I find them a bit TOO sweet though and I could never eat more than just one pouch in a sitting, which I guess is actually a benefit of the product...absolutely no temptation to keep eating.

These fudge drizzle caramel popcorn treats are incredibly good.  The caramel corn tastes better than the stuff from the expensive popcorn shop, and it's much more convenient.  The amazing thing is how fresh it tastes.  It also looks appetizing, not all soggy or sticky.  Oh, and there's chocolate, too!  Great combination, great idea.The individual packets contain more than enough for a satisfying snack.

This product comes in a nice size package for an individual serving. It is a tasty little snack that will satisfy your need for something sweet.  The carmel and chocolate cover up the taste of the popcorn and left me wanting some "real popcorn". This product is well packaged and was in great shape when I received it and very fresh.  Definitely would be a handy snack for traveling or lunches.

column4: Penny Pinching Polly "Check out my website fo...
column10: My 5 year old and I love these!  While it's true that you can eat much more plain popcorn for 130 calories, you're not reaching for these unless you WANT (or sometimes NEED) something sweet as well as a bit salty!  These do the trick and there's enough to satisfy your craving!I will be buying these in the future.  My daughter really enjoyed them, and so did I.  They give you the crunch, the chocolate, the sweetness, and the salty taste you just sometimes HAVE to have.

This is a portion-controlled snack that can be used to control the calories consumed.  I thought it was delicious but the portion is of course small (but then it's carmel corn, so we already knew that, didn't we?)If you are the sort of person who can't stop eating carmel corn until the bag is empty (I wouldn't know about that, heh) then this will be a useful product for you.  It's excellent and doesn't taste at all 'dlet-y'.I have already purchased other snack products in this same line, and have enjoyed them all equally.  I do recommend this one.

These snack packs are perfect size for those counting their calories or living life on the go.  Great size for an addition to lunch or just a traveling snack.  The combination of carmel popcorn and chocolate drizzle is just about perfect.  It is not "too much" chocolate as in some similar products.  SnackWells hits the mark with this great combination.

column9: Tastes great and perfect if you can eat just one
column10: In the past I have not had good experiences with Snackwell's products. I am talking to you Devil's Food cookies. But since I am a fan of carmel corn I decided to give this a shot. I am glad I did because it tastes very good. And the fudge is just the right amount of sweetness without going overboard. If you are dieting this is the perfect amount to satisfy your cravings. The real test is limiting yourself to just the one package a serving.

column9: These disappeared real fast in my household!
column10: I swear a box of these lasted for three days between my boyfriend and me.  It's a very tasty snack and I don't normally like caramel popcorn.  For the price, I would prefer the popcorn just in a large bag inside so I could put whatever amount I wanted in sandwich bag.  I find all this "convenience" packaging a bit hard for my green side to take.  I don't think I would buy this item due to its price, even when it is on sale at my local grocery.  They had them two boxes for $5 which comes out to 50 cents a bag.  If I bought a bag of popcorn or even popped it at home, I could make a bag of it to take on trips for a fraction of the cost.  Overall, the box did disappear in my household rather fast, so if you don't mind extra packaging and want to pay a bit more for the convenience, then this is probably a product for you if you like popcorn as much as I do.

I have to give this product 5 stars because as soon it arrived my teen daughter ate the whole order. I asked for some to try and she said sorry. She ate it all it was so good, and we don't normally care for the taste of most snackwell products. This one however was obviously delicious.

It's difficult for me not to be a little conflicted about Snackwell Fudge Drizzle Caramel Popcorn.  On one hand, there is no denying the fact that they taste delicious!  On the other hand, there is the misperception of many that just because it's Snackwells, it's better for you than a "regular" snack.  That's not necessarily the case.The advantage to this product is the portion control.  One packet totals 130 calories and there is no question that they are delicious!  Just don't eat 5 packets of them and think that you're adhering to your diet.

This popcorn is so delicious I would compare it to gourmet popcorns that retail for quite a lot. I also have a hard time believing that this product is so low calorie! An excellent afternoon indulgence, this popcorn is generously drizzled with a sweet and creamy fudge. The carmel coating gives the popcorn a satisfying crunch. This popcorn satisfied my desire for a salty sweet treat and didn't overload me on calories. Highly recommend!

column9: Be Careful... They are Deliciously Sweet and Yummy
column10: I didn't know what to expect from a "SnackWell's" carmel corn product, but I was delightfully surprised! This is a delicious snack, just the right amount of caramel and chocolate. However, I would never classify this as healthy or a "diet" food. It is simply packaged in small individual serving size packets, with 130 cal. per packet. And guess what... you need to have enough willpower to keep from opening two or three of the packets at one time, as I did when I first tried these delectable treats! So, they do taste great, but don't fool yourself into thinking it's something healthy. If you can manage to eat one serving occasionally (in moderation as we should with all high-sugar snacks), then go for it!

I love popcornI love chocolateand I love sugarThis box arrived with six small bags of chocolate drizzled caramel popcorn.  Generally prepackaged popcorn has a stale taste to it, but this stuff was fantastic.  VERY sugary which may be a turn off to some, and a little pricey for what is essentially crunch n munch with chocolate on it... but this stuff was good.  So good that between my boyfriend and I the entire box didn't last 12 hours.  At our rate of consumption the bags were too small, but if you were looking for something to have as a small snack or to add to a lunch then these are perfect.  I'll wait for the jumbo size to come out and buy those :)

I love this little snack idea!  I have tried a lot of the other handy, low calorie snacks (cookies, crackers, etc.) that a lot of different companies have been coming out with lately and I just love this one.  Sweet caramel popcorn and rich chocolate are such a great combination, and I love that this is so convenient I can throw it into my purse or lunchbag and know that I will have a satisfying and delicious treat later.  Will definitely buy again and am excited about trying out different flavors!
I guess if you're going to eat junk food, this is one way to do it without too much guilt.  The fudge and caramel made this popcorn tasty.  I wish there was more of them.

column9: Very, very sweet, not diet food
column10: I love caramel popcorn, and I assumed these were a "diet" version, but they're not.  What it is is a portion control item made from full caloried ingredients.  Brown sugar is the first ingredient, for example.  They're actually quite good, although the chocolate has little flavor.  The buttery caramel part is tasty.  I liked them as a portion control item, but they won't work for most "diet" regimes due to the amount of sugar.  I might buy them to toss in lunches.

I was hesitant to try these. I thought they may be dry, but they are really good! They taste like the tin can carmel popcorn you buy around christmas time that everyone looks forward to, only these are in calorie controlled packets which helps, so you don't eat the whole tin! ;)

These crunchy sweet golden nuggets are tasty, and thankfully for those of us with poor impulse control, in small portion pouches (one 130 calorie pouch = 3 Weight Watchers Points Plus).I wasn't that thrilled with the Fudge drizzle; it didn't taste bad, it just didn't have much taste. An occasional hint of chocolate, but mostly just waxy blandness. Thankfully, it's just a light "drizzle", and not a full coating.I don't know if they offer this option, but I would prefer just the plain caramel corn; without the fudge drizzle, they could increase the portion size a little for the same calorie/points value.

I can't say enough good things about Snackwell Fudge Drizzle Caramel Popcorn! I remember when Snackwell products were first introduced, and they were just not as good as "real" cookies. They've come a long way, and these packs (130 calories each) have a decent serving of popcorn in them. There is plenty of crunchy caramel, and the chocolate isn't overwhelming. A great balance.I've already purchased more!

"Snackwell fudge Drizzle Caramel Popcorn" is a good treat for calorie-counting sweet fiends, with each box containing five individually-wrapped portions at 130 calories each. However, I can't distinguish between the fudge and caramel taste...all I get from each bite is an overpowering taste of generic, artificial-tasting sweetness.Still, if you have a strong sweet-tooth and are watching your weight, you'll probably dig this, as the packaging is certainly convenient and the price is fair for what you get.

column9: a light snack, but very sweet and high in sugar
column10: I love popcorn, corn snacks, any snacks made out of popcorn or corn -- so I wanted to give these a try. As a popcorn snack, it's very hearty and yet relatively light, even though these are "caramel" and "chocolate drizzled" pieces of popcorn. It helps satisfy a sweet snacking urge.The popcorn itself is well-popped, with no hard pieces or excess bits of kernels. It's fluffy and airy. I really wish I knew how they can get popcorn this "perfect". Each piece is coated in caramel, and drizzled in chocolate, and some pieces are coated on the bottom with chocolate.And therein lies the problem. Although this is a "SnackWells" snack, and meant to be a healthy choice, each 1.06 ounce package (the box contains 5 packages) clocks in at 130 calories with 3g of fat, 2.5g of which are saturated. Additionally, each package contains 18g of sugar. Sure, it tastes good, but that's a lot of sugar for a "healthy" snack. Two of the first three ingredients are "brown sugar" and "sugar". If you're trying to avoid sugar for any reason, this really isn't a good option.I got through one box and enjoyed it, having it usually with a cup of tea in the afternoon. But I won't pick this up again. It isn't worthy of a "healthy" snacking label, although it really does taste good. If you just want a low calorie snack regardless of sugar content, then I recommend it.

If you love caramel popcorn drizzled in chocolate you will love this! Not much else to say about it than that. The only reservation I have about this product is the name "Snackwell" makes you think you are eating a health product. Not so! The packaging is in 130 calorie packs to prevent you from over eating the food, but other than that, this is a standard high sugar snack. 18 g of sugar in one small pack (30g). After eating one pack, there will be a serious temptation to devour the remaining 4 packs.

I really did not have very high expectations for Snackwell Fudge Drizzle Caramel Popcorn, so I was surprised when it turned out to be a tasty, satisfying snack. Nabisco has managed to strike a balance between the popcorn, the caramel coating, and the fudge drizzle. They are fairly sweet, but the sweetness is offset by a slight saltiness. I did not detect any stale or old taste in the popcorn. I found the 130-calorie portion to be adequate and satisfying, but I don't have much of a sweet tooth; my weakness is salty snacks.According to an article in the New York Times, "All of the new SnackWell's products have a suggested retail price of $3.19 for a box of five servings.". This works out to about 64 cents a serving, which seems in line with a lot of portion-controlled snacks. I expect they will available from time-to-time at a deep discount at many grocers and mass merchandisers such as Target and Walmart. There is a white fudge version of this product and two varieties of brownie bits being rolled out at the same time.Shipping note: It was in the 80's the day these were delivered. The package had spent at least a couple of hours in a postal van with no air-conditioning and sat in the sun on my porch for about five minutes after being dropped by the carrier. I opened one pack right away and found the chocolate to be gooey, but not melted. I put the opened pack and the box in the refrigerator immediately. Later when I tried the cooled packs I found a little clumping in a couple of the packs. I think if it had been much warmer or if I had left the parcel on the porch much longer, I might have ended up with five individually-wrapped popcorn balls.

These yummy popcorn snacks are definitely addictive, offering a pleasing combination of crunchy and sweet.They contain no artificial ingredients which I think is why they don't taste like "junk" food. The individual packages are only 130 calories which makes them a good choice for a quick but sweet snack when you don't want to  "go all the way" with a calorie loaded candy bar! For those who follow Weight Watchers, these packs are equal to 3 points. I will definitely buy more of these snacks.

column9: Fudge Drizzle Caramel Popcorn is too sweet for my taste
column10: These popcorn tasted too sweet, even though the nutrition facts didn't show large amount of sugar or calories.I have enjoyed caramel popcorn (that come in large tin boxes during holidays) in the past, but unfortunately I didn't like these. Even our candy-loving child declared these are too sweet and it is hard to consume one whole packet. (May be that is a good thing.)None of the family members were enthusiastic about these snacks, we won't be purchasing these, and will not recommend to others.

This caramel corn really does taste great with the fudge drizzle, the chocolate flavor is aparent but not overpowering, so you get to taste both caramel and chocolate.I was a little hesitant about them being in pre-packaged, 130 calorie sizes, as most of those 100cal pack snacks are very very small bags, and the bag I pulled out of the box looked no different, very small.  But I was surprised to find out that you do actually get a decent amount of caramel corn per bag (apparently they just LOOK small, they actually hold quite a bit), and they are well suited for bag lunches and snacks.Reccommended.

column9: Good flavor but not filling and very sweet
column10: This is not the perfect snack, but it does have several benefits.  On the upside, Snackwell Fudge Drizzle Caramel Popcorn has good flavor.  The chocolate and caramel flavors taste rich and real.  The popcorn is nice and crisp and not at all stale like some popcorn snacks.  On the downside, this snack is high in sugar (the carb count is 24 grams, 18 grams of which is sugar).  Because of the high sugar content and the fact that this snack is only 130 calories, the serving size is quite small--about 1/2 cup.In my opinion, there are many other snack choices that are more substantial and filling for the same or fewer calories.  A mini-bag of light popcorn, for example, is only 100 calories for about 3 cups of popcorn.  The Snackwell Fudge Drizzle Caramel Popcorn would be a good choice for an after-dinner treat when you want something sweet but aren't particularly hungry after dinner.  For afternoon hunger pangs, however, this snack is likely to be unsatisfying.

column4: Glenda Boozer "Live, live, live! Life is a ba...
column9: If you're craving a sweet and salty snack, this one is good!
column10: Sweet, chocolatey and salty - and satisfying, even in the little calorie-measured bags. This would make a nice lunch box dessert as well as something to grab anytime for a quick snack. It's popcorn with a sweet glaze and a chocolate drizzle, but it's not too sticky, and that's a plus. I'd buy it for traveling and camping as well as at-home snacking.

This snack isn't bad, but it isn't much more than average either.  The combination of sweet and salty is one I like, but the sugar content is pretty high for such a small snack (18 grams), so to balance it out, it seems the salty taste is pretty high too.  I did not notice much of a chocolate flavor at all. On the other hand, my husband, who is not a big chocolate fan and loves his salty snacks, thought the flavors were well balanced.  I received these to try through the Vine program but probably won't buy them for myself.

... per handful.It tastes good, but to market it as a low-calorie alternative to other snacks is kind of a stretch.
