After much anticipation, I have put my hands on this treasure that I have longed for.Noodle quality wise, I'd have to give this ramen a 5 star, simply because of the smooth texture and the chewiness of the ramen noodle was absolutely wonderful.Soup quality wise, I'd give it 4 stars as I am a Korean-American, I do prefer spicy ramen over not so spicy ones.Overall, it is a very good ramen.  However, I do realize that this ramen made its mark due to a Korean TV show and much of the "myth" was an over-hyped up propaganda.  Good ramen but I heard from many Korean folks that Nagasaki Udon is a much better ramen than Kko-Kko Myun, gonna try that next~

column9: Only for some people who don't have H-Mart around.
column10: This is way expensive.there are only 10 pc in a box.I prefer Saeng Saeng Woodon.Actually, H-mart will soon import this ramen so plz be patient little more.

We sampled this at the Buford Highway Farmers market in Atlanta.  DELICIOUS!  We bought it immediatetly!  Has a great taste, great noodles and it's SPICY - In a good way!  It was much cheaper there than here!  Such a disapointment on the price!

column9: Have you checked if your local H-Mart has it?
column10: Others keep mentioning how expensive this item is, but if like me, it's not found on your local Asian store then it's not overly priced. For right now it's a rare item, shipped directly from Korea, and from my first experience much better in taste than others in the market.If you think that adding chicken and bouillon will get you this taste, then you must have been using some fantastic brand i have yet to try. I'm used to using bouillon on my ramen, because i the usual ramen i use either have too much heat, and not enough flavor; or they amount is too little to really give much flavor with one packet. I have used both Maggi and Knorr. Also, there is always some grainy bits at the bottom of the pot or bowl, from the flavor packet. Something you do not have to worry with this brand.On top of all that, i don't feel there is as much MSG if at all in the flavor packets. Normally i know just how much there is based on the fat/grease left after i eat the ramen, because i have been fooled by not noticing any on the liquid before it cools. There was little to no grease at at all with this brand, which is a major plus for me.The best part? The "heat" level. It doesn't contain pepper flakes, which i hate, or the excessiveness Nong Shim tends to use. I always have to end up using only about half the amount from Nong Shim, and i love spicy food. This brand is spicy, but without heat, which makes the chicken flavor stand out.There is a second packet that brings dried veggies, including green/red peppers and chicken. It's a small amount, so you don't feel like the whole soup if filled with it. It makes it easier to avoid, if you don't want them, but still want the flavor they provide. Or if like me, you want sporadic pieces with every ramen slurp, or broth drink.Honestly, i wasn't expecting much because it's ramen noodles, and the idea comes from a comedian. Whom as much as i like, is a man who doesn't normally cook. But this was better than many i have tried. Should also mention i'm not a big fan of the chicken flavor ramen. I usually prefer seafood or kimchi, but it's not heavily flavored, just savory?

I had been buying this candy from a machine (for a quarter at a time) and filling a ziplock bag to take home.  I tried to find it in the bricks and mortar stores, and they don't seem to have it or even know what I am talking about.  I even checked the bulk candy place in the mall (which seems to have gotten very expensive), yet even they didn't seem to know.Nitwitz works well as a "candy dish" candy because the pieces are solid (no candy dust) and don't seem to leave a residue in the dish (like a gummy candy might).  These are very similar to Willy Wonka Runts, but somewhat smaller and more tart.  The only issue with it is that it seems that the oranges make up an outsize percentage of the mix.  I suppose that it is possible that buying it from the machine somehow filtered out the larger orange pieces.  Also, the orange pieces are more like jawbreakers and I will have to warn guests about trying to bite down on them right away.  The other pieces are not quite as hard.Overall, I am pleased with the 2.5 lbs. mix and it should last me for several months.  It arrived in an unlabeled, sealed plastic bag inside two padded envelopes.  There does not seem to be any broken pieces.
I loved barbecued baked beans but these British-style beans with a simple tomato sauce are so much more versatile.  Just delicious!

I never tried the gourmet food section before. I wandered in here recently on a long shopping trip through the Amazon.com website.I thought these truffles looked to good to be true for the price and decided to try a small quantity, the half pound box.Delivery was very fast for standard shipping, ordered Saturday and they arrived today (Wednesday).There are 8 truffles in the half pound package. Yummy truffle fudge surrounded by terrific hard chocolate. If you like chocolate, you'll be satisfied. My four daughters and wife confirm that these are among the better truffles that they have had.I was not disapointed and expect to be sending more of these to my friends and family.

I sent these to my mum for Mother's Day and I am delighted to report she was most impressed so much so that I will be re-ordering soon!  The truffles are large, coated thickly with a chocolate shell and have a mouthwatering, creamy, fudgy interior.  Hooray - I did something right for once!

I ordered this product because it seemed it would be good for everyone in the family. I did read the other reviews and knew they were going to be super crunchy, which they were, but they seemed to be stale.  My children said they tasted funny.  I checked if I could send them back but it stated non-returnable.  I threw them away and will bevery leary about ordering food products if there is no returns allowed if the product is not good.

I purchased this product after the stellar reviews.  I'm a big fan of granola and love to snack on handfuls of it at work and mixed with some milk or yogurt and fresh fruit from the farmers market here in N. Calif. I anxiously opened the package, grabbed one of the small "disks" of granola.  My first reaction was to look for the "use by" date, as I was sure I had stale product.  Hard as a rock and dry (sucked the moisture right out of my mouth).  I was scrambling for a glass of milk. The expiration date wasn't until 2013.  I've been eating granola my whole life and this product just doesn't do it for me.  There's no richness, no smooth texture, and as I mentioned, my mouth is so dry after just one piece, that it's not an effective snack for me. Regarding the flavor, I taste no almond, and the cinnamon is overwhelming.  I have given away the other three bags.  The only thing good about this product is the packaging and clever description (they must have good marketing talent).  Sorry guys....just not my cup of tea...

Reason for Smiling after eating this cereal is that you are on a sugar high! It contains brown sugar, evaporated cane juice and honey, but wait even the crisp rice contains sugar. Even with the antioxidants this is not a health food. There are so many better choices out there, including making your own granola, which I do. All you need is an oil, sweetener, roll oats and a oven. Add what you enjoy such as almond and cinnamon. Give it a try. Enjoy!!

I recently tried these clusters and WOW were they good. Great to eat as is, straight from the bag or would be perfect for an addition to a salad. Not only are they good.. but they are good for you as a healthier for you snack. Only problem is convincing yourself to stop eating them :)Enjoy!

One of the things I appreciated most about this granola is that the ingredient list was not overly lengthy and had not a single ingredient that I couldn't pronounce or identify.  Its primary ingredients are whole grain rolled oats, almonds, cocoa and cinnamon.  Another is that it is not overly sweet.For me, the biggest downside to the granola is that, when I first opened the bag, many of the "clusters" were HUGE...the size of maybe 1/2 of a small candy bar.  If you're the type that eats granola as a snack right out of the bag, then that is probably going to be an advantage.  For me, it was a disadvantage.  I don't eat a lot of granola; but when I do, I use it as a light crunchy topping for yogurt or ice cream.  As such, I want it in smaller pieces.  I took a meat mallet to my bag and rectified the situation. :)The flavor of the granola is excellent.  In some bites, I get mostly a taste of cocoa and cinnamon and the crunch of the oats.  In others, I get more of the nut taste and texture.  As noted before, this granola is not overly sweet, which I like.  Despite the preponderance of cocoa in this granola, don't buy this expecting it to taste like a candy bar--this is cocoa, not chocolate.  Sweeteners listed include brown sugar, evaporated cane juice and honey.I thought it was misleading that the this variety is called "Cinnamon Almond" when the primary flavor is cocoa, but perhaps that is because all of their granolas are cocoa-based?  Not sure.  To me, it tastes much more of both cocoa and cinnamon than of almond.  I would never consider almond a primary flavor in it and I eat almonds pretty regularly, so I know their taste.If you like a good crunch, you're going to like this.  Your jaw definitely gets a workout when eating it, esp. if you don't break down those giant "clusters."  Just be forewarned--it is pretty addicting!Last but not least, here is the per-serving nutrition information:Serving Size 1/3 cupCalories  160Total Fat  6gSat Fat  2gTrans Fat  0Cholesterol  0Sodium  85mgPotassium  120mgTotal Carbs  24gFiber  3gSugars  12gProtein  3gContains Calcium, Vitamins A, B6, C and E and several minerals.Recommended.

column9: Bland and Boring, Chunky and Stale
column10: The first few bites of these clusters were good, but I quickly grew bored of the taste.  It was too chocolaty, and within a day of opening the bag the product quickly became chewy, like it was stale.Although the shipment came with 4 bags, I ended up finishing only one.  Two were thrown away half-eaten, and the fourth was tossed altogether.

column9: Very tasty. All five member of my family enjoyed them. Fresh and delish.
column10: This is the first time I order these. I ordered them because they were on sale. I am very glad I did. These are very good. They are not too sweat and they satisfied our chocolate craving. I would recommend them to anyone who wants a healthy snack.

Ummm!I guess I'm not the right customer for this item. Although they are large chunks of granola type product, I just not into the taste that much. I mean - it's ok - but I'm not smiling after I eat these things.For those who like big crunchy gobs of granola this will probably be perfect for you.

So tired of Health Food Store bulk granola ~ sure can't find this one where I live.  We threw a couple of mini carrots in the bag overnight and they softened up.  A must if you don't want to break a tooth!  Cocoa infused makes it delectable!

column9: This stuff is great.  I toss a bag in my car and have a great breakfast in traffic
column10: I love the flavor of actual cocoa.  And the chunks are actually great because they're easier to eat.  If you want to break it up smaller to put in yogurt or something, well, it's granola and easy to break up!

Not a loot of sugar per serving but still tasty if you like coca.  There is some almond/oat flavor but mostly drowned out by the coca.  Most of the chucks aren't real large but are pretty big if you like your granola mixed with yogurt or cerial

column9: If there were laws against tasty snacks, this one broke them all...
column10: Here's my thoughts on these tasty granola clusters:LOOKS: When opening the bag, I didn't have to work very long to find large clusters, they were sitting on top. Each piece was coated in cocoa, and the oats and almonds were waiting below the surface.PACKAGING: I was pleased to see these bags were resealable. Easy to open, easy to seal, no fussin', no mussin'.SERVING SIZE: Each pouch has roughly 10 servings each. Keep in mind, it's easy to keep on snacking, so pour yourself a handful and leave the bag on the counter if you're trying to make the bag last more than 2 hours...TASTE: The cocoa flavoring really popped out, it's the first smell that hit me when I opened the bag. The next taste was an even mixture between the oats and almonds. I barely tasted the cinnamon at all, but that's just me.Simply put - I LOVED this dry granola snack. One of my coworkers said she would prefer these over Girl Scout Samoa cookies, that's a pretty bold statement!CONCLUSION?If you're looking for something to snack on while you watch Mad Men or plow through another dungeon in Skyrim, this is an excellent choice. Keep a glass of milk nearby!

column9: I wish the clusters are smaller
column10: I like putting granola clusters on top of my oatmeal or use them as cereal - I could not do it with this. This is purely for snacking, finger food, and it's perfect for that purpose.The chocolate isn't very chocolatey, but it's a bit bitter. The cinnamon is very strong. In fact, I think the cinnamon flavor is much stronger than the chocolate. Overall, I enjoyed this snack as a snack, but it really isn't more useful than a snack. I really wanted to use it in my cereal, or as a cereal.It isn't too sweet, which is a big plus. Even though I give it a four star, some of my friends loved it. They would have likely given it five stars.

I'd been seeing Eat.Think.Smile.'s products in my grocery store for a couple of months, so when the opportunity came to try this granola, I jumped at it.  I'm glad I did.  This is bite-sized chunks of granola rich with cocoa, cinnamon, and almonds.  It makes a filling snack and it tastes great.  But you should keep in mind that granola is not exactly a low-cal, low-fat, low-carb treat.  In a 1/3 cup serving there are 160 calories, 6g of fat, and 24g of carbs.  However, this snack has a goodly amount of potassium (120mg) and 3g of protein as well.  The ingredients include whole grain rolled oats, brown sugar, palm oil, almonds, evaporated cane juice, cocoa,crisp rice, honey, cinnamon, salt, natural flavor and soy lecithin.The granola pieces are very chewy, so it takes longer to eat them.  This is better than eating a candy bar that can be sucked down in a minute flat.  On the whole, I really enjoyed these, and so did the other members of my household.  I'll be buying more and trying other products from this company.

column9: Delicious...but more decadent than I anticipated
column10: I'd probably give this product a 3.5 star rating if half stars were allowed here.The good:The taste!  I honestly didn't expect to like this as much as I do, but I think the balance of cocoa and cinnamon is just right.  The cocoa, in particular, tastes VERY good.  I'm assuming a high quality cocoa is used in this product since it tastes much better than the mass market cocoa you'd likely find at your local grocery store.The texture.  This granola comes with lots of fairly large clumps, not just a bunch of small pieces.  It's definitely possible to eat this dry right out of the bag.  The almonds and whole grain oats contribute to a nice, crunchy texture.The not so good:The nutritional information.  If you are very good about controlling your intake, this could certainly be a fine addition as a snack.  I, however, have a hard time not overconsuming sweet foods, and this granola is definitely sweet (as most granolas are).  Just one serving of this granola packs 160 calories, with 50 of those being from fat and almost another 100 from carbohydrates (nearly half of those being listed as "sugars").  If you're doing your math, then you already know that that means this product provides very little protein -- in fact, only 3 grams per serving.  And here's the kicker:  All of that nutritional information is based on a serving size of only 1/3 cup, or 1.2 ounces of this product.  Each bag supposedly contains close to 10 servings.  I honestly think it would be far more reasonable to double the values above and double the serving size as I have a hard time imagining that most people would only eat 1/3 cup of this product at a time.

Keep in mind that 'clusters' is the key word here.  The size varies for all of the pieces (from tiny bits to pieces as big as a quarter if not larger), so I'm not sure I'd want to sprinkle these on my yogurt as suggested.  Dunk them in it? Heck yeah.  Eat them as is? Even better.  This is a very tasty, very crunchy snack that is big on the chocolate and cinnamon flavor.  Nothing overpowering, just a nice blend of flavors that lingers afterward and makes a great, healthy alternative to chocolates or other sweets.  The most difficult part is stopping after a handful of the things!

column9: I should have never ordered this...
column10: ...because now I have a new addiction.  These Cinnamon Almond Clusters with a nice cocoa taste are awesome.  If you are looking for a good snack or something healthier to take the edge of that chocolate craving, this is it.  There are several varieties available.  The only problem I can see is that they aren't currently available on amazon or stores, so I hope they are soon before my sample runs out.  As soon as you can, order this!  It is amazing!
The amazing cocoa taste is out of this world.  I'm waiting for more to be available to buy!  I hope this is soon available in grocery stores in Connecticut.

I tried two flavors of Eat. Think. Smile. Granola, and this one was the tastier of the two (the other was Walnut Cranberry). I like cinammon, almond, and chocolate, and they taste pretty great together here.The only problem with this product is that, as a granola, it's SO DANG HARD! I mean, I like a firm, crunchy granola, but this one can induce jaw-ache if you munch too much at one go. Perhaps it's a candidate for dipping in a mug of coffee or a glass of milk, like a hard cookie?

column9: Lots of calories, hurts my teeth.
column10: The taste of these granola clusters is actually very delicious, but the nutritional value exceeds the necessary intake. Also, since no other foods seem to cause this issue, my teeth get aches after chewing on these for a while. Not a very good sign.

column9: A wonderful blend of granola; too bad nutrition facts betray the serving size
column10: It has been my experience that granola has come a long way since I was a little kid.  My only real memory of granola was the bars and they were alright.  Now in modern times, granola is a versatile food item, finding its home on yogurt, as salad toppings, in baked goods and yes still in bar form (but even those are fancier). The one pratfall that most granola suffers from is a high fat and calorie count.  I have tried other top shelf brands of granola that is promoted as healthy and it really isn't.This leads us to "Eat. Think. Smile's" brand of granola.  There are several different flavors that ETS showcases, this is the blend is "cinnamon almond".  The staring flavors/ingredients are cocoa, whole grain oats, almonds and cinnamon.  The granola has a wonderful taste.  The flavors really blend well together, giving it a nice nutty and sweet balance.  The texture is crunchy with a slight chewy aspect.  In addition, since these are clusters, they would be great as salad or yogurt toppers and wonderful in baked goods.This product is all natural which is good, but this doesn't always translate to a healthy product.  A serving size is a third of a cup and is 160 calories and 6 grams of fat.  Personally I feel that is high for such a small amount.  Therefore, one needs to be careful not to eat too much of it.  In contrast, this product has no trans fat and cholesterol.  An interesting side note, I put some of this granola in a Pyrex container and it became a little stale.  Which is odd considering Pyrex containers are pretty much air tight.Overall, I really like this product.  It is much better than most granola I have tried, but it must be noted that this isn't a health food.  Actually, most granola isn't healthy, all natural or not.  However under moderation, this is a good snack and I am sure there are worst things out there to eat.

column9: Now we're talking... this is a snack that I can fully recommend!
column10: First things first, the Cinnamon Almond Eat. Think. Smile. Granola Clusters taste great!  An honest cocoa flavor, crunchy and tasty!  Too many "health" snacks fail that test within one or two bites.  This stuff is good!Now, to the more complicated stuff.  After discarding the 80 or 90% of healthy snack foods who's flavor doesn't agree with me, I then run into conflict with the "reality of the nutrition label".  You know what I mean, "only 60 calories per serving!", then you note that there are 30 servings in the package.  Sound the alarm!  At first, I was a little leery on this count.  A 12 ounce bag of granola clusters contains 160 calories per serving.  Not outrageous, but a piece of math that instantly worries me, especially when the product tastes so good (did I mention that?  It tastes real good).  This is where I give these guys 5 stars... what looked to me as being a 10th of the package, ACTUALLY SATISFIES!  Usually... something this tasty suffers the ignominy of getting cleaned out in one setting, leaving me disappointed and weighing a pound or two more the following morning; not the case here!  A little goes a long way toward leaving you satisfied.I have never had this to say about a snack food product before, this is the first snack food that meets all of my expectations.  No trade-offs!  Great taste!  Great texture!  Natural, healthy ingredients!  And a satisfying snack!  Thank you guys!

If you are more likely to eat granola dry as a snack food you may like this one because it is mostly in large chunks.  It's like eating hard irregularly  shaped chocolate cookies.  I did try it with almond milk for the sake of writing a well rounded review but although the cocoa did impart a chocolatly taste to the milk I did not enjoy trying to eat is as a cereal.  The second item in the ingredients list is sugar so I expected it to be overly sweet but it isn't.  Still I would not buy this granola because it was not delicious and although I like chunky granola as a snack food, these chunks are too hard.  Update - I put chunks of peeled sweet potato in the container I had the granola in, put the lid on, and next day the granola was way better.  Not nearly so hard so I could enjoy the taste more.  This would work even better with a cut up apple but I didn't have one.

column9: Tasty enough, just hard to chew
column10: The granola was alright and tasted good.  My issue with it was that it was very hard to chew.  I couldn't eat much before my jaw was exhausted.  It was so terrible because I was so excited about cinnamon, almond, cocoa granola - I found it addictive but it wore out my face!

column9: Crunchy and tasty Cinnamon Almond Cocoa Granola Clusters
column10: These granola clusters are highly addictive.  They are morsel size and can be eaten without spoon, so they are easy to carry around as a quick hunger-quencher or energy booster. They taste very much like cocoa, are crunchy and quite delicious. So far I can certainly recommend them.  Now the bad part: serving size 1/3 cup (35g). Servings per container: 10. Calories: 160! (50 from fat) Saturated fat: 2g (10%). Sugars: 12g.  Assorted vitamins and minerals. So the taste does not come for free but as I said at least one gets something quite tasty for the calories.

Not necessary to completely go sugar-free to maintain a healthy balance in your diet.  In fact, too much Splenda can, of course, do unpleasant things to your trips to the necessary room.  Try this; a 1/3 cup serving of these delicious, chocolatey, crunchy snacks, with only slight hints of cinnamon and almond, contains just 6g of fat and 12g of sugars to go with 3g of fiber and 120mg of potassium.  Better yet, it's filling and VERY chocolatey.  If this description appeals to you, I promise you will not be disappointed.

This is good granola. Straight out of the bag or in a bowl with milk this granola is good. Great taste of cocoa and cinnamon combined. The two flavors are not overwhelming on their own but mix together to make a party in your mouth!

column9: Chocolaty Goodness - I Love This Stuff!
column10: The label describes this as "Cinnamon Almond" clusters, but in a little word balloon mentions "the natural antioxidant power of cocoa." And it's really the cocoa that is the dominant flavor here - and I mean that in a good way! This has a hearty, healthy chocolate taste - not like a candy bar. The cinnamon is subtle, almost an aftertaste to the cocoa.  The individual clusters are solid and hearty; not too hard, not too soft. And OHhhhh, do these go great with morning coffee! Some granola products just seem like cookie crumbles, but this actually tastes like healthy (albeit very enjoyable) food. Highly recommended!

First, this is like granola, but it's not cereal. Sure, you could put it in a bowl and pour milk over it, I guess, but it's much more fun to just eat straight out of the bag. It's kind of like a broken oatmeal cookie.First, the ingredients are natural and pretty simple, and the calorie count for a serving is reasonable. I think it's about 160 calories per serving, except that trying to decide how much a serving is when you have bits and pieces of granola isn't easy unless you're inclined to weigh your food. I'm not.What I liked about the cocoa was that not only did it taste good, the granola clusters don't leave a mess behind on my fingers. Packing a handful of this into a snack bag and taking it to work makes a nice snack and is healthier than raiding the vending machine. I like to snack on cereal and this takes it a step farther with the addition of cocoa. My only complaint, and it's too small to mark down the product, is that I really don't taste the cinnamon very much. I think it's overshadowed by the cocoa, although if I could try the product without cinnamon I might notice its absence.If you want an alternative to cookies and candy bars for snacks, give this a try.

column9: Should be on the DEA's Controlled Substance List!
column10: These tasty little bites are incredibly addictive.  The cocoa adds the taste desired by chocoholics.  the almonds make it nice and crunchy.  These are perfect of snacks while watching a movie or late night television.  Luckily, I couldn't figure out the calories per serving size.  Highly recommended

Not bad at all.  Unlike some snacks like this, it isn't a bunch of broken up crumbs.  All pretty much bite size and very tasty.  I don't like to over do it on the cinnamon and this is just about right.  A generous portion  tops it all off...  Enjoy!  UPDATE:  The second bag was the same BUT...  had a lot of crumbs in the bottom.  Not so bad though... I put them on my cereal in the am and on my ice-cream in the eve. at snack time...

Eat. Think. Smile. Granola clusters Cinnamon almond is 12 ounces of good eating.  Healthy, yet delicious granola clusters with almonds and cinnamon get the extra treatment of cocoa powder!  This delicious coating adds antioxidants and taste.  Whole grains give these treats thumbs up for me.  But all these healthy elements do add up to 160 calories per 1/3 cup serving.Perfect for snacking right out of the bag, or I would eat them with milk or on top of yogurt.Although these are definitely vegetarian, I do not know if they are vegan; as the ingredient list includes sugar and honey.  The product's website did not disclose that it is in fact vegan, so I would assume not.I highly recommend this tasty, healthy snack!

Typical of granola snacks, this one packs quite a punch - in terms calories from fat (50 per serving). But it also packs a very generous flavor profile.  The cocoa clearly overpowers any of the almond (barely discernible) or cinnamon (very muted) in the granola - but the natural cocoa as opposed to the corn-syrup laden chocolate 'flavor' used in many brands clearly is a treat.  Paired with chai or even milk, this is a very good occasional snack. The favorite use in this household has been with plain or vanilla Greek yogurt.  Given the unique flavor, natural ingredients used the price/value is reasonable.  But due to the relatively high amount of calories from fat, this is at best an occasional snack paired with fruits/yogurt...

column9: Cinnamon Almond goodness with a balanced flavor
column10: This is bite-size granola in a package that can be eaten a few at a time as a snack. Each package is 12 oz. and there are ten 1.2 ounce servings in each bag. Each serving is 160 calories with 50 calories from fat. There are 3 grams of protein and 12 grams of sugar in each serving. Each serving also constitutes  a daily dietary intake 12% in fiber and 8%. The first three ingredients are whole grain rolled oats, brown sugar, and palm oil.  Almonds are 4th on the ingredient list with cinnamon listed as the 8th ingredient.I am use to eating my granola with milk so this was a new twist on a what was formally a cerael.  I felt these were dry but they tasted really good. Drinking a glass of milk took away most of the dryness. There was a strong cocoa flavor and a not too strong cinnamon flavor. I didn't taste the almonds at all.  However, despite the "cinnamon almond" being low on the ingredients list, I felt these granola bites had a very balanced flavor that made me want more.Obviously granola is a high calorie snack and it's hard to eat just 1.2 ounces, especially of this flavor. Nevertheless, I feel it's much better to eat this than candy and cake.  Although this flavor is very good and very balanced,  after having tried this as a snack,  I would probably not purchase these because of the dryness.  However, I've been eating these for a couple of days and have discovered that putting these clusters in a salad takes away the dryness and gives the salad a nice crunch (like croutons) in addition to adding additional flavor.I had my boyfriend try these and he likes them.

I like these tasty clusters.  They're quick and easy.  I like to eat them out of the bag, though somebody wanting a "cereal" could put them in a bowl with milk.  I also like that a serving (1/3 cup) has 3g fiber.I marked these down a star because my husband thinks they taste too chocolatey.  However, I think these clusters have the perfect amount of cocoa.

Eat Think Smile Cinnamon Almond Granola Clusters is a tasty snack that I enjoyed quite a bit.  It's not exactly health food, but I don't think there would be an issue in enjoying this treat in moderation.Eat Think Smile Cinnamon Almond Granola Clusters are made up of large granola clusters, too big to be eaten easily as a breakfast cereal but just the right size for snacking.  The most obvious ingredients are oats, almond bits, cocoa, and cinnamon.  Neither the cocoa or cinnamon taste is overpowering at all, and I found that the combination of these two tastes was much better than I would have expected.Now as I mentioned above I would not consider this product health food, despite the claims on the package about the antioxidant power of the cocoa and cinnamon.  After all, a small serving contains 6 grams of fat and 12 grams of sugar, and among the ingredients listed are brown sugar, palm oil, and evaporated sugar cane juice.  But as a substitute for more highly processed sweets this will do OK.  Overall I am a fan of Eat Think Smile Cinnamon Almond Granola Clusters and would likely buy it in the future.

Eat, think smile granola (Cinnamon Almond)are a very tasty snack although a buyer should be aware this product has cocoa in it and is chocolate based.  The clusters have a somewhat decadent taste and I would say a little goes a long way which is good since these are packed with calories and sugars.  I've tried them with milk and they actually taste better as a cereal.The package comes with a resealable ziplock fastener convenient for keeping the granola fresh.  Like most granola, the bigger clusters float at the top of the package and the bits and pieces end up at the bottom.  The clusters are big enough to hand individual pieces to kids are almost the size of small Halloween candy.

Granola isn't necessarily what I would call a health food.  Many mass produced brands have rather high amounts of sugar per serving size, and as someone that is watching her weight, it isn't necessarily a snack I choose for myself.  BUT, I won't deny to enjoying it!  I love the crunch, the sweet taste of the oats and the nuts-YUMMY!This isn't a cereal, which is how I usually prefer to eat my granola, but rather a snack.  And what a snack it is!  The taste of chocolate is rather overwhelming in some other brands, but this one was just right.  I liked that it seemed to have more of the bitterness of darker chocolate going for it, rather than the sweetness of milk chocolate.I will say the one drawback for me...it's hard!  As in, no one in my family wanted to use their front teeth to bite into it, choosing instead to use our stronger back teeth, but again it's granola so what did I expect?The price for this, if it follows the companies other flavors of granola clusters is pretty much standard for this product. $21.78 for 6 6 ounce bags. Actually, that's about $3.83 a bag, cheaper than many products on the market now.This is a good snack, though not one I would eat often as I mentioned I am trying to watch my weight, but my boys loved it!

I will admit I'm not a regular eater of granola (and I don't count those marketed-for-kids bars I got in my lunchbox when I was a kid). However, I really like this product.Basically, they are small clusters (almost like small cookies) of granola and almonds, coated with a "chocolatey" (think cocoa krispies) flavor and tinged with cinnamon.They are not chewy or moist, but granola's not really supposed to be. But it's not like you are going to break your teeth on them or anything. I like to eat them by the handful- they are a great on-to-go kinda of snack, when you don't want to deal with crumbs or packaging. I grab a handful every few hours to munch on. I find myself eating these by the handful throughout the day when I want something sweet and crunchy but don't want to sit down to a meal, and I eat a few to fuel me up before I go for my daily swim. It's sort of replaced my bad Pretzel M&M habit, which is a very good thing.I suppose you could pour them into a bowl and eat them like cereal, but the cluster are a little bit large for that. They seem like a good snack food to me.I'll admit- for the calories and fat, I'd *rather* eat something else (I'm a big fan of chewy and moist things), but then again, who wouldn't choose a soft cookie over a cluster of granola with all natural ingredients? However, there's quite a bit of nutrition in granola, and the ingredients are really healthy, much better than you would get in some processed product on the grocery shelf.I LOVE the bags these come in- resealable coated paper sacks. They keep the product fresh (the seal actually RESEALS!) and are easy to grab on the go.I'm not a granola convert yet, but these are definitely making me re-think my aversion to granola.

This product works best as a snack as the pieces are cut rather large. I thought it would work as a cereal, but the pieces are too big. The thing that surprised me is that it appears to be mostly a cocoa product, by the color, anyway. Looking at it, I see cocoa, but the taste does say cinnamon. Kind of a conflicted product, to me.The taste is not too sweet, but the crunchiness seems a bit low, almost like it is going stale. I don't think I got a stale bag, but it doesn't crunch as much as I'd like in a granola. Overall, I'm not real impressed. It's ok, but not significantly different than other granola options.

I just received my order.  Big box for 2 ounces of chocolate.  But I find it is all protected and cool inside a thermal container.  So that's why the shipping and handling cost more than the chocolates.  Okay.  Get through that and there is a little box with five little pieces of chocolate.  They must be pretty special and pretty hot I imagine.  So get a glass of water handy and pop one of the more than $5 each little pieces in the mouth.  Wait.  Those ghost chilis will kick in soon and set my mouth on fire... Right?  Nope.  Not that good a chocolate.  And no ghost chili kick.  I could get a good chocolate bar with real chili you can taste for about $1 at world market.  Oh well.  So it's all a learning experience.  I learned that the ingredients on the container actually says that somewhere in there they sprinkled some dried ghost peppers in there.  If you want to impress someone by telling them you ate ghost chili chocolate, but you can't take the heat of real chili, then this might be the way to go.  But I wouldn't waste my money.  Unfortunately there were no reviews for me.  But now you have one.  Extremely disappointed.

column9: Tasty with lots of fiber--I recommend it
column10: Needing to increase my daily fiber intake but not always able to ingest vegetables and whole grain breads to suffice, I looked around for a cereal to help. A couple years ago I came across Fiber One. I began with the Original Fiber One w/ Honey Clusters and was very pleased that they tasted good. When the raisin bran version of Fiber One came out, I jumped on it. With less sugar than typical raisin bran cereals and a LOT more fiber, I begin every morning with a nice bowl of this stuff. I usually add a sliced banana or fresh strawberries, but that's only because I just HAVE to have such fruit in my cereal--just an idiosyncratic thing, I guess.One thing to note--the typical serving that these cereals refer to when they indicate the % of RDAs is a rather small bowl. The cereal bowl I use takes way more than 4 ounces. I'd say that my cereal bowl, which is of average size, is about 6 to 8 ounces of cereal. Consequently, the % of daily fiber I get from Fiber One Raisin Bran Clusters comes to 65 to 86% of my daily needs, which is great. This one bowl of cereal provides for almost all of my daily required fiber. I can tell, too, because on days I have this, my (sorry to get rather detailed, but hey, Dr. Oz talked like this on Oprah once) bowel movements are what they're supposed to be. Without this they're more indicative of liquid slop. LOL

Look up "fiber one" and "Chicory root extract", also known as inulin.I had a few Fiber One bars at a conference a few years ago, and I was out of commission for several days, ruining my conference.  This past week, my wife bought me the Fiber One raisin bran.  I normally eat regular Fiber One and mix it with another cereal to give it some flavor, and I've never had problems with Fiber One cereal in the past.  Not so with the raisin bran, which unlike regular Fiber One, contains chicory root extract (aka inulin).The stomach cramps this weekend were killing me, and I thought I had food poisoning.  It was only after reading the ingredients this morning (monday) that I realized it was the chicory root in the Fiber One raisin bran cereal.  I can't believe the FDA allows this as an ingredient.[...]

He did not like the Lucky Charms, Cinnamon Toast Crunch, etc. my other kids were eating for breakfast. He also did not care for the Granola or the Post Raisin Bran I purchased.I ran into my youngest son's wrestling coach in the cereal aisle one afternoon, and he recommended this one. Jackpot! My temporary son loved this stuff. Come to find out, so did my husband. The flakes are crispier and have a sweet coating in comparison to the raisin bran you may be used to. It doesn't get mushy in milk for quite a long time. The fiber content is excellent, and you can find this even at my small local grocery store.Once I spotted this on Amazon with subscribe and save, I jumped to order it. The price at my grocery is $4.39 per box, so this was a nice little savings for us. Four boxes arrive each month right at our font door via UPS.I recommend giving this one a try. We all know the buzz about fiber, and this has lots of it. It also tastes really good. Not always an easy combo to find.

column9: the best raisin bran around--but it comes at a price
column10: Fiber One Raisin Bran Clusters are, simply put, delicious. Fiber One took a great type of cereal and made it taste much, much better than the other Raisin Bran cereals out there. In addition, this cereal is truly chock full of dietary fiber. It tastes great in milk and it even makes a good snack for when you're "on the go."In addition, the cereal has potassium, iron and zero cholesterol. Excellent!Unfortunately, however, all this goodness comes at a price. There's a lot of dietary fiber; but this also contains a comparatively level of carbohydrates in each portion. Perhaps you think that 45 grams of carbs per cup is OK; and maybe it is if you don't have a diet filled with carbs the rest of your day. Compare it to Cheerios or Quaker Oats, however, and you'll see right away you can get other healthy cereals that are quite good for you with far fewer carbs and much less sugar. Oatmeal has good dietary fiber, too, although not as much as this cereal has.Overall, Fiber One Raisin Bran is probably the best raisin bran cereal I've ever eaten. It's great; but because of certain health issues I wouldn't actually eat this every day unless you need carbs for some reason. It's a mixed bag type of product. Eat this and enjoy it; but also switch off between this and other healthy cereals like Cheerios and Quaker Oats.

column9: Best cheese curls - UPDATED: overpriced and poor quality
column10: I won't say I'm an expert in cheese curls, but these sure taste great. Slightly milky flavor, and a touch of blue cheese give these an edge (literally and figuratively) over the competition. It's great that part of the ingredients are organic (I wish of course that they were all organic at this price). Don't be surprised when you open the bag, they fill just under a third of it. I guess the empty space keeps them in shape! Now the bad part, when you buy 12 at once you expect a discount. The Amazon price of $2.58 each is the same as at my local high priced natural food store. Still, nobody comes close flavor wise, although flavor is, of course, subjective.UPDATE December 11, 2009Could I have been more disappointed with the makers of Cheese Curls? I stopped buying the baked cheese puffs from the same brand because the quality varies from one batch (by the expiration date) to another, and the last batch had too many puffs without cheese. Back to the curls, the previous batch (November) was just excellent (good flavor and crispiness as reported by my wife), but then came the one I bought just a week ago...there is not a single curl with proper cheese flavor in the bags. So why not complain? I am complaining, but the company doesn't care. I told them last year that the quality of the puffs varied from one batch to another, and it only got worse. The retail price has increased to $2.95 since then. At that price I expect a very good product, especially when I buy 12 at a time. Notice that it says on the back of the bag "freshness guaranteed." That's right, they don't care whether we're happy with the product, just that it's fresh. Thanks Michael Seasons, I guess I'll have to start making my own cheese curls (there is no other product on the market that uses (partially) organic ingredients). I'd give this one star today if I could.

Several years ago, I went on a tour of the Celestial Seasonings tea factory in Boulder, Colorado.  The guide showed us the bales of tea as they arrived, machines that ground and mixed the tea, and a machine that put the tea in tea bags.  The tour included a visit to the room where the peppermint tea was stored.  Our guide told us that peppermint was stored separately so that it would not contaminate the other teas.  He did not tell us what was to come.The doorway into the peppermint room was surrounded by bright red stripes. This should have served as a warning to us.  We all innocently strolled into the peppermint room.  The smell of peppermint was overpowering.  It entered my nose, my head, my lungs, and then my whole being was infused with peppermint.  What a rush!  The crowd stampeded out of the room in a hurry.  For the rest of the day and into the next, all I could smell and taste was the mint.I am now addicted to Celestial Seasonings Peppermint Tea.  Every time I have some, I am reminded of that fateful day in Boulder.  The events of that day have changed my life forever.  Amazingly, the tea is still legal, openly sold in stores and on the Internet.  I think that the tea is great, but then again I am not an unbiased observer.  On your next visit to Boulder, take the tour.  Or go a safer route; buy the tea from Amazon.

Gunpowder tea is green tea, most of which comes from a city named Pingshui in the Eastern Chinese province of Zhejiang, south of the Yangtse River Delta, where it has been cultivated for centuries and is known as the "green pearl" of tea. Pingshui tea market records date as far back as the Tang Dynasty (AD 618 - 907). The area's gunpowder tea was an important tribute traditionally given to the Chinese emperors; and with the growing trade volume between China and the West it also acquired an increasing number of lovers in Europe. Particularly during the second half of the 19th century, when gunpowder tea export reached its peak, its price on the London market was second only to then-popular Wu Yi Oolong (also from China). Even today, Zhejiang Province still proudly calls itself "home of silk and tea" for its two primary natural products.The name "gunpowder" derives from the tea's elaborate method of processing, which traditionally lasts several hours and during which the tea leaves are withered, steamed or stir-fried and individually rolled into small pellets. Early foreign traders mistook these pellets for gunpowder or gunshot.Gunpowder tea has a delicate aroma with a slightly smokey note. It should *always* be enjoyed without milk or cream.

I make no claim to being a tea expert. I simply like to drink tea. This one makes a nice change. The flavor is gently smokey and smooth; one could call it lapsang for beginners :-). column9: TRICLOPYR is what you need for POISON IVY...
column10: This contains Triclopyr, which is more aggressive than Glyphosate.  It is also more persistent which means that you don't want to spray it close to plants you value.Triclopyr is what you need to knock out Poison Ivy. Poison Ivy and a lot of other shrubs or trees can take a swig of Glyphosate (Round Up), gargle twice with it and spit it back into your face just for giggles.  I've used this and the Ortho Brush-B-Gon.  They contain the same active ingredient and I haven't observed any significant difference.This stuff is the real deal - I found it when I was trying to locate a product called Vine-X (discontinued?) and found out that it was 13.6% Triclopyr in a penetrating oil.  You simply brush it onto cuts or active vines and it would kill the entire plant.This is where it is really nice to buy the concentrate instead of the pre-mix.  I spray the diluted version but also use the concentrate in a small bottle.  If I cut a thicker vine or trunk, I simply drip the concentrate on it and it will kill the roots and vine.  Besides PI we also have wild grapevine, Buckthorn, Box Elder, and many other invasive and nuisance plans in the woods.Because Poison Ivy is a creeping vine with multiple roots along it's length, eradication is helped with a higher concentration than the label instructs. (My observation) I use it between 50% to 100% (double) strength.It appears that if you spray it in one spot you will kill that part of the vine, but if you hit it (in enough places) with something strong enough you can kill the whole plant down to the roots.Make sure you spray it when you think it won't rain for at least a couple of days or else you will probably need to spray it again. Make sure you get all "sprouts." From extensive hand pulling, My observation is that for every "sprout" there is another ~3 feet of vine lurking around and another sprout hiding somewhere nearby.If you've found this review helpful please let me know!

column9: Great for vines and small trees
column10: Had vines that were taking over. They were creeping / had buried roots growing horizontally, which can complicate killing them. Sometimes if the vine (or root or base of tree or shrub) is really thick, it can take more than one application. (It's best to apply the product to a fresh cut.) In order to apply it twice or three times, you want to leave enough length so that you can make the cut again. This stuff is strong, so don't get me wrong. But, for really large diameters, leave yourself some extra in case you have to come back.I've used this on oak trees too. Just cut the sapling down to size and spritz the stub. If anything grows back, you can spray the leaves or make a fresh cut. Eventually when enough of the root is destroyed, it will not grow back.Great product. Would buy again.

column9: Too weak to be called a concentrate

Also the description calls this a  "concentrate" yet there is no information about how much working solution this so-called concentrate makes.  The description also says "convenient no mix formula" which implies it is used right out of the bottle so it can't be a concentrate.  Again Mr. Wu says he uses 50 to 100% stronger mix, but this can't be a description of this product since it is a no mix formula and any mixing would reduce the concentration, i.e., there is no way to make it stronger.  It appears that Mr. Wu has pasted his description of another product into the space for this one and that is not helpful.  So it appears that this is NOT a concentrate, but a ready to use solution that is less than 1%.  Very misleading.
