column9: This is a very good salt-to-your-taste product
column10: Most people are accustomed to a fairly high-sodium diet (>2500mg).  It is everywhere and in places you wouldn't suspect.  For someone like me who has to pay attention to sodium because it spikes my blood pressure, this was a great find.  This product has no added salt/sodium.  As such, many will find it bland if they don't add a little salt (the cooking instructions do say "salt to taste").  Being used to not using salt in cooking, I found it tasty enough without adding salt.  For salt-sensitive folks, this is a great product.

column9: Excellent if you add a few easy ingredients
column10: I didn't realize at first this product has zero salt in it.  I neglected to read the package directions.  After experimenting a bit, I've found this tastes amazing when you add salt to taste, about 1/4-1/2 cup light cream, about 1/2 cup water and 1/2 stick real butter to every two pouches of sauce.  I add previously cooked chicken breast meat and simmer to warm through. Serve over basmati rice and YUM...quick and easy dinner.  Sure, it's not low fat, but it tastes very close to what I have had in Indian restaurants.  I have also made it with a vegetarian soy chicken called "FriChik" and it tastes great too.

I feel like I have a pretty good palette for Indian food, especially curry. While I'm no means an expert, I lived in London for awhile and sampled some of the best curry while also knowing you can find great flavors in local spots in metropolitan cities.As such and now that I'm back in a suburb, I really just wanted something that would satisfy my craving for a Tikka Masala-type curry that I can throw veggies and chicken into.This isn't it. While it's not horrible, there just isn't much flavor. There seems to be a lack of cocunut milk to give it a hint of sweetness and the cloves that are usually added to balance out the colors seems watered down. I say skip.

With the special deal going on through September 2010, I got these for a little over $1 a piece. The spicing was not the best I've had, and feel the Kitchen's of India, Patak's and Tiger Tiger make better pastes for Indian cooking.

I bought it hoping for a restaurant alternative. But, pay the extra money to go out, this isn't worth it. I cut the water in half and it was still watery and VERY bland. Its boring and not very Indian tasting.

column9: A little bland, but otherwise lovely!
column10: We cut the water added in half and added chili powder and some paprika to spice it up, but the sauce was a great base!

I was hopeful that Tasty Bite would be a nice, easy home alternative to expensive Indian food but it wasn't. The sauces are bland and boring. The Rogan Josh is equally unexciting. I added a lot of additional spices and other ingredients to both in order to get a decent sauce. I guess you could call it a workable Indian sauce base, but that's about it.
Tasty Bite Tikka Masala is a great alternative when I can't get out for Indian food.  I add my own meat and vegetables and a little yogurt or sour cream and serve it over rice or mashed potatoes.

column9: Take a pass people --- watery thin sauce, little flavor, yuk!
column10: This is the most bland boring sauce I've had the misfortune to encounter. It's not the salt (though certainly that's a piece of the puzzle) but the sauce itself tastes very watered down and with just a hint of any spice. And the only spice to taste is a little bit of pepper. That's it. It distinctly lacks in any sort of flavor. Indian flood is very flavorful (usually) so that pretty much makes this one a pass completely.Don't bother. Find a good Indian recipe on the net and make your own or find a good Indian buffet.

This simmer sauce wasn't what I expected. I made Chicken Tikka Masala with this sauce for my roommates. It didn't thicken like I had expected and had more of a curry flavor than a tomato flavor. I used to order this dish from my local Indian eatery, and this just didn't compare. It wasn't awful but it wasn't what I was looking for and I won't order it again.

This product has a nice flavor but I was hoping that the sauce would be thicker. It was probably wishful thinking on my part to expect it to be similar to what I can find at a good Pakistani/Indian restaurant.

we cooked this and to our disappointment its not the typical thick creamy sauce but some watery blackish sauce, or they left something out of the directions like adding yogurt or something. Id say it rates a 0

If purchased from Spicelab,  this product is much beefier than the photo would lead you to believe. Very solid and heavy.  Shipped rough cut.  After rinsing with water the salt block polishes up and looks even better. For the idiots out there,  don't soak in water,  it will disappear.  A nice short rince and pat dry cleans it up easily.

How cool is this?  It's a 10 on my scale.  You get this block of salt that's possibly millions of years old.  Yeah, I know salt is everywhere but a brick of pink salt is just too cool for words.  I figure on using it as a serving surface for a while and then recycling it in my mortar and pestle when the time comes.  If you are reading this then you know it's not anything close to a need-to-have item but it's a luxury that I'm happy to own.  I bought 4 of these and will probably buy a 4 more.  The Z-Shop seller that sells them for half the price is not selling what is pictured; rather, they are selling 8"x4"x2" bricks and not 8"x8"x1" salt plates.  (They're still pretty cool too!)
Good product had a problem with order wrote a review.I was contacted by seller problem resolved within two days.I am truly pleased with the fast response from seller.
It is Himalayan Pink Sea Salt... but it is a BRICK. Literally. No where near the 1" square shown in the image. More like 6"x4"x3"Not sure if this will heat the same way.

This is a nice salt block, but beware that the dimensions are not listed.  IT IS SMALL!!!  I thought it would be like the nice large blocks you see in Williams Sonoma that are a few feet wide.  This one is a little bigger than the actual photo (it's small!!!).  Kind of feel ripped off since I was expecting a thinnger flatter blick like the one in the photo, not a small super super super thick block like I got.

Buyer Beware!!!!!  I ordered two of these back in April 2008, I never received them and my e-mails were promptly ignored--when I contacted a salesman in august--I got lots of flowery words with a promise to double my order and have seen nothing--fortunately I purchased it through Amazon and they refunded my money.

We fell in love with this dressing a couple of years ago.  Its great on a taco salad or with a grilled chicken or sausage.  My hubby says it goes with almost any salad.  Our new local grocery does not carry it and we are so bummed.  We love it so much that we will order it in bulk with zero fear.  We will easily use 12 bottles in a couple of months. :)

Used to get these in the mid-80's while stationed in Japan. The 2006 packaging is exactly the same!! I love to pop one in my mouth while keeping a straight face and offer one to an unsuspecting victim...  The sour part is pretty awful, but the lemon candy underneath is quite tasty.

For those of us Sour Candy aficionados this is about as good as it gets.  It is a shame that the initial sour blast goes away so soon and all you are left with is a boring old lemon drop.  It has an advantage over the Warheads mega sour candy because the sourness tastes distinctly like lemon and does not have the chemical undertones that the Warheads do.  In addition the lemon drop is better than the pathetic candy that you are left with when the sour part of a warhead is finished.

First off, my 4-star rating is for people who WANT an extremely sour candy.  On a more objective scale this candy would easily rank zero or one stars.  I have heard this described as "disgusting stuff" and for most people, this would surely be the case.Nobel Super Lemon is often cited as "the most sour candy in the world," so it seemed like the ideal gift for my old boss -- who loves sour candy and has impossible standards.  He thought it was adequately sour, but he claims to have eaten candies that are stronger.  I'm less of a sour-candy fanatic, and found it to be extremely sour.  It makes my saliva glands sore and I wince in intense discomfort.  My mouth is instantly flooded with drool and my speech is impaired for a short while.All candies of this type appear to be normal hard candies with a thin layer of sour dust on them.  This means, of course, that the extreme sourness only lasts a few seconds before you are sucking on a generic lemon-flavored hard candy.Comparing this to other extremely sour candies I've tried, however, I can't say that this one is obviously any more sour.  Mega Warheads are about the same.  However, if you've tried Tearjerkers Extra Sour Gum, this definitely goes a step beyond that.  Skittles and other "tangy" fruit candy would not be considered sour at all in comparison.For people in North America, Mega Warheads are basically the same product, but at a better value.  Mega Warheads also come in a package with candies of different flavors, making for a marginally more interesting product.

column9: Not as sour as they say
column10: I ordered these from the internet after reading a review on how sour these were.  After the first 10-15 sec its gone and its just a regular lemon head, i would rank the sourness about a 7 on a 1 - 10 scale.

column9: A good, if unremarkable lemon candy
column10: These are coated with a fine, super-sour 'Warheads'-type of powder (ascorbic, citric and malic acids I belive)that once gone, reveals a pleasant, if unremarkable lemon candy. I agree with Shervyn below that the sour coating has a less chemical flavor than domestic Warheads brand, making them 'better'.They are good, but their (relatively) high price makes them a "Glad I tried them, won't bother again" item for me. YMMV.

These candies are very good - super sour for the first 10 to 15 seconds and then a nice lemon flavored hard candy after that.  My problem is the price - $7.99 for a 2.6 ounce bag.  Too much, in my opinion.

These babies are very sour!  Albeit, the sour coating disappears quickly leaving you with a sweet lemon drop.  The first time I put one in my mouth, I think it put hair on my chest.  I was not expecting such a sour taste, and I had never tasted something quite that sour before.  As another reviewer stated, these candies are great for surprising others.  I have given them out and watched guests spit them out across the room because they were not expecting the initial sour bite.  Even so, they are surprisingly addictive for me.  I get these from a local Japanese grocery for much cheaper than Amazon offers them (even before shipping costs).  If you like sour/bitter lemon, then these candies are the ones for you, with no chemical aftertaste at all.

I found this in chinatown next to the White Rabbit candy and thought I'dgive it a try. Wow! I love it and so do my co-workers. the only reasonI gave it 4 and not 5 stars is that it makes the roof of my mouth hurtbut I thinks it's because I pop 2 at a time.

column4: B. Eckert "I don't know how to quit AMZN"
column9: Better than a kick in the teeth
column10: My Brother introduced these to me about fifteen years- he found them originally in Hawaii.Although a large part of this candy is the novelty (the initial sour flavor is awful), there is a pretty good candy underneath. I doubt they will ever take the candy world by storm, but they are at least worth a try (and the packaging is awesome).
This is a good seasoning. My son really likes it but I find it a bit too fishy. I prefer the salmon & the wasabi flavors. The little glass jar makes a really cute juice glass.

I loved this syrup it was so yummy. I used it to make mango green tea bubble tea and other random fruity drinks. I'll definitely be buying this product line again.I do have a rather large sweet tooth, so I didn't find this overly sweet, but a few of my friends who do not eat sweets often said it was rather sweet. That can just be adjusted by the amount of syrup added.

column9: beats the jars in my opiniom
column10: very satisfied!  bought right after the jars and my conclusion is this product is my preference by far longer more robust sprouts seems as though you harvest twice as many.  I believe the amount of oxygen available versus the jars is the advantage of the hemp sprout bag.  I most definitely recommend this product.
This is similar to Nutella.  The flavor is slightly milder, but the texture is smoother and it is much easier to spread.

I have bought this Planter's mix several times and love the blend of sweet and salty crunch.  The nuts are big and whole, and the chocolate covered soybeans are just enough to satisfy a sweet craving.  I use this mix as a snack for myself - a great source of protein, too.

So, so bummed that they changed their formula.  I couldn't figure out what was different, but they must have stopped honeyroasting the mix.  Or changed the pretzel sticks they were using or something.  It's too bland for me now.  Boo!  At first I thought it was the batch I bought, but after the third can I realize they've definitely changed something up.  So sad.  Won't be eating this for snack anymore.  :(

Probably not the healthiest in the NUTrition lineup on account of the chocolate-covered and honey-roasted pieces. Nonetheless, it makes an ideal snack when you're looking for something reasonably nutritious with pronounced flavor (i.e. not "light" fare).

column9: Love it! Love it! Love It!
column10: I love this mix.  It is just the right mix of nut. I do not find myself picking anything out as I do with most mixes.  This is a great snack and is high in protein.

Can't find this item out West where I live, although have all the others in the new Nut-rition line.  Had a can of it back East and had to find it again.  Wonderful mixture of sesame, nuts, chocolate coated soy ball for a combination of sweet, salt, nutty, crunch, soft chocolate--a surprise in every bite.  Love it!  Actually addicting...

The Planters NUTrition Energy Mix is an excellent 'pick me up' during the workday. It can give you a quick burst of energy when you don't have time for lunch. It is an easy to eat snack that comes in a smaller can that doesn't take a lot of space on your desk.

I loved this mix when it still contained the sesame sticks. It was the perfect blend of salty, sweet and savory. Planters has recently changed the mixture, replacing the deliciously addictive sesame sticks with bland, nubby wheat pretzel sticks - quite possibly the worst pretzel sticks I've ever had. I didn't realize the formula had changed until I opened a can I bought yesterday and discovered the gross replacement pretzels. I don't know if it's the case with every can, but in the can I purchased the pretzels made up 1/2 the can's contents. I won't be purchasing this product anymore due to the formula change. The sesame sticks were perfect, the pretzels are anything but.

column9: Warning Added sugar and color additives
column10: According to [...] -- this has color additives and added sugars.Ingredients list: Almonds, Candy Coated Dark Chocolate Soynuts (Dark Chocolate [Sugar, Chocolate, Cocoa Butter], Oil Roasted Soybeans [Soybeans, Soybean Oil], Artificial Color [Includes Caramel Color], Corn Syrup, Gum Arabic, Confectioner's Glaze [Carnauba Wax, Beeswax]), Peanuts, Whole Wheat Pretzels (Whole Wheat Flour, Water, Soybean or Canola or Corn Oils, Malt Syrup [Contains Corn and Barley]), Walnuts, Pecans, Sugar, Peanut and/or Cottonseed Oil, Honey, Corn Syrup, Sea Salt, Xanthan Gum.

I like that this mix is **very** lightly sweet and salted (note, maybe too bland for some people). Not sure if the mix, or the can I got, but there were A LOT of almonds and pretzel sticks in mine. I have sensitive teeth so it was not a pleasant experience as I had to leave it in my mouth to soften before I could chew. I give it 3 stars for freshness and quality.

This is another combination by Planters that I like to have on hand in my office for clients to munch on if they come in hungry. It's also nice for my administrative assistant and me if we're fading fast (!) and can't get away for something to eat. Much better for us than cookies or the like.

column9: Loved the previous honey roasted mixture with sesame sticks!
column10: For years I have bought the Energy mix ...and had to stop myself at 3 cans per shopping trip. I do not like the new formula containing  pretzels instead of sesame sticks.  Please go back to the former recipe.  It was a wonderful, great snack - perfect in every way and I advertized the product by enthusiastically sharing with others!! I won't be buying any more unless I see the sesame sticks on the picture label!
Very good the first 2 deliveries  BUTthe last one was stale...doubt if I will order again

column9: Love This Stuff - Crunch, Sweetness, a Little Salt
column10: This satisfies all the cravings and has a crisp texture - but not too hard. Excellent flavor. I tried this after the Digestive mix, but like this so much better. It's a regular purchase now.Other mixes have too many peanuts or taste stale - this is awesome in quality and flavor - so give it a try.
Best one of the Planter's NUT-rition I've had. The chocolate and sesame sticks are amazing. I bought the 3-Pack for a party and it was gone in an hour.

The nuts were excellent as usual but the chocolateon the soy nuts had melted during shipping so bigchunks of nuts were all stuck together.They nuts were edible but I'd like to suggest thatthey be shipped refigerated in the future.
The delivery date changed a couple times (both were later than what was originally promised).  And then actual delivery was a day or two later than the last estimate.

I have no children, well I do but they are grown. This was suggested by my dog's vet, the Pumpkin settles their stomach and the apple is just a bonus but she gets a couple tablespoons mixed in her food and she loves it. Yes, I know SPOILED.

column9: Grandson not crazy about the taste
column10: My 7-month old grandson did not particularly care for this item.  It contains onions and that is new for him.  He may acquire a taste for it a little later on, but for now we'll stick with the green beans & rice.

My Daughters love the pumpkin apple! They've been eating it since they started on baby food. Now at 2.5, they still love it! I put a dash of apple pie spices in it and they eat it with a spoon like apple sauce and on pancakes/waffles instead of syrup!
My little one loves this combo!  Fair warning though, it seems to be a bit of a laxative!  :)

My daughter tends to prefer sweeter foods and I have a hard time getting her to eat an entire jar of anything in one sitting, but she will eat this without complaint.  She has her little mouth open for the next spoonful before I can get it to her, so I know she likes it!  A good option for picky babies.

column9: My Babies Did Not Appreciate This One.  Yet It Introduces Them to Onions
column10: I gave this product four stars because on the fourth feeding, my 10-month old twins ate it without complaining even though they were unenthusiastic.  They disliked it the first two times so much that they refused to eat it.I feel that at least they were introduced to new foods that they'll probably like when they're a bit older.When I purchased this item, I was unaware it doesn't have anything sweet like all the other Earth Best flavor brands I've purchased.  Others have carrots, for example, and my babies like that.The ingredients for this brand are as follows: "Organic Green Beans, Water, Organic Whole Wheat Flour, Organic Roasted Onions."Roasted Onions - what was I thinking?  At least they weren't raw onions.  No wonder they wouldn't eat this on the first attempts.In the end, I'm glad I purchased this product because my babies tried onions and new foods, and this may be a natural way to introduce such foods starting at an early age.

I wouldn't say that my son's a picky eater, but he definitely has his preferences.  He's just turning six months old now, but at our pediatrician's suggestion we started him on solid food on the earlier side (four months).  A couple of weeks ago, he transitioned from "first" foods (pears, apples, and other single-note wonders) to "second" foods like this one.  Although he's generally willing to try new foods, his responses usually range from "I guess I'll eat it" to "I might eat it if I'm desperate" to "I'd rather starve."  The Earth's Best "Creamy Apple Chicken Compote" fell into that last category.  To be honest, I tried it, too--sometimes it motivates him when he sees you eating it, and liking it--and it was fairly foul.But since he's big for his age (already in 9 and 12 month sizes) and growing quickly, it's important that he get enough protein--which means that, really, we can't so much give into temptation and be like, "fine, eat applesauce."  And it's been a challenge finding high-protein foods that he likes and will reliably eat.  BUT HE LOVES THIS STUFF!!!  He'll eat it morning, noon and night.  He'll eat it when the house is quiet; he'll eat it amidst distraction.  He'll eat it while the television's on; he'll eat it while the cat is staring at him.The Amazon price isn't, you know, earth shattering, unless you live in the Boston area and your only other source of organic baby food is Whole Foods.  In which case this is about half price.  We've started buying it by the case.
I bought these for the holiday season. My son just loves it. The texture is different but he did not mind that.

This is an excellent flavor.  I make a habit of trying a small portion of whatever food I give my son.  This one tastes like pumpkin pie and my son also loves it!  It is a bit runnier than other varieties, but otherwise I love this one.

I don't know how everyone else got these broken, but when I received them they came wrapped in plastic and in bubble wrap, not a single jar was broken.  My son loves them and the price was great and I had no issues at all.
My son really likes this baby food. Most of the foods with meat or poultry are quite disgusting. This one has a terrific smell and a really good taste.

my son loves this variety.  i had a hard time fiding it at stores, and with amazon mom it costs a lot less here.  the smell is sweet, the consistancy is smooth, and he loves the taste.  very good blend.

My son absolutely LOVES this food.  He's 8 months and we picked up a few jars and he can't get enough of them.  They taste delicious and they smell wonderful too... not like some of the other pasty baby foods he's tried before.  Two thumbs up!

I purchase Earth's Best baby foods for my GrandSon.  He loves it, perferring it above all other baby foods his mom buys for him.  I am confident that he is getting quality organic foods to begin his life.  Amazon delivers right to his door within two days of ordering.  How easy is that??

column9: Great Food at a Great Price!!

I love her to death but with a baby on the way I feel there are more important things to spend that money on but this dog food seems to have quality ingredients at a good price. The fact that it's American made was also something I really liked.

I really hate to write a review in fear of Hi-Tek boosting their affordable prices on their dog food. My dog loves this food, no issues, and even has stinky firm stools to prove it. My dogs (all four of them) love this food...even my 13-year old Pomeranian who gave up hard kibble a couple of years ago will munch at the bowl every now and again. Thank you for making a product that my dogs love and I feel good about feeding it to them :)
My dogs enjoy this high quality food. Read about the ingredients, they are the best! No digestive problems, happy healthy dogs. A good price too.
The product is great, but due to the price doubling, will not be purchasing anymore.  Very unfortunate situation.  My dogs did very well on this food.

At first I wasnt sure when trying this but the people at Savannah Bee company told be to try it with green apples, a slice of aged shedar and a slice of the honeycomb. It was amazing!!! All very natural foods, if you have never tried this, you need to try it, it is so good! Great hit at parties!

column9: Best canned tomatoes for pizza sauce I have tried.

column9: Tastes great, very healthy, and reasonable priced!
column10: We love the four bean soup mix.  It is easy to make, high in all nutrients, and extremely reasonably priced through Amazon.  It is tasty and easy to make just following the directions.  I also use it as a base for my own variations.  Adding a cup or two of water, and addtional barley, split peas, and lentils, fresh diced onion, choped carrot, and minced garlic makes it even heartier and more abundant.

column9: I can't believe I like this so much...
column10: I don't mind sweeter wines like a Riesling, but I don't usually go so much for fruit flavored wines like this, but this wine has changed my mind. This is a great summer sipper or party wine. Actually more of a gulper. It's so light and smooth, that you'll end up going through a bottle before you know it. So be warned...You might feel something cold on your face and you look up, and it's the floor. I'm just saying.Now for the technical stuff:I reconstituted this one to somewhere between 5 1/2 and 6 gallons. I meant to make a little less, but messed up. At that level it came out to a little less than 9% ABV, which I think is a little light. I would recommend reconstituting it closer to 5 gallons, because I believe it can handle the extra alcohol without affecting its drinkability. Ideally I'd say measure the specific gravity as you're adding the water and shoot for the middle of the suggested range. If you go this route, you'll need to add water, mix thoroughly, then measure. And you'll need to repeat that each time you add more water, until you get to the desired SG. If you don't mix it well, then your readings may not be accurate. After all steps were completed I left it in the carboy for about 2 weeks longer, then bottled and let it age for about 1 month. That was all it took, and it was ready to drink. I chill this one for about 20 minutes before drinking. I know it's a red, but this is more of a wine cocktail in my opinion and it really makes it refreshing.The Rating:The only reason I gave this a 4 instead of a 5 was due to how low the alcohol content would be if you mixed it to the full 6 gallons per the instructions. If you add a little less water though, you'll be in good shape. It also came with labels, corks and plastic heat shrink capsules for the top. Definitely worth the price and I plan to make it again...soon.

We have purchased this exact kit from amazon in the past. This kit was great,every function we went to we brought a bottle and it was a big hit. Everybody loved it. If you are new to wine making this kit has everything you need to make and bottle your wine, but you must have all of the associated supplies already example the bottles, carboy, hydrometer, and corker.

I didn't want to make this per directions after reading reviews on how sweet this was. I made this to right at 5 gallons including the addition of a little Everclear to boost ABV. I used half the F-pack during the initial fermentation process so it wouldn't be über sweet at bottling time. Wonderful raspberry flavor. So very pleased with Cornucopia. I have the Blueberry Shiraz fermenting now. I'm going to try a few others before the year is out.

This is a great kit for any home wine maker. Kit came with all chemicals needed with detailed instructions, corks, labels and even wine bottle shrink wraps. You will still need the bottles, carboy, hydrometer, and corker, but if you have made wine before you will already have those.All that tasted the wine produced from this kit loved it and now want more.

This wine is perfect for sitting out on the patio/deck in the summer.  Reminds me of a Sangria more than a Merlot, but I haven't found anyone that doesn't like the wine.  It is on the sweet side since you add the raspberry juice after the fermentation process, but it is a great price for a very nice tasting wine.  You can't go wrong with this one.

I have ordered chocolates during the summer months many times. Have always been satisfied, as they were packed in dry ice. Not so with this purchase. The bars were all melted. It was going to be a gift. Now I have to think of something else.

The costume size was perfect. its pretty true to size. Usually you purchase a costume and it fits smaller than the size chartthan it refers to. I cannot wait to wear it for Halloween. MOO WHO HA HA!!!
Fit perfectly. Size is true. Expected exactly what was described online and that's exactly what i received. Would definitely purchase another item in the future.

I was a bit skeptical, because most "sexy" costumes tend to fit a bit snug. But I'm a size 14 and the  large costume fit me perfectly! It is flattering and super fun with the buttons and ruffles. There were a few strings hanging off and the costume is a little shear in some places, but it's pretty good quality for a bag costume. column10: I am a culinary student thus I appreciate quality in foods. I was introduced to this variety of Cream of Wheat at the "Original Pancacke House" near me. It must be stirred during the entire cooking process to avoid lumps. After much experimentation, I use 1% milk and mix one cup of milk to one ounce of cereal. Heat on medium. Too hot cooks it too fast and creates lumps. It easy to make ahead. I prepare 10 oz servings on Sunday for use during the week. I serve with fresh fruit. For added richness, add one cup of heavy cream to seven cups of milk (ratio). When you reheat add several ounces of milk to each portion then heat (about 2 minutes, 45 sec.). Wisk briefly to get smooth consistency. Using 2% or whole milk does not seem to result in much difference in structure or taste.

He was going down the drain. Then I found this product. Simple as that, we put the medicine in the treat and he wolfed it down. He actually got to the point that when the 6 hour time was coming around to "get the treat" he would start whining and staring at the refrigerator where I had prepared the whole dosage plan ahead of time and put them into a plastic box with big lettering, "THIS IS ALEX'S MEDICINE - NOT CHOCOLATE!" We had a close call with my little sister - they looked appetizing to her as well! :) Now I use these for his vitamins and for anything that he has to take that is not appetizing. column9: For more economical choice, check out Pill Pockets for CATS
column10: I have a 100lb dog, an Akita who HATES taking pills. She has NOT had Pill Pockets for Dogs, but she HAS had Pill Pockets for CATS. Now, before you click the "No" button after "Was this review helpful to you?", read further -- my comments will be of value to those with dogs that take SMALL pills!Andie has been taking pills for hypothyroidism for the past 9 years. Her pills are TINY. Wrapping them in meat or cheese never worked; she simply ate around the pill or spit it out. For years the only way I could get Andie to take pills was to, literally, shove them down her throat. (My hands are small enough and her mouth is big enough for me to do this. Thankfully she's a very trusting dog!)Then one day I was at the vet and noticed packages of something called "Pill Pockets". They had two kinds -- one for dogs and one for cats. Both came in flavors that Andie would like, but the dog Pill Pockets came in different sizes (small and large) while the cat Pill Pockets only came in one size (small).I looked at each package very carefully and noticed that the packages for cats had 45 Pill Pockets, while the packages for small dogs only had 35 Pill Pockets. And yet, the packages for small dogs cost MORE than the packages for cats -- huh? (On Amazon.com they are the same price, but the quantities are different.) So I looked at Andie's tiny thyroid pills, then looked at the Pill Pocket pictures on the packages and decided, "I might as well save myself a buck and buy the kitty Pill Pockets. What the hey, Andie won't know she's eating something intended for cats!"I've been happy with that decision ever since.I've bought both the salmon- and chicken-flavored Pill Pockets FOR CATS and Andie likes them both. The pockets are the perfect size, just big enough for her thyroid pills, and to date she has gulped down every one, then begged for another! And I like the fact that I get 10 more in each package than I would if I bought the Pill Pockets "for dogs".Pill Pockets are GREAT product, for cats OR dogs. I wish I had discovered them sooner! While I have never used the Pill Pockets for Dogs, I am 100% confident that they are excellent. That's why I'm giving this product 5 stars. If Andie's pills were bigger I would get the Pill Pockets for Dogs, and I know she would like them just as much. For the time being, though, I will stick with the smaller Pill Pockets for Cats, since they last a few days longer.So, this review is to pass along an idea that perhaps some dog owners had not considered: If your dog takes tiny pills like Andie does, go with the more economical choice and get Pill Pockets for Cats. Your dog will never know the difference!

Rarely have I encountered a product that doesn't have at least ONE person who either thinks it's junk, or gives a (bogus) low review because the delivery guy accidentally dropped the package before leaving the item at the door.As of this moment, 100% of the people reviewing the Greenies PILL POCKETS have given them a five-star rating, and I'm enthusiastically joining the crowd!If you're a dog owner, you've almost certainly had to, at some point, give your dog a pill that he or she was reluctant to take. The usual remedy until now, (as suggested by our vet) was to simply shove the thing down the poor dog's throat, and then rub their neck to help the pill go down.Recently, one of our dogs --a large yellow lab named Chip-- was suffering from untreatable throat cancer, but he still needed to take a number of pills to make his final days a little more comfortable. The vet specifically mentioned AVOIDING the "shove and rub" technique as it would be very painful for the dog --who at that point was even reluctant to eat his regular food.Someone mentioned PILL POCKETS. We picked up a bag and lo and behold, they worked like a champ. Though Chip was still not really interested in eating a meal, the *very* meaty smell of the PILL POCKETS was irresistible to him, and he happily gobbled up his meds.Sadly, we lost Chip about a week later, but then our other dog developed a minor skin rash that required he take some antibiotics. Eubie is a Border Collie, and they tend to figure things out before you do --and we were astounded when he wolfed down his medicine and then looked at us as if to ask "is that all --when do I get another?!"My technique for using the PILL POCKETS is to stuff the pill(s) inside, pinch off the open end --and then, using my palms, "roll" the pocket into a smooth, round ball. With Eubie at least, he loves the smell so much, that he simply swallows it whole.In fact, I discovered another great use for the PILL POCKETS and that is to take a rawhide bone and smear the nooks and crannies with a single pill pocket. Since they're kind of "doughy" in texture, they're perfect in this regard --and for a dog that will happily walk around the house with the rawhide bone for days without ever chewing on it, we've found that the "pill pocket infused" rawhide is something that he HAS to chew on. (In fact, he was SO focused on this task, that for the first time ever, he actually ignored the fireworks on July 4th.... it was truly amazing!)- Jonathan Sabin

My dog Andy requires 3 pills 3 times a day. I started using Pillpockets almost two years ago. We have used the dreaded pill popper for many years. When the popper comes out, Andy beats a hasty retreat. We all hated it, as a lot of times the pills popped out, stayed in the popper, or he gagged on them. Since he had to have pills three times a day, it was a daily ordeal. It all changed when we tried Pill Pockets. He now looks forward to taking his pills. He loves the taste of the Pillpockets, I don't think we can now do without them. He likes them so much, we use them as treats for special occasions. They have made treating Andy a pleasant experience, rather than a ordeal. I wish I would have invented them.

As a veterinarian, I've dispensed a lot of medications for both dogs and cats...that is, until I had to start medicating my own pets.  I've became a lot more empathetic now that I've realized that I can barely pill my own cat (who runs away from me), and that my dog will not take pills in cheese or peanut butter. In fact, pilling my own pets has smartened me up on what meds pets really need. As a result, I've started prioritizing pills - in other words, I rank the order of importance of each prescription for pet owners, so they know which pills are an absolute MUST give, and which ones they can skip if they are getting desperately fed up with pilling.Since then, my life has changed... thanks to Pill Pockets. I regret not inventing these, as it was one of those "duh" products that came out, making you wish you had the money-making patent.  Whoever owns a dog that needs to be pilled chronically, pay heed. The Greenies Pill Pockets are awesome... that is, for dogs, at least.My dog recently got put on a bunch of medications, and he's super picky (although less so, since getting put on steroids!). Being that he needs a total of 5 medications a day, I found Pill Pockets to be a true life saver, as they improve both my dog's and my quality of life. These little tasty, greasy, soft, malleable pockets are designed so that you can stick the pill (or multiple pills) in the center, and seal them into a hidden ball of "treat."  It's like playing with palatable play-dough. Drop it in the food, and voila, it "makes pills a treat to give!"The pros: Pill Pockets are easy, convenient, tasty, and come in multiple flavors (Dog: beef and chicken; Cat: salmon and chicken. It also comes in a hypoallergenic flavor - duck and pea - for both species with food allergies). More importantly, they are palatable - dogs seem to love them. Another pro is that they come in multiple sizes, and I'm able to stuff 5 pills - yes all 5 pills - into the larger "capsule" dog Pill Pockets.The cons:  One of my two cats won't touch Pill Pockets. This is, of course, the cat who actually needs to take medication. He also won't touch Feline Heartgard monthly chewable pills either, so I suspect he doesn't like moist treats. So, try at your own risk, particularly if you have a finicky cat. The other con is that Pill Pockets are a bit greasy - they have a high vegetable oil content. One trick is to push the pill into a bit of hotdog--no dog can resist that.

Alright success until the receptionist at the vet said to use Hot dogs. Hmmm.  What dog does not like Hot Dogs?

I bought the capsule size Greenies for my pekingnese and cut them into four pieces and place the pills in them using tweezers to avoid getting the odor of the pills on the outside.  I wrap dog food around the Greenies and he eats everything.  If he's not eating and I try to put the Greenie into his mouth he spits it out as soon as he tastes the medicine.  If he's not eating very much he pushes the Greenie to the side.

column4: Bruce L. Nelson "'Alone Across Alaska' and '7...
column10: My dachshund recently needed to start taking pills three times a day. He figured out there were sometimes pills in hot dog pieces (something to try nonetheless) so he began carefully checking each piece and spitting out the pills. So I tried Pill Pockets. The first one worked, and that was the last time. He won't even taste them now. So for me, Pill Pockets were expensive and ineffective. I get him excited by quickly feeding him the trimmings, followed up by the main piece with the pill inside. On occasion he still finds them, but he likes chicken so much that it works quite well, so far, anyway.Obviously Pill Pockets work very good for most people, but not for me and my dog.
I can't believe these are veterinary approved.  Just smell one and that should tip you off....smells like chemicals.  Evidently my dogs think so too, because they will not eat them.

I found wrapping  my tiny tot's pills in a little ball of wet dog food was simple and seemed more palatable than the greasy, foul smelling greasies oops I mean greenies.  He used to toss them around but hesitated to eat them for ages until I became concerned.  Wrapping the pills in a wholesome freshly opened canned dog food is better in my opinion.

column9: A lifesaver for a pet owner whose pet spits out its pills!
column10: My 1-year-old Shih Tzu, Missy, was recently diagnosed with a skin infection and allergies, so the vet prescribed an antibiotic and an allergy med twice a day.  At first, I thought it was going okay with my hiding the pills in a piece of banana or cheese...but then, I started finding pills all over the place...she'd been appearing to eat the food while in front of me and then going elsewhere to spit out the pills!I was seeing my money go down the drain as these antibiotics and allergy meds went anywhere (including staining my carpet!) but IN HER TUMMY!  Finally, a friend who has a cat suggested pill pockets, so I ordered a small packet of these beef flavored ones to see if they would work.WELL!  She not only takes her meds now, but she BEGS for them as soon as she sees me open the package of pill pockets!  I am FINALLY seeing her skin clear up because the pills are FINALLY getting into her system...today I gave her a bath and her skin is clear!My only issue with the pill pockets (the ONLY reason I gave them 4 stars vs. 5) is that they are very soft and mooshy...I guess this is necessary so that you can mold the pill pocket around the pill, regardless of its shape or size...but I find it a little yucky.  A few months ago, I may also have complained about the VERY strong smoky smell (like beef jerky), but I've gotten used to that via some treats Missy that loves.I will definitely be ordering these again...in a larger quantity!

For those picky dogs that don't want to take pills, this is the solution. I tried to hide my dog's pills in peanut butter, cheese, and cold cuts, none of which worked. Even though the tablet sized pockets are large enough for any tablet, the capsule size allow me to get twice as many pill pockets for my money. She loves these stinky things and they don't aggravate her pancreas nor do they spark up her allergies.  She takes many pills in these little wonders with absolutely no ill effects.  Thank you sooo much.

Since my dog is a chewer rather than a chomper, it has always been difficult to give her pills.  I had tried hiding the pills (crushed or whole) in various foods or dog treats, but she'd always sniff it out and/or bite into it and then refuse to eat it.  Pill Pockets has an oily texture that she can just gulp right down.  I find one capsule-size Pill Pocket to be way too big for 1 capsule, so I just mash it down and mold it separately over the 3 pills that she has to take.

It's nearly impossible after a few days to get our dogs to take their pills. The first day you can stick it in some peanut butter and they're fooled. The next day they say no to PB but will eat it in salami. The third day maybe a dab of honey will do the trick. By the fourth day they won't eat anything with the pills in them....until Greenies came into our house! Never again will we have to worry about fighting with our dogs over taking their meds!!

These pill pockets are the best product ever. My dog is on oral chemotherapy, prednizone, appetite enhancers, and antibiotics right now. These things are a life saver!! The chemicals have really messed up how things taste, so we're constantly challenged to find something she'll eat (she's completely off dog food). Happily, she takes her pills in these pill cups with no fuss. She thinks she's getting a treat.

column9: What can I say? They're great
column10: It's really tough to give my dog his pills. He seems to know when there is a pill inside a lump of dog food. He'll enevitably eat the treat but leave or spit up the pill. column9: If you have a chubby dog...

column9: best price in town, free shipping with prime
column10: I got a sick dog that has to take 5 pills in the morning an 3 at night, these capsule size are large enough that they can be split into 3 doses each, They are maleable like putty so one can need them over several pills at once and my dog just inhales them, he has never spit out one pill.

column4: Uncle Fishbits "I am moving your eyeballs."
column9: This *may* give your dog diarrhea, but they do their job.
column10: My dog is 12, and has had constantly firm stool his whole life.  After a dental surgery, I used these, and assume the medicine was giving him diarrhea. column9: Great for Dogs on Hypoallergenic Diets
column10: I have been extremely satisfied with the Greenies Pill Pockets Roasted Duck and Pea Formula. To clarify, this is the same as "Allergy Formula" (it's written on front of the package), although on amazon it is listed as a separate product.My dog is on a novel protein source diet and cannot eat the beef or chicken Pill Pockets, although he must take daily medications.  Getting him to take his daily medications was a huge hassle until I found out about these.I do agree with a previous reviewer about the smell and color of these duck/pea Pill Pockets.  The smell is unfortunate, to say the least, and the color is interesting-looking.  If my dog did not have allergic issues, I would definitely give him the regular beef or chicken flavor Pill Pockets instead.However, comparing the two products, I believe one reason the Allergy Formula Pill Pockets have a certain odd color is due to lack of added color. In other words, they have a more natural color. In the beef Pill Pockets, "caramel color" is one of the ingredients, but it is not in the Allergy Formula.  In case, anyone is interested, these are the ingredients in the Roasted Duck and Pea Allergy Formula: duck, glycerin, dried peas, natural flavors, vegetable oil, water, salt, potassium sorbate (to preserve freshness), xanthan gum, citric acid, preserved with mixed tocopherals (a source of Vitamin E).My dog likes the Allergy Formula Pill Pockets just as well as the regular Pill Pockets, so the offensive smell does not seem to affect him at all.Finally, I saw in an earlier review where someone said these were smaller than the normal "capsule" size.  I have NOT found this to be true. I have ordered several times and every time, the capsule size is the same as for the regular beef or chicken flavor Pill Pockets.  This means that usually you can break one in two, so they go twice as far.  The texture of these Pill Pockets is just as malleable as the normal ones and it's quite easy to hide a pill in them.  All in all, I highly recommend if your dog has allergy issues and can't take the normal ones.

column9: good for capsules, too - success depends on flavor

Great product. My dog loves it and has no idea she's eating nasty tasting pills inside the yummy pill pockets.

column9: Duck Flavor makes my 2 dogs throw up
column10: Every time, every time, we give our two dogs their nightly pepcid in one-half of an "allergy formula," duck flavored pill pocket, they throw up hours later, whereas they don't throw up if we use the beef or chicken flavor.

column9: Be careful, made 1 of my dogs very ill
column10: I must admit these do work for getting your pets to take pills - 2 very finicky dogs who almost always spit out their pills in any food did scarf their pills down when put in these.  However, after only 2 pills (separated by 8 hours), one of my dogs (8 month old puppy) became violently ill about 2 hours after the 2nd pill pocket with numerous episodes of explosive diarrhea and vomiting (ultimately very bloody after 12 hours).  It ended up costing us money for a vet visit and medicine to get the dog to get well, and a major scare that the puppy was going to die (could hardly move after 18 hrs of this).  The medicine was not new, nor any thing else changed, so I presume it was due to these (certainly not going to try them again to see).  Our other dog (full adult) did fine, however.  Maybe it should just not be used for puppies, or maybe it's just an unusual reaction, but if you google "pill pockets diarrhea", you will see this is an occasional known side effect.Would suggest trying just one of these each of the first few days to make sure your pet is not intolerant of these. 1 out of 2 for me was not good odds.
This gets my dog to actually look forward to taking pills.  Works like a charm.  Not messy and the dog just loves it.
Such a wonderful and easy way to give your pet a pill.  And with Amazon, it's much cheaper than buying them at the vet's office or any store.  And, my picky dog loves the taste.

This product is great for giving my little dog his medicine.  So much easier and less traumatic for the little dog.

column9: Warning: using this product may have unintended side effects

column9: Pill Pockets - Great Product - Good Price
column10: My dogs love these. They think they are getting a treat and eat their pills, no problem. This is a good price for a great product. Fast shipping makes it even better.

Pill pockets are ideal for giving drugs to dogs, much easier than squashing pills into a piece of cheese!  Our dog sees daily pill times as a treat now and comes and sits patiently waiting.  We are on our 4th packet of these and will definitely order more whenever we are giving drugs to dogs!

Our puppy (a bernedoodle) loves these duck treats.  We started using them for pills, but now use them to spread inside of kongs and other toys.  She has a sensitive tummy, so these are great for multiple uses.

My pets love these things, and they make giving medicine so easy!  I no longer have to chase my dogs down and hope that they take their medicine.  With these I KNOW the pill is going to get swallowed.My dogs love anything duck flavored.  They went wild over these!

If you've ever tried to get your dog to swallow pills, you know how wonderful these are.  We have four dogs (three Corgis and a mixed breed), and all like them, and these have been successful with them all.Our mixed breed dog was about 13, and her disease was terminal, and we weren't ready to lose her (not that anyone ever is).  We had medicines that would make her comfortable in her final stages, but the problem was getting her to take them...we tried all sorts of things: peanut butter, apple sauce, fruit, meat--all had a certain ability to disguise the taste, but she got wise to them pretty quickly.But the Greenies Pill Pockets ALWAYS worked.  We were able to extend her life, with comfort, for a couple of months longer, and for that I'll always be grateful.A NOTE: The Greenies come in several flavors (chicken, beef, duck & peas), sizes, and also flavors for cats.  If you need to be more economical, you can also "shave" them down by squeezing off a little of them (depending on the strength of the pill they're taking).

We have had a number of cats with medical problems and tried any number of ways to get pills into them.  Pill Pockets are by far the easiest method.Most of our animals have considered Pill Pockets as "treats" and readily eaten them.  Our current feline gets three pockets in the morning and three in the evening, so we go through a lot.One suggestion:  if your smaller pet needs to take many meds, buy the pockets designed for capsuls for dogs.  Product pricing seems to be related to the number of "doses", rather than the weight.  I believe the small package for cats is 1.6 oz and costs only a few $ less than this 6.6 oz package. If you go through the pockets like we do, the savings are substantial.  We simply tear off a piece of the larger pocket and wrap it around the pill.  It takes 15 seconds.Another suggestion is to get a selection of flavors.  Our cat goes through periods where certain flavors are unacceptable, so it is good to alternate and have backups.If you are really desperate, you can always use human meat baby food.  We haven't seen a cat yet that would't take that.Summary:  A much better way to give your pet meds than a pill shooter.

First off, I have found that buying these treats on Amazon is cheaper than purchasing them at PetSmart. I buy the capsule version of the Pill Pockets versus the tablet version because the bags are larger (it holds more ounces) and the cost difference is almost nothing. I then break that one capsule up into many pieces because they are soft & malleable. I am able to get that one bag to last me for many servings. I only use it to wrap up my dog's Prozac pill.  He will gobble it down with no problem. However, if I try to use any larger pill such as a Heartworm pill or Allergy pill in them, he will eat the treat part off & spit out the medicinal pill. For those types of pills, I just crush them up and stir them in some wet food for him.

we tried alot of things to hide pills in.  our dog would maybe fall for it once or twice, but then would spit out the pills and eat the cheese, peanut butter, hot dog, etc. that it was wrapped in.  But then we found pill pockets and he likes them enough to eat them and the pill inside.  the best thing is how easy it is to form them around different pills, and how you can only use pieces of one pill pocket on smaller pills to make them stretch farther.

These pill pockets are the easiest way to get a dog to take its meds.  My dog scarfs them down no problem.  They can be kind of pricey, especially if you have a dog that requires daily medication, as they only come 30 in a pack and retail for $7.99 (cheaper on amazon of course!).  I would definitely recommend them if you have a dog that has trouble taking his pills.

I have been giving my dog all his medication using Pill Pockets. He just loves them. I prefer the smell of Beef over Chicken, but he doesn't care. They definetly were cheaper through Amazom. I will buy these again.

However, you can easily just take a piece of mush and wrap it around the pill.  The dogs don't care if it is shaped properly or not.  Our dogs just swallow it hole and sit there waiting for another one.

It has won awards from CeBIT, the world's largest and most international computer expo. Atatürk would be proud!I found that my grinder could produce very close to the powder-like nature of ground Turkish coffee. But I wanted to try "the real thing," so I ordered this brand and another. Standard stove-top boiler pots are cheap, but the Bekos are not. As all coffee tends to come from the same sources, I suspect I will be able to find similar quality locally, grind it or have it ground, and store it in this can.  Makes it easy to spot the Turkish grind!

It is one of the best Turkish coffee available!  I love Turkey and went there twice.  Every time I was there, I always ordered their cai (tea) or Mehmet Efendi Coffee.  I'm so glad that it is available from Amazon.comThere is a little tips in brewing Turkish or Greek coffee.1) Use filtered water if possible.  It does make a difference.2) Use medium high heat.3) When you place the pot on the stove, ensure you don't over boil it.  After it is boiled for 1-2 minutes, the coffee should have very tiny-bubbled foam.  If you have BIG bubbles - you are over boiling it. Turn down the temperature.4) Once the tiny-bubbled foam starts to rise up, remove it from the stove and spoon the foam into you cup.  Within seconds, place it back to the stove and continue to boil it w/medium to medium high heat.  After 10-15 seconds, your coffee is ready to be served. To me, the tiny-bubbled foam makes the coffee smoother.It takes a few good trys to make a perfect cup - Enjoy!

column9: Boot Scootin' Green Chile Chili: Great packaging, but...
column10: It was the packaging that sold us with this Leonard Mountain Boot Scootin' Green Chile Chili when my son and I were online here, looking for some interesting new chili variations. This one seemed different from some of the others, so we bought this pack of three 12oz bags. Not cheap, but it seemed interesting at the time.We unpacked the shipment upon arrival, and found that each one had the following:> One genuine Boot Scootin' burlap bag, with a drawstring (see the user photo)> One miniature bottle of genuine Tabasco® green pepper sauce, enough for one person.> Chili Seasonings, containing onions, garlic, salt, black pepper and green chilies> 10 oz. of whole pinto beansThe nutritional info states the following: Serving Size 12 oz. Servings Per Container About 6, Calories 90, Calories from Fat 10, Total Fat 1g, Saturated Fat 0g, Trans Fat 0g, Cholesterol 0mg, Sodium 101mg, Total Carbs 19g, Dietary Fiber 2g, Sugars 1g, Protein 2g, Vitamin A 0%, Vitamin C 0%, Calcium 4%, Iron 2%. Based on a 2,000 calorie diet.The Product Description was quite unusual, to say the least:"Uncle Charlie jus adds in sum of his real special dried green tabascy plants to het up this chili. Now the boys `round these parts reely lak this chili bettrn the red sissy chili. Most the womens think the green's a little hot fer thur sweet lips."Taste Test:Without all of the boring details, we followed the enclosed directions to the letter, adding ground beef to keep the initial batch as simple as possible. It smelled good as it was cooking, but we had to increase the cooking time, simmering it gently for an extra hour as it was a little flat. Let's just say that it was disappointing, and that's an understatement. For the next attempt, we tried the time tested method of cooking the chili the day before, letting it cool down, then refrigerating the batch overnight to give all the flavors time to blend. That was a very slight improvement, but not by much. Let's just say that it was reminiscent of some chili that I once had at an obscure New Jersey diner that's no longer in business. There never was a third attempt.Sometimes it's just better to do it yourself. This is the recipe that I use for "DIY Slow Cooked Chili" that I learned years ago when living in the South, and the one that I fall back on when in the mood for cooking:* 2 lb. ground beef* 1 1/2 cups chopped onions* 1/2 cup chopped green pepper* 2 garlic cloves, finely cut (not chopped)* 28 oz. can whole tomatoes* 2 (16 oz.) cans kidney beans* 2 tbsp. chili powder* 2 tsp. salt* 2 tsp. cumin* 2 tsp. black pepperBrown the ground beef; add onions, green pepper, garlic, tomatoes, kidney bens, salt, chili powder, pepper and cumin in a slow cooker or crock pot. Cover and simmer on low setting for 6 to 8 hours. Makes 8 to 10 servings. Serve with cornbread and whatever hot sauce you like. Looking forward to trying Tabanero Hot Sauce Picante, as it's been highly recommended.Notes:This company also makes Redneck Chill E SPICY and Redneck Habanerah Allives (you'll just have to look at that one), but to date this reviewer has resisted the temptation to try either of these or their other offerings. However, I did receive a box of Leonard Mountain 3 Amigos Enchilada Stew as a gift from a friend, and this product was easily worth a 5-star recommendation. That was one of the reasons that I tried their chili mix. Go figure.Bottom Line:Cannot say that Leonard Mountain Boot Scootin' Green Chile Chili was the worst chili mix that I've ever had, but it's probably borderline close. What one pays for here is cute slogans and clever packaging, and this product is highly overpriced for what you get. Sad to say, even those chili seasoning packets you find in the spice section of your grocery store are better. But the burlap bag packaging was clever, and my son kept the miniature Tabasco green pepper sauce bottle, so I'll give it one star each for the creative packaging and the tiny Tabasco bottle.9/4/2012
