column9: Tabasco Original vs. Tabasco Chipotle: a fair comparison
column10: First, let me say that while I consider myself a journeyman hot sauce eater, I have never been a fan of regular Tabasco sauce. Regular Tabasco is, as the name suggests, made with ground tabasco chilis soaked in vinegar and the result is a very simple but lousy sauce: salty and with a strong, instant, biting burn and no flavor to speak of other than vinegar. It can be used to add necessary heat to heavily flavored dishes when nothing else is available, but the flavor sucks and I'd sooner eat my pizza plain than ruin it with that crap.Tabasco Chipotle is made with smoked jalapenos (chipotles) and is a lot thicker than regular Tabasco. It has an excellent smoky flavor and not a lot of heat, but just enough to let you know it's there. An important point is that the burn isn't progressive and never overwhelms your mouth; regular Tabasco has a cumulative burn and a definite point at which the intensity of the burn completely negates your ability or desire to eat more. That never happens with Tabasco Chipotle, so it's great for pouring and dipping when you're actually looking for flavor. I eat probably a bottle of this stuff a week and it's good to eat on just about everything and also makes an awesome meat marinade. Mix it with mayonnaise, you've got chipotle mayo.A better comparison in terms of heat might be between this and the cayenne-based red pepper sauces (Frank's Red Hot, Crystal, Texas Pete, etc.) This isn't a nose-hair scorcher and it respects your taste buds and tries to work with your food instead of taking over and dominating. A lot of people seem to think that hot sauce is about pushing your pain threshold to the limit, but in my experience you're either in it primarily for the flavor or primarily for the pain. This sauce definitely falls on the more flavorful side of hot sauces, and I strongly recommend you try it if you've never tried chipotle sauces before.

Sporting the curse of the Chilehead, I find Tabasco Chipotle lively, but leaving me not only wanting - but needing - more smokiness, more richness and more burn; essentially, more Chiptole. Before you buy this again at the supermarket, I invite you to search out El Yucateco Salsa Chipotle (5 oz). This hot sauce ratchets things up a bit and is truer in taste to Chipotle proper. Even better, just pickup a small can of Chipoltes in Adobo (Spanish foods aisle or store), blend in a food processor, thinning with distilled white or cider vinegar to desired consistency and cut with some brown sugar to balance it out. It might take a little tweaking, but jar that puppy up and you're good to go - with the real deal.
This sauce is not too spicy, but has a delicious barbecue-like flavor. Perfect on nachos, hamburgers, pasta, and more.

column9: A must for Tex-Mex foods... warning: addictive!!
column10: Tabasco brand Chipotle Pepper Sauce is a vinegar based hot sauce made with chipotle peppers (smoked jalapeno peppers), and spices such as garlic and onion, and is absolutely delicious!! It has a smooth, rich, smokey, complex, hot flavor that's awesome on chili, tacos, fajitas, popcorn, any Tex-Mex style food, or to really kick up a salsa... by far, my favorite Tabasco product!

This is my go-to seasoning.  I have all of the other Tobasco sauce flavors, but the Chipotle Pepper sauce is my favorite.  Not too hot, yet spicy enough to add some peppery kick with a slightly smokey flavor.

column9: BEST LITTLE HOT SAUCE IN TEXAS!!!
column10: I just returned from spending the holidays in Houston, TX.  Stopped by a place called "Willy's", where they had this sauce on each table.  It blew my mind!  I think it is the TASTIEST of all the hot sauces.  It has heat, but the flavor of the chipotle shines through.  I am a true convert.  I can see me having a long and wonderful relationship with this Tabasco brand product!  Try it, you will like it!
I started sprinkling this stuff on fresh-popped popcorn a few years ago. Now I find it hard to eat popcorn without it!

column9: Tabasco's Best.  I'm not generally a fan of Tabasco products but their Chipotle is superior
column10: This Chipotle Sauce offers some gentle heat along with the rich taste of a smoked Chipotle pepper. It makes a great Bloody/Virgin Mary and will add some interesting flavors to any dish that needs some heat. As another reviewer said -- this is probably the best tasting product within Tabasco's ever expanding lineup.I've taste tested 7 different Chipotle hot sauces and the Tabasco Chipotle is one of my favorites. The taste is very rich, smokey, semi-sweet and, for once, there is not too much vinegar! Yet make no mistake - there is a good dose of vinegar yet it is not over powering. It is quite simply one of the best Chipotle sauces I have taste tested.Keep in mind that this sauce is relatively mild when compared to the other Tabasco products.  In this particular sauce, the heat is far more subdued and not what I would have  expected from a Tabasco product. This sauce needs to viewed as a completely different product.  This is the best tasting Tabasco sauce I've ever tasted and beyond that -- near the best tasting Chipotle I have found.I paid $3.29 for it at my local supermarket. I doubt you'll have any trouble finding it locally and since tastes differ - I'd recommend you first buy a single bottle close to home. Then purchase a half gallon on-line.What sets this chipotle apart is the richness of its flavor. It is concentrated in the best possible sense. Rich, with some sweetness, smokey, some vinegar and a bit of gentle heat.I have repeatedly taste tested the following Chipotle:  Tabasco, La Victoria, El Pato, Cholula, Goya, Bufalo and El Yucateco.The El Yucateco Chipotle is also superb and the only worthy competitor to this sauce. Both are rich - the Tabasco has more vinegar and the El Yucateco has a bit more sugar and a hint of tomato.

Yep, it's one of the truly great chipotle sauces around.  It's probably my favorite chipotle sauce although there are a few others that are in still in the running.  It really tastes nothing like the original Tabasco, another favorite hot sauce of mine.  I probably use the chipotle sauce more than the original Tabasco.  One of my favorite ways to use it is in spicing up ranch-style dressings for use in salads and dips.  It works wonders in barbeque sauce and to spice up bastes to use on the smoker.  Great smokey flavor.
Never seen this version at the Local Super Markets. Both my wife and I think it's a great change of taste!

column9: The Fourth New Flavor of the Quintessential Condiment!
column10: This was the fourth modern variation on an essentially unchanged, bestselling product for more than 140 years.  Other flavors are:Orginal Pepper Sauce (hot) (2500-5000 Scoville Heat Units),Green Pepper Sauce (milder yet) (600-1200 Scoville Heat Units),Habanero Sauce (hottest) (>7000 Scoville Heat Units).Garlic Pepper Sauce (milder) (1200-2400 Scoville Heat Units),Sweet & Spicy Pepper Sauce (mildest) (100-600 Scoville Heat Units),but this is Chipotle Pepper Sauce (mild) (1500-2500 Scoville Heat Units).Dueling histories of the McIlhenny Company are available: (authorized) Tabasco: An Illustrated History and (unauthorized) McIlhenny's Gold: How a Louisiana Family Built the Tabasco Empire, for those curious about how this most remarkable product and business empire came to be.Note: "A pharmacist named Wilbur Scoville invented the Scoville Scale in 1912 to measure the heat of peppers. A 'Scoville Unit' is actually a measure of capsaicin (the chemical in hot peppers that is responsible for their heat).Scoville's test was a comparative taste test that is considered subjective by today's standards. A more sophisticated method is in use today, but in honor of Wilbur Scoville, the unit of measure is still called the Scoville.The capsaicin level in peppers can vary from plant to plant due to local environmental conditions. This means that a pepper's rating is an average measure.The hottest pepper on record is the Bhut Jolokia with a pungency of over 1 million Scoville Heat Units (1,001,304, to be exact). By contrast, the Bell Pepper comes in at less than 100 Scoville Heat Units."

For well over a year, I have been using different types of hot sauce on different types of food.  Before I started doing this, I only ever remember using hot sauce on barbeque sandwiches.  Even though I have tried numerous types of hot sauce during this period, Tabasco Brand Chipotle Pepper Sauce has set itself apart from the others.  Tabasco Brand Chipotle Pepper Sauce is hotter than most hot sauces that I like, but I do not consider it to be an overpowering heat.  It is a good, nice-tasting hot sauce to have around, and I recommend it.

I enjoy fresh ground pepper, who wouldn't.  This innoative product allows that.  There are however, two very minor drawbacks, but not serious enough to keep me from buying this producct again.  There is no way to adjust the grind for fine, or coarse.  Lastly, it is very difficult to turn the grinder because it's small, and I can't get a good grip on it.

I love freshly ground pepper and especially love a little kick that having red peppercorns in a mix provide, so I normally use Alessi Whole Mix Peppercorns, 1.12-Ounce Grinder (Pack of 6). There are times, however, when all I want is freshly ground black pepper, like when I am having vine-ripened tomatoes, insalada Caprese, and the such. That's where this product comes in.The peppercorns are high quality and give off a nice aroma when ground. Like its more colorful sibling, the grinding mechanism tends to produce very coarse pepper, so if you prefer yours to be finer, a dedicated grinder may better suit your needs.  I have had no problems with the grinding mechanism - I use a clockwise-counterclockwise motion and it works well. Too well if I am not careful because it will grind a lot of pepper with minimal motion. It does not clog like some dedicated grinders, which is another plus.This is a convenient way to enjoy fresh ground pepper, and - in my opinion - is priced low considering that the grinder is disposable and I get nearly nine months of use from a package of six of these.I always have one on my table (in the kitchen I use a dedicated grinder that allows me to adjust the grind.)

I must have ordered the  wrong one I was having trouble finding any artichoke pastas that did not come in a 10 pound box, it is hard to commit to 10 pounds of pasta since so many gluten free varieties are nasty tasting!

column9: Better than many choices out there
column10: While this isn't my very top choice of cat foods available, it has worked very well as a transition food for the six months that we need an all-stages food until our kitten gets older.  When she was very small, we were able to give her her own kitten food by setting up her feeding station in a box that our adult cat couldn't get into.  Now that they are the same size, we can't keep them from stealing each other's food, so we needed something they could both eat.  We tried a couple of holistic all-stages foods, and this one has been the best, by far.  Both cats prefer the little "T" shape kibble over round kibble, they seem to enjoy the taste, and it keeps them and their digestive systems happy ... and that keeps ME happy.  ;-)  My older cat does better on a grain-free food, and has gotten a case of the itchies on this food, but it is not nearly as bad as with most grain-inclusive foods we've tried. column9: Put good in, get good out

column10: I tried a few dry food brands after the pet food recall of 2007.  I tried some grain free, and noticed some problems from the cats. Will be giving the Weruva Paw Lickin' Chicken Cat Food, 5.5-Ounce Cans (Pack of 24) a try.Wellness Adult Turkey Canned Cat Food (I prefer the Chicken, but until it reappears, this will do just as well).Felidae Canned Cat Food for Adult Cats and Kittens, Chicken and Rice Formula in Chicken Broth (Pack of 12 13 Ounce Cans) (Its not grain free, but I personally don't like the mix for the regular, and neither do my cats)Innova Cat and Kitten Formula Canned Cat Food (Also not grain free, and Multi protein source. However, cats have reacted positively to this food).Holistic Select Feline Radiant Adult and Kitten Health Chicken Meal Recipe Dry Cat Food, 3-Pound BagI feed a little dry first thing in morning every day. The next day, we have 5.5 oz can of Weruva split between 3 cats, and 1/2 can of the last flavor.  The next day we have another 5.5 oz can, and the remainder of the previous can. column9: A food that works for both new kitten and fussy adult cat
column10: My 8 year old cat is one of the fussiest eaters on the planet. She will not even touch a food if she sniffs it and decides she doesn't like the smell of it. I have tried the tactic of just leaving it out and not giving her any other options for food and she just ends up starving. She has been eating a cheap brand of dry cat food with ingredients that I now know are just horrific for cats her whole life. The first five ingredients were brewer's rice, chicken by-product meal, corn meal, chicken fat and soybean meal. As you can probably see, this is a food I was desperate to get her off of. She has also been a very skittish cat and would often have anxiety attacks about seemingly nothing. Like, at the very slightest noise she would literally jump 4 feet in the air from fear and if you were near her or touching her when it happened she would unintentionally scratch you to ribbons in her mad dash to get away. I was sad when this happened because normally she is such a gentle cat and has never bit me in her life, there is no way she would scratch unless she was terrified and completely out of her mind. I had an inkling that the junk food might be exacerbating this problem, much like how gluten and dairy could exacerbate the problems of autistic children.All of my attempts up until now have ended up in failed attempts and money wasted on food she wouldn't eat. This happened again and again and I almost thought it was a lost cause until Holistic Select chicken meal formula. We recently rescued a kitten off the streets and I knew I didn't want to start feeding her the same junk that my older cat had been eating for years. I was looking up some grain-free formulas and decided to go with one of those brands since cats shouldn't really be eating grains. To make a long story short, both the kitten and cat didn't like it. The kitten will nibble on it if there are no other options (she's easier to please, thank goodness), so I've kept it around and leave it out so there's something out when their other food is gone, but all in all, not a success by any means. I had a sample packet of Holistic Select chicken meal lying around that I received probably about a year ago and never got around to giving to my cat and the kitten got at it and bit away at the packaging to get the food inside. I looked at the ingredient list and hey, not too bad! I hoped beyond hope and offered some to my older cat and she eagerly ate it! Hallelujah!So I quickly bought a bag from Amazon and prayed that she would continue eating it. Well, I am now down to a quarter of the bag and I recently had to reorder. Both of the cats eat it with no problems and my older cat actually has far less anxiety attacks. She seems much more calm and is now willing to let my husband come up to her without running away in fear. He can even pet her a little. This is a miraculous change than just a few months ago when the mere sight of him had her diving under the bed. I have recently been eating healthier and I know what a difference it makes for me and there is no difference with our pets. What we feed them has a drastic affect on their well-being and behavior. This is not the absolute best food out there, but it's pretty darn good. I have recently ordered some wet food cans from Holistic Select since I know little kitten will go crazy over that and it's good to supplement the diet with some wet.

column9: Premium puppy food at a very good price!
column10: My apologies in advance for what is a lengthy review.  However, if I can help anyone save a little time compared to what I spent trying to choose a good puppy food, that's my goal.  So I wrote this not only to review the Castor & Pollux product, but also to provide some information on other types of dry dog food.It is no secret that you can buy some very cheap and some very expensive dog/puppy foods.  Common sense tells you that you can spend very little and get lots of filler and by-products, or spend a good deal more and get wholesome, healthy food.  My personal opinion is that long term, both your dog and you are better off if s/he is fed good food.  The little extra money spent now may offset potential medical bills and heartache later.That being the case, I set out to find a really good dog food for my Golden Retriever puppy, while, of course, trying to keep cost down.  I spent a good deal of time researching foods.  I disregarded low end foods that are largely grains, fillers and meat by-products.  I looked at average to premium foods.I narrowed my choices to several including Castor & Pollux Natural Ultramix.  The others were Blue, Eukanuba, Innova EVO, Merrick, Natural Balance, and Wellness.After that I used a few review websites and ratings tables.  These can be helpful.  I used one that starts each perspective food off with 100 points and then subtracts for poor ingredients (example: -10 points of containing by-products) and then adds points for any really good ingredients - vegetables, etc.  The foods are then rated in grades from A through F.  Of my choices, all but one were in the A or higher range.  From these I eliminated Ekanuba first, which had a B rating.  Although it is what the breeder was feeding my puppy's litter, it appears to be average, at best, with some decent ingredients, but also containing by-products.Once I had established that the remaining contenders all ranked in the same range, I looked at price.  Now all of these will cost more than a store brand, but in the end your dog may end up healthier, which will make both him and you happier.Castor and Pollux ranked in the top 5 or so of the foods I looked at, and in the end it costs about $1.71 a pound using Amazon's "Subscribe and Save" program.  Plus it ends up shipped free to your home - which makes one less 15 pound item you need to lug home from grocery shopping!Now, this price is perhaps double a store brand, Alpo, or Purina, but those brands contain a lot of fillers and meat by-products, and you have no way of knowing what is in by-product.  Manufacturers are very good at fooling our eyes.  We read "Meat By-products" and we see "meat".  Yet at 85 cents a pound, you many no longer consider it a bargain when you realize "meat by-products" can include bones, blood, heads, lungs, intestines, ligaments, feet and feathers.  Not so yummy any more.The present ingredient list (all from the United States, by the way) for Castor & Pollux Natural Ultramix,  is as follows:Chicken, Chicken Meal, Turkey Meal, Milo, Ground Whole Oats, Ground Whole Barley, Dried Bananas, Chicken Fat (Naturally preserved with Mixed Tocopherols and Citric Acid), Brown Rice, Dried Peas, Natural Chicken Flavor, Salmon Meal, Tomato Pomace, Brewers Dried Yeast, Ground Whole Flaxseed, Dried Sweet Potatoes, Dried Carrots, Dried Egg Product, Potassium Chloride, Salt, Freeze Dried Peas, Dried Cranberries, Dicalcium Phosphate, Fructooligosaccharide, Calcium Carbonate, Zinc Sulfate, Vitamin E Supplement, Choline Chloride, Ferrous Sulfate, Niacin, Copper Sulfate, Thiamine Mononitrate, Calcium Pantothenate, Vitamin A Supplement, Manganous Oxide, Pyridoxine Hydrochloride, Sodium Selenite, Riboflavin, Vitamin D3 Supplement, Biotin, Vitamin B12 Supplement, Calcium Iodate, Folic Acid, Rosemary Extract.It contains very good protein sources such as poultry and poultry meal, as well as salmon meal, and its grain content comes from oats and barley.  It also includes a good mix of dried vegetables and fruits.  The dried fruits are easily visible.  They are decent size pieces, not microscopic.At first glance, you might think these ingredients aren't all that different than a less expensive brand like Iams.  However, aside from the aforementioned meat by-products, another key thing to look at is whether a food contains corn, especially in the first few ingredients.  Iams and many others will often include corn, which isn't worthwhile to your puppy.  Typically they lack dried vegetables/fruits, which Casto & Pollux contains - so while other brands might seem less expensive (and are per pound) in the long run you are paying for fillers.All in all, I think Natural Ultramix is a high grade dog food, but not at such a high cost as to prohibit using it on a regular basis.  It is smaller size kibble to make it easier for puppies to chew, and it does not have an offensive aroma (either in the bowl or in the air, if you know what I mean).PS - for anyone wondering why I chose this brand over the others, once I was satisfied I had found a few very good brands, it really just came down to the price and shopping availability among them, while still having the ingredients I desired (including vegetables & fruit).  I can tell you I found Dick Van Patten's "Natural Balance" to be a sleeper in the bunch.  I assumed that if the company tied a celebrity name to it, the product probably couldn't stand on its own, but based on ingredients, that looks like a good puppy food as well.

It is an excellent source of nutrition, though I also supplement with Standard Process formulas, Springtime garlic, and the Missing Link so that my crew gets all the nutrition they need for optimum immune support.I rescued an 11-week-old Welsh Corgi puppy recently - he came from a backyard breeder that didn't know what they were doing. He also had a bad case of tape worm, which I found out after I brought him home, and adjusted poorly to the food at first.  So, I put him on Science Diet canned I.D.  - basically a pablum for dogs - just to get his system calmed down and then gradually added the Castor and Pollux - just a few pieces at first and working up from there while keeping an eye out for loose stool.  Anytime his stool became too loose, I backed off with the Castor and Pollux.  It's been a month and we're at a 75% to 25% ratio with Castor and Pollux at 75%.  He is MUCH healthier and looks like a completely different dog.Castor and Pollux doesn't contain the same kinds of processed foods - or at least not to the same extent - as other dog foods, even so-called natural dog foods, so it's harder to digest. By and large, however, this is an excellent food - just introduce it slowly so your pup eases into it.On a side note - no dry dog food can give your dog everything that he/she needs nutritionally, so it's likely you'll need to supplement with something like The Missing Link or another whole food supplement.

column9: This sauce is a bomb, for sure.
column10: I'm a fan of spice. It's almost a problem, in that I put hot sauce and/or seasoning on almost everything I eat lately. It's not uncommon for me to have a mean sweat going on while I eat. Yeah, some people would probably find that weird or even crazy... but for me, I enjoy it. I love spicy food.Which brings me to the review. I bought this 4 pack of Da Bomb ghost pepper sauce looking for a kick similar to what I experienced with the Dave's Gourmet Ghost Pepper sauce. But it's not. It's nowhere near the intensity as the Dave's sauce. In fact, Da Bomb's sauce is mostly habanero based, according to the ingredients. Habanero usually has a kick, but this sauce is no spicier than the habanero hot sauce I can get for a buck per bottle at my local grocer. I feel like I basically paid a premium for a sauce because they call it "ghost pepper", even though it has ghost pepper listed as the last ingredient in the list. Lame.Taste wise, it's ok. Spice wise, it's mild for me... particularly when compared to competing brands. With Dave's, I'd put a couple of drops on my food and the level of heat was fantastic. With Da Bomb, I'm dumping this stuff on my food and adding some habanero powder on top to give me my fix.Bottom line -- if you're looking for a really tasty, spicy hot sauce, this probably isn't for you. If you're serious about spice, try the Dave's Gourmet sauce. Amazon doesn't always carry it, but it's worth hunting down. Just don't waste your time with this.

I thought it'd be a great idea to get this since it's better than paying a bunch for a single bottle online. I also assumed quantity equals quality...GOOD: doesn't override taste of the food you put it in (in moderate amounts), very spicyBAD: smells bad and tastes bad in large quantities (you may like it though, but I "tolerate" it), doesn't give that nice hot-sauce body glow (for me, anyways), more likely to cause a stomachacheOverall, try other hot sauces at your local store before this. And don't expect it to taste good if you pile it on.I edited this review from a 3-star to a 4-star because I discovered that this doesn't taste bad or give you a stomachache if you DON'T PUT TOO MUCH ON. Seriously, it's pretty good stuff in moderation.

Reviewing this product as a training treat:First and foremost, the dog loves this treat better than any other food/treat item.  Better than meat, better than cheese, better than other dog or cat foods.  Five stars for taste.  The dog will work for this treat.  There are a couple less-than-optimal factors with this treat, though.  It is a dry treat.  It is also a low-density dry treat (low-density being better than high-density, because of the number of treats required per session).  Dry treat means crumbs everywhere with extra cleanup.  The dog spends too much time searching for dropped crumbs and not enough time training.  Trainers also recommend a moderately moister treat for other reasons.  For example, dry treats require drinking interruptions, moist don't.  The treat size is way too large for a training treat.  We go through a couple dozen "payouts" in a session, so treats should be small.  This means breaking up the biscuits into smaller chips with a whole lot more crumbs.Recommend the manufacturer 1) shrink the treat size to about the size of a green-pea, 2) Is it possible to create a moist(er) treat with the same flavor incentive?  Accomplishing #1 might be sufficient, because without needing to break up the biscuits, the crumb factor would go way down.Bottom Line: The dog loves this treat.

The only downside I have noticed is that it makes his stools VERY smelly - not sure if this is because he's sensitive to an ingredient or a result of the probiotics/supplements the food contains.

column9: Confident giving this to my dog
column10: After careful research on the best dry food for my dog's diet, I chose Wellness Core Reduced Fat. My mixed breed dog is low energy and has a tendency to put weight on easily. It was very difficult to find a dog food that does not compromise quality ingredients to make a food low fat. Since my dog is low energy (by no means a sled dog), her diet does not require her to have extreme protein intake. This food is the prefect balance of protein, quality meat sources, fat content, as well as important sources of fruits and vegetables and fish oils.  Her eyes are bright and coat is shiny. While she hasn't lost any weight, she hasn't gained any either, which is a good thing!You get what you pay for when it comes to dog food. When purchasing this brand, one is paying for high quality food (meat content, veggies, fruits) without fillers or extreme levels of protein.For a more comprehensive analysis of dog food, check out [...]

column9: I definitely would buy from this seller again
column10: I got it on time, the package was in perfect conditions, it was as described and I definitely will buy from this seller again.I would really like if this seller have PAYPAL as a payment option, this would make it perfect for everyone!
We have not tried these yet as they just arrived today, but they are NOT organic as the description says.

This is the kind of cinnamon, cassia cinnamon that has been touted in various "health" conscious magazines since summer 2011. This 12 oz container of cassia bark was a much better price than the pulverzied baking forms of cassia cinnamon that cost two or three times the price for only 3-4 oz of product. But, you get what you pay for and this bark is very durable (hard), so it takes awhile but with my Osterizer pulse-matic I can pulverize into granuals that mix with astragalus tea or green tea for a nice morning beverage. Also, this granular form cooks well and is palatable in oatmeal and other hot breakfast meals. Also, bark pieces that I have not broke down are good to put next to my gums, it has a bitter-sweet spicey taste without the nicotine that tobacco use would give. I never was into tobacco use, but hey, maybe someone trying to give up "chew" might try cassia bark as a natural alternative.

column9: The best dark choclolate you can buy!
column10: I had tried this choclate at a food show a few years back, and i do look forward to purchasing this product whenever i can!  worth the price!!

I was waiting for a friend to check out at a U Penn food court, and she asked if I wanted anything. I rather mindlessly noticed Berkshire Bark in a display stand and handed her a bar, which she paid for. Imagine my shock when I looked it up on Amazon and found this "candy bar" is priced at $5.99! Absolutely wonderful chocolate -- but embarrassingly expensive, especially when it's on a friend's tab! Sorry, but 6 bucks for less than 3 ounces is just ridiculous. I won't be buying my own (but I owe my friend a drink!).

I love this chocolate and the Midnight Harvest flavor.  The dark chocolate has a wonderful rich flavor.  An unlike many other bars trying to capitalize on this idea, they have whole nuts and dried fruits, not indescribable little slivers. Keep up the good work!

This chocolate is practically good for you.  Dark chocolate, hazelnuts and almonds, cranberries...and orange zest.  It's pretty much impossible not to gobble up the entire bar as soon as you open it.  But it's, like, full of antioxidants so that's okay.

I bought this to be shipped to me in Afghanistan. The packets are packaged in a box, and I use the box as a dispensary. I love that I can ways keep 3-5 packets in my pocket. A few for me, and one or two for whoever happens to notice. These are much more portable than the traditional glass bottles I've had shipped to me before, and a lot less likely to be abused/stolen.I really enjoy the flavor of Tapatio as opposed to other sauces whose main ingredient seems to be vinegar. Just enough heat to let you know it's there, and the flavor compliments everything you put it on. I use it on eggs, pizza, chicken, beef, popcorn, nacho cheese flavored tortilla chips, and even schnitzel, believe it or not.This is one purchase I will definitely do again when the time comes.

Caveman Bakery has made the best tasting, yummiest, freshest gluten free, high protein cookies!  Plus they are lower in calories than most cookies.  They do indeed taste old fashioned.  For those of us sensitive to gluten, they are agreat alternative to being able to enjoy a cookie while staying "safe" from gluten or corn products.  I took a couple with me when we went to see Avatar on Christmas - I was very happy to have them while the guys were enjoying eating theirpopcorn.  This item will be a staple in our home for holidays, special occasions, or going to the movies.I do have one big problem with these cookies.  They are so delish that I have difficulty in only eating two per day.A friend recently told me that she could never follow the strict anti-inflammatory diet that I do.  I told her that I know how bad I felt and it's not worth it to me not to follow it.  That's one big reason why I am so excited about these Caveman Cookies.

This is the perfect treat for any Paleo-dieters out there!!  Although the cookies were a little thinner than I expected them to be, they are pretty dense and filling.  I recently tried all three flavors that Caveman Bakery offers and all of them are excellent.  I think I might just order a whole bunch and hand them out during the Holidays.  Gluten free is the way to go!

column9: Perfect for what they should be used for!
column10: These are a great grain-free treat! I do believe that the fresher the food, the healthier it is for you. And nothing is fresher than making your food from fresh ingredients straight from your kitchen! Sometimes, however, you don't have access to a kitchen. I bought some of these to see if I liked them. (I actually bought the sample packs of all four flavors.) The reason I did so is because I'm going to be in the hospital in a few months attempting a VBAC, but I might be there for more than a few days if the attempt fails and I end up with another c-section. Because I react to even the tiniest bit of all grains, and because I don't trust the people at the hospital to really know how to handle that (although I'm more afraid of grains in meds they will try to give me), it's great to know that I can order a few snacks before hand and bring them with me without having to worry about them going bad or making me sick.So would I recommend eating or buying them for regular consumption? No. But for situations similar to mine I think they are perfect.The cookie itself is of a soft, chewy nature - as one would expect with ingredients like honey and almond flour. Personally, I enjoyed all of the flavors except for the Alpine - but read the ingredients and see if it contains things that you would normally enjoy. I believe this one in particular contains a bit of cinnamon, which combined with the raisins creates a nice cinnamon-oatmeal-raisin sort of flavor (the texture is completely different, obviously). I liked this one the best. The rainforest and the tropical flavors were very good as well, and both of them have a hint of a kick to them due to the pepper and ginger.
I found the cookies to be DEE-LISH-US! The shipment was SPEEDY, and the experience was TOTALLY pleasurable.  I highly recommend 'em :)

The cookies are moist and chewy. They might be a bit on the sweet side, I'm guessing that's the honey in them, but they're still great. I'm very happy with my purchase, I'll be ordering more in the future!

I'm constantly on the hunt for foods that are Paleo friendly, to toss into my kiddo's school lunch or take with us as we're running out of the house and I haven't prepared otherwise. I have to say, of the cookies out there, these are by far the best and really only viable option for a grain-free, gluten-free quick and simple snack.Chewy, full of flavor and they let me feel good about letting my kiddo have a "cookie".

Very delicious and the ingredients are probably very close to what our ancestors had access too but I still worry about the amount of sugars in such a small serving size. Definitely healthier than your typical Chips-ahoy  but I feel the sugar content is too high for a low carb dieter.
I ate two cookies. I ate the second one after I decided that the first one couldn't have been so bad. I was wrong.

column9: Great taste but not low cal
column10: As someone who has gone Paleo diet for weight control reasons as opposed to gluten allergies, I was looking for something that stuck with the restriction of the diet while still offering satisfaction in taste and satiety.  Up till now I have been using coconut flour and other low cal ingredients to tend to that snack/indulgence urge, but its a hassle and prone to heating up the house too much with the oven use.  These cookies come in small, individually wrapped servings, about the size and thickness of a oreo's single waffer.  They are dense and chewy and give a fairly pleasant experience both in mouth feel and taste, in fact they taste IMHO better than most home baked cookies, and even better than what I made for myself.However don't expect them to arrive with a week or so, I guess they make them in small controlled batches (given the individual packaging this wouldn't surprise me) and that takes time.  I tried all 3 and though all were great, I liked the oatmeal raisin the most.  I will definitely keep a few bags of these on hand as I think they should freeze pretty well and I can thaw them in small batches, my only complaint about them is their size and calorie density, for how good they taste, I want to be able to eat a lot more than I should lol.
Not fresh tastingWay too expensiveNot worth the cost,I would not recommend, there must be better alternatives to this product.

These cookies are great!  We had our first taste when these "Original" cookies were the only Caveman Cookies around, and though we've tried the others our heart still lies with these.  We've stored them in our cupboard for several months and found them to be just as good as when we first opened the package.  Very delicious, and filling if you don't let yourself sit down with the box and absent-mindly munch away.  If you're looking for cookies without all the processed preservatives and only a few, easy-to read ingredients, these cookies are amazing.  If you're looking for a cookie that's cheap, are okay with loads of processed sugar and don't mind an intense ingredients list, then any cookie off the 7-11 shelf will probably be your preferred choice.And if you didn't get this vibe from the other reviews, these are incredibly tasty!

Great flavor and texture! The main sweetener is honey, so if you are not a honey fan, you may not be fond of these. Fortunately I love honey :)  They were chewy and satisfying. A bit on the small size, but you really only need 2 cookies.

I purchased four boxes - one of each variety for around 40 bucks total. These things are the size of an oreo and you're paying almost a dollar a cookie and they're way too sweet. You have to be crazy to spend this kind of money on these things. I'll take the Kashi cookies any day over these. They may be healthier than Kashi but you'll tire of Caveman real quick and I still have some in the fridge because they're horrible and I can't even finish them off. Dr. Oz recommended these cookies and it cost me $40 bucks to find out I hate them. Save your money and buy KASHI. Enjoy a real cookie for God's sake. I can't believe this company can stay in business with these overpriced novelties.

I was enchanted by the packaging design only to be disappointed by the taste.  If you are a true cookie connoisseur then these aren't for you. First they are individually wrapped, something that always seems wasteful to me. Yes, I understand that it keeps them fresh, but there are other solutions.  Also the images make them look larger than they are.  They basically fit in the palm of your hand.If you are looking for something similar to a Kashi cookie I would try these.  If you are looking for something on parity to a homemade cookie, don't count on it.

..and I won't because cookies aren't paleo! Snacking isn't really paleo, and processed food is most definitely not paleo! This is a gluten-free cookie, a processed factory food. If you have celiac, I'd guess these are your best cookie option, but cookies are not healthy natural food. People! Seriously!

Don't get me wrong, I still love Reese's Peanut Butter Cups, but after trying these there is a definite difference in how they're processed. When I first tried the Nectar Nugget Peanut Butter Cup I was surprised at how smooth and creamy the peanut butter was - imagine a spoonful taken right from a jar. This is not at all like the firm, grainy, very sweet filling of the Reese's cup. In addition the chocolate was very good, in fact it begins to melt in your hand the minute you remove it from the wrapper, which is why I'd suggest eating it out of the wrapper. These were definitely a treat and something I'm glad I was able to try while they were on special here on Amazon, but unless Amazon restocks them or I am able to find them locally, I probably won't be buying them again anytime soon at the current 3rd party pricing. I would definitely pay a premium for these, but anything more than $15 a box is too much in my opinion.

I ordered these to see how they would ship because I wanted to order them as gifts. It is mid-March, upstate NY, so it's pretty cold here now. Most of the candies arrived in a semi-melted state or most of them were broken or crushed. They are wonderful snacks, but I think they need to be purchased directly from a store and not sent through the mail.

column9: Unfortunately mail order is not the way to go with these.
column10: These are by far the best cups I have ever eaten, when they are fresh.  Had my order been fresh, this product would've gotten 5 stars, there are no other cups quite like these, they are divine.  But find a whole food or organic store near you and see if they can buy in bulk for you.  I did, and I get them by the box in my hometown and, let me tell you, the box doesn't last long... these are DELICIOUS.
This is hands-down the best peanut butter cup sold. It must be eaten to believed, unfortunately it is hard to find...

I bought 1 can of the Pumpkin Spice Latte at my local Target store. Immediately came home to prepare a cup and boy was it delicious!!! So good infact that I now have it sent to me (via Amazon Subscribe and Save) every 2 months....very inexpensive on Amazon....It's $13.79 for 6 cans delivered to my front door. Highly recommend:))))

Bought this for my mom after her local Starbucks stopped offering the Pumpkin Spice Latte (I guess it's a seasonal drink they don't offer year-round). It tastes pretty good, nice and foamy, though the flavor is slightly different from Starbucks'. It makes crackling sounds (must be the cinnamon) when you add it to the warm milk, which I thought was cool. You really get your money's worth with this one.

Good flavour, nice foam.  I like that you only need 4 tsp to make a cup (some of these International coffees need up to 6 tsp) so this particular flavour will last a bit longer.  For the price of a single can of this (which you can make about 8 drinks from) you can get a single Grande Pumpkin Spice Latte from Starbucks... This is good for your bank account, too!

Several years ago in a Target grocery aisle far, far away I found Maxwell House International Cafe Pumpkin Spice latte. (Formerly General Foods International Coffees. Remember the "Jean Luc" commercial? Yes, that stuff.) It was a limited edition flavor... it was on clearance... I bought all the tins that remained... even the one with the huge dent. This stuff was that good. Then it was gone and all I had left was a single empty tin to remind me that this flavor wasn't something I only imagined or conjured up in a dream. Now it is finally back! It has a different formula that becomes distinctly frothier but it tastes just as mmm, mmm good as I remember.

column9: Not what I was hoping for.
column10: This did not have the flavor I was hoping for.  It is a little too heavy on the coffee taste and not sweet enough.  It really doesn't taste like pumpkin spice drinks I have enjoyed other places.
This product is the closest I've come to finding the pumpkin spice latte at 711...it only comes out in the fall so stock up!
$52 for 6 cans.  What made this jump to such an overpriced item?  Love the stuff but won't be paying almost $9.00 a can.
Great product. I love the real coffee house taste of all Maxwell international products.  The pumpkin spice is without a doubt my favorite!!

After reading the other reviews and discovering that the Pumpkin Spice Latte was no longer available in the grocery stores, I thought I had truly missed out on a great new flavor.  Well after receiving my six cans, at almost ten bucks a can, I can honestly say the only flavor I taste is sugar!  Hmmm, could this be because sugar is the first ingredient listed?  I was expecting a pumpkin spice taste, but it's just not there.  In fact, the "coffee" is so bland I'm considering adding a teaspoon or two to a cup of my regular coffee just so the entire order isn't a bust.  What a disappointment!

column9: The taste of fall all year round
column10: I personally always look forward to the fall, the weather changes, the holidays are just around the corner, and of course pumpkin spice makes a comeback.  If you are like me and are constantly craving pumpkin spice this is a great product.  I love latte's and this is a convenient way to cure my cravings without leaving the house.  The only real downside to the product is that it's a little high in sugar (8g per 1 1/3 tbsp), but other than that its a great product.  It reminds me of fall, and its great to have it year round.  This is definitely a great addition to your coffee for that extra punch of flavor.

column4: ChibiNeko "Sooo many books, so little time!"
column10: I got this a few weeks ago and I have to say, I almost think I've wasted my money. This is just an incredibly disappointing drink.I wasn't expecting much from this, so it's not like I was expecting this to taste like a freshly made professional drink or even a cup of pumpkin spice coffee from Wawa. I expected something that would taste good but more importantly I was expecting something that actually had the taste of pumpkin spice to it. I didn't get that in this drink. It's decent enough to where I'm willing to bring it to work and let my coworkers drink it (I'm not mean enough to bring nasty tasting things for them to finish off), but it's definitely something that I know I won't be finishing off on my own.My recommendation is that if you absolutely must try this drink, wait for it to go on sale. I like some of the other drinks MHI puts out, but this was just disappointing.

I've been drinking these Maxwell House international coffees for years, but this pumpkin spice latte was a new flavor for me.  Well, it's also now my new favorite flavor.  This is just as handy and easy to make as all the others.  If you have any kind of taste for pumpkin flavored items, I'm sure you'll also like this as much as I do.

I found this product online after deciding that keeping 7-11 in business single-handedly with my pumpkin latte addiction wasn't the best choice for my wallet. I'd read online that this is the same mix that 7-11 uses-but it's a lie! This mix has much more spice in it (or maybe I just got a bad batch), and since I'm technically allergic to cinnamon, I can't really enjoy this. I'm bummed out because now I have I bunch of unopened tins of the stuff. I'm thinking of making care packages just to give them away.
I'm so glad I found this on Amazom. I have never seen it at my grocery store, so this was new to me. I just love the flavor.
This has a quite good pumpkin flavor, however, by the time I had finished the can, I had had enough. No more for me.
Why am I getting emails from Amazon to review something I didn't get? They were out of this product, so there is nothing to review. I rated it one star because I had to rate it.

I have breastfeed two children and have tried every breast milk storage bag on the market and after trying them all I landed on lansinoh storage bags and used them for 2 years with my first child. After I had my second child I decided to look into the market again to see if there was a better bag for reasons: better for enviroment, cost effective and no leaks. Well I tried the honey suckle brand because they were everything I was looking for with very good reviews so I bought 300 bags.Well im terribly disapppointed, THEY LEAK! I have had them leak by just setting them on the table the bottom seal pops open, during thawing process, and ive had a few that were thawed and placed in fridge and all of the sudden started leaking for no reason. Evertime it is the bottom seal.I tried to contact the company by email several times to let them know of the problem im having so they can hopefully prevent this problem for furture customers but no response..In the 300 bags I purchased probably 100 leaked, some I could save some milk while others lost all which is very furstrating
No complaints. Great for storing baby's pureed food. I was thrilled to find a bulk amount of bags at a great price.

column9: Great bags!  And a great deal!
column10: These are great bags for a great price!  I had 1 or 2 bags leak, but out of the hundreds I used, I can't complain.  I like them much better than Medela (too small, and too stiff) and Lansinoh (too flimsy and thin).  Bonus!  They are biodegradable!  Ditto to Raivyn's comments.  You won't be disappointed.

Don't know much about milk bag brands or styles, but I do know this one is biodegradable, comes in two sizes and works like a charm. We freeze them lying down so we can file them flat by date in a rectangle container in the freezer.

I was using a different bag for 4 months now (Lansinoh) and got these bags from Milkin Mamas breast milk donation. They are much better bags! more reinforced on the bottom where my other bags would occasionally leak. More reinforced on the sides. Completely tamper free. & they are similar in price!

These bags are wonderful. After trying four other kinds of bags, these are the best - and cheapest! These bags hold a large volume and do not leak. They are cheaper than other brands and I will purchase these from now on.

I like these better than the lansinoh ones which are the only other ones I've tried. The bags feel thicker, more sturdy, etc. Seal well, double zip lock seems secure. The bags being a little thicker, they freeze nicer. I lay them flat to freeze, but with the Lansinoh bags, I felt like they were too soft and deformed during the freezing process which makes them hard to stack later for storage. I don't have that problem with these bags. We haven't had any issues with thawing milk in these bags either. The price is good, especially in the bulk package so I'm a happy customer.Just wanted to update, I've been using these for 3 months now, and am still very happy with the result.
I'm a repeat buyer. I have froze over 300 bags of milk so far and not one has leaked. Good price. Fast shipping too.

I have been using these bags since I came back to work full-time. They are durable and do the job well. I also love that they are more environmentally friendly. Somebody had mentioned not having space to write out the amount, but I just put that in the space above where I write out my daughter's name and the date as there is plenty of room.

I'm a huge overproducer and have stored over 8000oz using these milk bags. Because of the amount I produced, I also stored 6-8oz in each bag. Only 2 bags have leaked out of the thousand+ I've gone through. The seam on the sides are much thicker and stronger than Lansinoh bags.  If I have another baby, I will not hesitate to use them again.

Bought the bag just a few weeks ago.  I ordered the 100 pack.  Only 1 50 pack was accidentally sent and when contacting the company, they replied back pretty fast and let me know that the other 50 was on its way.  5 star on the customer service!  Now on to the bags.  I LOVE them!  I really like the fact that they are very VERY affordable and a great product as well.  The bags are durable, tamper proof and has a place for me to write the name, date and amount.  I am back at work and I use these bags every day.  When I'm low, I will definitely be buying more along with the baby food storage too.

I go through a lotta bags, up to 5 a day. I'm amazed and happy to have discovered this product: it's cheaper than the others, can come in a case of 300, works just as well, and is biodegradable to boot. We don't recycle plastic bags in my town, so this makes me feel less guilty about having to throw 5 plastic bags/day into the trash!

I've been using these bags for only three weeks now, and so far no complaints. They seal easily, haven't leaked yet, quality feel and thickness, and can either stand up or lie flat in the freezer. They are larger than I thought - can hold up to six ounces. Although, I do wonder if the oz count is correct - I pump into marked bottles (from two different manufacturers) and when I transfer the milk into the bag, it usually shows a larger volume based on the ounce markers than the bottles. But it doesn't bother me at all. Also - hard to beat this price, I compared a lot of different milk storage bags before buying.

Nice storage bags and the cheapest ones. At first I was concern with quality (didn't want to spend too much and be stuck with junk). So far I had only one bag that leaked out of 30 or so, which is very impressive. Although i don't know if the bag leaks when you thou the milk in the fridge, since "Lansinoh" brand had this problem most of the time. Overall very happy with product.

I love these bags. I love that they are biodegradable. I can lay them flat in my freezer and not worry about leaking. The have a very strong seal and good base to pour the milk. I like the space to write on the bags. Great customer service and prompt attention to any issues I had. Great service! Thanks Honeysuckle!

This bags are wonderful.  We use multiple bags a day and they have yet to leak!  I am very impressed.  It seems to be a great price for such a large quantity.  I would most definitely order these again.
I bought these after reading the reviews & I'm so happy I did. So much better than the medela bags I was using. Highly recommend them.

column9: Bought these for a milk donor
column10: My daughter has had some issues with failure to thrive and other medical conditions. Because of this, I couldn't keep up with her demand and had to do something. We were fortunate enough to find some amazing women willing to donate milk to my daughter. We had been buying bags for our donors to store the milk in and finally, after buying a box here and a box there, I decided to look into some bulk options.I found these bags and I was a little skeptical but have been pleasantly surprised! When we go to thaw the milk, we have had far fewer leaky bags with the honeysuckle bags than with lansinoh or medela bags! Anyone who has used thawed milk knows exactly how tragic a leaky bag can be!Great bags and a great price!
Considering the price, these bags are a great value - as easy to use as other bags and even better quality.

I wish I had discovered these bags 5 months ago!  I have tried the Medela (too small, stiff plastic, spill easily) and the Lanisnoh (frequent leaks) and was desperate for a milk storage solution that wouldn't take up our entire freezer (i.e, glass bottles).  The Honeysuckle bags arrived sooner than expected and I put them to use immediately.  After 3 weeks of use I can say I'm impressed - the plastic is much more flexible that the other brands I've tried, making defrosting much less of a gamble.  I feel less concerned that a frozen milk chunk will penetrate the bag and the seams appear stronger than the Lanisnoh. The size is great (I store 4-5oz at a time), and there is plenty of room to mark the date and amount. Great product!

These bags are just "okay". Lansinoh bags are more durable, easier to pour into and out of, and the form at the top of the bag makes more sense. It's also much easier to push the air out of the Lansinoh bags before sealing.

These bags are AWESOME!!!  I got 50 of these bags to try after trying the Lansinoh bags.  The Lansinoh bags were ok but just seemed too thin so I searched Amazon for other bag options.  I read quite a few reviews on these and decided to try them and I am glad I did.  The price is reasonable, there is more room in mu deep freezer, and I like the fact that they are biodegradable.  Great bags!!!

Update 2/7/12:I just got an additional order of these. The new bags do have a spot for volume to be written.Also the bags were shipped in a very discrete brown box with no extra writing on them to say breastmilk bags, so that was nice.-------------------------------I was introduced to these bags when I started donating extra breastmilk. All I have to say is OMG sooo awesome. I wish they were available in stores. Previously I was using Lansinoh and I had sooo many leaky bags. I felt so bad for my daycare because it seemed like every other bag I was bringing them were springing leaks. I haven't had a single leaky bag with these.Yes there is limited writing room in the official spaces, but there is plenty of room above the boxes to write in the volume or whatever else you want to write.If you are looking for bags, buy these! I've tried all the other ones and these are the only ones I haven't had problems with. And yes, I have completely filled them with 14ounces of milk and haven't had any problems with freezing or thawing.

Previous to the Honeysuckle my wife was using the Lansinoh bags.  I remember some issues with the Lansinoh bags rupturing while she would thaw the frozen milk so we decided to try a different product when our second child arrived.  My wife is pumping exclusively and ever since we started using the Honeysuckle I think we only had 1 or 2 occasions where the bag leaked.  What is particularly nice about these bags is that they are biodegradable.  It makes us feel good to know that we are using a product that is environmentally friendly.

These are great milk bags. They are the best deal I have found out there plus they are supposedly biodegradable in the landfill. My husband uses them while I am at work. He says they are the best bags we have used so far. They heat the milk up well in a glass of water and pour the milk into a bottle well. They are thin enough to heat the milk well but thick enough to be quite durable. I will buy them again.

These have potential to be great, if not for the leaks.  The bag is well designed and lays flat to store which is all good, but we have had 1 out of 3 leak, usually around where the ziplock ends. Not sure if we got a bad batch, but having to throw away 1 out of every 3 makes this a much more expensive product, not to mention the spilled milk.

For those of us that express milk like cows, the most important quality in a breastmilk bag has got to be limited leaking. Any bag is going to leak if it gets bumped around too much or folds improperly while freezing. Out of over 120 of these bags used, I have had one leak. Less than 1% leaking is acceptable to me.The other bag I would recommend is Simplisse (http://www.amazon.com/Simplisse-Breastmilk-Storage-Bags-Pack/dp/B00363M0Q0), which are double-walled. I have used over 50 of those and one has leaked.Both types store flat in the freezer, which is a huge plus. (I used Medela with my first baby, and these did not lay flat.)

These bags seem very thick and strong. The bottoms are reinforced. I've never had a leak (but I do not freeze a lot of milk). Every bag is sealed at the top and you have to remove the plastic top where it's perforated, which gives me peace of mind that each bag is sterile. The measuring on the front is accurate, but you must expand the bottom of the bag to get the accurate reading. There's not a designated spot for volume (which is nice for freezing flat) but there's plenty of writable space to put it if you want.I don't freeze a lot - my daughter goes to daycare 6 hours a day so I usually just send in the fresh milk that I pumped the day before. At the end of the week, if there is milk leftover besides the milk I pumped on Friday (to use on Monday), I freeze it. I really like these bags and will continue to buy them if I need more.

column9: These are the best bags i've ever used.
column10: I first was introduced to these bags through their free sample. I've been pumping/freezing milk for 11 months as well as nursing. I started with the Lansinoh® Breastmilk Storage Bags because they were available in the store to me. I had SEVERAL leaky bags and lost close to 50 ounces of milk. Anyone who is nursing knows this is a heartbreak. I switched over to Honeysuckle bags and have had NO leaks. The plastic is thicker and more durable. I freeze mine flat then put them upright for storage. They thaw quickly and store easily. These bags i would HIGHLY recommend and have bought many as shower gifts. I also love they are a small business and their customer service is quick and friendly. LOVE YOU HONEYSUCKLE!

I've never used this kind of bags before. People told me that bags werent secure, that they use to leak etc etc But I havent had any problem using this ones, they have a good quality and a great price. I looked for many bags before taking the desicion to buy this ones and I can tell you that they were the best I could find in the market in terms of price/quality.

I searched for breast milk storage bags for months prior to deciding on which ones to get & I am super happy that these are the ones I bought!  I asked my sister who used Lansinoh if she ever had any leak & she had quite a few that did, just like a lot of other people stated in their reviews.  When I bought some Lansinoh nursing pads, they had 2 of their bags inside & you can tell a HUGE difference in the quality.  They both claim to have a "double zipper", but only the Honeysuckle bags hold true to that.  The Lansinoh bags has one decent zipper & a line, I wouldn't even constitute as a zipper.  With these Honeysuckle bags, I have not had ANY leak out of the 300 bags (& 6 months later) I have filled & used.  Yea, there is no designated space to write the ounces, but there is plenty of space above the name & date.  I write the amount on the tip of the "bottle" on the bag.  Has worked great.Also the company had super fast shipping which I was originally worried about it taking a week or two to arrive, but they were at my house within 3-5 days of me placing the order.  Would recommend to anyone & I plan on buying a whole bunch more!

After losing so much breast milk while using the Lansinoh brand bags, someone turned me on to this brand. I'd never heard of them before, but am so, so glad I did. They are wonderful, they hold large amounts of milk very well, are sturdy and thick and so far, I've never had a problem with them leaking. I'm so happy I found these, I'll never buy another Lansinoh bag again.

I have been EBF for 5.5 months and pumping a bottle a day as well. I have gone through LOTS of these bags and never experienced a leak. I love how there is a three tear system to get into the bag and they are very sturdy. The main reason I bought them was because they are recyclable and biodegradable! This is a big concern of mine. I donate milk and have never heard bad things about these bags from my milk bank or donors.

I got some hand-me-down Lansinoh breastmilk bags when I went back to work three months after my little one was born, and after the third leak I decided to start looking for an alternative. These fit the bill perfectly--no leaks so far, and I love the fact that they're biodegradable.

I have used several other brands but none compare to Honey Suckle. I received a free sample and since then I haven't even thought about buying another brand. They are easy to use and do not leak like others I've tried. When DS is eating foods I'll try the baby food bags.
So much easier to close than the Medela ones. I love these. So glad I got them. The only downside is they kind of slouch over more in the freezer but that really hasn't mattered all that much.
I loved these bags when I was breastfeeding. The are so much better than the Lansinoh brand. They hold more volume and the material is stronger (will not bust in the freezer).

After much research I decided on these bags because of its features (biodegradable and BPA and PVC free).  Have proven to be an excellent choice.  Super easy to use, my sitter loves them.  lay flat in freezer for easy storage.

I travel for work and wanted a bag that would be reliable, durable and convenient. In addition to Honeysuckle, I tried Lansinoh, Medela, Ameda and Simplisse. Honeysuckle was the best. Lansinoh was similar to Honeysuckle in that they are larger and easier to zip, but the bags are a little thin and would sometimes stick to the freezer and/or other bags. The "easy pour spout" of Ameda wasn't any easier than pouring out of any of the other bags. Medela was the worst - horrible zipper making it hard to get out the air and you were never sure it was fully zipped. The only advantage Medela has is that you could pump directly into them. So, I just cut little slights in the Honeysuckle bags and pump directly into them using the adaptors that came with the Medela bags. These bags are wonderul!

I've been pumping and EBF for nine months now and recently switched over to these bags. I had such high hopes for them after reading the reviews and my initial experiences with them were fine. In fact, I love the design and size and the fact that I could lay them flat in the freezer and then move them upright for storage as a space saver. The problem?  I recently had two bags in a row leak. I have never had this happen before with any other bags and it was clear that the leaks were coming from the side seams and not due to punctures or improper sealing of the bags.  The bags were not overfilled or stored improperly.  It is so time-consuming and difficult to pump and try to keep up a decent stash that it was heartbreaking to see my milk go to waste like this. I was so upset that this is the reason I am writing this review -- I'm a frequent Amazon shopper but this is the first time I felt compelled to comment on a product.  I don't know if my remaining bags are okay or not but it's just not worth the risk.

column9: Great bags, no issues, freeze and defrost well and love that they are biodegratable.
column10: I have nothing but good things to say about these bags.  No issues thus far.  They freeze well, they defrost fine, no leaks, and pour out easily.  They appear thin but are strong.  I would recommend them as they end up being cheaper in the long run with this bulk 300 bag purchase for $44.99

These bags are not only priced wonderfully (cheaper than you can get bags at a local store), they're also very sturdy. When I'm going to freeze my milk I only put about 6 ounces in the bag per recommendations (which is really closer to 7 because the bag's markings are off) but when I'm just storing milk in the fridge I put all the milk from my pumping session, which varies from 9 to almost 12 ounces. And the bag holds it! Not only that, but I had a full bag fall off the top shelf of the refrigerator and it landed on the bottom, intact. Yay for dual closures and sturdy plastic!

I'd been paying $23.00 for the 100 count bag of Medela breastmilk bags at the local BuyBuy Baby.  I go through a LOT of bags, because I want to have another child.  This baby is an IVF baby, and the next one will have to be as well.  My son has to be weaned from the breast for three months before I can cycle again, so I pump and freeze three times a day, because I want him to have enough breastmilk to see him through until at least 18 months.  I was going through bags like crazy and spending tons of money.  There's nothing wrong with the Medela bags, other than the fact that they are pretty pricey.  I found they Honeysuckle bags while searching on Amazon, and I just had to give them a try.  I'm so glad I did, because I certainly wasn't disappointed.  They are strong.  I haven't had one tear, and I haven't had any leaks either, which says a lot since I freeze my bags flat instead of upright.  I'll be buying these again.

I purchased these after reading reviews on Amazon.  I have used several other brands of bags and have found that I really trust these over the other brands.  They appear more substantial than other bags and to date I have not had a problem with leaks.
These bags are great quality for the cost! I will definitely keep buying them. I also lovet aht they are biodegradable. They freeze flat very easily and are very thick to prevent leaks. Great!

column9: Requested samples, but then just went for it.....
column10: I have been using Medela, Lansinoh, The First Years, and Nuk bags.  Up until I tried these, the NUK were my favorite.  Here are the features I love about Honeysuckle Bags:1.  The bags hold so much milk (I freeze in 5oz. quantities) and still freeze flat2.  Dual-ziplock bag to prevent leaks3.  Sealed top to ensure sterility4.  They are biodegradable and better for the environmentI am disappointed to see so many women complaining about not receiving the free samples on Facebook.  They're free!  It is not like the company didn't fill a paid order.  It is a nice gesture that the company was even offering them, but at some point you have to just decide if you want to make the purchase.  I initially requested samples, but then I just placed an order and I have no regrets.

I was in the NICU when I got my free sample. I shared my sample with another mom with twins and one of my lansinoh bags. I tried out the one bag and was happy. Not to waste I used up the lansinoh bags, made sure I was getting a better price on the Honeysuckle and ordered the 75ct, as I wasn't sure I still needed the 300ct (supermega-producer in the beginning). Well I'm sad that I didn't order MORE (just a super-producer now). So I didn't save as much money. But very happy with the bags. I made boxes out of paperboard with a hole at the bottom to pull out the "oldest" milk similar to the gift bag idea. Halfof my 7 cu. ft freezer is full!  Also these are such a great deal I'm planning on donating some to a woman in Brazil that lost her baby and is producing for the local NICU. Buy the bags, you'll love them!

We haven't yet thawed out any of these bags so I cannot yet remark about strength. It doesn't really matter...I thaw my bags in a container. It's just a safety net no matter what (and a no brainer if you ask me).  My main motivation was cost. At 15 cents a bag, vs 20 cents a bag for the lansinoh, I was sold. We go thru approx 1 case of these every 35 days. It's a savings of $15. Not everybody will need 300 bags but my daughter is on 100% donor milk and we thaw approx 8 bags a day. The free shipping is great, and it's fast. With alot of babies on donor milk, moms really need more options out there because the cost adds up!

I recently had several hundred ounces of milk shipped to us from the women who donates milk for our son...I purchased a bulk pack of these bags for her and I received the first shipment a few weeks ago.  I am sad to report that 95% of the bags have leaked...I had such high hopes for these bags but have since gone back to Lansinoh, while I had a fair amount of leaks with them it was nothing like this! I usually defrost 6 bags at a time and all 6 usually leak out the side seams and/or top.  Needless to say defrosting milk has become a total nightmare! Our donor only put the recommended 6 oz in each bag, froze them flat and shipped them with care. I was careful putting the bags into the deep freeze so this was not a user issue.  If you're planning to ship or freeze any milk I would definitely not use these bags.

I was using Lansinoh bags, because those were recommended to me. I live in a fairly rural area and those are the ONLY bags available in a 35 minute radius. Ordering these is actually less expensive (no tax and free shipping, which means I don't have to go to the store)and the bags are better quality. The side seams are thicker and so is the plastic and I have not had a problem with leaks. These are BIODEGRADABLE and tamper resistant(the others were not). I am on my fourth box of these. They will fit at least 12 ounces, but I usually only freeze 6 to 8 ounces at a time for convenience. Great bags overall...the ONLY problems are that there is no place to mark how much you put in the bag and the markings seem very generous on the outside; example...if you put in 6 ounces it looks like you only have 5. Overall I have been very happy with them and plan on ordering more next month.

column9: Better than Lansinoh or Medela bags
column10: After 7 months of pumping I tried these on a whim and really like them. They are around the same size as the Lansinoh bags, but I had several instances of the Lansinoh leaking when thawing. I never liked the Medela because they are a little smaller and if full (4+ oz) don't freeze flat.Only thing a little strange is that there is no indicator on the label for # of oz (it has a spot for date and baby's name). So a small design flaw. But otherwise, I'm very happy with them.

Hello, my name is J, and I hoard breast milk - and these bags help me do it!  Thanks honeysuckle for feeding my addiction with storing a giant stash of milk.I've used every bag on the market, and since finding these, I won't use any of the other ones because they are THAT awesome.  Now you're probably thinking "why do you want to save so much? (my husband keeps asking me the same thing every time he opens up our chest freezer to see a bunch of paper gift bags stacked with milk)"  Well, with my daughter started teething at 4 mths then had 6 teeth by 8mths, therefore ruining our breastfeeding relationship.  She was also eating like a pig and due to my hectic schedule in the military, I was unable to keep up with her demand, so I burned through my stash quickly and was supplementing formula sooner than I would have liked.  I smartened up with my newest offspring and started pumping early and built up a nice little oversupply.  With that overage, I'm burning through bags left and right.Honeysuckle bags are thicker than others and they easily stand up on their own.  They don't feel remotely flimsy at all or leak in the slightest.  The best part is the biodegradable aspect.  I already feel guilty enough going back to work, I don't have to feel even worse about chocking out landfills with a ridiculous amount of plastic breast milk bags as well.You can also request free samples on their facebook page.  There is also a dollar off coupon code floating around as well.And a tip for storing the milk is to freeze it laying down, then stacking them up.  As said above, I put them in small gift bags, but I know people that have taken the ice cube buckets and stood them up in there.  Depends on what you have room for.Just buy the bags already, its a purchase you won't regret.

column9: Best storage bags I have found!
column10: BEST BAGS EVER! These bags are a good value and they are durable. I was originally using the Lasinoh or Medela bags. Usually whatever was at Wal-Mart.  However, after searching on Amazon, I decided on buying these bags in bulk. I got soooo sick and tired of going to the store 1x a week to buy milk bags. I was actually searching for the lasinoh ones in bulk. Then I came across the honeysuckle bags. These are totally worth it!  Before, I would have to defrost my milk bags in another little ziplock "just in case"... some of my other milk bags would have little kinks and end up leaking.  However, I have had NO PROBLEMS with any of the 200+bags that I have used so far. Also, I'm lazy and don't lay them down systematically. I pretty much just throw them in my deep freeze. No leaks! Like many of the other bags they have a double seal and are easy to write on. You just pull off the little tab at the top and pour in the milk. Once, I opened the bag with a little too much force and it ripped the bag. But that was my only problem and obviously my fault. If you already buying the bags at your local store, then you will be happy with these. Go for it. It is so nice not having to worry about running out of the house at random times to get storage bags.

column9: Good if there is a subscribe & save option too.
column10: These are very good quality bags and i recommend them to all moms who do exclusive pumping. Moms like me need lot of storage bags which are durable. I previously used Lasinoh bags and they used to leak every time. I had returned my recent purchase of lasinoh bags because of leakages and shifted to the Honeysuckle bags.I suggest a Subscribe & Save account for this item so that moms can benefit buying these.

column9: Just take the plunge and buy a box! These are great!
column10: This is a GREAT milk storage bag! I've always had a hard time throwing those plastic bags into the garbage after one use, as they will not decompose for a VERY long time! Well after my grandchildren are born! Having this alternative is spectacular!I would recommend just buying a box, rather than waiting for a sample! I decided to just go for it and I am so glad I did!Big kudos to the creators of this product! These are the small types of products that will help change the world. I know it sounds funny, but it's true! We need this type of design for all of our products - the design for the environment. I really hope the founders of this company go to bed at night feeling great about all of their efforts.

This is the third type of bag that I've tried. The first was Medela which I liked but they were pretty expensive, then simplisse which was a big less expensive than the Medela brand. They worked just as well but I'm always out looking for something better. I'm trying these right now and so far they are just as good as the Simplisse brand when it comes to storage. I don't really but my baby's name on the bag because she's in family care and the caregiver only watches her so i don't have a problem with the small space provided. I just write how many ounces are in each bag in that area. The bags seem a little bit thinner than both the Simplisse and the Medela brand, but they are a bit thicker on the bottom. Maybe that's the part about them being tamper resistant. I freeze my milk flat and in a sandwich bag to save space and they are doing as well as the Simplisse bags. If they holdup in the thaw then I will definitely be hooked on these as they are significantly cheaper than both the Medela and Simplisse brand.
These bags are great because they are double sealed and a great value.When you using 2-3 each day to pump for your LO, value is essential.
These bags are THE BEST.  Hold up to 6oz, that's more than the other bags, they're easy to use, simply love them.

While I do not have anything to compare these bags to, I must say that I am very happy with the Honeysuckle Storage Bags.  Heavy plastic, stay upright when filled, seal easily.  I did have one leak in the defrost- but that may be partially my fault as I left it in water for more than an hour.  Overall, what I expected, and more than enough for my baby's useage (infrequent pumper!)
Surprisingly pleased with the product, especially for the price. Not as thick as Medela bags, better than Lansinoh. Would buy again.

column9: Great bags with one silly problem...
column10: These are great bags. They are sturdy, the closure works well and they freeze and thaw with ease. There is just one really stupid thing they did when making these bags - there is NO PLACE to write the volume. Really? During the testing and development process NO ONE noticed this!? It seems almost impossible to me, yet it's true. Now, don't get me wrong, you can easily write the volume anywhere on the top of the bag, but really? (And, if I'm being picky, the "name" box is a bit too short if you need to write first and last name, which most daycares require.)
Great customer service and good price for product. There is an expensive market for breastfeeding families, especially with storing milk. This was the best price and product I found.

column9: Deceiving marketing tactics means they have lost my business (updated)
column10: **UPDATE** Shortly after posting this review they decided to change the price back to the discount pricing - I'm guessing they were getting a lot of bad press around the new pricing changes.
