This flavor of coffee has the strong aroma and subtle taste of a county style french toast breakfast.  One cup brewed and the whole office is soon joining in the pleasure!

I recently purchased a single-serve coffee maker and love using it. The variety of coffee flavors gives you the opportunity to experience coffee at its best. French Toast flavor is smooth and very tasty.

column9: Fragrant and Delicious ... No Bitter After-Taste
column10: I truly enjoy the taste and aroma of this delicious K-Cup selection, which does indeed remind me of those special mornings during childhood when my mother would make French Toast and serve it to the family with warm maple syrup on the side. The coffee is medium-bodied (I would describe it as "mellow"), and doesn't have the bitter after-taste that so many flavored coffees seem to leave. And I very much like the fact that it is Fair-Trade certified, which means that the coffee grower was paid a living wage for their crop.I heartily recommend this K-Cup flavor, but of course taste is highly subjective ... especially when it comes to coffees, which we all "doctor" in our own unique way. (I drink mine with fat free non-dairy creamer and artificial sweetener.) So I might suggest that you read as many reviews as possible when you are considering an unfamiliar variety, and base your purchasing decision on the general consensus rather than any one review. Enjoy!
This coffee is worth the price just for the smell. You can fire up one of these babies and have the smell of fresh cooked french toast within minutes. Unique coffee.

column9: really does smell like French Toast
column10: this is one of those coffees you have to try one time, just for the aroma. The aroma is 5 stars. It smells like IHOP when the waitress brings your order of french toast, and you pour maple syrup over it. The best way to describe the coffee is eat some french toast with maple syrup and wash it down with coffee, and you get this flavor. Great for a change from a different flavored coffee. Green Mountain has a wide variety of flavored coffees to choose from, and this is just one of the many.
This is one of my favorites. Alone, it is pretty good, but with a little cream and sugar, it tastes like real french toast, the good kind (not too eggy).

I should have known that ordering Golden French Toast before its release date was too good to be true.  Either this seller sold me very old boxes or it was regular coffee that was packaged to look like Golden French Toast.  The label was a shade of orange.  When I bought a "real" box from a local coffee supplier, the label was more maroon in color.  When it's brewing it smells like really strong regular coffee....NOT french toast!!!  My husband and I were VERY DISAPPOINTED!
This coffee smells much better than it tastes.  I am going to put some sugar free syrup in and see if that makes it better.
Just as the name says. It's a hint of french toast with maple syrup.A great morning coffee with a wonderful aroma that fills the room.

This is my most favorite Keurig coffee flavor (followed by Timothy's Winter Carnival and Green Mountain's Caramel Vanilla creme), so of course the coffee receives FIVE STARS. However, I am really disappointed in how the coffee was shipped. While it was in it's own box, the coffee box itself was horrifically damaged and ripped and smashed to the point where it looked like an elephant sat on it. D: Some of my pods were damaged, too, so I am very disappointed because I had coffee grounds all over. This is the first BAD packing experience with Amazon, so I won't be discouraged from ordering more coffee in the future, but this experience was among the worst. :(
If I didn't tell my friends that it was french toast flavor...they would have never guessed what flavor it was.
I expected a cinnamon and slightly toasty flavor for this brew.....soooo weak in flavors.  Had a very strange flavor and will not buy it again.

column9: Smells and tastes like BURNT TOAST!
column10: DO NOT BUY THIS limited edition Green Mountain Golden French Toast, do not even take it if it is given to you for free! When it started brewing it was horrible, it literally smelled like burned toast! I thought "There is no way this coffee can taste as bad as it smells!" I WAS SO WRONG! I took a drink and gagged! My fiancee loves strong coffee and he spit it out! No amount of sweetener or creamer can fix this! I would like to say that I am a huge fan of most Green Mt Coffees, but this one is the worst I have ever tasted!

column9: A real treat.  My favorite coffee to date.
column10: I've only recently started drinking coffee, but I was turned on to Douwe Egberts Aroma Rood by a work colleague from the Netherlands.  I drink it black, and haven't worked up the courage to taint it with sugar or creamer... I somehow feel that would upset the balance of the universe causing the earth to stop spinning, hurling us all into the air at 1000MPH.  But maybe its just the coffee talking there.In all seriousness, the only down-side to this coffee that I've found is that it makes all your standard Folgers', Maxwell Houses, and other cheap blends taste like crap in comparison.  I am not a coffee snob/connoisseur, I don't know a darn thing about ingredients, or how to describe flavors... I just know what I like, and this is it.

Have had tasted alot of coffee but this one is without a doubt the best cup of joe I have had. looking foward to tasting other blends of this product as for this one it jump starts the taste buds hands down.

Absolutely the smoothest full flavored coffee I've ever had the opportunity to taste! Only wish this was a package of 3 large bricks of coffee instead of the small parcels... each 8.8oz pack is good for 10-12 12cup pots of coffee depending on the concentration you choose. For the full Dutch flavor I recommend no less than 9 scoops (standard cone shaped coffee scoop) per 12 cup pot of coffee... it is more grounds than you'd use for Maxwell House but trust me you will enjoy it much more! Now if we could only get the "Koffemelk" like the lucky Dutch enjoy!!!
A Dutch/Belgian coffee with great flavor. The blend is ground from Arabica and Robusta beans, not Arabica.Thank you Amazon for bringing one more international flavor to the US.

I had this coffee at our local country club.  (I was a guest!)  Then my employer started using it.I can't get my home recipe down.  It just doesn't taste the same.  Then I found out that what my employer uses is already made and is in a cardboard box (like some wines), so the taste is always the same --- delicious.  I will continue to work on my recipe.

I had this coffee at a hotel once and fell in love with it.  I searched everywhere and finally found it here.  It is a little pricey but my husband and I use it only on the weekends as a treat.  Very smooth.
The Douwe Egberts Aroma Rood Ground Coffee, 8.8-Ounce Package is an excellent buy and taste great first thing in the morning.

I love this coffee! I first had this while visiting friends in Holland and I bought some there and brought it home. Everyone I served it to and gave as gifts loved it too. It's a very fine grind and the taste is excellent.
I'm glad this coffer is available thru Amazon. I used to order it from The Netherlands and it took 3 weeks to receive my purchase. This order took days!Thanks

I grew up in a Dutch community in the mid-west and this coffee was always served.  When I visited my hometown this Spring, I bought 3 packages at the local bakery to bring home.  Living in Boston, I could never find Douwe Egberts!  Now I have through Amazon and am so grateful.  The coffee has a smooth, rich taste - and I used to be a Starbucks loyal fan.  Try it...I think you'll be happy you did.

I was first introduced to this coffee at a restaurant. I normally have coffee with cream. The flavor and aroma were so noticeably better than regular restaurant coffee that I had the server find out what kind of coffee it was and write it down for me. I did an internet search when I got home and found it on amazon. I've been buying it exclusively since then. It's amazing how we have all grown used to mediocre coffee regardless of what brand it is. I serve this to my guests and they all notice a positive difference. I've gotten spoiled now and really can't stand the taste of regular coffee anymore. It's a bit more expensive but well worth it. I find it humorous that so many people will fawn all over starbucks and pay ridiculous prices for a mediocre product. This is the best, Consistently. Try a cup of this after drinking a cup of starbucks mud, the flavor and aroma will amaze you.

column9: Coffee is a matter of personal taste and the water.
column10: Writing that this is among the best cups of coffee in the thirty-five years of consumption may be of interest to you, however this coffee is very good and tastes even better when made at a coffee shop or restaurant.  The reason is the water and equipment.  Several coffee shop owners have explained filtered water is more important than the coffee, followed by the coffee, and then the equipment (same pressure and temperature every time).  At home most of us have yet to invest in the expensive equipment to achieve this.  We use a simple single cup drip maker and it works well but the coffee at Glory Days, where we first discovered this coffee, is better and it's the same stuff.  They showed me the label at the restaurant which is how we knew what to order.

Good coffee, nothing special. We frequently order this coffee at a restaurant we visit often, and there it's a "fantastic cup of coffee", but at home, we can not achieve the same taste. From now on, just buying "Folgers Gourmet Supreme"!
I had heard that this was hard to track down, but it was well worth the effort. I expect I'll get some more soon.

column9: Other companies could learn some things
column10: These are very tasty nori strips.  I like the teriyaki flavor on these strips, and I am picky when it comes to teriyaki.  I also love how these are packaged.  One complaint I have with sea's gift and annie chun's seaweed snacks is the packaging.  You get a tray, in a foil wrapper, with a silica packet, in a box.  These jars are jam packed with much much more nori.  Plus the jars are useful after you are done (if you don't mind a slight fish smell... works great to store cat food haha). All in all a great product!FYI (I've seen this complaint on other nori reviews)... if you have never eaten nori... STOP... go to the grocery store... throw down a few bucks on some nori sheets for sushi.  Take those home and eat them.  If you don't like the flavor, you probably won't like these.  Nori has a fishy taste.  I hate when I see reviews on nori with people whining about the fact it tastes like fish and they just spent $20-$30 on something in bulk.Hope this review helps!

I had bought some roasted teriyaki seaweed from the asian food grocer, and because amazon has fast shipping I decided to see if there was some here. Well, there is and it is delicious. You get a lot of seaweed in this thing; 100 packs in each bottle, and each pack has 5 pieces of seaweed. The seaweed had a crisp, thin texture and taste like teriyaki. It smells like fish, but honestly its not a bad smell and is to be expected since it is seaweed.

I love flavored nori, but this brand just doesn't do it for me.  The taste is pretty... plain.  We purchased the two pack about 6 months ago and still have one container sitting around, which says a lot in our family of seaweed lovers.  In the future, I will be sticking with the brands that I know to satisfy my taste buds.

This is my favorite brand of nori and I used to buy as many packages as the local asian market had on hand. Then they started to raise the price on me quite a bit. I am happy to find this on amazon and for such a good price. I like the packaging as well it keeps them very fresh, and it helps to keep me from eating a whole bottle in a day.

column9: Really tasty and theres a lot to go around
column10: I had an idea the 2 pack was big but dang these are huge.  My 18 month old daughter loves this stuff though and if you can tolerate the fishy taste its a great snack.  Me and my daughter will snack on it during the day between playtimes and naptimes. The product is fresh as can be and has a nice crunch to it. She enjoys playing with it and its better then her having candy thats for sure.
These would be very nice for a cocktail party, when you didn't a snack that would clash with your drinks.  Good quality peanuts, nice and unusual flavor, though a little too nuanced for my palate.

I love V8.  It looks and tastes mostly like tomato juice but it's really a vegetable juice because it contains more than just tomato juice.  V8 is very tasty and refreshing as a beverage - and it even works as a snack.  A nice tall glass of V8 will give you a healthy way to tide you over when you feel a little hungry between meals.V8 hot and spicy is my favorite flavor.  I love spicy food and this V8 flavor has a real nice kick to it.  The only problem with V8 is I have to keep myself from drinking an entire 46 ounce bottle in one sitting.

If you like coffee and ginger, these candies are for you!  You start with the excellent coffee taste and finish with ginger heat.  It's the best combination I've tried so far. In the afternoon, these candies are the best pick-me-upper. In terms of a portion control, 20 calories per candy is not too much for the big taste and only 5g of sugar. A lot of my friends felt intrigued enough to give this candy a try and were very pleased with the taste.
I find this product yummy.  The ginger plus the caffeine helps my sinuses unclog.  I also like the Spicy Apple Ginger chew for uncloging my sinuses.

My husband and I were first served Primolio oil in a restaurant, Trattoria del Merlo in Chicago.  It is a splendid oil...peppery but very nuanced and smooth.  We had the waiter write down the name of the oil.  The moment we got home from dinner, we went online and purchased the oil from Gourmet On Line.  It was shipped promptly and without hassle.  A winner all around!

Without a doubt the most amazing and pure product we have ever tried.  My wife (a medical/dietary professional) has done the research and believes this oil is the healthiest money can buy. My concerns are more "taste based" and was shocked by how natural and great tasting this brand of olive oil is.The seller shipped immediately and the packaging technique (kept cold) shows how truly special this product is.  A must for any kitchen or health conscious person.

I bought these mints some time ago, and while the "mint" itself has no real anise flavour (they are quite bland actually), I really bought them for the tin, which is beautiful. If you want actual absinthe flavoured mints, these will disappoint, but if you are like me and wanted the lovely tin for later use, then it's worth the purchase price.

Just OK for these EXPENSIVE mints.  There were only 80 mints and very tiny  ( 1/2 the size of a tic-tac brand mint )  and the flavor isn't that strong at all.  I bought this mainly for the tin to keep sewing pins in it ;  other than that these are no better than licorice altoids which are way better.  I wouldn't ever buy this again but had to try the Absinthe Mints just to say I had that experience.  I rate this 3 stars as it's too pricey and not even 100 bb size mints in the 2 inch tin.

These really taste like absinthe, or at least like black licorice.  The packaging is adorable, and the tin is small enough to fit into the tiniest of purses. My mom loved these as a stocking stuffer this year!
Love the tin! They are slightly flavorful however they're not what I was hoping they would be. At least I have a lovely tin!
I was drawn to buy these because of the tin.  The mints themselves are ok but they haven't got much flavor.
I found these for much less ($2.50 + $2.55) at two other places here on amazon, do not buy from here, free shipping not worth it

column9: Very good tea for a tea bag
column10: Personally I like to brew loose leaf tea and don't use tea bags.  I decided to try this out and compare it with my usual loose leaf tea - Lipton.  Don't laugh but Lipton is quite good tea and is very inexpensive.  I found the difference between the two very subtle. I find my loose leaf Lipton to be very refreshing and having a clean taste.  The Higgins & Burke English BreakFast Black Tea I found refreshing but having a "dusty" or "grainy" aftertaste.  What I mean by that is I think the tea in the H&B bags is ground too fine and some passes into the brewed tea thereby giving it a "dusty" or "grainy" aftertaste. It is surprising because the bag they use seems to be superfine mesh, much more than in you standard tea bag. So it appears to me that in the product that I got some of the tea was powdered in the bag and was able to pass through the fine mesh.  I'm sure it won't hurt me. :)  Apart from that I found the tea very good.  Would I buy it for the price presented - no.

column9: A flavorful tea, even if it is mild
column10: Being a green tea drinker, typically, I enjoy the stronger flavor of Higgins and Burke English Breakfast Tea.  I have only ever tried one other brand of English breakfast tea, so bear this in mind.I enjoyed the flavor immensely.  It is not as strong as I thought it would be, but I still enjoy the flavor.  Maybe it's because I do not drink coffee and my drink of choice is green tea, but I found it a good way to start the day, as well as a nice, relaxing drink for after dinner.If you are looking for a bolder taste, you should search elsewhere for something stronger.  If you are like me, though, you will enjoy the smooth and flavorful taste of Higgins and Burke: recommended.

I like tea, but find usual tea bags too weak.  Lipton, Bigelow, Trader Joe's teas don't seem to have flavor, I usually have to brew two bags per cup to get any flavor.  However, I brewed one bag of Higgins & Burke English Breakfast Black Tea at work and I think it is better than any other tea bag tea I have tried before.  This tea has a deep dark color and a great flavor.The reason for the four star rating is because, although I find this tea to be very good, in my opinion, it is not as good as some loose teas I have tried.  However, I think this tea strikes a perfect balance between the flavor and the convenience of a tea bag.

column9: Kind of weak flavor for English breakfast tea
column10: Higgins and Burke is a new-to-me brand of tea. The packaging is very attractive, and there are twenty individually wrapped teabags inside the box I received. English Breakfast is usually my first tea of choice, but I do prefer it stronger than what I got here. Don't get me wrong, it wasn't bad at all, but neither was it overwhelmingly good. Just not enough flavor for my preferences.

Nice bold, black tea flavor. Very little bitterness. Brews quickly and is one of the better black teas that I've tried. Choice Organic English Breakfast Tea, 1.1 Ounces 16-Count Box (Pack of 6) is still my favorite--not only for the flavor, but also because it is organic.

column9: I'm not a fan of English Black Tea, but this will satisfy your needs
column10: Length:: 1:17 MinsSee video. I rarely drink black tea, but for those who like it, this product will serve them well.I would have given it 2 stars because I really don't like black tea, but I want to be a fair tester. Someone who wants black tea will be happy with this product; hence, 4 stars. Good packaging.

Smooth.  Very Smooth.This English Breakfast Tea is very smooth, yet full-bodied.  It doesn't have quite the bitter tannin punch I expected, considering I accidentally steeped it a bit too long.  It still has a pretty robust tea flavor, just not as much bitterness I expected.  This is a good thing.Highly recommended.  Surprisingly good even without sugar or cream.

column9: A Great Start For The Day
column10: I have been drinking several of the Higgins & Burke teas for a while and they Never disappoint.I love to start the day with the flavorful English Breakfast, Hot in the morning to wake me up and then a tasty glassof a very strong and delicious English Breakfast cold over ice in the afternoon.This tea is wonderful both Hot & Cold, Strong but never bitter, just tasty!

column9: Very polished, classic blend, not too strong, not too bitter
column10: If you like English Breakfast tea, or black tea in general, this one is easy to like. The quality is refined, with just the tiniest note of bitterness and the lightest tannins lending a pleasant accent. Definitely doesn't need milk, and doesn't need much sugar.If you like a "blast" from your tea, or an attention-getting unusual flavor, this isn't the one. But if you want a really smooth drinkable tea that will be hard not to enjoy, this is it.

Well, I don't claim to be a tea expert. My basis for comparison is Lipton's Orange Pekoe and Black Tea, which I drink regularly and like. So, this tea I judge as just as good and perhaps a touch better, a bit richer. And, it does seem to dissolve fast, maybe a testament to its richness. So, between the two, I prefer this, but not enough to change because of the cost and what I judge as only marginally better with regard to its naturalness claim. Its claim for being ethically produced, I think worthy, but really can't judge and I haven't heard anything bad about Lipton's processes. That said, if its cost is not important to the buyer and/or its claim of ethics is important enough, I recommend this because I judge it a superior tea based on what I like, as described in this review.

column9: I'm something of a Breakfast Tea Maven
column10: I admit it... I love English tea. I don't drink coffee, I drink tea. My favorite tea is English Breakfast tea, so when Vine asked me to try this tea I jumped at the chance. I have tried all the big brands and so I feel I can make a very honest report. Well, this tea isn't bad, but it isn't the best, either. It has a slight aftertaste, and isn't as enjoyable as I had hoped. It also has a slight "raw" taste. As a result, I can only give it four stars. Truthfully, for me Twinnings has a fuller, richer flavor, and I will continue using that.

There is nothing real special about the Higgins & Burke English Breakfast Black Tea as it's not bad but it's not special either. The flavor of the tea is reminiscent of most breakfast teas, but I would not say it's as bracing as some other breakfast teas I've tried.Overall, I'd recommend this tea, especially if you are looking for a less bracing cup of breakfast tea.

Higgins & Burke offers here an English Breakfast tea that is all-round quality. It does not have the strong, full-bodied taste of some teas of this kind; neither is it weak or not palatable. There is no bitterness to it and I would say it is medium to strong-bodied.What I like about it is that it is natural. I recently ordered an organic, natural tea from England that turned out to have a very unpleasant taste while at the same time being overly strong. So it is a relief for me to find a natural tea that is a pleasure to drink. It does not leave any unpleasant aftertaste either.The company that makes this tea is very environmentally conscious. It is 100% sourced and purchased under Ethical Tea Partnership standards. The cartons are made with 100 percent recycled fibres, and each bag is individually wrapped and sealed for protection. Their website states that even their working environment "encourages employee wellness." How often do you see that!I also find it fascinating that Higgins & Burke also produces a white tea. Never heard of such a thing but someday I'll be daring and order some.This English Breakfast tea is superior to what can be found in mainline supermarkets. But one can purchase a more full-bodied tea in specialty shops. However, "natural" is important to me as I try to keep pesticides out of my system so I will probably make this tea a regular part of my kitchen staples in future.

Higgens & Burke English Breakfast Black Tea is a nice, strong cup of black tea without being too overpowering or containing any hint of bitterness.  It makes for a really good morning cup of tea, easy to prepare, but considering that I've had quite a few English Breakfast blends, it didn't stand out as anything spectacular.  This one counts for being a nice and reliable blend, as well as something you can take with you into work or while traveling (since it comes in bags and in sealed pouches) rather than in a tin or a loose leaf blend.

English Breakfast is one of my favorite blends, but this Higgins & Burke tea is not my favorite brand. It's a weak tea without any distinctive flavor, and is easily overwhelmed by the average amount of sweetener and lemon that I put in my tea. It tastes almost identical to standard Lipton's. I prefer more upscale bag teas (Twinings) when I don't want to pay for fancy loose gourmet tea (Peets or Coffee Bean Direct). On the other hand, I have met many people who are not picky about their teas and think Lipton's is just fine, so they will probably like this tea.  Note, if you want low-quality but very low-priced bulk tea, try a local Indian grocery.

Higgins & Burke's English Breakfast Tea brews up into a flavorful but mild morning cuppa, and doesn't come off bitter when steeped longer for a stronger brew. It pairs well with either honey or sugar for sweetening.

I've had four mugs of this tea over several days and can only  conclude that I do not like it.  I've tried it plain, with sugar, stevia, and soy milk but have not enjoyed any.  To me this black tea (a Ceylon/Assam blend) has a slightly rotted taste.  I do not know if it comes from the variant  blend or the processing.  I like what I've been drinking for years - Prince of Peace organic green.  It's wonderful plain and even better with Silk soy milk.

I love the tea with my breakfast.  I've tried it plain, with honey and now with milk and sugar. All three ways are delicious.  I'm typically not a tea drinker, but for a change I wanted to try something different.  I'm so glad to have chosen this tea.  It's a new flavor to experience and I can see having this for breakfast instead of coffee for a nice change of pace.  In short, it tastes great and I never thought I'd say that about a tea.

column9: Good, but pricier than my standby (Taylors Yorkshire Gold)
column10: This is a good, well-rounded, mellow English breakfast tea, an Assam/Ceylon blend.  It has a distinctive, sort of floral undertone or aftertaste, not unpleasant but unusual.I prefer to do without the additional packaging of individual foil packets.  And today's Amazon bulk price is $0.18 per for Higgins & Burke compared with $0.11 for my favorite everyday bagged tea, Taylors Yorkshire Gold.  I won't be switching brands, but I'll enjoy the rest of this box.If you're a tea-drinker, you probably have a good idea of what you like in a black tea.  There are many good ones to choose from.  I have my favorite, but that's a personal thing based on my budget and taste.  Above all, I'm grateful to Amazon for providing us with such variety and reasonable pricing.

This black tea had a very interesting taste. It was kind of strong for my taste, but nevertheless it had a comforting taste. The tea is very strong, so I suggest using the minimal amount of tea bags when making tea for multipe cups. It's good to keep in the cubboard for company, but I don't think I would purchase it for myself.

Usual Higgins & Burke quality is shown via this spot-on variant of English Breakfast Tea. It is a balanced English Breakfast Tea -- being rich, strong and soothing. It compares favorably to other variants of English Breakfast Tea. This was especially evident after I accidently let a semi-thermos mug of hot Higgins & Burke English Breakfast tea [with cream and brown sugar] sit for a while -- ending up with just lukewarm tea. It was still excellent and I finished this cuppa. This accident was final proof for me of the quality of this tea. Not too many teas [or other drinks] are still good lukewarm. The box and enclosed tea bags in individual envelopes are well done as well +++

This is the second Higgins & Burke tea that I have tried and I am not impressed.  I find the flavor rather flat and weak even if I steep the teabag for a long time.  I have tasted some really great teas in all the years I've drank teas but this is not one of them.  From the written description I really thought this tea would be great but it's not.  It isn't bitter or acidic tasting but it is blahhhhhh.  I'll use up my remaining tea bags since I like to drink plain hot water but I will not be buying any more of this brand.

column9: Super-mellow, tasty, which mends the bones!
column10: OK, I'm close to  tea fanatic. I've probably sampled 100's of tea types over the years, and like them all. Originally, it is said tea was a muscle and fatigue relaxer, a drink to calm the spirit, and mend creaky bodies. So when I wake up, mending the bones is first on my agenda before heading out into the real world. So, I ordered this Higgins and Burke tea here, and now it's a staple. Not only for the taste, but more important, the fact that it calms my bones; so it is good for all meals and all breaks. If you've ever wondered why the Brits, Chinese, and many others go for a tea break, this particular tea is the top reason!

column9: I liked it better than their other ones
column10: I generally drink tea straight up (no sugar, no milk) and I like it strong--I let it steep at least 5 minutes.  In previous reviews, I've found Higgins and Burke Higgins & Burke Green Tea, 20-Count (Pack of 6) and Higgins & Burke Earl Grey Black Tea, 20-Count (Pack of 6) rather weak tasting relative to other brands I've tried. But since I have found English Breakfast teas (esp. in restaurants and in England too) to be a bit strong/bitter to my taste, I thought this might work for H&B English Breakfast--and it did!  I find this a pleasant alternative tea and like it better than any other English Breakfast tea I've tried.BTW, I also sometimes add 10 drops of Sinus Formula 1oz to the tea which not only opens my sinuses, but gives it a nice minty taste.

column9: Too much Ceylon; not enough Assam
column10: Tea snob here, so be forewarned.  If I were comparing bagged tea to loose tea, the very best bagged tea would get about 3 stars.  So, I'm comparing only bagged teas.This tea held a lot of promise but didn't deliver.  English Breakfast should be one of those stronger teas that has a nice robust flavor from Assam tea.  Instead, I got a mildly strong flavor with the astringent bite of Ceylon at the finish.  Ceylon?  Yep.  I could go to Lipton tea for that.So, what you basically have is an upscale version of Lipton tea.  I gave it three stars because, well, it's okay.  Not undrinkable.  Someone out there is bound to rave about the flavor, and that's good, because it'll show them there's more to tea than just the generic stuff.  But I really expected more, even from a bagged tea.If you really love this tea, start trying loose teas.  There are plenty of companies out there that provide some great black teas.  Adagio is one, but not the only one.  Try Adagio Teas English Breakfast, 4-Ounce Tins (Pack of 2)  Much better stuff.

I have tried other teas from Higgins & Burke including Green Tea, Earl Grey, and Peppermint. They were quite good with good flavor. Now I have tried the English Breakfast Tea, which, like the Earl Grey has a good amount of caffeine.  The caffeine rush that I got after a few minutes of drinking this tea was impressive.  I am not surprised that the English call it breakfast tea.Each tea bag comes in an individual packet, which preserves its freshness. The ingredients consist of only black tea leaves.  The tea brews quickly into a nice color.  The tea has a pleasant aroma. The taste is that of black tea.  This tea is as good as others that I have tried.  It will go well for occasions when caffeine is desired, in the morning or afternoon, for instance. I definitely recommend it.

This tea reminded me of a rose milk tea that I used to like (but have since grown tired of). It was a little bitter, even though I didn't leave the tea bag in very long. I probably won't buy it again, but if you like strong teas, this is for you.

What do I really know about tea?I'm sure there are some experts out there, but I'm your average, run of the mill shlub. Normally I drink my tea iced, but over the last few weeks with b'fast, I've been having hot tea in the morning.Many teas end up just colouring the water and not providing much taste, let alone anything robust - and that's really what I want if I'm going to drink it. Overall, I don't drink caffeine at all.Still, since I was on a tea kick, I thought I'd try and I'm glad I did. I found this Black Tea to have good flavour and it beats the normal kind you get at the grocery store.Since I'm not a huge tea drinker, I'll see how far the box will get me and then consider purchasing more. Even for company, it is so much better than the standard stuff that is out there.

I make my tea weak and drink it without milk or sugar.  My favorite tea used to be Earl Grey flavored with bergamot until I tasted this Higgins & Burke English BreakFast Black Tea.  It is flavorful and I detected a faint sweetness.  There is no bitter aftertaste.  It goes well with chocolate chip cookies. Try it; you might like it.

column9: A bit boring;  I've had better..
column10: Earl Grey is one of my favorite teas.  I don't drink that many different types. It's either Earl Grey for the caffeine, taste and aroma, or chamomile to help me go to sleep! I try a few others here and there, and usually drink more hot tea in the winter months.I normally drink the foil pack single serving bigelow, and I even get the de-caf version if I'm having a late night dessert!  Can't eat dessert without Earl Grey!Anyway, the good news is that the tea bag did not leak any leaves and the tag didn't fall off the string!  Other than that, and after steeping per the directions, I still felt that there was no punch to the tea; it was kind of bland.  I use an artificial sweetener in my tea, and sometimes, depending on my mood, I use the liquid vanilla coffeemate, which doesn't cover up the taste of the tea, and in my opinion, it adds to the flavor.However, when using it with this tea, there really was no sense of the Earl Grey; covered up the bergamot and it also has lemon in it, which I normally don't find in my Earl Grey be it decaf or leaded!So, overall, I don't think I would go out of my way to find this brand. I didn't find it disgusting, but not much to get excited about.  I do like the 6 boxes for the low price on Amazon and as also like that I can get an extra 15% discount with the subscribe and save program.  I would not, however, sign up for it for this product.  I did use the service however for my Earl Grey tea by Bigelow.

This chai is both fragrant and flavorful. Each teabag is wrapped within its own sealed package to ensure freshness up until you actually decide "it's time for chai." Unsealing the teabags produces and aroma that is reminiscent of Christmas for me - and why wouldn't it with Cinnamon, Ginger, and Cloves making up half the ingredients on the tea? The flavor is robust and sweet, leaving a little dryness behind as it slips beyond my uvula and into my belly (honestly, the back of my mouth "tastes" dry after I drink this, and I rather like that). Higgins and Burke chai leaves a pleasant aftertaste as well - always a plus.

Higgins and Burke Earl Grey tea is a pleasant cup of quality black tea. It has a nice floral aroma and a mild tea blend taste.  There is very little bergamot flavor and aroma. And that is what some Earl Grey drinkers want-a nice mild black tea and a hint of bergamot. This is a blend that probably works well in a restaurant or office situation since it makes no strong tea statement.  A middle of the road choice for occasional tea drinkers.

I rarely drink hot tea, but wanted to give the Higgins & Burke Chai Black Tea a try. The tea tastes great, and while I'm not sure about the characteristics of Chai tea myself, I did enjoy the tea's flavor. If you enjoy drinking hot tea and like black tea, his product is a good choice.

column9: A great choice for the chai tea needs
column10: I love chai teas and was anxious to se how it compared to what you would find freshly made on your own or even from a restaurant.  I did it a few ways so you can see the different results.Iced tea maker with a medium brew - this made a good light tea that showed off the cloves that are in this blend.I added a light cream and once with a milk to it to make a thai type iced tea but the milk quickly overpowered it at the lighter brew.  But as an iced chai everyone loved it and we went through numerous bags before I stopped them so we could test the other ways.Iced tea maker with strong brew - this was much better for an iced Thai type and the cloves were stronger and held flavor when adding milk or cream.  Keep in mind the manufacturer says Assam which is there but the spices are stronger.Hot water light brew - just ok.  I did it once and didn't like it.  Simple enough in explanation I think.Hot water strong brew - this was by far the best result of the four showing off the care they did in individual packaging. While not fresh, it was great for home, blended well with the milk and held up enough as a chai.I wish there was more Assam strength but I was quite happy and will buy this type again.  I recommend hot strong brew, iced strong and iced medium brews for the best results.

Comparing this to adagio chai which is what I normally drink, this wasn't all that different taste wise.  I drank it cold and hot and it had a very pleasant taste.  Strength and smell wise, adagio has it beat.  Not a bad at all.  Of course this isn't the best chai you can buy, but the price isn't bad at all for what you get.

These pricey little air-tight pouches reveal a delightful scent when opened, but the flavors are too light. Neither the tea nor the spices are sufficient to make an enjoyable cup. I have used more tea bags and less water, and finally got to a strength that is palatable, but there isn't enough juice in these things.And the flavor isn't that great. I am not a huge fan of flavored tea; I drink a lot, but usually just straight black tea,. However, back in the olden days I used to drink Constant Comment, and I've enjoyed many cups of chai at my favorite Indian restaurant. It is much better than this stuff.

This tea is very pungent and flavorful. One cup of it will be enough to keep you awake for quite a while and will fill the whole house with a very soothing aroma. it is perhaps even better chilled with a little milk.

Tea is not the best quality, but good enough for chai.  It professes to be an Assam blendand I just couldn't taste it enough to tell.  I have about a dozen Assam estate varietiesat the moment, so it's not that I do not know what Assam tastes like. The Karha for this blend is a bit unique but flavorful in a pleasant way.  The tea isjust background noise, not even a binder.  Ginger and cardamom were barely detectablein my box. The cinnamon was a spicy variety (like a Saigon) not a warm variety, so itadds some bite.  For those used to Masala Chai, the spice blend is a little differentthan some, and reminds me of eastern flavorings more than south or west.  Meaning cloveand cinnamon was the stronger of the flavors.  If you're used to cardamom and pepperheavy chai, you will be disappointed.This  cries for cream and sweetener.  Got for just a little half and half rather than amoderate dollop of milk, and a lighter honey (like wildflower, not buckwheat or the like)over sugar. Enjoy!

column9: Not too strong, not too weak
column10: There is a nice blend of flavours in this blend. It's always nice to sit and enjoy a cup of tea and ponder life's mysteries and this tea doesn't get in the way of that.The strength is easily controlled by the length of time you let the bag steep.Each bag is individually sealed in its own packet so it won't go stale too quickly.

I am a huge fan of tea but I have never liked chai teas, for some reason.  The first bag I opened smelled so lovely...very much like cloves. I was pleased to discover that the chai spice was not overwhelming and I thoroughly enjoyed my first cup of Higgins & Burke Chai Black Tea.  I also like the box as it has the punch-out section at the bottom so that all of the tea bags don't fall out at once...always a nice feature for single dispensing.My next cup of tea had an extremely strong taste of cinnamon.  Now, I like cinnamon but this was even too strong for me!  I found the next few tea bags to be inconsistent in flavor.  Sometimes they were good,and sometimes the flavors were too overpowering.  I tried the tea both hot and iced.  If you like the strong chai flavor, I suggest trying it iced as the cold really brings out the spicyness.I gave this product three stars because of the inconsistency in the flavor.

column9: A Nice Masala Chai, but what are the "natural flavors?
column10: This is a perfectly nice Masala Chai.  The bags are individually wrapped, so that the freshness and pungency of spices is preserved until you use it, something I really appreciate.The ingredients list includes the usual spices, followed by "natural flavors". I am not surprised that a dried convenience product like this might need a boost from some sort of flavor additive, compared to tea infused with freshly grated ginger and whole spices, but still, I'd like to know more about these "natural flavors".  Nevertheless, it is still a great spiced tea.

I was skeptical at first, as I generally like to make chai tea from scratch, using black tea and spices from my pantry, but this is almost as good.  It tastes better than the chai teas you get at coffee houses (which are usually from pre-made factory mixes) and definetly than powdered varieties.  It also holds up well to milk (though if you're looking for more than a 10 oz cup at time, I'd double bag it) and isn't overly-sensitive to a too long or too short steeping time.And, it's as good as the loose leaf chai teas I've tried from fancy places like Teavana.This is the only bagged chai tea I'll ever buy, I think.

column9: A nice cuppa, but it's not Chai!
column10: While these tea bags make a decent cup of tea, I wouldn't call it chai. It does not taste very spicy, nor does it have a very fragrant aroma. The only spices listed as ingredients are cinnamon, cardamom, ginger and cloves. Celestial Seasons India Spice Chai tea bags list those four spices, plus nutmeg, black pepper, Chinese star anise, chicory and vanilla bean, for a much better cup of chai.

I'm certainly no tea expert, but the Higgins & Burke Chai works for me. For the uninitiated, Chai Tea has been popular in Asian countries, especially India, for centuries. It consists of black tea, brewed strong, with a combination of spices. In this case, we have Assam Black tea with cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, cloves and "natural flavors". Each box of H&B contains 20 tea bags.Traditionally, Chai is consumed hot and sweet, and diluted with milk. For my taste test, I tried the H&B three different ways: with milk and honey, with honey and no milk, and the tea alone with nothing added. I lean toward the undiluted tea, but all three are very pleasant and aromatic. If you dislike cloves, however, this blend may not be for you.Perhaps the Higgins & Burke Chai is not the hippest, trendiest Chai available, but most tea drinkers should enjoy it, especially considering its reasonable price. I would certainly get it again in the future.

column9: Black Tea not my first choice.
column10: This is a good product, however, it isn't my favorite.  It comes will packaged, and smells good, I just don't care for the flavor.  I wish I could provide more input but I really think these are one of those things you have to make your own mind up on.  Sorry, wish I could be more help.

column4: Leah M. Brown "Leah Marie Brown, Author"
column9: So sorry.  Chai just didn't think it was a good cup of tea.
column10: Although the box states that this Higgins and Burke Chai Black Tea includes the robust flavor of Assam tea, I found it to be a rather bland cup of tea.  I much prefer the full-bodied flavor of Teavana's Samurai Chai blend - with its infusion of oranges and cinnamon.  This Chai was pale and watery tasting.  I carefully boiled my water to the desired 167 degrees and let the bag steep for 3 minutes, but it was still as bland as Queen Victoria's love life.  Sorry, Chai just didn't think this was a good cup of tea.

I'm always looking for a good chai, and I'm kinda picky about it since I really don't care for anything that tastes like licorice.  Many chai blends include star anise, which ruins it for me.Higgins & Burke's chai doesn't have any nasty licorice-y flavors in it, so hooray!  It's a tasty chai that's heavier on clove and cardamom, and I really enjoy drinking it with a bit of vanilla soy milk.I would suggest steeping it for a solid five minutes, though.  I steeped for 3 and a half minutes the first time, and it was pretty weak.  At five minutes (or more; I like strong tea), it's perfect.

I haven't done an extensive search trying to find a spicy tea that didn't have black pepper as an ingredient, but as far as I have looked, I haven't been able to find one. This is one such tea. A spicy flavor without the addition of black pepper to which many people are allergic. How nice. Plus, it's possible to overbrew this tea without getting the bitter taste that happens with other teas. I like it and two of my friends also like it.

Traditional Chai is made by heating milk with black tea and spices. When ordering a Chai at a Coffee or Tea House it is usually made with frothed hot milk and a liquid concentrate of tea and spices, so it is somewhat similar to the traditional method. Chai from a teabag is a bit dodgy, but worth try to see how well it is executed. Black tea is my favorite type of tea, and I usually enjoy it with milk. Since Higgins & Burke's Chai tea consists of Black Tea, it should also be enjoyed with milk,  As with all black tea the water should be near or at boiling when pouring it over the leaves or bag. The directions on the box indicate that the tea should steep for at least five minutes. I doubled that and let it steep for ten minutes before getting ready to enjoy what I hope would be an invigorating cup. When I poured just a little bit of milk into my cup, it immediately lightened the tea to a point beyond where I would normally lighten it to. It was at that point that I realized what I hopefully would be a cup of relaxation would be disappointing. I didn't initially think that the pre-milk color of the Chai was too light, but I was obviously mistaken. My first sip of Higgins & Burke Chai Tea had a clove taste to it, with undertones of some other spices, nothing really discernible. I could not distinguish the black tea at all, the flavor was a rather murky blend of spice and water, with a little bit of milk. I wish I could say something better about this tea, maybe I can. So, I steeped another cup, this time for only five minutes, took a sip without adding anything, just drinking the tea straight up, but it was too weak. I let it steep for another five minutes. I tasted it again, once again without any milk, I liked it even less. The weak spicy, thin liquid just had no zip. Sorry Higgins & Burke, maybe some of your other teas are better, but I will pass on your Chai Black Tea.

This tea is fragrant and spicy with cinnamon, cardamom, ginger and cloves along with assam black tea leaves.  This brand is quality and brews a lighter cup than I am used to and I could use less creamer and sugar than with a heavier chai tea such as Tazo.  I liked the smoothness of the flavor as the spices did not overwhelm my palate but I prefer the black tea to be a big stronger for more tea strength and a bit bolder cup of tea.

This is my first nonw book review but when Amazon offered this for the vine review program I couldn't resist.  I love me some tea. For me tea and books go hand in hand, so this random review doesn't seem so strange. Now on to the tea.  Most chai teas in the bag are flavor flat.  However this one by Higgins & Burke is very flavorful. While I let the chai seep in the hot water, there was a nice and strong aroma. When I simply hold a tea bag in its individually sealed package close to my nose, I still get a great sense of the flaovers.  The tea goes down well and this is no lingering bitter after taste. It also taste great iced.

column9: Nice tea, but not like chai I've had
column10: Each teabag is individually wrapped; when you open it, you'll definitely notice the spices.  Mostly I notice cardamom, but also some cinnamon (not as much as I would like -- I love cinnamon!) and perhaps cloves.  Not sure what else.  The tea itself was smooth, not overbearing.Without milk, it brewed up to be a pleasant, mildly spiced cup of black tea.  Not bad.  With milk, the spices were just gone.  Perhaps I needed to make a more concentrated brew, but even so...It's probably not realistic to think that you're going to get the real chai experience from a teabag, but if you like chai spices you might like this tea for that.

I like the balanced flavor of these tea bags -- not too heavy, good for a refreshing cup of tea, and not too heavy on the cinnamon. Each tea bag is sealed in a foil pouch and comes out fresh and fragrant.

column9: Lighter than Expected, but Still Good
column10: The description here of this tea is that it's a "robust" Assam. What I found instead was that this tea is very light, even when steeped for longer than what I am normally used to. The first time I made this tea, I steeped for 3 minutes. In that cup, the tea was extremely light, and I would describe the aroma and flavor as more floral than spicy. The next few times, I let the tea steep for 5 minutes or more. The tea came out slightly darker, and with a more definite cinnamon and clove flavor. I didn't try it with milk...I don't normally put milk in any tea I drink. But I wondered if the tea would ever be "robust" enough to hold up to a full milk and sugar or cream and sugar application. It's not a bad tea overall, but I do tend to like my tea darker generally. But, some people do favor lighter teas, and if that's you, I would recommend you try the Higgins & Burke Chai.

As a big chai fan, I jumped at the opportunity to sample Higgins & Burke's version of chai tea (which has all natural ingredients). The first time I made the tea, I steeped it for five minutes, since I prefer a stronger tea, and sweetened it with honey. My initial reaction was that it's good, but not the best I've ever had. The spices overwhelm the tea, mainly the cloves and cardamom. I really love Yogi Chai Black, Herbal Tea Supplement, 16-Count Tea Bags (Pack of 6) for a nice blend of spices and tea. On my next try, I added one part soy milk to two parts brewed tea. It was delicious! While the strong spices overpower the tea and aren't as evenly blended as they could be when alone, the added milk almost turns the chai into perfection. This works iced as well, but with maybe more milk and less brewed tea, depending on your preference. If you're a fan of a more spicy chai, or just chai in general, I'd highly recommend it.

This chai has a very good flavor, particularly if you let it steep in a little less water than you'd normally use for brewing black tea. You want it to be somewhat concentrated, because chai is best enjoyed sweetened, with milk.

This chai tea focuses on spices such as clove, cinnamon and cardamom rather than the sweet sugary stuff you get from a box.  This strong black tea is a strong and powerful representation of traditional Indian spices.  Some palates might find so much flavor off putting.I tried it both hot and iced, with sweetener and without and all combinations were tasty, though some sugar and milk really brings out the flavors well.A great do it yourself and versatile beverage solution

I have tried several brands of Chai and I must say this one beats of them all. It has a nice flavor with a great blend; the fusion of traditional masala spices and the Assam tea leaves blend perfectly giving a fine taste. The cinnamon flavor is just about balanced. I drink black tea without any sugar and sweetener. This works well for me.Tea India Masala Chai Tea, 72 Tagless Tea Bags, 5.8-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)

When your using tea bags, things are never quite perfect as you are always getting someone else's "ideal" amount (or perhaps their economically driven amount) and never quite your own.  Thus it is a bit unfair to compare tea bags to loose tea that you can choose to your own preferred strength.  Of course, tea bags are a lot less hassle and hence the tradeoff.  So I will judge this as a "tea bag" chai and not something one might make from loose tea or have in a restaurant.I have sampled Higgins & Burke's Chai Black Tea both in its normal setting with milk as well as with honey.  In both cases it had a pleasant aroma and a soothing taste.  It is not as strong as I might like it but it certainly was not weak and compared to comparable teabags it is a definite winner.  I have enjoyed it as an evening counterpoint to the morning coffee and it is both relaxing and refreshing.  The flavor is solid without being overwhelming and there was no noticable aftertaste.While they say you can't please everyone, this should please most.  It may not be perfect but this is not a perfect world.

I think that this Chai Tea has a very good flavor.  All of the spices mesh well without the tea coming out with an overtly cinnamon flavor.  That being said, it's a very weak tea.  I've steeped it for 5 minutes and it is still really weak in flavor.  If you like a strong Chai Tea, this won't be for you!

I am not a fan of cinnamon, but I like tea and wanted to give this product a try.  Surprisingly, although the cinnamon flavor is quite strong, I enjoyed the overall flavor combination of this tea.  For me, other spices are muted with cinnamon being the main flavor.I let a tea bag to brew for a while and to cool off in my spill resistant cup.  I drink it rather quickly and did not mind the cinnamon flavor.  I find this tea to be energizing, and I usually have it either in the morning when I get to work or at about 2PM when I am crashing from lunch and falling asleep.

I drink tea, not coffee, and I drink a lot of it year-round, so I'm always looking for something new.  I like chai, but some versions are too heavy-handed with the black pepper.  This Higgins & Burke product has the perfect balance of black tea and spices.  The black tea, which is the foundation of chai, seems to be of high quality; it is flavorful and not bitter, so I can drink this without adding any sweetener.  The tea bags come in foil packets, which keeps them fresh, something I appreciate as well.  If you are a tea connoisseur, I highly recommend this as a full-bodied but not over-powering chai.

Chai?  Really?  I'm used to most bagged chai teas to be a bit on the weak side when it comes to spice, but this is by far the most weakly-spiced chai I've ever tasted.I even tried it in water rather than milk, and I still can barely taste any spices; however, that way I did learn that the tea is of good quality and taste.But if you want some spicy kick to your chai, let alone some depth of flavors, I'd definitely look elsewhere.

As soon as you tear into the packet, you know that this Higgins & Burke Chai tea is going to be good. The aroma is intoxicating! The blend of Assam black tea, cinnamon, cardamom, ginger and cloves is just right. I enjoy my Chai tea iced as well as hot. When drinking it iced, I simply brew as usual then add mild, a packet of sweetener and ice. Perfect for a hot summer day!

column9: Smells great, but black tea is too weak
column10: I received a box of Higgins & Burke Chai Black Tea free from the Amazon Vine program, in exchange for writing a review of the product.I'm a big tea drinker, and have always enjoyed chai, so I was excited to try this brand. I had the water at a rolling boil when I poured it over the teabag, and I left it to steep for 5-6 minutes. I added just a little hot milk and some honey after removing the teabag, and enjoyed the nice clove-y fragrance of the tea.Unfortunately, the black tea in it isn't strong enough to balance out the spices. Classic chai is supposed to be a strong infusion of Assam tea, with subtle flavors of cardomom, cloves and cinnamon. This product has it backwards.Perhaps using two teabags would help.

column9: Nice:  pleasing aroma with complex taste
column10: I like a nice tea, but prefer black tea rather than herbal tea. So I was excited to try out this Chai blend. I find it to be very nice, with an aroma like mulling spices, and a sharp but not bitter taste.Packaging and content:This comes in a box of 20 individually wrapped bags. The ingredients are Assam Black Tea, Cinnamon, Cardamom, Ginger, Cloves, and "Natural Flavors" (whatever that means). When I opened the package, it smelled so good that I almost wanted to just keep the tea bag out and not put water over it.Taste:The package says to brew for 3 to 5 minutes, but I like to leave the bag in the cup until it is empty. I am impressed that the tea just gets stronger, but never bitter. The taste is akin to "mulling spices" that are used with wine. I can smell the cinnamon and cloves, and taste a bit of the ginger and and other flavors. The tea is Assam, which is definitely better than other black teas. All of this comes together really well - the taste combines nicely into a wonderful flavor.Summary:If you like a tea with caffeine and a complex flavor, this is an excellent choice. Highly recommended.

column4: Mrs. K "From the wilds of the Mojave"
column10: In the world of brew-at-home chai, you have the purists who watch for spice sales ("Oooh, oooh, I found star anise in the bargain bin at Vons!") and people like me who are just looking for a more exotic version of English breakfast tea with milk.The Higgins & Burke Chai was alright. If my supermarket choice was this, Tazo or Good Earth, I'd get this in a second.However, unlike other brands I buy frequently, you can't really see the individual pieces of spices (cardamom pods, arms of star anise). I prefer the more premium teas that have identifiable spices. I did notice more spice/tea dust than usual inside the envelope. More finely powdered teas lose their flavor quicker than the more chunky stuff.If homemade/authentic restaurant chai is a 10, Good Earth a 1, I'd give this a solid 4. (Two Leaves and a Bud Black Chai is an 8, Bombay Chai is a 8, Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf is a 6, Stash Double Spice is 6, Tazo is a 3, Bigelow/Twinings are 1s, any premade chai liquid/powder with sugar is a -3).Numi made with Roobios doesn't count on the scale.

I am a huge fan of chai teas.  There are so many variations on the balance of spices that one must find one that they prefer.  I have made my own chai and definitely drink it often at Indian restaurants.  I really, really liked Higgins & Burke Chai Black Tea.  The aroma was nice and spices are nicely balanced in a way that I like them.  If I choose to make it as a latte (with milk), I brew two tea bags to one cup of water and I add soy milk to it and it's wonderful.  Definitely a fan here!

Rating 4.5 starsI'm a big tea drinker and you'd be surprised at the variety out there.Tea needs to do two things to be good for me: 1- it has to be strong.  A weak tea is simply water to me, and too many teas lack a strong, but not overwhelming flavor; 2- it has to be as good iced as hot.  I realize that's not the traditional English view of tea, but I make a lot of iced tea and I want it to be as good cold as hot.My verdict is that this is a variety I would buy again.  The flavor is good, the strength is good.  I tried the Chai Black and would love to try their other flavorings.  You can't really go wrong with this one, though.

I enjoyed Higgins and Burke Chai Tea. The flavor is more varied and subtle than a lot of the bagged chai blends. Each bag contains notes, in varying strengths, of clove, cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, and of course cardamon. At the moment, it's unseasonably chilly where I live, and I've been drinking several cups per day.This blend serves well as a hot tea, an iced tea, chilled with milk, but is best when it's a heated milk blend. It isn't nearly what you'd get in an Indian restaurant, but as far as boxed chai tea goes, it's nice.My biggest complaint is the strength of the tea. Even when doubling the tea and the time, it never gets as strong as I like (that said, I like "motor-oil" tea, as black as possible.) It isn't watery or remarkably weak, but I was disappointed that I couldn't get the flavor as strong as I wanted.Overall, this is a more-than-decent tea. I enjoyed it enough to buy a few more boxes, and I would confidently recommend it.

column9: Delicious, with a hint of bergamot
column10: Higgins & Burke Earl Grey tea is simply delicious!  It's hard to resist the aroma while the bag steeps.  It is perfectly blended, an excellent flavor with the hint of orange citrus from the bergamot.  I love it as is, and it's also tasty with a small squeeze of honey.If you're a tea drinker, I highly recommend this Earl Grey.  You'll love it!

If you like your chai flavorful but not too strong I suggest that you check out Higgins & Burke's Chai Tea.  This tea,by itself or with a little cream and honey or sugar is a wonderful alternative to a cup of coffee. No aftertaste or bitterness, just the spices of a beverage which is enjoyable and tasty.  If you are a caffeine junky it's still there!

This is the first tea bag Chai that I've tried that I love. Most others are either too spicy, too weak or just blah. This one has all the right spices and is a real treat. I prefer plain without cream or sweetener, but it's equally good either way. I've found my new favorite tea!

I drink a lot of Chai tea so I was excited to try something new. This tea is delicious but the clove flavor is a bit strong. Also there are some natural flavors which I haven't figured out yet. They add a sort of perfume to the tea not unlike Earl Grey. I suspect there are some essential oils being used as flavorings. This is a nice tea to drink in the afternoon. It might be a bit strong first thing in the morning. I used two teabags to make it strong enough. Also to get that milky texture I use powdered milk. This is also great with stevia instead of sugar. When you make this be prepared for a very aromatic experience. Enjoy.~The Rebecca Review

A good chai should have a complex flavor of spices and be strong enough to accommodate the addition of milk and sweetner. This one just didn't fill the bill. Some of the more subtle spices, especially my favorite, the cardamom, were just not full-bodied enough in this tea to be savored; in addition, I didn't feel there was enough loose tea in the bag to brew a strong enough cup. It tasted fairly bland and watered (or milked) down, even after the brewing time suggested on the box.  Perhaps two bags per cup would have done the trick, but that would be pretty pricey. Overall, I was not impressed and would not order this chai again.
This chai tea has a good but subtle taste. I usually drink a slightly stronger black tea but this is still pretty good and I'd recommend.

column4: Eustacia Vye "a lover of books and everything...
column10: I drink a lot of tea... from the dollar store plain black tea to exotic loose leaf.  I have so much tea that I've been placed on a "tea diet" and have to sneak new teas into the house.  Needless to say, I was thrilled to try this new tea.Sadly, this tea fell very short.  I dont expect bagged chai tea to taste like real chai.  I do expect a nice spiced tea with a little bit of a kick.  I found this tea very weak.  Even leaving the tea in my 8 oz tea cup for 10 mins, the tea was still too weak.  I found the only way to drink this tea was to double up on the tea bags.  At 20 bags per box, this box would only last me 5 days with my 16 oz "morning commute" tea cup.On the plus side, this tea does smell nice.  I'm currently mixing it with no name cheap black tea with good results.  However it is likely that I will not purchase this tea in the future.

I'm not a chai tea expert.  I drank this tea, straight.  No milk, cream, sugar, etc.  It tasted nice & refreshing & spicy.  I loved the aroma.  It's suggested to let it steep for 3-5 minutes.  I let it steep for 5 or 6 minutes & it was a nice strong tea, which is what I prefer.  It was a bonus to read that Higgins & Burke belongs to the Ethical Tea Partnership, which works for a responsible tea industry.

I enjoyed this tea and so did my friend. She said there was nothing "special" about it, however; it was just nice tea.I didn't think a real Chai could be found in a teabag, but the combination of spices, for me, is just right.  I admit it was a little weak, but then I put cream and sugar in it and only steeped it for 4 minutes.  The Assam in it does not have a smokey taste and I'm grateful for that.I do intend to drink more of it and offer it to friends.

column9: This blend smells as heavenly as it tastes.
column10: I am a lover of hot tea, but I've never tried the Higgins & Burke brand.  I figured this Chai flavor would be a great place to start.  The tea bag was quite an experience even while it was still dry.  The spices are very pronounced, especially the cardamom and the combination was quite an intriguing smell.  For my first cup I started with cold water and boiled it in a kettle, poured it over a teabag in a mug and let it steep for three minutes.  I'm telling you, that aroma was amazing.  (When I'm drinking hot tea I almost always drink it from a mug which holds approximately 8 - 10 ounces of water.)  After removing the teabag I tasted the tea without anything added.  The spices come through very strongly, not overpoweringly strong, but stronger than other brands of Chai flavor hot tea I've tried before.  The blend here is Assam black tea, cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, cloves, and other natural ingredients.  I thought the flavors were very nicely balanced, with none overpowering the others and yet remaining distinctive.I am not a tea connoisseur, but I do brew several pots of hot tea each day and I love to try all kinds of flavored teas.  The second cup of this Chai tea I made I started with cold water in the mug and heated it in the microwave.  Tea experts probably cringe when they hear that, but my palate is not trained to tell any difference and I couldn't taste any difference between the kettle boiled water and the microwave boiled water.  Each teabag comes sealed in an individual foil style pouch to keep it fresh.  My personal preference is to add a small amount of honey and a splash of milk.  The aroma coming off the hot mug of tea was enough to make me close my eyes and simply relax.

This was my first experience drinking any Higgins & Burke tea and I found their Chai Black tea nicely spiced. It was a very mellow blend, not quite as biting as some chai tea blends, and blended well with my soy milk. I added a splash of soy milk as I like tea with a bit of "cream".Overall, this was a pleasant tea that I would purchase for later usage.Recommend.

I live Chai tea, and this is one of my new favorites. Very strong smell, but a mellow full flavored taste but not bitter as some chai's can be. I will be buying this should me staple chai tea ever not be available.

column9: The best tea bag Chai tea I've ever had
column10: I've had a LOT of different varieties of Chai teas, some from bags, others home made.This is a strong tea, smelling much like strong cinnamon at first, yet a second smell or taste yields another different smell, more like allspice, but not quite.This is great with cream (classic Thai tea) or soy or rice milk (regular if you are OK with it I suppose).Great strong flavor that reminds me of chewing on cinnamon bark after drinking apple cider as a child, as far as taste.Might be a bit strong for newcomers to chai or Thai teas, but is absolutely wonderful! I mix half & half with soy or rice milk, but if too strong, you can add more milk to ton it down, or less to make it stronger.

I drink a whole lot of tea each day, hot & iced and this delicious tea works great either way.I've tried several of the Higgins & Burke teas and the quality is outstanding.It makes a wonderful hot cup on these cool mornings and I look forward to a long glass of the iced tea with my lunch in a few hours.It's delightful and makes a great strong tea, just the way I like it...

I like chai, but it's not always my favorite tea drink because so often it wreaks of strong clove that overpowers all the other flavors. When I smelled this tea bag it did seem to smell very strong. But I was surprised when I tasted it. It does not taste as "clovey" as the tea bag had smelled at all. I was really happy with the flavor. I love cardamom but so often barely taste it in other boxes of chai. Finally I could detect it here very pleasantly among the other spices. This tea has such a nice blend.I have seen recipes of chai from India, and they sound amazing (crushing almonds, warming milk over the almonds, add the spices, etc.). But I know I am not about to do that when I want a quick cup of tea. So far, this has been my favorite chai tea that I have tried. Just thinking about it now is making me want to go brew a cup!I like it with a tiny bit of sugar and some whole milk. It's really smooth, delicious, and hits the spot.The box says it has 162 mg of polyphenols per serving (I am assuming a serving is one tea bag/cup). Which is apparently good for your health. So that's another nice bonus.edit: It's now October 2012 and this is still my favorite chai tea. The other day was very damp, cold and rainy. I had a chill, and wanted a nice warm drink but wasn't sure if I wanted hot cocoa or chai. Then it came to me ~ how about a hot chai cocoa?! I brewed a cup of this Higgins & Burke Chai Black tea, let it steep as usual. Then I added a teaspoon of unsweetened cocoa powder (I had Hershey's cocoa powder on hand) and a scant teaspoon of sugar, and then added some whole milk. It was deliscious! Spicey hot cocoa! YUM! It hit the spot.

This delicate black Chai tea comes in an attractive box containing twenty (20) individually wrapped tea bags. With a pleasant aroma, a cup of this tea does not require milk or cream to soften it for a smooth afternoon "pick me up."

column9: very good even if they are bags
column10: I normally use loose tea since teabags get bitter because the leaves are broken. But I don't exclude teabags because sometimes they can surprise you...This surprised me. It's very good tea, and the added flavors are complementary and make for great cup. The flavors aren't overwhelming at all but you can easily taste them. The cloves were the biggest flavor. Very earthy/malty slightly sweet tea (in a good way).

column9: It had me at the first whiff
column10: Tea lovers know that tea is a sensual experience.  We enjoy how it smells before we even taste it and if the aroma is off it reduces our enjoyment.  This tea smells wonderful: cardamom, cinnamon and other spices combine to create an aromatic treat for the senses.  I made my first cup with honey and a bit of soy milk. It was delicious.  So have a cup of chai.  Ingredients: Assam black tea, cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, cloves and other natural flavors.

Very tasty black tea. It has strong clove smell, along with some cinnamon. Taste good, without bitterness, burning lips from spices and weird aftertaste. It smells even better than taste;)I like the idea of regular chai teas for example from Starbucks, but I don't like the amount of sugar they use. This chai tea with some milk and honey turns to delicious indulgent (without tone of ingredients preparation, like they suppose to be made).
One may find that the Chai tea becomes something just short of addictive. :) It's an exotic, rich flavour, and, as usual, Higgins and Burke teas are of a very high quality. Definitely recommended.

I have tried several brands of chai tea, and have been disappointed:  they have either been too heavy on certain spices, had an odd aftertaste, or not flavorful enough.  This tea doesn't suffer from any of these problems!  Richly flavorful with no odd aftertaste, and excellent made with either water or milk.

column9: smooth, but mild spiced black tea
column10: A perhaps too-mild Assam tea with spices, packaged in Canada, that makes a reasonable mid-sized cup but needs a long steeping.I drink a variety of black and green teas, though my true love is coffee.  Thus I similarly prefer stronger tasting black teas, deeper, ones with intense but nuanced flavors.  Also, I drink my black tea (and coffee) plain-- no milk.  Tasted that way, this Assam is an unassuming, mild tea, full-flavored, but not robust.There's a pleasing scent of spices on opening the packet, but less distinct spicing in the brewed tea.  For south-Asian inspired tea, I'd expect more scent/flavor of cardamom (I don't detect any).  It may be that getting a more robust tea with vivid spicing would mean moving to loose-leaf-- there's only so much room for tea leaves and water circulation in these little bags.Using boiling water, I made a 16oz mug with a 6 minute steep, and a 10oz mug with a 5 minute steep.  Both tasted fine (not over-extracted) and were almost surprisingly mild.  I don't suggest steeping at the low-end of the range (3 mins) considering how mild this tea is already.The tea drinks easily and is pleasant both hot and at room-temperature.  While I find it a bit too weak, if you like your tea mild and smooth, this one is a nice choice.
This chai black tea is so good I did not need to use any sweetener in it. It has a great, bold chai flavor. I just wish it had been certified organic. Otherwise love it!

I prefer "Earl Grey" tea, so I rarely drink a "Chai" tea.  Higgins & Burke has produced a very nice quality Chai product.  I didn't expect to like this tea.  I thought it would be too strong.  I'm pleasantly surprised to find a nice gentle flavor which isn't overwhelming and is quite enjoyable for a change of pace.The aroma is also pleasing and not overwhelming.

column9: A good spiced black tea for a non-chai guy...
column10: I'm not much of a chai fan, since I don't care for milk or cream in tea or coffee except on very rare occasions, so I got this to try primarily as a spiced black tea. Chai sacrilege aside, I liked this quite a bit. The spices do tend to overcome the taste of the Assam tea, but better that than the other way around. The flavors are distinctive, with the clove and cinnamon predominating. I steeped for five minutes, and may go longer next time, since I like my tea strong. I also used sweetener, but I plan to try it without, as the spice flavors are strong enough to not need more sweetening. All in all, this is a good spiced black tea at a very reasonable price. When I don't feel like taking the time to make a full pot of something else in my iron Japanese teapot, this will be a fine substitution.

This is quite a pleasant spiced tea. The flavor of the spices doesn't overwhelm the black tea flavor, as it does with some other chai teas I've tried. Instead there's a nice even balance. I agree with another reviewer that this product isn't as strong as the masala chai you'd get in an Indian restaurant, but I don't mark it down for that; I think it stands on its own as a valid variation on the "theme" of chai tea. But you should be aware that you aren't going to get the robust, tongue-tingling product you might be used to from restaurants, and if you add milk, you may want to do so sparingly.

This is the third tea from Higgins & Burke that I have tried.  The other two, Green Tea, and Earl Grey were quite good with subtle flavor.I have had traditional Chai Tea in Indian restaurants.  This Chai Tea is not prepared exactly in the same manner.  However, as a tea-bag product, it does stand on its own merit.The H&B Chai consists of Assam Tea with spices including: cardamon, cloves, cinnamon, and ginger.  When the tea is brewed, it takes on the dark color of the Assam.  At first sip, I found the dominant taste to be that of the Assam Tea. Then the spices asserted their own flavors.  It made for an interesting spicy but not overwhelming drink.  One downside was that there was a spicy aftertaste which lasted quite a while.  This is definitely a tea to have ready for special occasions.

column9: Well balanced.  Similar to my favorite brand.
column10: Earl Grey is my favorite tea and my favorite brand is the T brand from London.  I found this Earl Grey to be very similar but with perhaps a slightly stronger bergamot flavor than the T brand.  I drink my tea black so I find some of the other brands to be too dark.  This one was well balanced.I have tried many other brands but the T brand and now Higgins & Burke are my two favorites.

I am a huge fan of chai tea, so i was pleased to see this come up on the Vine program to let me try a brand I was unfamiliar with.TO cut to the chase, I found this to be a really nice blend of chai tea.  Some other brands like Tazo have a little more of a stiff bite, and the Stash double spiced chai has an excessive amount of cinammon that overpowers the flavor of the tea.  This Higgs and Burke Chai Black has a very nice mix of chai and black tea that has a great chai flavor but does not overpower the taste buds. I'll definitely buy more of this tea.

This chai is one of the nicest ones I have ever ordered on Amazon. It has a great, robust, rich spicy quality to it. This tea is great when infused with a healthy splash of milk. It opens up your senses. Just great.

A box of Higgins & Burke Earl Grey Tea was sent to me by Amazon Vine for review. Here's my take on it.Higgins & Burke, a Canadian company promising sustainable friendships amid socially responsible production (not sure what all that really means) produces Earl Grey, among several other types of tea. I received a box of twenty foil-wrapped tea bags. Upon opening the foil package, I was immediately aware of the slightly sweet scent of Italian bergamot (a fragrant orange) and anxiously awaited my first sip.I let a bag steep a full five minutes as directed, then added milk (actually, half and half). While pleasant, there was very little tea flavor, a disappointment. Today I decided to bolster the flavor by brewing in a pot. I used four bags, placed in a pre-heated pot, and 2 ½ cups of boiling filtered water. This brew steeped five minutes under a tea cozy. Since I'm a tea-to-the-milk type, I poured my tea into a Dunoon china mug which contained about 3/4 of an inch of half and half. Again, disappointing. The beverage was mildly sweet from the bergamot, but there was barely any tea taste.I consider myself more than a casual tea drinker, and Earl Grey is my tea of choice. I have tried nearly every available blend and still go back to Bigelow for real Earl Grey flavor. The Higgins & Burke, while pleasant and nicely scented, didn't do it for this tea-drinking reviewer.

Chai from a teabag is always a dicey proposition because it can't possibly live up to the chai served in Indian restaurants. Part of the problem is that every chai from a bag that I have tried cannot live up to much milk and authentic chai is creamy, milky and strong.
