In order to even come close to authentic chai, you have to make a very tiny portion and use a light hand with the milk in most cases.I tried this tea three different ways in order to find the best alchemy for a good result. The first way was straight with no milk or sweetener. I noted that it has a very strong scent of cloves. Though tasty enough when drunk straight, it doesn't really feel like "chai" without milk, so the second variation I tried was with a little bit of low-fat milk added cold after steeping for 5 minutes. This tended to wipe out all but the stronger spicy notes (with the clove coming out on top of cinnamon, cardomom, etc.). Finally, I tried my standard method for chai in a teabag and that was to heat 1/3 of the total volume as low-fat milk and 2/3 as water. Heating the milk makes it creamier and steeping the tea with it makes the overall flavor stronger. I recommend using no more than 8 oz. of liquid total and would say it's better to use 6 as it'll make a more intense and flavorful cup of tea.Though the box says that this includes the "robust" flavor of Assam tea (a tea I enjoy greatly), the tea flavor was largely overwhelmed by the spices, and again, especially cloves. I would recommend always steeping for the maximum time (5 minutes) and a light hand with the milk and water. This could be a much better chai if they had been more generous with the Assam and less heavy-handed with the spices, but it's still a pleasant enough drink.

Unlike Celestial Seasonings Chai Tea, India Spice, 20-Count Tea Bags (Pack of 6), which I occasionally drink (both tea bag and Celestial Seasonings India Spice Chai,  K-Cup Portion Pack for Keurig K-Cup Brewers, 24-Count), H&B's chai tea does not have that exotic a fragrance, being more along the lines of a minty, almost medicinal aroma. The tea, however, tastes quite good. With a little bit of fruit brandy, this is just the stuff to get me going in the morning. Tea bags are individually wrapped in a foil pouch, which seems to keep each bag fresher than a paper bag. It also keeps more of the aroma in, with a refreshing blast of that fruity mint coming out when opened. I found that steeping the tea for at least five minutes gets the most of the spicy aroma and the rich chai texture and flavor. This is really good, delicious stuff, and a definite break from run-of-the-mill tea.

This tea tastes cheap and artificial. One of the ingredients is "natural flavors" which is basically an additive. I would suggest getting a tea that doesn't resort to these flavor enhancers.The best chai tea I have found is from Peet's which has a strong, bold flavor. The Rishi brand is not bad either.

column9: Flavor a little weak for my taste buds
column10: The flavor of the chai seems a bit weak to me. Even the smell right out of the foil wrapper was mild. I expected a much stronger spice note. I could smell the cloves, but the cinnamon caught my attention first. I brewed up a cup and added a small amount of half-and-half and a teensy bit of sugar. The result was a mild, smooth tea with topnotes of spice, but not much spice flavor.I tried Higgins & Burke Earl Grey and enjoyed it, but this chai is a disappointment for me. I had expected something much stronger. I would categorize it as a scented tea because there wasn't much flavor, only some fragrance. Still, it is a nice tea -- it's not objectionably strong or bitter, and that's fine. It's just doesn't have the gusto I was expecting.

I am a Tazo tea fan and love all their teas. So it surprised me that I loved this English Breakfast tea more than Tazo's Awake tea. Usually I use two teabags per mug of tea. I tried two teabags of the Higgins & Burke tea but it was way too strong. So today I tried just one teabag and it was perfect. I'd say this tea is on the mild side but is perfect with a few spoons of dried milk powder and a packet of stevia. Since I drink coffee in the morning I save this tea for an afternoon drink. I like the pure flavor and will probably use this to make ice tea too. If you are a fan of Lipton then this tea is going to be a little more gourmet!~The Rebecca Review

We drink a multitude of beverages in our house.  Everything from soda, coffee, tea, hot chocolate and flavored water, so we always enjoy giving new drinks a try.  Higgins & Burke English BreakFast Black Tea is a pretty standard morning tea, here are my thoughts;Pros+ As with most tea, it's easy to make.+ Box dispenses tea packets easily and is made from recycled materials.+ Tea is sourced under the Ethical Tea Partnership.Cons- Taste is a bit mild.  Had to use two bags for a real taste.- Aftertaste can be bitter.Higgins & Burke English BreakFast Black Tea received a lukewarm reception in our house.  A lot of tea is really, well just tea and this is a perfect example of that.  Higgins & Burke English BreakFast Black Tea isn't a bad tea by any means, but it wasn't particularly memorable either.  While it was mildly enjoyable I probably wouldn't consider purchasing it again.

column9: Good tea, but there are better ones
column10: I do like the natural tea (without a lot of additives, or chemical procedures that make it "caffeine free"). Because of that, these Higgins & Burke black tea bags seemed interesting. However upon trying them I decided to stay with what I currently have.The tea flavor is actually nice. It is a little bit strong, but not too bitter. The real tea taste is not masked with additional flavors, and with a little cream it tastes great.However, it is not strong enough. I needed two bags per my usual cup, whereas one bag of PG Tips would suffice. Also, while there is no after taste, there is a small (really minor) amount of bitterness. I like smoother tastes. And this takes the tea quality down a notch from perfect.Overall, I can easily give it a high rating, but I would remind that there are better alternatives on Amazon.

column9: It has a nice floral taste that would go well with rose petals...
column10: I'm quite a tea lover, and I often brew up my own iced teas out of loose leaf teas and herbal ingredients.  I even have an entire section of my recipe book dedicated to homemade tea blends!  So, when I saw some tea up on the Vine page, I figured, "why not get it?  You can never have too much tea!".Truthfully, though, I wasn't expecting this tea to be any good.  I've tried out a ton of boxed black teas, and they tend to not compare too well to their loose leaf counterparts.  Most of the boxed black teas I've tried tend to be either bland and flavorless, or bitter combined with a lack of flavor.  So, I wasn't expecting much from this tea.I started off by smelling the tea bag, and I was surprised that it had a pleasant floral tone to it.  So, I brewed it up and I'm pleased to say that they pleasant floral tone is also there in the flavor!  In fact, I was very pleased with the flavor of this for a boxed tea.  It has that nice floral taste (as mentioned previously) and it wasn't bitter at all!  I much prefer a very smooth black tea, and this tea greatly fulfilled that desire.  Not bad at all.So, do I recommend this tea?  Well, yes!  If you are the sort who prefers milder black teas and doesn't enjoy that bitter tannin taste, then this is the plain black tea for you!  In fact, I'd recommend you pick up some dried rose petals too because that would taste great combined with this tea (1 to 1 ratio, I'd say)  If you do like a stronger black tea, then you'd best look elsewhere, but for the rest of us, Higgins and Burke English Breakfast is a fine choice!

column9: Any way I brewed it, a bit of a stale taste
column10: To give this tea a fair shot, I first brewed it exactly as the box said to, and had a cup black, as I usually drink tea.  I was underwhelmed.  There just seemed to be some kind of stale taste there---it didn't taste sharp or whatever the taste is called that I like tea to have!  It wasn't just that it was mellow, you want that in a breakfast tea a little, but it just didn't have a standout taste, and it made the bitter bit of taste not something that complemented the tea flavor, but took away from it.  Then I tried it with sugar.  I liked it a little better that way, but no better than very basic tea like Red Rose or Salada.  Finally I brewed it strong and made ice tea.  I liked it the least that way.  The flavor issues came out more with the strong and the cold, and I didn't finish my glassfull.I like the ideas of this tea---that they are part of the ethical tea partnership and that the box is made from recycled materials, and I will certainly use the rest of the teabags, but it is not a product I would seek out or pay extra for.

I'm not a fan of the milky, sugary "chai tea" that you get in coffee houses, but I do like all of the spices that go into masala chai.  (FYI - according to Wikipedia, the word "chai" means "tea".  Masala chai refers to the spiced tea.  "Chai tea" means "tea tea".)  This particular version of Masala Chai contains Assam black tea (that's from India), cinnamon, cardamon, ginger, cloves, and "natural flavors".  I'm not sure what those "natural flavors" are, but I like the other ones.  (OK, to be honest, I'm not sure what plain cardamon tastes like, but I frequently put cinnamon and cloves in my plain tea, and the cardamon doesn't seem to be screwing up the flavor of this tea.)I steeped the tea for 3 minutes.  It tasted fine, but it tasted a little better with about a quarter teaspoon of sweetener.  That punched up the cinnamon, ginger, and clove flavors (and probably the cardamon's too) without making it sweet.As of this writing, you can get 6 boxes of this for $18 on subscribe & save.  This is definitely worth $3 for a box of 20.  This has a lot of flavor without tasting like Kool Aid.

All Earl Grey tea's aren't created equal.  I've always heard this but just recently experienced it.I've recently discovered I love all sorts of flavored teas..from loose leaf to quality bagged.  So, when I rec'd this Earl Grey I was excited to try it.  Full flavored tea that tastes a little like some lavender tea i've tasted recently.Guess I should add here that when I first brewed this tea I tasted it hot and can tell you it was just nasty to me.  I brewed a little more and iced it.....wonderful tasting with just a little bit of sweetener.I traveled to Washington, DC this past week for a short vacation and happened to pick up some Bigelow Earl Grey for breakfast.  It barely had any flavored compared to the Higgins and Burke brand.  I'm quickly learning that all tea brands are different, just like people.Try this brand and you won't be disappointed.

This variant of a Chai Black [tea] is quite authentic-tasting. Chai means "tea" in India by-the-way. It has a rich smell and taste like a "real" India SPICED Chai -- plenty of cardamon and cloves [and other spices] added to a full black tea. They have done well to balance the spices and tea. Even when adding a modest amount of whole milk and brown sugar -- the above is evident. A typical way to actually brew an "India Spiced Chai" is to put black tea, sugar and spices into whole milk [in a pot] and boil it for a while -- even to the point that there is a thin skin over the top of the brew. That this tea [under review] works well made like a usual [Western] black tea -- AS a Spiced Chai -- is excellent. I was a bit wary -- until trying a batch just now -- being very familiar with India spice-tea as well as Western tea. Tiga Garrum Chai +++

I've been a tea drinker for about 30 years... I love tea. And although I have been a professional tea blender, and I know my Darjeeling from my Assam, I'm not one of those hoity-toity tea purists who just won't touch it if it tippy golden flowery orange pekoe, or worse, mixed with flavorings (you heathens!). No, I am more the kind of tea lover who thrives on Earl Grey and Orange Spice, and will drink Red Rose if that's what's around, because it's better than no tea at all.This chai is delightful. It has just the right balance of tea-ness and spice-ness, with just a hint of bite. I can taste cinnamon, cardamom, and I think black pepper, and it goes so perfectly with sugar and milk that I'm restraining myself from a third cup because I don't want to set off my arrhythmia. I could drink  this all day. It definitely goes on my list of "yes" teas.

Higgins & Burke Chai Black Tea makes a pretty decent cup of tea. I've tried it hot with a little milk, and iced without (both with sugar, of course), and enjoyed it both ways. It's flavorful and spicy, with the ginger giving the tea a bit of a bite. It is on par with the best chai I've tasted from store-bought teabags. I like it a lot better than Tazo Tazo Chai Filter Bag Tea, 24-Count Packages (Pack of 6), for example, with the main difference being the particular blend of spices. Recommended.

This is a black tea with cardamon, cloves and cinnamon and ginger. As a "chai" tea, it's, well, not exactly true Indian Chai, which in addition to those sweet spices, has black pepper and is prepared by stewing the tea along with spices into an evaporated milk and water mix in a pot on the stove. How do I know? I have a friend overseas, a Sikh from Thailand, and he has his assistants make it in a little kitchen behind his office and that's how they do it. Chai masala, CTC black Assam tea, raw sugar and evaporated milk. And it's so delicious, served in little glasses and it cools you on a hot day by making you sweat.The Higgins & Burke tea, however, has the spice mixed in the tea bag, and no black pepper, which personally, I find is the best part of chai. But it's convenient and it makes a nice pot of tea, rather reminiscent of Bigelow's famous "Constant Comment" except it has no orange peel. The bags come in individual envelopes, so it's nice for serving in an office setting or at home to guests if they want to brew a mug on their own. It's pretty nice iced, and you can throw in slices of oranges for a real treat, or add some fruit juice (apple is nice) diluted fifty-fifty for a sort of summer punch that is slightly sweet but not cloying. But don't expect "pulled tea" or Indian Chai. For that, go get a box of chai-masala and follow the directions.

column4: A Research It Maven "Just the facts please"
column10: This Higgins & Burke Earl Grey tea is the perfect one for morning refreshment. It is full flavored, smooth, and delicious - plus it really perks me up to get ready for the day. I was told its a traditional English breakfast tea - don't know about that, but it sure is my favorite am tea!

This Chai black tea is quite delicious.  It has the flavor of chai with a trace of halloween, pumpkin like spice added to it. And it must not have too much caffeine since I did not get the usual energy boost that black tea normally gives me.  That is why I savor this tea for mid day to early evening. Since I do not use milk or sugar, I get the true taste of the tea with each cup because I let it steep to get that full bodied experience from each tea bag. It is dark and rich!  It is truly quite enjoyable and I will be purchasing this again.  I recommend it to who ever would like a little spicy flavor in their cup of tea.

The Higgins & Burke Earl Grey Black Tea smelled delicious as it was being brewed. But unfortunately it does not taste as good as it smells. No matter how long we steeped the tea it never got strong enough for us. It was okay but not as good as the Bigalow I usually drink.

column9: Earl Grey as it should be
column10: I didn't used to like Earl Grey tea because the brand that I bought was very bitter. But this Higgins & Burke Earl Grey is excellent. It has a very nice light citrusy aroma, but the bergamot flavor is not overpowering. The tea is not bitter and does not leave an aftertaste.I left one teabag in the cup for more than 3 minutes and the tea was still very smooth -- even without adding milk or sugar. This is excellent as a hot tea, and even when it cools to room temperature it is still flavorful. The tea lacks the sharp astringency that some other brands of Earl Grey have, so I think it would make a very mild iced tea, although I have not tried it on ice. If you like tea but don't want the harshness associated with some brands, try this one.

I didn't know what to expect when I got this tea. After my first cup I sort of turned my nose up. It was a taste I wasn't familiar with and I didn't think I liked it, but when I was a little girl my mother used to tell me to try something three times, before I made up my mind that I didn't like it.I think the first time I heard that was when she gave us (four girls and one boy) spinach for the first time (well it was canned). I really didn't like that. Didn't like it the second time either. But the third time I heaped butter on it and liked it a lot.So, I tried it again and I liked it a little better. Then I thought back and remembered the above spinach story and remembered what the butter did for the canned spinach and I thought, why not try cream and boy of boy did that do it for me. Delicious. So there you go, the third time was the charm for me. Just like with the spinach.

I love tea. I make it from bags, and brew it from leaves.  I drink pretty much every flavor, including chai.  Twinings is my favorite brand for chai, but I'm always looking for new varieties.  This Higgins & Burke is tasty, but also quite mild.  I found it to have a more prevalent nuttiness than other brands of chai, but it is also far less sharp.  As another reviewer touched upon, this won't stand up to much milk.  I made it with just a dollop and found it to be relaxing and flavorful, but not distinctly chai.  It was also good without milk.  This would be best for tea drinkers who avoid chai because it is too bold for them, or those that just like to switch things up (like me).  Sometimes, I want that chai flavor without the spicy bite (such as Twinings Ultra Spice Chai-yum!).  This a nice alternative for those occasions.The price here on Amazon is very competitive.  Most decent/good teas are about $3 a box in a grocery store.  The Subscribe and Save price is the same, without the hassle of going to the store.  Overall, this is a good tea for the right people.

Honestly, I'm a tea snob.  I prefer loose tea and eschew bagged tea. So I was  surprised with this tea. It's tasty and everything you'd expect in a chai. I think it would be an excellent iced tea, and it's great hot too.

This Higgins & Burke Earl Grey tea is quite nice. Reasonably  strong and well flavored but without the overwhelming amount of Bergamont oil found in  some Earl Grey blends. This is pleasant to drink hot or cold  and does not leave a per-fumy aftertaste or oily chemical texture in the mouth. It does not seem excessively caffeinated either.

column9: A decent cup of earl grey tea
column10: I am a frequent drinker of black tea, so I am able to compare this with the many other brands of tea I have purchased before.  It's an OK cup of tea, not bad, but nothing special either.  The ingredients are natural, just black tea and oil of bergamot, but it somehow lacks the flavor of a fine earl grey.  Though the name Higgins and Burke sounds English, it appears to come from distributors in Canada and Texas.  It doesn't say on the teabag where the tea comes from and when I visited the manufacturer's website, it wasn't clear there either.This does not compare with some of the better quality tea makers, such as Barney and Sons.  But for the price, it offers a decent value.

Pleasant blend of spices. Yummy aroma and taste. I prefer my tea on the stronger side and steeped for a full 5 minutes. Not quite as robust as some chai teas I've had but all in all a good cup of tea.

Earl Grey is one of those blends you often see done a hundred times over, and it's hard to find one you like. Earl Grey: you know when you brew a cup whether that brand is going to be a love it or leave it! My biggest problem with EG blends is that they tend to taste mossy to me, like someone dragged my tea bag through a pond swimming with algae bloom.Higgins & Burke's Earl Grey is not mossy, nor is it overpowering. It's a mild flavor that I was able to enjoy, and didn't need to add anything else to it. No sweetener, no milk/cream, it was great on its own. And I know someone somewhere will cringe, but I even liked it when we added a bag to our usual ice tea brew. Definitely will buy this.

I compared this to Ahmad Tea -London- and Twinings of London versions of Earl Gray Tea.  I let them all steep one minute in the same amount of water.Higgens and Burke had the strongest bergamot of the three.  Ahmad was most astringent, H&B second, and Twinigs smoothest.By the third cup. (re-using the same bag) H&B was practically perfect.Since I prefer subtler and smoother  Earl Gray, my recommendation is to use more water (like a small teapot for one bag rather than a cup or mug) and be careful how long you leave it in.If you are a fan of strong tea or double bergamot tea, I think you will really like this.

I'm really more of a loose-leaf tea drinker, when I have my morning cuppa, and I like it the English way, strong enough to stand to stand the spoon on end, a good dollup of milk and a spoon of sugar. Earl Grey, with the citrusy flavoring is better with honey and no addition of milk. Higgins & Burke is milder than I like when jumpstarting my morning with caffine, but is still a very nice and convienient way for that one single cuppa.

I first tasted Earl Grey tea in college, after a lifetime of Lipton tea bags.  I was in awe; I never realized tea could have such a seductive aroma, such a delicate subtle flavor.  From then on, I was a convert to naturally fragrant teas, so I was happy to try this one.It is slightly less aromatic than the Earl Greys I have known, and the flavor is even more delicate than the ones I am used to.  But is has a very clean flavor, and a wisp of the smell that endears Earl Grey to me.The tea bags are well constructed, but do leave a  tiny bit of sediment in your cup.Overall a refreshing subtle cup of tea -- Earl Grey Lite?

The sign of a good Earl Grey tea is the use of real oil of bergamot, not just flavoring. Bergamot is a yellow citrus fruit, in the orange family, native to southern Italy. The fruit is considered inedible, however the oil extracted from the skin has been the foundation of the cologne industry for many, many years. Higgins & Burke Earl Grey is provided in individual, foil-wrapped tea bags. Open a pouch and you are immediately aware of the distinct aroma of bergamot.Higgins & Burke chose asian black tea as the base for their Earl Grey. Unfortunately, the tea is almost dust and somewhat weak.If you allow it to steep long enough, you can end up with a drinkable cup of Earl Grey. If they had chosen a better tea base, the beverage could be better.

I drink tea 3 to 4 times per day. I prefer black tea in the mornings, especially Earl Grey. This is a rather bland Earl Grey tea by Higgins & Burke. This is the second tea I try by this brand. The first one was a Green Tea that was also bland.I steeped the tea as directed directly into my mug. As mentioned it was very light in flavor and color. This might be a good thing for those that do not like strong teas. Next time I made this tea I steeped it longer to attain the desired flavor. The tea was not very aromatic.I was rather disappointed by the tea, especially when you consider the price. Stash has a better tasting Earl Grey.

column9: Pretty good for a non-tea drinker
column10: I pretty much drink coffee non-stop and only drink herbal teas when I am not feeling well. I've heard of Earl Grey tea, as I witnessed people from older generations drinking it. First, the fragrance is strong, however pleasing. When I took my first sip, I wanted to spit it out. However, I decided to give it a chance and continued drinking it and I actually like it. Initially, I wanted to throw a pack of Splenda in it, but I found it tastes good with or without sugar and it was a definite pick me up. Perhaps, I'll drink tea more often.

This is a nice Earl Grey tea with a good balance of bergamot flavor and black tea. I'm a big fan of Twinings, and this is comparable to that brand in terms of quality. The tea bags are individually foil-wrapped, preserving freshness. This tea doesn't stand out as anything special for me, but it's quite good for what it is and I gladly recommend it if you're looking to try a different brand.

This review is for Higgins & Burke Earl Grey Black Tea, 20-Count (Pack of 6). A fresh, pleasing aroma is the first thing you'll notice about this tea. But it's the wonderful flavor that will keep you coming back for more. Earl Grey Tea is one of my favorite teas, and this one is perfect.

column9: It does taste like average earl grey
column10: I find just about all earl greys taste the same to be, unless they have a creme note in them.  This tea is good, but reminds me of average earl grey, no bells or whistles here.  I like the design of the box, especially the part where the bags come out of and the bags brew well.

column9: Smooth & Subtle Taste, But Caffeine Content is High
column10: Higgins & Burke's Earl Gray tea is mild but soothing. I've noticed that this company produces very subtle, mild tasting teas and I've sampled their Green Tea, which also has a light, clean taste. This Earl Gray is a little bland - certainly not as strong as the Mighty Leaf or Tazo, and it's easy to assume that the tea must not be very strong. Was I wrong! I drank two cups just before bedtime, and stayed awake almost all night! I usually have a cup of Lipton black tea before bed, and the caffeine content in it must be very low compared to Higgins & Burke. Needless to say, I won't have any more of this Earl Gray so close to bedtime.

column9: A few steps above other Earl Grey teas
column10: As a general rule of thumb, I like black tea, but I don't like Earl Grey. It's never strong enough for me, or it tends to have a bitter feel going over the tongue.This tea was so sweet, that I could drink it with no milk or sugar.This tea was so smooth, I could drink a whole pot.This tea was so strong, that I only brewed it for two minutes and it was perfect, and I could dry out the teabag and use it again.This stuff is legit. I'm totally going to have to order more of it when I run out. And I'm going to have to look into other teas by this company.Love it. Totally love it. Good any way you serve it.

Higgins & Burke is a company in TX and Canada. This is their blend of Earl Gray Black Tea.  The tea has a wonderful bouquet; which makes each sip all the more enjoyable.  The taste is very mild. Most certainly more than other brands I've tried.  My husband felt it was too light w/ barely a kick of caffeine.... I'm use to drinking lighter blends.The individual tea packets are probably the most attractive I've seen. I took some on the go and even layed them out on a flat surface -- just to test reactions. I noticed more men stopping to look them over than women. The company name and colors are masculine, so I'm guessing that's what caught their attention.I think those who enjoy their tea mild will enjoy Higgins & Burke's Earl Gray Black Tea.

Whether you like the Higgins and Burke Earl Grey will depend on how strong you like your Bergamot. This one had too-strong a Bergamot aroma/taste for me, almost a lavender aroma/taste to it, so much so I actually checked the ingredients.  It wasn't by any stretch a bad tea--no bitterness, no aftertaste (I don't put anything in my tea), and it brewed a good second cup.  I guess I prefer a bit more black tea flavor and less bergamot. I mostly use loose tea, and when I use a bag tea, I usually use the Twinnings or store-brand (Wegmans) Earl Grey and I'll continue to do so, though I'll finish this box with no real complaint ; it just wasn't my, um, cup of tea

This is a fairly mild Earl Grey, although it is an excellent black tea. When you open one of the individually-wrapped tea bags, you can clearly smell the bergamot oil -- it is quite pleasant. After steeping for about 3-4 minutes, the tea is very dark, but the bergamot remains somewhat subtle. Considering the great aroma when you open the package, I was hoping for more flavor. Regardless, it isn't a bitter tea and is quite smooth.20 bags are in the box, each individually wrapped. The individual packets do a great job at preserving the product, because you can barely smell the bergamot oil through the packaging. The box is made of 100% recycled fiber, and the product is blended and packaged in Canada.Overall, a good tea, but I wished it was a little more "Earl Grey".

One of the better earl grays I have had.  Nice aroma, great taste.  Even though this comes in your standard tea satchel instead of the new pyramid bags the flavor is one of the best Earl Gray teas I have had.  Excellent bergamot aroma and taste.  Great tea, I will buy this again.

column9: A little weak for my taste
column10: I was excited to receive this product for review through Amazon.com's Vine program.  In the afternoon I prefer a good cup of tea over coffee.  And I prefer loose tea over a convenient tea bag.For the purpose of reviewing the tea I decided to leave the bag intact and brew it as directed.  The scent was inviting but not as potent as when I brew loose tea, so I decided to skip the Half & Half and taste it pure first.  Hmm, not bad, but not great either.  I added a little sugar and tried again.  It seemed to bring out the flavor a bit more but still, so I tried it with a splash of Half & Half.  That washed out the flavor significantly.All in all, it's a good tea for those who are used to a lighter flavor, but I prefer bold taste and am still hunting for the Wow factor I remember from a loose tea that came from Russia I was in love with when I still lived in Germany.  This one didn't even come close, although it does brew a nice cup of tea.  It's just a bit too bland for me.
this tea has a very nice flavor, true to the Earl Grey blend. I highly recommend it as a good value.

column9: Not as "robust" as some, but overall not bad
column10: Though the box shows "1912", I've not heard of this brand before.  I'm certainly not a "tea connoisseur". . . but. . . but I know what I like.. . and I've always had a fondness for Earl Grey. . . and I like this Earl Grey.First, the packaging.  Each sachet is of course individually-wrapped.  But instead of being just a plain paper wrapping, the wrapper is lined with plastic to help hold-in the flavor even longer.I noticed that there was no staples used, which led me to believe that the product was kosher, and upon checking the box, it is indeed kosher.I certainly don't find this to be a "robust" Earl Grey, so if that's what you're looking for, then you might want to try another brand, such as Kusmi, which is one of my favorite teas, but considerably more expensive than Higgins & Burke.  FYI, Kusmi offers a few different "styles" of Earl Gray.  One of which is not even called Earl Grey but "Anastasia".  If you have tried other brands of Earl Gray and felt they were somewhat "overpowering", then you might want to try Higgins & Burke.  Especially for the reasonable price, it's not bad at all.Kusmi Earl Grey (20 Tea Bags)Kusmi Anastasia Tea Bags

As an Earl Grey fan, who has tried numerous branded (boxed, loose and/or tea bag)and specialty types, I found this to be one of the best I ever drank.True, it's not inexpensive for bagged tea, but you can purchase via Amazon subscribe'n save to bring the price down. Given what else is out there in the market at similar price points, this is, in my opinion, a superior offering.It's interesting to read the other reviews: Some folks find it too bland while others say it is too strong. Obviously, it's relative and subjective based on your own taste buds and sense of smell. I find it to be mildly strong and just love the bergamot fragrance. (Opening the individual teabag package is a wonderful start to tea drinking, whether by the cup or the pot. I really loved the fragrance, which seems really fresh and vibrant as opposed to some bagged teas that have a strong fragrance but seem "old" and musty.)If you're an Earl Grey lover, this tea is definitely worth a try. And for those who say it tastes like an herbal tea, I would beg to differ. I have tried numerous herbal teas (which I simply cannot, literally, stomach) and this is not at all in that category.I used two bags in one four-cup pot and it was perfect. I didn't need any lemon or sweetener and drank it "as is" from the pot. To me, this is a sign of a really good tea. You need nothing more than good cold water, proper brewing and it's ready to go.Drinking this tea elevates the experience from "just another cup" you grab on the fly to one that makes you feel as if you're in a really nice tea parlor (OK. Having some homemade scones with it doesn't hurt!).It's the kind of tea I'd brew even if I wasn't in the mood for tea just to enjoy and get a lift from the fragrance.This is my new favorite tea for those times when I need a moment to de-stress and regroup--and pretend I'm living the good life with not a care in the world (Yes, tea can transport me.).

Earl Grey is essentially a carefully selected blend of black tea with Italian bergamot, an orange flavored fruit with a lemon color.  I brewed mine for five minutes and the result was a mild black tea flavor.  i personally did not notice the orange, but then I'm probably not that taste sensitive.  It's a fine, mild flavor, and black tea is very healthful.

Definitely an earl grey.  Perhaps a little muted.Before getting this Higgins & Burke, my tea drinking habits were guzzling PG Tips and a cup of some Bigelow Earl Grey when I felt like having dessert.  The Higgins and Burke is somewhere in the middle.  It doesn't smack you with that flavor/fragrance of fruit loops like the Bigelow, but has more substance than the PG tips.Regardless of all that, everyone's sense of taste is different and our moods and cravings do swing.  This Higgins and Burke tea is well worth testing to see where it hits your personal palette.

column9: Citrus fights the strong black tea flavor
column10: I usually like Earl Gray teas for my morning brew, but this one has more of that bergamot oily/orange flavor than I'm used to. It's not the bright orange rind taste of Constant Comment, more of a lemon/orange oil taste. It's not awful, but it's not the straight and strong Earl Gray I like best.I'd recommend buying this in a smaller quantity first and trying it out before you buy in bulk. I think this is a flavor you'll either love or hate.

Earl Grey was one of my favorite flavors before I got into loose leaf tea and I still come back to it on a regular basis. The comforting aroma of bergamot the it's flavor mixed with black tea is hard to beat. Of the many brands of Earl Grey I've tried over the years, H&B's is without a doubt one of the better ones.It rises above an average tea bag in that it can produce a well balanced cup over at least two steepings. Just brew it for a shorter time than recommended on the packaging. For me it is under 2 minutes for the first cup and longer for the second. It mixes well with cream and sugar too, though I prefer mine black. Another plus is it's ability to taste good as a cold tea as well as a hot one. The citrusy bergamot flavor is prominent in this mix so perhaps that is its secret.In any event, quality tea leaves and flavorings are evident here and I would purchase it again. There are better loose leaf tea blends available, but as a bagged tea it is hard to beat.~ Kort

column9: Good way to start your day
column10: This tea has a wonderful aroma. Earl Gray is a tea used to fight depression, stress, and tension.  Frankly, I just like the taste hot or iced.  I prefer it in the morning as it awakens my senses and gives me just the right jolt to start my day.  Who couldn't use a little "de-stress" tea before their morning commute?This is the best Earl Gray I have tasted, very smooth.

column9: Strong bergamot flavor, but still pleasant
column10: I drink tea occasionally and Earl Grey is usually my tea of choice. I typically drink Twinings brand with some honey. I tried the Higgins & Burke the same way. While it was pleasant, it wasn't quite the same and I think I prefer the Twinings brand over H&B. This tea is, like others have said, very strong on the bergamot and light on the tea. While it tastes good, it tastes almost more like an herbal tea than a black tea. While this won't keep me from drinking the H&B tea, I'll probably still keep buying the Twinings brand.As an aside, H&B has good sustainable practices and uses recycled materials. While I applaud them for being green, I doubt it's something that will carry significant weight for most tea consumers.

column9: Best of Britain in a cup
column10: I know, most people think the best beverage of Britain is the beer. Ok, for some it is but not for me. I used to live in the UK and have wonderful memories of brewing a kettle, making a wonderful cup of tea with milk and sugar and it was like heaven on earth. When I moved back to the states I didn't do that anymore and forgot how amazing it was. Until I received this tea. WOW! It is authentic, and uses the most amazing, fresh ingredients. The bergamot and orange oils are fresh and aromatic and the blend of the flavor with the tea is spot on and delicious! The flavor is perfectly blended and not at all overpowering. This may be the best black  tea I've had, and I love tea! What a find. I am so happy I discovered this!

Long a fan of Earl Grey tea, Higgins & Burke's is my new favorite. It has an exceptional taste - a strong, rich flavor with the essence of Italian orange bergamot. This premium tea is not bitter. It tastes good both hot or cold. If you're a fan of Earl Grey, do yourself a favor and try this one.

I have been drinking more and more tea lately, as I have been trying to cut back on coffee. One of the things I have noticed is that it seems like more and more brands of tea are getting "weaker". I don't know if they are going to cheaper tea leaves, or are using less leaves per tea bag, but in many brands I have had to go to two tea bags per cup of tea. I was pleasantly surprised that this Higgins and Burke Earl Grey led to a robust, flavorful cup of tea with one bag.I make tea using RO (reverse osmosis) water. 99.99% of a cup of tea is water, so for good tea you must begin with good water. I only use RO water in making tea. I steeped the tea for four minutes and then removed the bag. The cup of tea was most excellent, and you could detect the Bergamot, which is the key part of Earl Grey.I often drink Twinings Earl Grey, but between the two, I must say that I prefer the Higgins & Burke.

I drink a lot of coffee and tea, I start the day with coffee and graduate to hot and ice tea depending on my mood.I had afternoon tea yesterday and loved my first cups of the delicious Higgins & Burke Earl Grey tea.I then brewed two pots of this tea for glasses of ice tea this afternoon and I love the taste.It's a strong, yet smooth Black Tea with the tasty oil of Bergamot to set off the wonderful Earl Grey taste experience.I Love it!  Let's have another cup...

When this arrived today I was impressed by the packaging. Each teabag is also nicely wrapped to preserve the delicate aromas in this tea blend. I brewed the tea for ten minutes which seemed perfect. As I went to take a sip the aroma of bergamot definitely got my attention. I would almost go as far as to say this is a very romantic tea. But I could be under the influence of all the other romantic things I've done today including reading poetry and eating French chocolates. Since I wanted to stay up late reading in bed I took the chance and drank this delicious Canadian tea. As they say on the packaging..."indulge...escape." I'd love to try other teas by this company.~The Rebecca Review
This is a great tea - good flavor and aroma, and very smooth.  As other reviewers have noted, it is less bitter than some other Earl Greys I have tasted.  A good tea!

column9: I Love This Tea, I Have for a Long Time
column10: I have long loved Earl Grey Tea and I've long loved Higgins & Burke's Earl Grey, so it is with pleasure that I type these few words. If you like Earl Grey, you'll love this tea. I don't know any other way to say it.

column9: Aromatic and smooth tasting for Earl Grey Tea
column10: I had never heard of Higgins and Burke tea before, but am so pleased with this tea that I will be trying more.The first thing that hits you when you open an individually wrapped tea bag is the wonderful aroma....very pleasing to the senses and a nice, not harsh fragrance.  The tea is equally smooth.......it does not become bitter if you leave the tea bag in the cup while you drink it.  More like darjeeling base tea than other black Earl Grey teas that I drink.If you're spending a fortune at Teavana, then try this instead and save yourself a trip to the mall.  Because individually wrapped tea bags are in a dark brown waxed paper type wrapper that is airtight sealed, it is not likely to lose this quality over time, like your tea in the tin will.  Graceful enough to give as a housewarming gift or small remembrance.Highly recommended.

column9: Mild Earl Grey flavor, not too strong
column10: I pretty much only drink black tea. Other than the occasional mineral water, I drink nothing else. I love black teas and the stronger the better. For those like myself, you will find this version of Earl Grey mild and pleasant. I don't find this tea bitter at all, no matter how long I let the tea bag steep for. If anything I find it even milder than other common brands of Earl Grey, like Bigelow and Tazo. The bergamot is not overpowering at all and I find this even makes for a great to to go with meals because of the mild flavors.After drinking almost the entire box, I rate this as definitely one to order more of. It's a great way to introduce someone to Earl Grey who may not be accustomed to the bold flavors of the blend. It's also a great blend for those who like Earl Grey, but who sometimes find the flavor bitter or too strong. Probably one of the mildest blends I have ever had.No issues with the tea bags releasing any tea leaves into the cup and it makes a nice clear drink, with no cloudiness. No powdery residue left behind and no bitter after taste. This Higgins and Burke blend is delicious and goes really well with an meal.

This tea has a really strong bergamot flavor. Personally, I prefer Earl Grey teas with a good strong black tea and only a hint of bergamot, so that the flavor of the tea itself is the focus.In this tea, the bright oily citrus tang almost overpowers the taste of the tea. It's a little better if you let it steep for a full 5 minutes, but even then, the bergamot taste is still prominent.It tastes a lot like Stash brand Earl Grey, so if you like that, you'll probably enjoy this one too.

column9: Quality black tea with a little KICK to it!
column10: I liked this tea.  The Italian bergamot orange adds a little extra punch!  Well sealed packets keep the tea fresh, tea bags make it handy to use without the fuss of loose tea.  Definitely a notch above the usual black teas and I'd rate it higher than other brands of Earl Grey that I've used.  Cost still a consideration, but, hey, who doesn't deserve a bit of luxury now and then??  FIVE STARS for this HIGGINS & BURKE EARL GREY tea.

This is the second Higgins & Burke tea that I have tried.  The other one was Higgins & Burke Green Tea.  Usually, I drink either Darjeeling tea or Green tea.  Of course, I am familiar with Earl Grey tea, which is essentially black tea with oil from the rind of the bergamot orange, The Earl Grey in question was a nineteenth century British prime minister.This tea is is indeed very dark; it turns almost black after very little brewing time.  It has a very pleasant aroma and a taste that is not overpowering. Each tea bag is sealed in an individual packet for freshness.It does have a very nice kick, meaning it has a good level of caffeine. I recommend using in the morning or afternoon but not in the evening for anyone whom caffeine keeps awake.

Generally I am a coffee drinker, but drink herbal tea in the late evenings before going to bed. I found this a smooth flavored tea with a medium body and a great blend. It has a touch of orange flavor with a correct amount of bergamot. This is what makes the tea unique. I really enjoyed this delicious cup of tea.1. Tazo Awake Black Tea, 24-Count Tea Bags (Pack of 6)2. Taylors of Harrogate, Yorkshire Gold Tea, 160-Count Tea Bags3. Newman's OwnOrganics Royal Tea, Organic Black Tea, 100 Individually Wrapped Tea Bags, 7.05-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)

column9: Not bad. A touch bitter; better with sugar.
column10: Amazon sent me some for free to review.If you took away the bergamot ("Earl Grey flavor") leaving only the black tea, I would say I was disappointed with the weak yet slightly bitter flavor. Combined with the bergamot, the bitter begins to make sense. With a touch of sugar the whole thing wakes up and the flavors work pretty well.I would willingly drink this tea again, but it will not be my preferred brand of Earl Grey tea. I think others have a nicer balance and less bitterness.

I'm generally a fan of Earl Grey tea, and this is a good one. The flavor is strong but not overpowering. It comes in a nice box. What else is there to say? There may be some slightly better teas out there, but I don't think you'll be disappointed if you select this one.

I have always loved a good cup of Earl Grey tea, and this Higgins & Burke Earl Grey is no exception! The black tea is quite subtle, and less acidic than most, which makes this an excellent choice for anyone with stomach problems. There is a strong flavor of bergamot orange, which may be a bit off for those die-hard Earl Grey drinkers, but which I found delightful, especially when drank first thing in the morning with my breakfast.I give Higgins & Burke Earl Grey tea five stars and big thumbs up! I highly recommend it for anyone who enjoys tea, and especially for the tea connoisseur.***DISCLOSURE: This product was provided by Amazon Vine in exchange for an independent and non-biased review.

I recently tried Higgins & Burke's green tea and thought that the taste and quality of the tea was excellent so I jumped at the chance to try the Earl Gray as this is one of my personal faves.  Again, I wasn't disappointed.  No fancy packaging here, just 20 individual tea bags full of high quality and excellent tasting Earl Gray tea.If you are a fan of Earl Gray you would not be disappointed.  I would definitely consider buying more of the Higgins & Burke teas as I have been very pleased with both teas I have tried.

column9: Very tasty. A good alternative to my standard PG Tips.
column10: I usually drink PG Tips, so I'm used to filtering the taste through a half-cup of "waste-water." This tea, however, has a sweeter backtaste unlike PG Tips, and you actually don't need to filter it.I use one bag per 8oz. mug with half boiling water and half milk, then a teaspoon of sugar. It tastes great, and, of course, the second cup is better.There isn't that bitter aftertaste the Tips is known for, so I may actually be looking into Higgins & Burke in the future.

I am a huge fan of tea - I never acquired the coffee taste and so I drink tea for my relaxation, for my morning boost, and just because I like the flavor. It has actually become sort of a hobby of mine, so I enjoy trying new companies and new blends. I was excited to see Higgins & Burke had an Earl Grey tea, as that is one of my favorite flavors. Finding a really good one can be difficult - so much depends not just on the tea itself, but on the Bergamot flavor that is an essential part of this tea. Sometimes the flavor is weak, sometimes it seems stale, and sometimes it is just...off. So I was curious to try this one.I am so pleased to say that it is excellent. There are only two ingredients in this tea - "Premium Black Tea, Natural Oil of Bergamot". The Bergamot aroma is strong and fresh - I could pick up the slight aroma on my fingers after I put the tea bag into the cup. I let the tea steep in the hot water for 4 minutes (suggested time is 3-5 minutes), then added a touch of honey. The overall flavor of this tea is wonderful. It is fresh and light, slightly sweet, not stale in any capacity. I am very impressed. I have had two cups already, and both were consistently good. Higgins & Burke seem well on their way to making me a fan!If you like good tea, then I would have to say I highly recommend this company. Their Earl Grey is excellent, as is their Green Tea.

I am a big fan of Earl Grey tea, and have been for many years.  The aroma and flavor does vary from tea to tea, ranging from delicate to robust, but I like them all. I consider that to be in the nature of full disclosure; I am pre-disposed to like this stuff.  And like it, I do.Higgins & Burke's Earl Grey falls on the delicate side, with a warm suggestion of bergamot that offers comfort rather than a stirring rendition of "God Save the Queen."  It makes a tasty cup of tea which would be just as good with milk and sugar as it is black.  At least in my opinion.  The only thing I find curious about it -- and it wasn't really a drawback for me, but it might be for some -- is that when I took the packet out of the box, I got a fleeting whiff of Aspergum.  It dissipated quickly, and wasn't evident in the brew, but I found it odd.Don't let that strangeness put you off if you're an Earl Grey fan; it could just be me losing my mind.  If you've never tried Earl Grey, this isn't a bad place to begin.  And if it matters to you, Higgins & Burke support sustainable tea-growing practices, and all their teas are ethically sourced.  Definitely a plus for me.

column9: Rich, a Bit Malty, but Balanced +++
column10: This Higgins & Burke Earl Grey Black Tea compares well to other Earl Grey black teas. I have tried many teas, including a number of Earl Greys. I just tried this variant brewed moderately strong -- and served in four ways -- hot alone and with milk then iced alone and with lemon -- each way with moderate brown sugar as well. I took an initial sip [before adding the brown sugar] and after smelling it carefully and looking at the exact color. It was just fine then and excellent after serving with brown sugar -- but in two ways hot and two ways iced as stated. This Earl Grey black tea is rich, a bit malty [which I like] -- but well balanced with the bergamot adding well to the quality black tea -- with a good amount of tea in each bag being enclosed in foil-lined packets +++

Higgins and Burke is hardly a household name in the crowded tea market, nor is it an easy one to remember, but their Earl Grey is faultless, with a medium body, delicious flavor and a subtle rather than overpowering bergamot presence.

I am more of an iced tea person than hot tea so my review is based off brewing this for iced tea. Even though this is black tea if you're expecting a typical Lipton flavor you will be surprised.I found this tea to be very enjoyable and reminded me of the type of iced tea that is common in California at upper end restaurants.Would I make this team every day, maybe not but it is a great to break up the routine and have a tea that more special.

column9: Good but a little lemony for me
column10: Smooth taste and no bitter aftertaste, not too strong or too weak but it is just a little too lemony for my taste. If you like lemon in your tea you should like this Earl Grey.

I have always preferred fresh-brewed teas to the store-bought, over-sweetened teas that are so readily available these days. As such, I like finding a nice tea that I can brew up myself. Higgins & Burke's Earl Grey is quite good - a nice, smooth black tea, with just the right mixture of oil of bergamot. It makes for a refreshing cuppa, especially first thing in the morning, out on the deck, under the sun, and with some nice almond cookies.I like it a lot!(Review of Higgins & Burke Earl Grey Black Tea)

These tea bags produce quite a good cup of tea.  I generally go for loose leaf tea, but there are times when a bag is simply more convenient.  This Earl Grey has a strong bergamot scent.  The bergamot flavor is strong once brewed, but not overwhelming.  It was easy to brew a cup that was smooth and not too bitter.  I brewed for approximately two minutes, which is my usual for bagged black tea.  The tea was fresh and flavorful.  This is definitely a good choice for those in search of a bagged Earl Grey.

I usually prefer green or herbal teas, but this Higgins & Burke Earl Grey is a nice alternative. One thing that I usually dislike about black teas is the strong, sometimes bitter, flavor. This one is smooth and mild, and I was very pleasantly surprised. I did not steep for even three of the recommended 3-5 minutes, but it was strong enough for me. The package claims that it has a mild lemon flavor, but I could not distinguish any lemon flavor at all.I also liked the individually sealed tea bags that keep everything nice and fresh.

I love tea but my favorites are all very mild. I love Chrysanthemum, most fruit teas, some mild green teas (not Japanese green tea) but I am not a fan of Earl Grey. It's the same with coffee for me, the milder the better. My experience with Earl Grey in the past (Twinnings) is that it was so strong that I couldn't drink a whole cup. But this one is a milder tea than the other brand so this time I liked it better.I really think that whether or not you will like it depends on your personal preference. Do you like milder or stronger tea. If you prefer milder, go with this one. I smelled the teabag before preparing the tea and noticed that it smelled milder to me. Strong tea is just harsh for me.

column9: A Spot of Tea . . . but not quite Spot On Earl Grey
column10: I think it was Jean Luc Picard with his "Earl Grey, hot." on Star Trek:TNG that first had me try that particular type of tea.  But it rapidly has become my favorite in the family of black teas with flavoring. I've enjoyed trying out many different brands of Earl Grey to narrow in on my favorites, so when the opportunity came along to try Higgins & Burke's Earl Grey, I snagged the chance.Among other brands I tend to dislike Bigelow as being too mild and flavorless.  Twinings and Stash both make a fair cup of Earl Grey, and they tend to be my regular brands to buy from the store shelves when I'm in need of more.  Both have a robust black tea with a nice balance of bergamot oil and fragrance that appeals to me.  I tend to prefer a stronger tea that holds up well with milk.  When I'm splurging on my favorite, it's usually Good Earth Earl Grey.  Higgins @ Burke's Earl Grey, I'm afraid to say, falls somewhere between Bigelow and Stash teas for me.My chief complaint is that it is too mild--it's a very delicate version of the tea that really doesn't hold up well with milk.  There's also a very odd sort of dry anise flavor to the tea that doesn't match up with my expectations for Earl Grey.  The bergamot flavor is there, but it isn't super strong.  This is best for tea drinkers who prefer lighter blends, more delicate teas and probably drink their Earl Grey plain.  It just doesn't match up with my preferences.Given that I've also tried Higgins @ Burke's Green tea, my observation would be that this company overall delivers a milder version of teas with some unexpected flavors.  Not bad, certainly, but not really *my* cup of tea.Happy Drinking! ^_^ Shanshad

Earl Grey is perhaps my favorite flavor of tea.  But I wasn't impressed by the flavor of Higgins & Burke Earl Grey.  The first cup was far too strong.  Admittedly the second and third cups made from the same bag are much better, still the flavor is unremarkable.The first cup left a lot of sediment at the bottom of my cup.If you like Earl Grey, give "Numi" a try instead.

column9: It's an okay cup of Earl Grey
column10: I'd had high hopes for Higgin's & Burke's Earl Grey tea, as I truly enjoyed their green tea blend.  An avid tea drinker, I've sampled a lot of different Earl Grey blends. This is the first one that upon trying a sip, I had an overwhelming taste of licorice, not bergamot.  Since I am not a fan of licorice, it wasn't a pleasant discovery.  Thankfully, the taste does 'mellow' out after a few more sips to a more 'Earl Grey' flavor, the bergamot becoming more prominent, but it's not the strongest cup of Earl Grey that I've ever had.  I'm keeping in mind that people can have different reactions to flavor and will probably offer this to friends who enjoy licorice more than I do.

I'm big on organic and all natural teas from manufacturers that are environmentally friendly and free trade approved. Higgins & Burke serve an all natural tea and do a good job environmentally - 100% recycled (55% post consumer packaging), and are certified from the Ethical Tea Partnership, Rainforest Alliance, OCIA, US Organics and have Kosher certification (according to their website). So check, check, check and check. Great pedigree but how about the taste?This Earl Grey is a mild mix that tastes clean and crisp. A very good tea for sipping while unwinding at home (or on the star ship Enterprise.) I think I could go with some brands at the local market that are less expensive but compared to the organic section at local markets this is a very good value as the cheapest I've found good all natural teas in this quantity would be closer to thirty-five bucks.Overall, this is a good tea from a socially responsible company at a very good price. Recommended.

Earl Grey tea is a favorite variety of mine and although the Higgins & Burke tea is delicious, it is a bit too mild for my taste. In hopes of deepening the brew and depth of flavor I let the tea steep for twenty minutes but it was still very weak. It is quite smooth without a hint of bitterness, but also rather bland.This tea would be perfect for someone who dislikes strong tea and/or has a habit of forgetting the tea bag in the cup or pot because this tea never reaches an undrinkable state.

The Higgins & Burke Earl Grey tea is delightful. The box is really easy to open as are the tea bags themselves. I think the scent of Earl Grey tea should be evident as soon as you open the wrapper for the tea bag and that distinct aroma is present but not overpowering. Earl Grey tea should have a specific flavor and Higgins & Burke has used the perfect blend of bergamot and black tea. I love that these are the only two ingredients as well.Higgins & Burke Earl Grey tea is the perfect way to start your morning or for enjoying during afternoon tea.

A tea expert I am not. However, my husband and I recently switched from coffee in the morning to English breakfast yea and we drink green tea with dinner and since we use and like Higgins & Burke green tea, we were anxious to try their Earl Grey. We've had Earl Grey in the past and I'm not sure why we settled on breakfast tea instead with breakfast, probably just because of the name, you know breakfast tea with breakfast. But now, after having tried this, we're switching. We drink it with milk and it like it very much.

This Canadian tea carries on the great tradition of the fine English purveyors of what would seem to be Great Britain's national beverage (if one omits warm ale). I note with pleasure Higgins & Burke's participation in the Ethical Tea Partnership, details of which one can find on the Web. It is gratifying to find companies willing to commit to social and environmental responsibility.As to the tea itself, I chose to sample my favorite flavor, Earl Grey, often a good test for the ability of a tea manufacturer to provide just the right amount of distinctive flavor, which for Earl Grey is Bergamot, without overwhelming the taste of the tea itself. It passes that test admirably to the tongue but is a little lacking in aroma for the nose--mine at least. The tea, brewed according to the instructions--for about 4 minutes--is not too strong on the tannic acid, smooth rather than astringent like some teas.A quality product.

Lovers of Earl Grey tea come in various varieties. :) Contrary to the norm, I like my Earl Grey strong and sweetened. Though the Higgins and Burke version is not the most intense I have tried, it has a very pleasant flavour, with none of the 'liquorice' tones I've sometimes found in other brands. It is sufficiently full-bodied that one need not use multiple sachets to get a nice pot. Highly recommended.

column9: Not the Earl Grey flavor I expected
column10: This didn't taste like either of the Earl Grey teas I love, namely Twinnings and Bigelow.  The bergamot flavor is extremely mild, to say the least, but the fragrance of the brewed tea smells a bit like perfumed soap--not tea.

I'm a big Earl Grey Black Tea drinker. This tea was flavorful, but not as good as Twinings Earl Grey Tea, Tea Bags, 50-Count Boxes (Pack of 6) or a Trader Joe's house brand that I buy. The flavor is more subtle and less pronounced. Food flavors like perfume essences are very personal. I prefer the more pronounced flavors in Earl Grey. If you prefer a lighter Earl Grey, you'll love this!

This tea has a fairly strong and distinct flavor, unlike many of the other black decaf teas.  I use it to make ice tea.  For just drinking a cup, I use Bigelow's Organic Breakfast blend.  Really nice, aromatic, heavier flavor.  Amazon sells it, too.

This is one of the best tasting tea's I have tried hands down.  I am not a frequent drinker of Earl, but bought some for the winter season.  Higgins & Burke seems to have a good offering so I am looking forward to picking up some of the teas I drink more frequently like green tea.

column9: I like my tea how I like my women: intelligent, interesting, with a good sense of humor, liberal politics, and non-smoking
column10: This is okay tea. I think of English Breakfast as being a big, bold, full-bodied tea, and on that measure this stuff falls short. With one teabag to a mug, it's pretty mild. The flavor and aroma are there, but you have to go looking for them; they don't jump up out of the cup and grab you by the lapels and give you a shake. I have to use two bags to a cup when I want a real English Breakfast experience, and that feels profligate.

This is a solid tea a bit stronger than most but hardly up there with the powerhouse sort of teas. I prefer a strong tea such as Twinings Irish Breakfast or Taylors of Harrogate Yorkshire Gold. This tea is a bit more complex than most others but in the few cups I've tasted, it doesn't seem consistent. I tend to steep my tea longer than usually recommended which I find imperative here to get the full flavor. No 3 minute steeps here or you'll surely find the tea weaker than it should be.The inconsistency is in flavor. Some cups have had a fruity slightly citrus complexity to them while others miss that.As a note, I drink my tea with nothing added using purified water as a base. The box states that this tea stands up well to use with milk and sugar. I think you'd end up with a candy-like confection adding those two but it's your choice, I suppose.The tea comes in individually foil wrapped bags and each bag has a string attached which is something I infer the British tea drinkers find redundant. Anyway, the foil wrap should guarantee fresh flavor which leaves me baffled at the somewhat inconsistent flavor between cups.

I am a devoted tea drinker and I have tried many different teas in my time.  The Higgins and Burke English Breakfast tea is pretty mediocre in my opinion even though it is nicely packaged. Individuality bagged tea can deliver the taste and pleasure as loose teas plus its great when one doesn't have time or inclination to brew from scratch but don't expect that from this product.

column9: There are better brands out there
column10: I'm a huge fan of tea and drink a LOT of it.  This is the first time I tried Higgins & Burke brand and have to say that I've never heard of it before.  English Breakfast Tea is probably my second favorite packaged tea to drink (Earl Grey being my first choice), but most brands I've tried are usually pretty similar.  Not so with this brand.  The aroma didn't seem as rich and flavor seemed somehow "off" to me, but I couldn't quite put my finger on what I didn't like until I read one of the other reviews here on Amazon and the reviewer described it as "musky."  That's about as accurate a description as I can think of.I like my tea strong (leaving the bag to steep the entire time I'm drinking it) and do not add sweetener or cream or lemon.  After trying the first cup, I knew that I'd have to add something so on my second mug I added a bit of sweetener and it helped take the musky edge off, but it still wasn't what I consider a flavorful English Breakfast blend.If you're a fan of traditional English Breakfast Tea I would recommend Twinings English Breakfast Tea, Tea Bags, 50-Count Boxes (Pack of 6), The Republic of Tea, British Breakfast Tea, 50-Count, or even Tazo Awake Black Tea, 24-Count Tea Bags (Pack of 6) over the Higgins & Burke brand.

column9: Comes in a easy dispensable box
column10: The first thing I did was to sniff the box. The tea is so well sealed in its packets that the box smelled like a box. I suggest they put a little loose tea in the box to lure you in. Then I noticed a perforated section on the box to use your thumb to make an opening to dispense the packets.  Each serving comes in an individual foil packet with a little tear to show where to open the packet.  Inside the tea looks more like granules. They are sealed in the standard tea bag that has space in the middle when it unfolds. There is the tag tied to a string for dunking and extracting the bag after steeping. The ingredients description is black tea.The tea itself looks and tastes like the standard Lipton tea. If you close your eyes you cannot tell the difference.  It does have a nice dark amber look in a clear glass.  In my cup it left a little residue that could be seen when using a paper towel to clean it later.

I've been a tea lover and connoisseur ever since I was 11 yrs old -- and I've enjoyed many types of teas from all over the world.However, I find this Higgins & Burke English BreakFast Black Tea to be musky with an almost oily aftertaste, and that does not please my palate. I tried it with sugar -- and then with cream -- and the musky taste is still overpowering. Now this robsutness/musky/oily taste might be something I would appreciate on a cold winter night, perhaps with some grains and butter added, like the barley and butter that are added to the tea that the Buddhist monks drink, to make Tsampa -- and I would not hesitate to try that, in the colder months, as the musky/robust tones of this tea might very well make a satisfying (Americanized) Tsampa.But frankly, this tea was meant to be enjoyed as a stand-alone brew, and unlike their WONDERFUL Early Grey tea, Higgins & Burke English BreakFast Black Tea, is not really my cuppa tea.

I am a big tea drinker, I normally drink tea all day, switching to de-caf at some point during the day.  This is my first experience with Higgins & Burke English Breakfast Black tea and I am drinking it now.  I love this tea, it is just strong enough without being overbearing and very good.  I added a bit of milk and really like the flavor of this tea.  So many teas I have tried are so bland or weak and this one is a good strong flavor with or without honey or milk. I would buy it again.

column9: Get the Boost You Need with This Great Tasting Tea!
column10: In my opinion, Higgins & Burke English Breakfast Tea is quite pleasing to the taste buds. This black tea is the perfect way to start your day and it's also a great afternoon pick me up as well with an adequate amount of caffeine.I found the flavor to be quite robust! I tried drinking this tea as is, with sugar, as well as with milk and each way tasted delicious being uniquely different but in each way full of body. It also smells as wonderful as it taste.Each box of tea comes with twenty individually wrapped bags of tea which is good for space savings and ideal to take along with you wherever you may go. It also gives you tea that will stay  fresher longer. I like that the box  has a perforated edge so you can easily keep the bags inside the box too if you prefer.This tea company is totally thinking of the environment by using 100% recycled materials with a minimum 55% post-consumer in each and every tea box. I love too that all of this companies  black, green and white teas are 100 percent sourced and purchased under the Ethical Tea Partnership standards. I would highly recommend this to anyone looking for a exceptionally great tea from a company that is giving back in more than one way. And it's a great price too through Amazon's Subscribe and Save!

column9: Hearty Breakfast Tea with Robust Flavor
column10: A cuppa Higgins & Burke English Breakfast Tea can be a delicious start to your morning or a great pick-me-up in the afternoon.  Delicious served alone, it tastes wonderfully with a splash of milk--somehow partnering with milk brings out a warm almost honey note of the tea that is comforting in its familiarity and association with a cheery kitchen filled with the aromas of a large and hearty breakfast.In fact, English breakfast tea was designed to compliment a large hearty meal.  Its toasty aroma combined with its robust full-bodied taste has a nice albeit slight aftertaste of light floral.  Supposedly created in Scotland it is usually a blend of black tea that includes  Assam, Ceylon, Kenyan and Keemun teas.  The English of the 19th century were fascinated by anything Chinese.  This tea was Anglicized by putting the "Engilish" in front of "Breakfast."  Its been popular since the days of Queen Victoria.Higgins & Burke's English Breakfast is a blend of rich and malty Assam and full-bodied and earthy Ceylon black teas.  Remember a black tea is black due to the level of oxidation that the tea leaf is exposed to during processing not because it comes from a different plant.  Also don't confuse English Breakfast tea with Earl Grey which has a citrus-y bergamot flavor or Lipton which is blended from over twenty different teas to achieve the distinct Lipton tasteI drink my Higgins & Burke red--the Ceylon black tea produces a dark red liquor with a little Teavana German Rock Cane Sugar (1 lb).  One 8 ounce cup provides me with just the amount of caffeine I need to bolt me into my day when I am not waking up through exercise.  The preparation is simple:  Boil your water, pour over the tea bag and seep for as long as you choose.  I'd recommend around three minutes if you don't like your tea too strong.In terms of price, Twinings English Breakfast is definitely less expensive if bought in bulk.  Lipton's is more expensive.  However, I like the flavor of Higgins & Burke and the convenient packaging of receiving six 20-count boxes makes it easier for me to store.Bottom line?  Canadian company Higgins & Burke knows how to blend a nice cup of English Breakfast Tea at a reasonable grocery store price.  For tea drinkers everywhere, there is nothing as arousing as a brisk eight ounces of English Breakfast tea in the AM to jump-start your day with a familiar comfort beverage.  Recommended.Diana Faillace Von Behren"reneofc"
I really enjoy a great cup of tea when I want to relax.  This tea has a good strong flavor and I look foward to drinkinh it.

I thought this tea was about average. I prefer a bit more taste in my Earl Grey tea. After making a cup of this I  made a cup of the Stash Earl Grey and it really eclipsed the Higgins and Burke in both taste and aroma. This isn't a good enough tea to make me leave Stash's products.

column9: Not bad if you like a lighter Earl Grey
column10: This is pretty good Earl Grey that seems to not have much of a bitter after taste at all. It does lack a bit of the flavor I'm used to with other brands of Earl Grey tea however.I would say if you would like a lighter Earl Grey that tastes a bit watery, this is the tea for you.

As an Amazon Vine participant I'm required to write reviews about the Vine products I order. Accordingly, I'm writing this review, knowing it won't be helpful for potential shoppers. For that I apologize. In writing a review, one is forced to "rate" the item (one to five stars). I had to choose a rating so I chose a neutral one (3 stars). I know some people, myself included, get peturbed at reviewers who leave an unfavorable rating for a product when the bad experience they had was with the merchant and not the product.I tried to be fair in this review which I was required to write to remain in the Vine program.

At 18.4 cents/bag, this is a very expensive tea.  Stash Premium Double Bergamot Earl Grey Tea, Tea Bags, 100-Count Box is 13.8 cents/bag (100 bags), Bigelow Earl Grey Tea, 40-Count Boxes (Pack of 6) is 13.1 cents/bag (240 bags), and Twinings Earl Grey Tea, Tea Bags, 50-Count Boxes (Pack of 6) is only 10.8 cents/bag (300 bags).  Other quantities are also available but the price/bag tends to be small compared to the company cost differential.  Is the quality worth the cost difference?  No.  I drink my tea straight up--no sugar, no milk, no lemon (except when iced).  This tea has far less flavor than say Twinings--it's thin even without adding sugar or milk.  I tried steeping it an extra long time too but that didn't help.  The Bergamot is less compelling, and the tea taste is almost absent.  I cannot recommend this product.

column9: Higgins and Burke Earl Grey tea
column10: while Earl Grey is not my favorite tea flavor i usually like it, especially in the morning, but i didnt like this tea. There is flavor that is left in my mouth and its kind of biter. I love their green tea and was looking forward to a good, full bodied tea, and i was disappointed. It wasnt awful, id drink it if it was herd, i just wouldnt go out and buy it.

I drink coffee at breakfast, but regularly enjoy a cup of tea in the early evening.For last night's tea, I used the Higgins & Burke English Breakfast blend. The first thing I noticed was the fresh aroma of the tea leaves inside the tea bag.  That was a nice start, as with some other brands, you smell nothing at all.After brewing the tea for about 4 minutes, I added sugar (2 scant teaspoons) and started sipping.  The tea had a strong, hearty taste, and that good aroma held on throughout the entire cup.Enjoyable!The packaging is also good. The box opens in a way that allows each individually packaged tea bag to drop to the bottom, where it is easy to remove. The individual packaging of each tea bag preserves freshness.The only reason I deducted one star from this rating is because I did notice a VERY SLIGHT bitter aftertaste when I finished the cup.  Not that it bothered me, but it might not be agreeable to those who object to any bitterness at all in their tea.

column9: In this case, tea is tea
column10: I had two cups of the Higgins and Burke English Breakfast Tea and found it acceptable, but not remarkable. I primarily drink Twinings tea and did not feel that Higgins and Burke was as pleasing as my regular English Breakfast Tea. The first cup was weak, so I let the second (made with a fresh tea bag) steep longer than normal. The second cup was stronger but left a slight bitter aftertaste. I use sugar but no milk and no lemon in my tea. While I will certainly use the remaining tea bags in the box, I will stick with my normal Twinings in the future.

column4: Shana "That's my opinion- I could be wrong!"
column10: I usually steep tea bags to make iced tea and some tea bags don't steep well or you have to use two or three tea bags to get a nicely flavored tea. With this tea it only took one bag to get a nicely flavored glass of iced tea.I'd recommend this tea for iced tea or for those that like their tea unsweetened with a bit of lemon juice as I do, as it does have a very pleasant flavor.I'd definitely recommend this one for tea drinkers and I'd repurchase.

column9: TEA - THE CUPS THAT CHEERS BUT NOT INEBRIATES
column10: HIGGINS & BURKE ENGLISH BREAKFAST BLACK TEAI do love my tea, hot and sweet or cold and sweet, just love it.  I have never enjoyed Higgins & Burke before, but am glad I was able to check it out.The tea comes nicely packaged in an eye-catching sturdy little box.  Each tea bag is handily sealed for freshness in its own private tea sachet.  When I took the tea bag out of the sachet I was immediately aware of how good the tea smelled.  It's very fragrant with a rich aroma, smelling somewhat floral.I take my tea with sugar and leave the bag in my mug the entire time while drinking.  The taste was full-bodied and rich, with a very flowery taste to it. This tea has a different and satisfying taste to it, not over-bearing or weak, just darn good.While duty called, my tea cooled off.  I decided to add some ice to see how that would taste.  WOW!  It tasted even better than while it was piping hot.  My next pitcher of ice tea will be made with Higgins & Burke Breakfast Black Tea.I think you would enjoy this tea; many have as Higgins & Burke have been around since 1912.  While I've always enjoyed Celestial Seasonings and Bigelow flavored teas, along with Twinings Earl Grey and our old stand-by Lipton, this tea drinker now can add another tea to her list of favorites.Higgins & Burke has a good many different varieties of tea to choose from.  This Breakfast Black Tea is made with Assam and Ceylon teas and is very good. If you enjoy tea and would like to try something a little different in the taste department, this tea would work for you.Thanks.Pam

I really like the Higgins & Burke Chai tea, so I was looking forward to trying this one.  I was disappointed.  It is not horrible, but to me it tastes very, very weak with no depth of flavor.  I like my tea on the stronger side (I love Harney & Sons Russian Country tea, for example), and this one doesn't even taste as strong as a basic Lipton tea bag.  On the plus side, each bag is sealed in an airtight packet.

column9: I Do Not Wish to Appear Too Fulsome with My Praise
column10: But, wowser! did I love this tea. Which is unusual for me, because, as a general rule, I am not fond of cloves.  But this tea is so fragrant and delicious that even the cloves won me over.  the ingredients listed on the box include: Assam black tea, cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, cloves, and natural flavors.  Each tea bag comes in its own foil package.  When steeping, it gives off a wonderful aroma, and the taste is wonderful, rich and spicy.  It's great for getting my motor running in the morning. When this package is gone, I intend to buy more.  I don't ever intend to be without it.  And that's the highest praise I can offer.
The scent of cinnamon and cloves is authentic and strong, but it has far too many cloves.  The overall flavor profile seemed skewed. The black tea portion could be stronger.

Higgins and Burke makes a decent Earl Grey: it has a splendid burst of bergamot coupled with a rich blend of black teas.I like tea that has the ability to hold up to milk and sugar, even if I'm not having it with either. I often choose to not put milk in Earl Grey, but even then I still want it to have some pluck. This tea has pluck. Granted, it is not an Irish Breakfast but then there is a reason for that - if you filled a bag full of Assam then you would overpower the bergamot.Some teas can achieve that strength by filling their bags full of fannings. That is not what Higgins and Burke are doing. I took apart one of the bags to check. They are using real tea leaves.
