They aren't using fannings nor are they using crush-to-curl.I rate this as one of the better bagged Earl Greys.

Most tea lovers are very familiar with Earl Grey tea. Many first learned about it from Star Trek, since it was Captain's John Luc Picard's favorite hot drink. Earl Grey tea is black tea with the addition of oil(or other flavor elements) of bergamot(a citrus fruit mostly grown in Italy). This brand uses Asian black tea with oil of Italian bergamot. It has a very full bodied flavor and the bergamot also comes through prominently. It comes in stay-fresh foil packets. Another nice little feature is that each tea bag has a string attached with a stitch and no metal staple, so there are no metal staples or glues to affect the taste for purists. Highly recommended for those who appreciate black tea and also like citrus additions.

Normally I prefer a strong chai that I brew from the actual spices and tea but this chai in individually wrapped bags imparts a delicate and pleasant taste.Higgins & Burke has been in the tea business for one hundred years. They pay attention to quality in all their teas and their chai made from select assam black tea, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and ginger is one example. I tried it with half and half, one time unsweetened, the other time with a little honey added. Both were equally pleasing.A perfect cup for sipping while curled up with a good book.

I have never heard of this brand but I'm glad I tried it. I've always drank Tazo Chai, so this is what I'm going to compare the higgins & Burke Chai to. When you take the Tazo and the H&B tea sachets out of the wrappers, both have a wonderfully spcy chai aroma. The difference is in the brewing. I didn't expect to prefer the Higgins & Burke over Tazo but I DO!!! It brews a nice "red" colored spicy cup of chai. No bitterness but the aroma and flavor is just as rich. It does not matter now long you leave the tea bag in your cup. On the contrary, the Tazo will become very dark and bitter. The bitter tea flavor of an oversteeped cup of chai masks the spices. I think I'm converting to H&B becuase the flavor is great. And no matter how long you steep you just can't go wrong with this blend. Every cup is delicious!!! I recommend you get some :) It comes in a pack of 6, but if you love it like I do, it won't last too long. Or you can share. Your co-workers are bound to ask to bum sum off you when they try it.

Well, first off I should say that I'm not new to tea.  I'm not sure I'd describe myself as a "tea connoisseur" but I'm pretty experienced with tea.  I've tried just about every type of tea out there (white, black, green, herbal, even puerh tea!), and I regularly make my own custom blends using loose leaf herbs and spices.  I'm a pretty big fan of tea, so I naturally jumped at the chance to get some nice chai tea.  I already have my own homemade chai recipes that involve simmering loose spices and adding in milk and sugar, and it's great, but I've always wanted to try some plain chai without the milk.So I got the Higgins and Burk Chai in the mail and decided to brew myself a cup to try out.  I steeped it a full 10 minutes because I steep all my tea for 10 minutes (I suspect a lot of people would find this too strong for their tastes, but that's how I like it).  My first impressions of this tea is that it's pretty weak for a chai style tea.  I felt like the strongest taste was the cloves, and it really could've used stronger notes of ginger and cinnamon.  Not to mention, the black tea portion of it tastes a bit not-so-good to me.  It's difficult to describe, but I'll explain it as best as I can.  I once bought a huge box of cheap crappy pekoe black tea and it tasted terrible.  It was just lacking in good flavor and only tasted of bitter tannins and blandness and nothing else.  This tea is not nearly as bad as that one was, but the black tea portion of it seems to have a bit of that taste to it.  I had my own Assam tea (before I used it all and ran out) and it seemed to taste much better than this - even plain with nothing else in it!  Of course, it could've been because of the source of my teas/spices (I get everything from the mountainroseherbs website); maybe the tea is better from there.  Anyway, the other spices in the tea hide it well enough so it's not a big deal.  I did decide to make my own homemade blend to see how it would turn out using the same ingredients (I used 2 parts black tea, 1/2 part cinnamon, 1/8 part cloves, 1/8 part cardamom, and 1/2 part ginger).  Then I did a side by side taste test using the exact same amount of sweetener.  The Higgins and Burke version is not terrible or anything, but I still think my version won by a small margin.Anyway, if you're a casual tea drinker, this tea will probably be fine for your tastes, and far more convenient than making your own loose-leaf blends.  In addition, if you are the sort who prefers a less spicy chai then this tea would be great!  In the course of further usage, I also discovered that the Higgins and Burke tastes better as an iced tea.  Go figure!  Well, my overall opinion of the Higgins and Burke Black Chai is that it is a decent choice for anyone who wants a mild pleasant chai in a convenient tea-bag option, but I think I'm going to personally stick to my own homemade formula because I love making loose leaf tea blends!

column9: Taste like Spiced Tea but its pleasant.
column10: I am a big lover of Chai tea and I understand how hard it is to reproduce the same results you see in Indian restaurants (another one that is hard to reproduce is Thai ice tea but that its another story).The package states 20 teabags/satches, but they really are just teabags. Each is individually wrapped in its own black wrapper for freshness and it makes a difference compare to Celestial Seasoning, as it is highly more aromatic when opening. However, you do end up with a lot of paper waste, which is ironic since they state in their package that they are "working for a responsible tea industry." C'est la vie. The carton is made with 100% recycled fibers though.Moving on, I have the habit of sometimes leaving my tea bag in my cup and forgetting I made tea in the first place until I realize it about 30 minutes later. This happened with my first cup and I was expecting a too strong bitter tea, but was pleasantly surprised that the tea tasted just fined over-steeped.Its hard to taste the various notes in this tea however. It mostly taste like cloves and it leaves a spicy aftertaste in your mouth for about 5 minutes after you have drank the tea.Cold milk eliminates some of the notes, so its better to have it with warm milk added.Does it taste like true chai tea? No. It tastes like spiced tea. But the price is reasonable, it taste fine when over-steeped, and you can have it in various ways (plain, with rock sugar, with hot milk, with condensed milk, cold milk with ice cubes). The various methods of enjoyment lets you find the one that is "just right" for you (for me a bit of sugar with a bit of hot milk).

column9: Nice tea but needs more flavor
column10: This is a nice tea with subtle flavors.  It's not very tanic like some teas can be but the flavors I expect in Earl Grey are just too mild for my tastes.  I allowed it to brew longer in my second cup but it was still pretty weak.  I enjoyed it but would prefer something a little stronger.

I haven't been to England in half a dozen years. My wife and I used to go every year, but for various reasons, we haven't been in six years. We drink tea there, not so much at home, but we got this tea and it brings back fond memories for me. It's very good tea. I'm not a connoisseur, but I know what I like and I like this tea.

I love Earl Grey tea and will pretty much try any brand at least once.  I got a box of the Higgins and Burke which was the first time ever trying this brand.  The fragrance is very strong and wonderful.  I was a bit surprised at how light the tea was was when steeping and thought maybe the flavor would be weak but I was pleasantly surprised when I took my first sip. It is not weak at all and the frangrance that hits your nose while drinking this just adds to the experience.  My wife was near me drinking her regular tea and she laughed because she could smell the fragrance of mine and it made her tea taste like Earl Grey.  I like this tea enough that I will be buying more of it and plan on trying other teas by this company.

As a lifelong tea drinker I usually prefer loose tea but on occasion and for convenience sake I make my tea with tea bags. Here are my comments with regards to the Higgins & Burke Earl Grey tea bags:GENERAL:1. These tea bags are individually wrapped to preserve their flavor - a plus in my opinion because too many tea bags produce rather bland tasting tea when they just come unprotected in large boxes.2. When removing the wrapper the tea's scent is pleasant but not overwhelming, quite balanced.3. It produces a good strong and flavorful cup of tea which is not bitter (I use 1 bag per cup and steep for 3 minutes).4. According to the manufacturer this tea is produced under Ethical Tea Partnership guidelines.FLAVOR/SCENTThe flavor of this tea is a bit more on the citrus-y side and does not have as strong a bergamot note as is normally the case with Earl Grey. However, I did not mind this - the flavor was a good balance between a slightly more dominating orange flavor and a subtle but noticeable undertone of bergamot which gave a kind of earthy depth to the orange flavor.This is a pleasant tea and a slightly different interpretation - at least to my taste buds - of the usual Earl Grey which tends to be heavier on the bergamot. Recommend.

My wife and I drink a tremendous amount of tea. I just went through our pantry a couple of hours ago and found no less that 23 different varieties stashed here and there. These varieties include quite a number of different brands. Not of the different blends we drink, the on constant is that fact that we continually return to Earl Grey; it could sort of the considered the corner stone of our tea drinking. Yes, we like variety, but for general everyday use, we are never without Earl Grey.Now of the various brands of this blend we use both Higgins' & Burke (That which is being reviewed here) and for years have also used Twinings. Which one we use depends greatly upon which is available at the local store at a given time and which one happens to be on sale during that time. To say that we are "frugal" would be a kindness. I can tell you that in our opinion and according to our taste, that either brand is quite satisfactory. Now I know that each individual's taste differs greatly so I can only comment on our personal likes and dislikes. That is one of the reasons I am quite happy with the fact that we now have a wonderfully large variety of not only blends, but also brands to choose from...it has not always so.This tea has a rather rich earthy taste and if you drink it straight some may detect just a hint of bitterness. Since we both use sugar in our tea (my wife also uses cream), that is not a problem with us. To be frank, most of the Earl Grey tea we have encountered, no matter the brand, has that hint of bitterness...that is the nature of this particular blend. We are perfectly satisfied with this Higgins' and Burke and will continue to use it.If I may though, I would like to offer a couple of suggestions. Use pure water. Water found in many city water systems simply is not adequate due to the various junk they add to it. If you find yourself with no other water source, then it is best to use purified bottle water. The second suggestion is to let it steep long enough. The directions for this particular tea suggest 3 to 5 minute timing. I personally have found that closer to 6 minutes is required to bring out the full flavor of almost all tea bag tea.Anyway, this is an excellent product. We have used it in the past and will most certainly use it in the future.Don BlankenshipThe Ozarks

column4: Ursula K. Raphael "AstraDaemon of The Zombiep...
column10: I'm the first American born into my mother's UK family, so when I say that I was raised on tea, I am not exaggerating. The thing is, unlike coffee, I never have sugar with my tea - just a little bit of milk...drinking it this way makes me more aware of the subtle differences between tea brands and "flavors."Even with all the herbal teas available, Earl Grey will always be my favorite tea. The Higgins & Burke Earl Grey has just the right amount of bergamot. When I opened the individual foil-wrapped bag, the orange aroma hit me first...not overpowering, but rather inviting. This was a surprise because I've had some Earl Greys that had so much bergamot, I couldn't detect any other aromas.The taste is very smooth, and I've enjoyed every cup, but the real test was with my mother. She's always complained that many Earl Grey teas at our local store are so weak that she has to saok more than one bag per cup, but she loved Higgins & Burke!!

Earl Grey is not one of my favorite flavors of tea but I really liked this Higgins & Burke version. For point of reference, my favorite black tea is  Bigelow Tea Constant Comment -- 40 Tea Bags.  I compared the Higgins & Burke to the Twinings Earl Grey that I had on hand as part of Twinings Variety Pack of Four Flavors, Tea Bags, 20-Count Boxes (20 Tea Bags).I brewed both cups of tea for 4 minutes, right in the middle of the 3-5 min range suggested on the H&B box. Compared to the Twinings, the H&B had a milder flavor that I personally much preferred.

I received my sample of this tea free from the Amazon Vine program, in exchange for writing a review of the product.I brewed a cup this afternoon and sat on our front porch to enjoy it.  My first impression was of the fragrance of the black tea, followed by the bergamot scent.  And that's how it tasted too - more of black tea and less of bergamot.  I prefer a bolder bergamot flavor in my Earl Grey, but this was fresh and tasty too. For those who prefer a more subtle flavor, this would be a good tea for you.I liked that the box comes with a tear-out panel for easy dispensing.  Some of my boxed teas pop open and spill the bags out too easily.  I also liked that each individual bag was sealed for freshness.If, like me, you prefer a bold Earl Grey tea with lots of bergamot flavor, try Stash's Double Bergamot, available here on Amazon.

This is the first time I experienced the wonderful brew from Higgins & Burke. As tea goes, the aroma and flavor were pleasant and enjoyable. I love black (and white) tea with a little evaporated milk and no sugar. This was no exception.  As chai goes, it seemed bland. Ingredients include cinnamon, cardamom, ginger and cloves.

column9: Good standard English breakfast - decent brand!
column10: This English Breakfast tea from Higgins & Burke, is good: it's basic, good tasting black tea (English Breakfast blend) and is tasty.  I wasn't blown away by the flavor, but it was good: I enjoyed the tea, it brewed up quickly in these nice tea bags (I recommend about one minute of brew time), and then added a splash of cream: it was quite nice!

column9: Nice tea, not as strong as the stuff from the U.K.
column10: I love all sorts of teas. My friends know this, so when they travel they often bring me teas from overseas to try. Years ago, a friend gave me some English Breakfast Tea from her trip to Britain. What a full-bodied tea that was! When I had the opportunity to try this I jumped at it, assuming it would be identical. Although close, this is not quite as strong as the tea my friend bought in London.I do like the blend of Ceylon and Assam. It has that nice zing that cuts through a hearty breakfast, like the traditional English fry-up, but still tastes delicious with milk and sugar or honey. Be careful not to oversteep, though, or it can get quite bitter.

"Hand selected premium black teas from Asia provide the foundation for this regal blend. But it is the essence of Italian bergamot, a fragrant orange, which gives Earl Grey its flavor and aroma of distinction."There's that word 'regal'. Have you ever met someone who used that word in a sentence? And not as a joke?"Higgins & Burke excites your senses with premium teas that will inspire and revitalize you. Indulge...Escape."It's Earl Grey. I steeped it for three minutes and I steeped it for five minutes. I had it plain and with 1/2 & 1/2. It's still Earl Grey. Don't get me wrong, I like it. But please, tooting your own horn gives me a headache.Guess I'll go drink more tea now.

I received the Chai, the tea I most drink after Earl Grey. This has a nice flavor, strong cloves, light cardamom. I like lots of milk, latte-style, so I steeped it the full five minutes. If you're just adding a splash of milk, I recommend about half that time. I found it flavorful and aromatic.

column9: It's just tea, nothing that amazing
column10: So I do drink alot of tea, bagged, loose, with cream, without cream, sugar, lemon... what ever works for the tea.  This tea is overall just tea and really not worth the extra cost.  I found it to be a bit bland/weak when brewed to directions and bitter if left to sit too long.  This is in a class with any of the mass market breakfast tea.
...for a tea is that it taste good black.  This one passes the test, though is perhaps not as flavorful as a quality Earl Grey.
My daughter was told that Earl Grey tea is the blend most favored by the British.  So she had to try it.  Success!  Excellent aroma and flavor, easy to prepare, a real classic.

Love this tea!  I have been looking for a good Chai that I can make here at home and this is it.  I really enjoy the exotic flavors.  I only need to add sweetener and I am set.  Thanks for offering such a great product.

This is a very nice, full-bodied English Breakfast blend.  I am a long-time tea drinker who appreciates a good tea.  This is a nice one, comparable to an Earl Grey but slightly lighter.  It is delicious for tea-time or anytime.  Try it plain or sweeten with agave nectar or turbino sugar.  (I do not like stevia or any of the artificial sugars, but if you do, go for it).  Each bag comes in its own heavy-duty sealed packet, so you can pop one in your pocket or purse and take it with you. (I take my own tea bags to work and just get a cup of hot water there.)

Nice flavor, mild and spicy. Heavy on the cloves and aromatic. This tea is so robust I would only steep it for two and half to three minutes, no longer. This is quite the eye opener and is a good rood to head down for anyone trying to break away from coffee or just cut down. Two or three cups of this and might find yourself "quite animated" which isn't really a bad thing.I'm a huge fan of creamed honey as it has better flavor than any sweetener or real sugar and blends well in the tea giving it a more natural taste.Very nice.
I'm the ultimate lover of tea, and Higgins and Burke will not disappoint. It has a fine flavour, provided at a reasonable cost.

I have always enjoyed a good "cuppa" and thought I had a lucky break when I had a chance to sample this new tea through the vine program. Unfortunately, the only good thing I can say about it is I didn't have to pay for it.Folks, I gave it every chance. I brewed it strong, medium, weak. I had it plain, with milk, with lemon. I offered it to friends and family both tea lovers and haters. And we all had the same reaction:It has no flavor! For some reason, this tea is absolutely tasteless, flavorless and insipid.So what to drink?If you like a strong cup with milk you can't beat Yorkshire Gold. Awake by Tazo is a close second.If you prefer it medium strength Twinnings English Breakfast or PG Tips will do nicely.And while I'm at it, the most outstanding Earl Grey I've ever tasted was Rishi Silver Needle Jasmine. Impra Black Currant makes a lovely iced tea.All of these may be purchased here at amazon.

Although not a big tea drinker in the morning, I do enjoy a cup of tea every now and then.  This tea had a nice aroma when I opened the pouch, and has a flavorful taste.  I found it to be refreshing ( I drank it with just a bit of sweetener), but would I buy it if I say it in the stores, probably, if it were on sale.

This is good, basic black tea.  I'm not a tea connossieur, so I don't know that I have any particular insight -- but I enjoyed it just fine, though I didn't find anything special about it.  I generally prefer more strongly flavored teas.  I have used it to make hot tea and iced tea, both of which were just fine.  If you're looking for a good, basic, tea, this should fill the bill.

The packaging helps to insure freshness. I found the taste robust enough to stand up to hazelnut creamer.Also found it mild enough to drink with no more sweetener than I would use with Lipton. I'm not about too give up coffee for "breakfast" but would drink this tea at other times of the day.Based on the packaging I'd be likely to try other flavors from Higgins and Burke.

I must admit that I am hardly a connoisseur of teas. You don't drink tea on a frequent basis, either in iced or hot fashion. I do drink it on occasion during the winter as a warming beverage on a cold day, but it is not by me frequently. My wife, on the other hand, drinks a significant amount of tea, both in iced and hot forms.When I drink this tea, it tasted like every other bag tea that I have ever tasted. I didn't particularly notice any difference between it and the other brands that I have bought over the years. My wife, however, tasted it and mentioned that it did not have the bitter aftertaste that some of the cheaper bagged teas have. Since she doesn't drink tea with anything other than a light touch of lemon, I suspect her taste is much more refined than mine. I am a milk and sugar type tea drinker.To me this is a fine tea for those who drink tea and would be a good addition to the pantry. It is more costly than standard store brand teas, but if my wife is correct and there is no bitter aftertaste, then it would be a worthwhile investment.

If you like English Breakfast tea there is absolutely nothing wrong with this blend. It is aromatic and flavorful...though maybe a bit dry. But I like that somewhat astringent tongue cling.Works for me in the morning when I want a change of pace from Sumatra coffee. Also good with a little milk if you like it that way.The box acts as a dispenser and the bags are individually foil wrapped so if I saw this in a store I would buy it if I needed tea.

column9: Kind of Makes Me Feel British
column10: I have never been much of a hot tea drinker, but in fairness my only exposure to hot tea was Lipton or the green tea you get in Chinese restaurants and I liked neither. However, I like this tea a lot. I drink it with just a little half and half and I've been doing it every morning since I got this tea and I've since gone to the store and purchased more. I recommend this tea, it kind of makes me feel British.

column9: A bold, fresh tasting tea with individually enveloped tea bags
column10: A very nice Black Tea!Each tea bag is individually enveloped, and they do stay fresh. and the tea is sourced by Ethical Tea Partnership standards -[...]It has a nice semi-bold taste that comes fairly close to loose tea in a steeper, which is hard to find in prepacked teas.I like my tea with no milk and a little sugar, so your tastes may vary, but as for me , I really like it.Jim

column9: Delcate and mild. I would buy again
column10: Black tea is my preferred tea flavor, and I always add a dash of sugar. I usually favor Tazo brand for all my teas. I would say Higgins & Burke is a good, very comparable flavor albeit a bit weaker and more mild. It surpassed some other brands because of that fact. Its mildness was easy drinking, especially when iced. I didnt feel the need to do two bags. If you like stronger black tea flavor, you would have to double up on this one which would make it not as good of a deal. Personally I like the light nature of this one, and would repurchase.
I really enjoy this tea.  It tastes quite nice and brews well just following the instructions on the box.  I am looking forward to trying some of the other flavors they offer.

column9: Not bad, but I'll probably stick to my usual.
column10: I love English Breakfast tea, and robust, full-flavored, almost malty without being bitter is how I'd describe the ideal blend.  Sadly, while the Higgins & Burke blend isn't the worst, I wouldn't say it's ideal.  Firstly, it's far from robust, almost weak when brewed according to the given directions of using one tea bag to brew a single cup of tea.  Secondly, it has a slight tannic/bitter aftertaste, not enough to be off-putting, but enough to be noticeable even for a tea novice.  That said, the Higgins & Burke blend has a slight floral/fruity flavor just at the edges, which is unusual for an English Breakfast blend; perhaps the weaker nature of the blend explains the ability to detect such a delicate flavor.Though the faint floral/fruity notes are an interesting flavor addition, they don't make up for the slightly bitter aftertaste, and while I can appreciate, even admire the ethically and ecologically friendly nature of the Higgins & Burke label, I'd like to have a tasty tea in addition to a clear conscience.  So I think I'll stick with my usual EB blend from Twinings and give a skip to the Higgins & Burke blend.

I've been a tea fan for decades; I've written about tea and published stories about tea. I can tell you about second flush Darjeelings and "tippy golden" varieties. Like most self-styled "serious" tea drinkers, I've never been a fan of bagged tea, preferring to brew from "loose" leaves.Given all of that, I have to say that the Higgins & Burke was a very nice surprise. English Breakfast can mean a lot of things, but the leading element of the blend is usually Assam tea, which is known for its supposedly "malty" flavor. The H&B lists Assam as a main ingredient, which was good to see.The bags have a "flow through" design, which is also a good thing; this gives more surface area to the bags and allows for fuller brewing.I brewed up a pot--- not a cup. These tea bags really ought to be put in a pot. If you brew them in a cup, unless you cover it the water will cool too quickly during brewing, and besides, you'll have to reduce the brewing time to too short a length for best results.I was very pleased with the pots that I tried. The Assam flavor was rich and husky; the finished brew was smooth rather than rough; there was none of the staleness that sometimes comes with inferior bagged tea (which is sometimes made from sweepings and leavings). While I wouldn't have this for an after-dinner tea--- Assam is just too assertive--- it's a terrific breakfast tea, as the name implies.Of course, you can argue that if you're making a pot you might as well use loose-leaf tea and be done with it. That's a valid argument, but use of the bags certainly makes for faster clean-up and less effort overall. So besides being good, these tea bags do have a definite role.I'm pleased to be able to recommend this product. It has made me rethink the idea of bagged tea.

First let me disclose that I am not a tea connoisseur with an ideal English Breakfast tea in mind to which to compare this Higgins & Burke tea.  That said, I have tried quite a few different English Breakfast teas over the years and like this one as well as any other.  It seems this tea is not strong enough for many other reviewers, but this being a matter of personal taste, this tea is plenty strong enough for me.  I find it to be stout and crisp, just what I expect from a good English Breakfast tea.  I know this might appall some of the tea purists out there, but I vary wildly in how long I steep my teas.  One morning it might be 2 minutes, another morning it might be 10 or 15 minutes.  I tend to get distracted around the house.  I've occasionally forgotten about the tea only to rediscover it a half an hour later, at which point I warm it in the microwave and drink it anyway.  I know - it's so tragic and wrong where tea is concerned.  This morning was a 10-minute-steep with this tea, and I was pleasantly surprised to find that the tea, while quite strong, was just fine and had not developed a bitter or sharp edge. It still made a wonderful sipping tea and dunking companion for my homemade biscotti. I would be quite happy to purchase and enjoy this tea again.

I am a big fan of English Breakfast teas and I have to say that I really like this tea. I can't say that I am too familiar with the Higgins & Burke brand, but I am impressed with the quality of their offering. It had a nice, mild flavor, but didn't tase "weak" like some mild teas do. Some people don't like mild tea, I am a fan of it in the mornings, or as a relaxing cup in the evening, so if you like very strong flavors, then I wouldn't recommend this (unless you want to use two bags per cup). It also has a bit of a bitter aftertaste, which I think is characteristic of English Breakfast teas, but it's not overpowering or terrible. My wife likes her tea a bit sweeter and a little stronger than I do, but she did like this when she tried it plain (and liked it more when she added a bit of sweetener!). I would definitely recommend this tea ot any English Breakfast or black tea fan.It was also nice to see that this brand is part of the Ethical Tea Partnership.

column9: Not bad, but not great either - bags have staples
column10: I've tried the Earl Grey from the same company, and wasn't impressed.  The same goes for the English Breakfast Tea.  This tea is not very robust.  Perhaps this is just a personal preference, but I prefer a bolder tea, such as from Kusmi Tea. . . but it's a lot more expensive.It should also be noted that these teabags have staples, if that is of a concern.

A bag tea is usually made of such fines that you get lots of leakage throught the bag.  I was pleased to see so few.  I like the foil packaging.  The bags stay fresher and it makes them portable.  Nice clear flavor.

column9: Incredibly Smooth Flavorful English Breatkfast Tea
column10: I LOVE tea. On my recent 9 month tour of schools in my performing incarnation I had several boxes of teas of all kinds: standard and flavored. Part of this stems from my having lived in India for two years where I became almost addicted to tea. I may skip breakfast, but each morning it is tea. English Breakfast tea is not as easy to buy as you'd think. I find that many teas are too sharp or they make them a bit too weak. Or they are not as flavorful as a GOOD English breakfast tea. THE GREAT NEWS is that Higgins & Burk English Breakfast Tea is incredibly smooth, yet not watered down, and wonderfully flavorful. I decided to put this tea to several tests. First, I let the bag seep in a VERY big tea cup I use that I bought on amazon (my favorite...it's thick glass). I always add some sugar. This was strong yet smooth and wonderful. Then I added soy milk the next morning. SUPERB. Then I added milk the next morning: also SUPERB. This is one brand I had never tired before and I've tried all kinds. And I will say it: it is now my favorite brand of English Breakfast tea. It passed all my tests.

While there is nothing special to really distinguish this tea from Twinnings,  Stash, or any other better grade commercially available tea, in this case that is not a bad thing. Both Mrs. Boilermate and I thought this was a decent cup. She drank hers plain, and I drank mine both plain and with lemon and sugar. If this were on the shelf when I went to purchase tea, there is a good chance it would end up in the cart.

I am not a large consumer of teas but when my wife saw this was available, she requested that we order it. She was very impressed. She likes stronger tea as well as coffee and this fits the bill well as a "robust start to the day" - just like the packaging says.Overall, highly recommend this product.

I am a huge tea drinker and enjoy having a good chai in my tea stash. Unfortunately, this tea is a very average chai tea. This is not a bad product. The tea had good flavor and tastes like chai tea should. There is, however, nothing extraordinary or unique about it. It tastes very much like other chai teas I've had (from a tea bag). I don't know that I would recognize or pick this brand of tea over any other boxed chai tea bags. If you need a good staple chai tea to have around, this one is okay. Just don't expect anything special from it.

I drink several cups of black tea every day, often Twinings or Stash English or Irish Breakfast tea, or Tazo's Awake, but sometimes I pick up other English Breakfast teas to try and enjoy.  But this Higgins & Burke... another reviewer said it had an almost soapy taste and I agree.  When I first opened the tea bags I noticed this floral/soapy scent and it ended up tasting this way too, even after adding milk and a little sugar.  It was hard for me to get past that floral taste, especially since it was followed a weird aftertaste, maybe bitter.  Regarding the aftertaste, perhaps the water I use is too hot for this tea or perhaps I brew it a few minutes too long, but I prefer my tea to not be so finicky if this is the case.  I'm not a connoisseur, I never use loose leaf tea, and I use regular tap water... I'm just an everyday tea drinker.  And I prefer that my English Breakfast tea not have floral/soapy notes to it.

column9: Sweet flavor, no tannin, great for any time of day
column10: Note: I drink my tea straight and strong, at least 10 minutes for the bag in hot water while I work. I use no sugar or milk.I usually drink the Taylors of Harrogate, Yorkshire Gold Tea, 160-Count Tea Bags and like it very much. This tea is somewhat sweeter than the Yorkshire Gold and I like it. There is no discernible tannin taste or effect when it is either hot or warm. When left to cool it gave a bit of a tang, but not too much to be unpleasant. It is a very comfortable tea and  perfect for any time of day and with any accompaniment. I will continue to get this drink both this and the Yorkshire Gold, just to keep things fresh, and will purchase more when this box gets close to running out.

column9: Nice Blend, But Milder Than Expected
column10: When I sample a tea for the first time, I do so black--no sugar, milk, or other additives. I also brew according to directions given on the package in order to set a base line for taste. This English Breakfast had a lovely rich aroma, but was actually much milder than I expected; not unpleasant, nor left an unpleasant aftertaste.Adding sugar didn't dimish the flavour, but adding a splash of milk, unfortunately, did. It wasn't egregious and after some experimentation I found the perfect balance of milk and sugar, but this still isn't one of my favourite sachet English Breakfast blends. That honour remains with Stash and Twinings. But I would have no problem recommending it to folks who might prefer a lighter, but not overly so, blend of black tea.

The tea is a hardy, warm tasty brew.  The taste of the tea is strong and not delicate but its flavor is very nice.  It is similar to Earl Grey tea.  I added a little milk and sugar to the tea.  The tea goes great with toast and other breakfast items such as danish or croissant.  Very appealing and nice to drink.

I am not a tea snob.  I enjoy a "snobby" cup of tea, well made in a tea shop but at home, I like the convenience of a tea bag.  Twinings brand English Breakfast is one of my favorite blends so that is my comparison tea.I made this tea with 6 oz. (3/4 Cup) of boiling water poured over the tea bag.  If you use more than 6 oz., your tea will be weak; these premeasured bags are not meant to steep a big US mug of water. If you are using a big mug, use 2 tea bags. I steep for 3 minutes so that the tea doesn't become "stewed"; that funky, bitter taste.  You should use the water immediately after reaching the boiling point because oxygen will evaporate the longer the water boils & your tea will taste flat.The Higgins & Burke is a nice cup of tea.  It has a strong, not bitter flavor with a little maltiness & a hint of smoke.  I think the Twinings is a little more refined, more malty & no smoke.  I like my English Breakfast tea with just a splash of cream; no sugar.The Higgins & Burke is a blend of Assam & Ceylon teas.  The Twinings is a blend of Assam & Kenyan.  If you like a bit more brash black tea, you may like the Higgins & Burke.

I didn't have great luck with my last Higgins and Burke tea--the Earl Grey, finding its Bergamot overly emphasized. I'm happy to say the English Breakfast was much more to my taste. It has the standard pros of this brand--the packaging is made from recycled materials and the company purchases its tea under the Ethical Tea Standards.  The tea itself is a nice tea, especially for bag tea (I almost always use loose leaf).  It has a nice scent and the flavor had a distinct assam taste to it, which I quite liked. It distinguished itself from a lot of bland similar-tasting English Breakfast bag teas.  It had a good full but not overpowering flavor with no bitterness at all.  I've seen some reviewers have found it overly mild, but I didn't have that problem and I like my tea strong and with nothing added.  It also holds up to a second washing decently, but not a third (no surprise there, few teas do). As mentioned, I don't normally drink bag tea and while I keep some boxes in the cupboard for the times I need to just throw a bag in, my choices are almost always Lapsong Souchong and Earl Grey. But I have to say that I was pleasantly surprised by this one and might just add it to the rotation.  Recommended, especially for those who like assam.

column4: Shawn Kovacich "Author and Creator of numerou...
column10: I just recently started drinking tea as a substitute for coffee in the morning and soda in the afternoon. I have fallen in love with Red Rose tea for the afternoon but I find it is a bit light for mornings. I have tried a couple of the breakfast teas in the grocery store with mixed result.When I saw this tea up for review on the Amazon Vine, I figured what the heck, let's try it. The first thing I noticed is that each tea bag is wrapped in foil packets. They were also easy to tear open without tearing up the tea bag. I noticed that there was a nice smell to the tea.I brewed up a quick iced tea, one cup of hot water and two tea bags. Then I pour that over ice and add a little sugar. I noticed that the flavor is a little stronger than Red Rose tea, which is what I'm looking for in a breakfast tea. But in the end, it is still a mild flavor without the bitter taste I tend to find with other breakfast teas.This is a great, mild breakfast tea for those that like tea without the strong bitter taste.Shawn KovacichAuthor and Creator of numerous books and DVD's.

column9: Smells phenomenal, and with a little milk it tastes great
column10: Usually sticking with brands like Stash, Tazo, or Celestial Seasonings, this was my first outing with Higgins & Burke. The tea's packaging talks about an "intoxicating fragrance," which normally would just be nonsense to help sell a product, but in this case the box blurb is correct. This tea does smell phenomenal - both in the packet and brewed.But how does it taste?  Frankly on its own the taste is a little mediocre and just slightly on the bitter side. There are definitely teas out there much more pleasing to the palette straight out of the box, but throw in a splash of milk (and maybe a little sugar) and you've got something well worth drinking here that's much more cost effective than getting a chai out at the coffee shop.  For something a little different from the standard black or herbal teas, I recommend giving this one a try.

I drink a fair amount of tea, and black 'breakfast tea' is one of my faves. I prefer to drink it plain/black. I really like this stuff! It can get a bit bitter if left to steep much longer than the recommended 2-3 minutes, so beware of that (I have a tendency to forget about the steeping). But it otherwise has a nice, full flavor and isn't too strong. And I have been able to re-use the teabag for a second cup later in the day with no problems. Note: I make it using the hot water tap from my office coffee maker. Classy! I like tea, but I'm no connoisseur. Just an average tea drinker :)

column9: Good Black Tea, but there are stronger choices
column10: I'm a tea drinker.  I do not drink coffee.  I like my tea dark, black and with lots of sweet notes and plenty of caffeine.  I don't even use general store brands like Lipton, etc, they have no flavor in my view.This Higgins and Burke tea is good, but I had to use 2 teabags in my cup.  Just not strong enough, even though the flavor was excellent.I prefer Taylors of Harrogate Pure Assam Tea.  I only need one bag per 16oz cup.  I use my Keurig and Ekobrew Refillable K-Cup.  Just place your tea bag into the reusable cup, run Keurig for 2 8oz cycles and you have the most perfect cup of tea imaginable.

It's about on par with Lipton, so if that's good enough for you, then so will this be. I prefer teas with more aroma and flavor, of which this one had neither, really. Brewed hot at the temperature suited for black teas, it was bitter. Prepared iced, it was not, but it lacked the qualities that make iced teas so enjoyable--the perfumed leaves and mellow taste, and in the case of really great teas, a filling sensation and slight sweetness without the need for sugar or honey. Leaf size was quite small, so again, this is not the highest quality, though the packaging is the only good part--individually sealed envelopes. I would not buy this product again. It wasn't bad, but it wasn't good either.

By itself, this tea is very strong and bitter (almost soapy). However, with a little doctoring to include cream and sugar, this is not so bad. I think I would have rated it higher if it tasted better by itself, but it did not. I don't think I would get this type of tea again.

We've always drunk green teas or flavored teas such as Constant Comment and chai.  This was the first time for us to try a black breakfast tea.  We LOVED IT~.  Full flavored and brisk, it will now be included in our tea servings.

Higgins & Burke English Breakfast Tea  is a full bodied blend, with a rich aroma, making it a perfect start to your morning. But what really sold me on this tea is the fact it makes a wonderful iced tea. Not some watered down wimpy iced tea, but a strong, full flavored iced tea with no bitterness.  The companys  teas are 100% sourced and purchased under Ethical Tea Partnership standards. From looking at their website all indications are that this company is  committed to making a difference.  Good tea, good company, win, win

Higgins & Burke is a name in tea that had escaped me until now, but I'm glad I found it. There are teas out there that I won't return to, but this tea has what's required: body, aroma, and flavor. I waited for the first reasonably cool morning to really appreciate it, and I'm just finishing my first cup. It won't be the only one today, now that I've had it. This is a take-it-out-on-the-front-step-and-watch-the-world-go-by sort of tea. A day-off, good-music-on-the-radio tea. I guess you could say I like it.

column4: B. McCarthy "Engineer, CERT, Amateur Radio Op...
column9: A Decent Cup of Chai Tea
column10: It needs a lot of sugar and milk, but this is a pretty good tea.  It looses one star because, like all the others I have tried, it fails to be as good as the restaurants make it.

column9: Excellent Tea with Delightful Ethical Aftertaste
column10: This is fine tea. English Breakfast Tea is a bit of a commodity, and an increasingly familiar one. This variation is quite good, not as piquant as some alternatives--and not leaving the rather bitter aftertaste one sometimes finds in combination. If you tend toward a milder tea, this one may well please you.The company that produces this product is part of the Ethical Tea Partnership. For those interested, I would suggest visiting ethicalteapartnership dot org. The list of participating companies includes giants such as Tetley and Twinings, and is missing some other familiar names.Something more to think about, something else in favor of this product.My overall suggestion: find a tea you like, and find one that is from a member of the Ethical Tea Partnership. There's no one rule for taste--but there are universal expectations of ethics, realizable ideals.This tea will meet those criteria for many people.

I love English Breakfast tea, and this was not a disappointment. With some cream and sweetener, this made the perfect cup to get me going in the morning. Normally I'll make a coffee drink (with a lot of Torani sugar free syrup and real cream) but this tea just hits the spot some mornings.It has that full bodied chewiness about it that makes a good English Breakfast tea. It's not thin or flat tasting at all. Love it and would purchase.

This is the first time I've tried Higgins & Burke Teas.  I really enjoy Bigelow English Breakfast Tea so I thought I might like this as well.  It is NOT the same, or really even similar, but it is a good tea, in my opinion.  I confess, I drink coffee almost daily and tea, only occasionally.It's not too strong for me, as I don't care for really strong drinks, but is flavorful.  I use a bit of sugar in my tea, and sometimes cream if it's stronger and depending on the variety.  This tasted good with just the sugar.  I enjoyed this the few times I've tried it and still have quite a few bags left.  I will update if I have anything to add.  I do like the individual packs that this comes in as it is kept fresher longer.If Bigelow EBT and this were side by side, I'd pick the Bigelow, but of course that's personal preference.  It's a good tea and an worthwhile and interesting change from the usual.

column9: good quality, smooth tea, quite enjoyable
column10: This is a surprising good quality tea from the Canadian company, Higgins and Burke. In years past, I have had English breakfast tea that has been bitter and overly acidic. This English Breakfast is smooth, without any bitter after taste.It has a pleasant, almost floral aroma as well.It can also be served chilled, with good taste, as well.This tea is recommended highly for general home use.

I love Chai tea!  So I jumped on the Higgins and Burke Chai Black Tea.  I noticed when I opened the carton that there was a slight scent of spices.When brewing the black tea, again it was a slight smell.The taste was slight in spices, more Cinnamon then anything else.  I found it a little watery using one tea bag, so I made another cup of tea using 2 tea bags, still even with 2 tea bags, the flavor lacked a nice taste.I would say this tea needs to be re blended as I was disappointed ion this offering from Higgins and Burke.

Higgins & Burke Gourmet Tea was established by an old and trusted Canadian coffee and tea manufacturer - Mother Parkers. Higgins & Burke's English BreakFast Black Tea is a delicious tea, with a wonderfully robust taste that makes it good in the morning or throughout the day. It's delicious hot with lemon and milk, or iced with lemon and sugar.It's a very good all-round tea that is good iced or hot, and it goes good with just about any food.

column9: Citrus notes of Bergamot and lemon in a soothing black tea
column10: This premium black tea is made with natural oil of Bergamot and natural lemon flavor to make a soothing cup to relax the senses. The black tea strength comes through and the finishing notes of citrus are slightly tart. I added a bit of sugar to mine to smooth out the taste.  I love the 100% recycled packaging and it is easy to select one tea bag at a time as they are individually sealed and retain their freshness. There are also NO staples to deal with as the string is stitched to the tag. Higgins and Burke teas are quality through and through and I would highly recommend them as I have tried several flavors and have not been disappointed.
This is a rich smooth tea that is not bitter at all.  A delicious chai that doesn't require sugar or milk to be enjoyable.

I like to drink my tea hot and with a splash of milk.  I also prefer 'plain old' black teas to anything fancy or flavored.  I found Higgins & Burke to suit my taste, although it's not a very strong tea when compared to something like Pg Tips 80 Ct Tea Bags, even when I increase the steep time to 7 minutes.Each teabag is individually wrapped in a 'stay fresh' foil sachet.  The tea blend is Assam and Ceylon black tea, with 180mg of Polyphenols per serving (8oz water).  Overall, I found Higgins & Burke to be a good cup of breakfast tea, with a medium strength taste.

I am a tea fan. I tried this tea both hot and cold. It is much better hot than cold. The tea itself is just your average black tea. Nothing special. It does seem to have an odd aftertaste. I like that the tea bags are individually wrapped and they open without tearing the tea bag, so that is a plus. But as far as tea goes, this tea is like other mediocre black teas I've had. Nothing special.

In a word how would I describe a sip of Higgins & Burke Chai Black Tea - "mellow."  It is the kind of tea you might have after a fine dinner with guests and sitting around the fire for light conversation.  I expected it to be overpowering in flavors since it has nutmeg, ginger, cinnamon and other spices in there but it wasn't.  It is a pleasant experience - a mellow experience.  I would consider buying it as it is a unique product.

This is a really good flavor and it's helpful to get fiber wherever you can. I prefer to use just half a tube per bottle, just to lighten the flavor a bit. The seller was fast and friendly. I will buy from them again.
this moscatel vinegar is wonderful tasting.  it is so good you want to eat bread with it or even drink it....i personally think this is the best vinegar ever!

I felt the need to do this review when I noticed Amazon doesn't tell you this is SUGAR FREE candy. I actually bought a bag of this candy while leaving Japan at the airport in Nagoya. I saw them and thought, 'omg those look delicious green tea/green tea latter candy, yes please!' I was so happy to see maccha (green tea) that I wasn't much paying attention. So of course, when I put the first piece in my mouth, I immediately thought, 'okay, this tastes really gross, what in the world...?' I then noticed that not only was it green tea candy, it said 'non-shugaa' (non-sugar) at the top. I took off a star because I personally found them very gross buuuut I'd imagine if you're used to/enjoy sugar free candies, they'd probably be quite good. I was just disheartened that I would not be enjoying happy green tea candy on my ridiculously long return flight.So yes, important point: THIS CANDY IS SUGAR FREE!

This is excellent quality mole poblana sauce. Mexican mothers don't make it from scratch, they buy these little jars that incidentally are designed to be used as juice glasses--they aren't threaded. You can use a bottle opener to break the seal, otherwise it can be a little difficult to remove the lid.I don't add extra sugar or salt as suggested, only chicken broth, although I do add dried chipotle to make it a little spicier. Makes about four cups of thick sauce.It's great on chicken but also wonderful as a sauce for anything in a corn or flour tortilla, any kind of meat, on rice as you would use gravy, as a sandwich spread, or even to eat with tortilla chips or cornbread.Ingredients:Sesame seed, vegetable oil (cottonseed and/or sunflower, and/or soybean oil), toasted bread (wheat flour, vegetable shortening (soybean, cottonseed and/or safflower oil), sugar cane syrup, salt, leavening agents (sodium bicarbonate, ammonium bicarbonate and soy lecithin), sugar, dried red peppers, iodized salt, cocoa, caramel color, spices, natural flavoring, FD&C red no. 40, FD&C. red no. 40 lake.Nutrition:Serving size 2 tbsp (28g), about 8 servings per containercal. 150fat cal. 100total fat 11gsat. fat 2gtrans fat 0gcholesterol 0mgsodium 270mgtotal carb 12gfiber 1gsugars 4gprotein 3gvitamin A 4% DVcalcium 8% DViron 8% DV(based on 2,000 cal diet)

column9: not as good as Dona Maria
column10: I ordered this mole sauce, rather than picking up a jar of Dona Maria at the local store, because I had read several reviews which claimed it was much better.  I disagree.  I found the Rogelio Bueno mole to be much sweeter, with more cinnamon; with less complexity and less chocolate and smoky flavors than the Dona Maria.  My husband compared the Rogelio Bueno mole to spicy gingerbread.  Everyone in my house strongly preferred the Dona Maria. I know mole varies greatly, but the Rogelio Bueno mole did not remind me of the mole I've had in Mexico.  I will not be buying it again.

What's not to like?  The treats are low in fat, which is importamt for any dog, but especially important for yorkies, which are prone to stomach problems that can progress to pancreatitis.  The pups love these treats, and the mint flavor gives puppy breath a nice scent, or as nice as a dog can have.  The price is pretty much standardized.  I rarely ever see a bargain, and this purchase was no exception.  Shipping was prompt - no complaints.

column9: My dogs go nuts for them
column10: The dogs love them.  They wait for them when they come in from outside.  Give them as an after meal mint and your dogs will never have "dog breath".

I was very disappointed when I could no longer find these at my Pet Store.  Thank you for having them at a reasonable price.  Shipping was fast and received in a few days.  My doggies have these as a treat in the morning and have had them since they were puppies.  They say thank you also!!!

Ok, ok, I apologize for the title. It can be irreverent and insensitive to some so again, my apologies.  But I have to tell you my two French Bulldogs have been getting these as treats for NINE years - first for training, then for being good, now right after they both get their daily eye & arthritic medication in morning and they are totally, completely hooked on them. We sit on the kitchen floor and go through our daily morning medical ritual. Then reward time. They see their favorite canister in the whole world come out (which I keep in the refrig, they seem to like it a little better chilled, hey they're French, what do I know!).  Anyway, their big beautiful brown eyes seem to double in size, glaze over in a memorized trance, thoroughly fixated and totally focused like a beam of hot white light on what I irreverently now say to them, "ok, time for your puppy crack cocaine". You'd think after 9 years it would lessen a little but it hasn't one bit.  They're pyscho for this stuff and for Talk to Me Pup-RRR-Mint Sticks more then any other treats I've ever given them in 9 years.  And believe me, I spoil my Frenchies like no one else lol and rotate treats constantly, every few days, so they are never bored. I should be so well treated. haha  But the two little Talk to Me Treats they each get after their medicine every morning remain far and away my druggie doggies favorites. lol  Like I said, I'm sorry for being irreverent - but both my Frenchies' reaction to this all is adorable. Maybe urs will be too.  And Im glad that it's healthy for them.  They're my Frenchies, I love 'em to death and love making them happy.

We and our six precious pet family (Chi's) love this product.  Our kids know each evening when it is treat time and if we forget, they sit at our feet and look at us wishfully until they they receive these treats.  We believe they are good them and have had no issues with these treats.  They have such a clean and minty smell.  We were happy to find them through Amazon when our local stores & major pet marketing chains discontinued providing them.
My malti-poo loves these treats.  They are fun for him to eat and they make his breath smell fresh & Minty.  The are one of only two treats that he will eat.
My dog loves these & my local stores no longer carry them. So glad Amazon found a place for me to get them

LOVE talk-to-me treats. I was sad when local pet stores (like PetSmart and PetCo) stopped carrying these, so glad to find them available online, and even for the same price as they were in the stores!

My dog and I have had a bedtime routine where he "gets naked" (has his collar taken off), and then gets his 3-4 "minty treats". I had one store where I could purchase them. As others have commented, these are now extremely difficult to find. So glad to have an online source to continue our bedtime ritual! After having it in place for a few years, I didn't know what I would replace these with. Glad I don't have to think about it again for awhile since I stocked up!

column9: Talk To Me Select Treats - 14 ounce Mint Flavor
column10: My girls love them.  They have a fresh flavor, a fresh, minty scent, a nice crunch and are economical (as revealed to me by my fluffy girl Bichons).  I highly recommend these treats to any Bichon lover.

The dog loves these things.. and I love them since they're tiny so you can give alot and not feel like you're giving your dog a weight problem. I use them as just treats, but they also go in the treat balls that roll around and dispense treats randomly!

I was purchasing these treats at our local PetSmart store.  However, they have decided to carry their own brand of treats.  Rather than buying something that my dog may not like, I turned to the internet to find this product.  It is a wonderful treat and is great for dogs' teeth.  I hope I can continue getting them from places like Amazon.  Thank you Amazon!

These are terrific little treats that are great for training. My dog loves 'em, they are small so that I don't have to break them up (although I can if I need to...) They are neat, nothing smelly or messy or oily. My dog seems to love the minty flavor. Since they have no meat in them they fit the guidelines for his allergies. Great product.
Great for the dog's breath, they like them and they are good for the pups.  Highly recomend this product also a good training tool

Our two Maltese absolutely LOVE these treats! I buy several canisters at once because they eat them so quickly - and they are very fussy. It took many tries to find just the right treat. It has been getting more and more difficult to find these treats in stores, though.  I sure hope that Booda continues to make these or we are in BIG trouble!

I have never had a dog treat that made my dogs respond so quickly!  This treat even got my reluctant standard poodle to start using the dog door, which even steak wouldn't do.  The aroma of these treats is pleasing, even to me, and the size is perfect for both the standard poodle and the mini doxie.  The only thing the manufacturer could make better is the container.  It's a big pain to have to unscrew the lid every time I want just one treat.  Great product.

I have tried every GoldenValleyNatural.com Jerky product.  By far the best are all the Sweet N'Spicy and Peppered Flavors.  Beef tends to be smoky and fatty, while Turkey is dry and flaky, making their Buffalo meat varieties the best of them all.Avoid their Low Carb Jerky unless you are willing to bite off tic-tac size bites and chew for a minute each time.  All the Teriyaki Jerkys have the texture and taste like sweet Corned Beef, so I'd skip them as well.If you want to try different flavors, instead of 8 of the same from Amazon, just go directly to their web sight and buy them for only 15% more than Amazon's sale price.

This is the best turky jerky we have ever bought.  I buy most of the Golden Valley Jerkies throughout the year.  My family loves the Beef and Buffalo jerkies also and they all taste great and are healthy too!This is a great jerky to send to military family memebers serving overseas.  Keeps wonderfully and they love it!

This product has good flavor and texture. Some of the pieces are a little tough but still taste very good. The sodium is rated at 16% of daily requirement, half of some other products.If you are near a store, Trader Joe's Turkey Jerky is also recommended.

I am a jerky lover and decided to try out this turkey jerky and I was highly disappointed. The jerky was way too sweet and had dry gritty texture almost like eating liver. I like liver but I don't want my jerky tasting like it. I never finished the first bag and eventually threw the other bags away.
these taste great and are soft and easy to chew.  The spicy could be more spicey in my opinion.

column9: My kids love this high-protein snack
column10: This is delicious jerky. It's high in protein, softer and chewier than other brands, and it's relatively low in sodium for a jerky. It's easy to pack for snacks or lunches.  It keeps well so I buy it by the case and munch for a while. Excellent product for the whole family.
This makes a very satifying snack and a suppliment of protein to a meal.  I like that it is low in fat and calories.
This has wonderful flavor--quite spicy but deliciously rich.  Not as hard to chew as some other jerkys.  Would highly recommend.

column9: How good Amazon Shipment be more tender
column10: I was amazed when I opened the first package of this Turkey Jerky.I used to buy the exact same item at Whole Foods but they were out before my last backcountry trip, so I got it from Amazon.com and wow! I could believe how tender the jerky was, nothing like when I got it from Whole Foods.It might just be a quirk and I can't test for a while since it will take a year to get through 6 packages.

This stuff is very tasty and a great source of protein, but not cheap - even at Amazon prices.Maybe someday they'll genetically engineer turkeys whose meat automatically turns to jerky.  Until then, I guess this'll have to do.

Ok I have to say I am baffled by the numerous negative reviews of this Jerky.It is wonderful, tastes great, lower sodium than other turkey jerkys, and perfect for snacking.I read almost all of the reviews before I decided to order it, usually I have purchased the Jacks brand in the past, in my opinion Golden Valley is far better.  I also read people saying they received very hard/chewy pieces of jerky?  I had a few tougher pieces here and there but for the most part all of it was soft and just the way turkey jerky should be.Highly recommend this to anyone -- don't let the negative reviews sway you.Great jerky.
Please just save your money it has a very sweet after taste from a carmel coating that also has a very off smell.

column9: Golden Valley Natural Turkey Jerky (Barbeque Flavor)
column10: This was not that great.  I only tried this brand's Barbeque flavor so I don't know what the rest tastes like (to be fair).  I will not be buying this again.  I have tried several brands and so far the best one is Perky Jerky Turkey Jerky.  Someone complained about Jack Links being too salty but I rather that than this bad tasting barbeque junk.

For the most part, I'm a non meat-eater. However, I wanted a high protein non-sugary snack to keep in my purse for when hunger strikes. This fits the bill perfectly and the taste is excellent. Not salty like other jerkys! And one or two can hold me over for a long time.

golden valley natural  turkey, beef, and buffalo jerky  I think is the best very tender meet and it's not to salty.  I already  ordered  40 bags  and they go quick  everyone at my job is crazy for them

I bought this jerky to satisfy a craving that has long been neglected. There used to be a local company in San Diego called Smitty's jerky, and he made the best peppered jerky ever. They disappeared for some reason and that left those of us that were his fans in the dark.Now on to the real review... I ordered this based on reviews here at Amazon, and figured I'd give it a try. The turkey jerky is literally exploding with flavor, and is so tender that it requires no more effort to chew than an oven-cooked turkey. I order 8 bags and they were gone in just a matter of a few days. I even shared a bag with co-workers, and everyone raved about how surprisingly good this product was.Without question or hesitation, I would highly recommend this to anyone who even remotely enjoys jerky.

Short and Sweet:  this jerky is quite sweet, compared to commercial jerky.  In a one ounce portion, there are seven (7) grams of carbohydrates.  For those on a low-carb diet, that is a significant amount.I notice that in the more "natural" jerkies, they tend to use more sugar.  Perhaps it helps the texture and make the jerky a little less likely to dry out.It does show this on the label, which Amazon makes available, so don't make the same mistake I did and buy impulsively.If you are trying to find a beef jerky without preservatives, and from animals raised without antibiotics, etc, then this product is acceptable, if a little sweet.  But if you are on a high protein diet, avoiding carbohydrates, then beware.

I ordered this because it was natural and nitrate free.  I just received my shipment - it is very tender as others have said but I found it much too sweet for my taste.  The sugar overpowers the pepper flavor and is not what I expected.  If you want something that is more sweet than peppery or spicy you will like this brand.

I have always been very pleased with this product and have purchased it monthly for a very long time.  However, the product I received last month should have been called "turkey BURGER jerky".  It was very granular and difficult to eat.  We take this in our lunches, and it is very inconvenient.  Hopefully, it will improve, or I will have to find another option.

column9: Great Taste - but has soy sauce
column10: These are very tender and tasty - perhaps too sweet. I wish they could have skipped adding soy sauce and just had a more plain variety with minimal added ingredients.

column9: Best Turky Jerky I have tried
column10: It's delicious, and while it is expensive, it's just not that expensive for what you get. They sell this at the local "green" grocery store here at much higher rates.Everyone I know who has tried this brand loves it. It's not dry and tough like some others; the texture is just tender and moist enough to overcome typical jerky flaws. The blend of spices are quite good, even though there's a slight sweet taste. Normally I would hate even the slightest hint of sweetness in a product like this, but somehow it works.I cannot recommend this product highly enough.

Wish it was a little cheaper but it is good quality.Very juicy and tender.Like mentioned, you will get some pieces here and there that are a little greasy but I don't expect every single piece of any jerky to be perfect; just the nature of the product.If they ever lower the price a little I will re-subscribe.Enjoy!
Turkey is one of the foods I can eat and finding Turkey Jerky was hard.  The taste is great.  Provides good source of protein.

column9: golden valley natural black pepper turkey jerky
column10: I am completely upset that our order of turkey jerky is MOLDY!  The expiration date is September so it should have been good.  So obviously I cannot recommend this product.  How sad because I try to buy natural products and had read good reviews for this.  I am not sure how to contact the seller, but if you read this post, please work on quality control.

I started a low carb. diet and have been trying different brands of turkey jerky.  Golden Valley Natural Turkey Jerky "BLACK PEPPER" was by far the worst I have ever tasted.  I've never left a review about any product I've purchased, good or bad, but I had to say something about this. It literally tasted like candied meat. It has 6 grams of carbs per serving (all from sugar)....double that of any other I've found.  Why would any company put so much sugar in a turkey jerky labeled black pepper?  They should have just called it brown sugar turkey jerky.  I threw it in the trash and got a refund from Amazon.  Amazon truly is an incredible company and I will continue to make purchases via their venue, but this turkey jerky......?

I usually love this product - and I have subscription for it. But this time it came all with mold! Just awful smell and look! Not sure what's going on - I think I have to end the subscription - it's not a cheap product.... Very disappointed.... :(
The flavor is good, but about half of the pieces were too tough to chew. I wouldn't order this brand again.
My boyfriend is very pleased to receive this for Christmas !Tastes great and has a little kick to it. Will definitely reorder this!

This turkey jerky is good in the fact that it is preservative-free, no MSG, no nitrates and all-natural.  But, I was disappointed - it's too dry and difficult to eat.  Not a great pleasure to the mouth, but okay in general.

This stuff is yummy and great for healthy snacking.  Interesting, there is some variation between packs, and some pieces can be a little hard on the teeth, but not a big problem.  Much better than the brands offered in major stores.

column9: Very delicious, but NOT free range
column10: This is a very delicious jerky, and I find the consistency to be very nice: not too dry, but not oily or stringy either. Based just on taste, I'd give it a 5 star rating.However, this product does not come from free-range turkeys. I noticed that the packaging didn't say anything about free range birds, which I thought was odd, so I called the company and they confirmed that the turkeys are not free range. They said they would work on getting this amazon product page updated, but until then, I wanted to put the information out there.

Our household is addicted to this stuff.  It's a little pricey, but when you break it down to the delicious, fulfilling, low-calorie, high-protein nutrition you get, it's worth it.  At least to us.  We finally got on the regular shipment plan to save 15% per month.  Yay, Amazon.[Time passes]Hmmmm... I am starting to suspect there are two versions of this product.  One you buy in the health food store and pay top dollar for... and this one.  I have never had an issue with quality control with this product before.  However, with this multi-pack I am finding that in every pouch there are a couple/few pieces that should have not made it past inspection - cut too thick to eat without soaking and/or too grisely to consider worthy of this price.So, hopefully it was just a few bag bags and maybe that's been straightened out.  But I hope this is not the new version.  We really do love this stuff- the high quality product we are used to, not the thick, grisely version.

Ok, I know this is turkey and not beef.  It tasted really good but there isn't much actual turkey jerky in the pouch.  You could finish an entire bag as a small snack.  The product is advertised as 4 oz but the bags I received were only 3.5 oz and I question if that included the weight of the bag.

These jerkys are pretty good and flavorful. My daughter loves them and eats them instead of candy or high carbohydrate snacks but they can get pricy. It is not cheap and it is also a bit too sweet for me but its salt or sugar that preserves them naturally.I do like all natural meats without any presevatives such as Nitrate, Nitrite or TBHQ, too much of these ingested can lead to cancer.

After an initial positive experience with the product, I ordered a second pack of 8. The first pouch we opened was fine, however the second was where we encountered a problem. The meat in the bottom of the package was covered in a thick nasty mold. I reached in and was about to take bite when I noticed the mold covering it! I'm guessing the seal must have somehow broke on the packaging? Just make sure you check before eating!

This is not the best turkey jerky I have had, but for the price is is worth it and I may re-order. This company also sells beef jerky, which is way too sweet and poor quality and processed. The turkey jerky is not nearly as bad as the beef. It has thicker pieces and is not as sweet. Because the price for this turkey jerky is pretty low, it makes it worth it, but it could be improved by being less sweet. It's not as bad as he beef, but still too sweet. Texture and meat quality were good, but not excellent.

column9: Probably the Best Turkey Jerky EVER!
column10: I have had a love affair with Turkey Jerky for a long time, but as I have gotten wiser and started paying more attention to the foods I put into my body, I stopped buying it at the grocery store: it all has MSG and high fructose corn syrup and artificial color, et cetera, added.  Not this stuff!  And from free-range, hormone-free turkeys, too!  The whole family loves it. We've been giving my son beef jerky to help cut his teeth and thought this might be a bit too peppery for him ('cause it is a bit peppery), but he really seems to like it (granted, I ate nothing but Mexican food when I was pregnant with him & later when breast-feeding, so he's fairly accustomed to spicy foods).  And when you sign up for the automatic shipments, i think the price is quite reasonable for an organic and healthy snack food.

I have ordered this product several times in the past and found it to be good. This last shipment was lacking in flavor and was greasy. After eating the jerky my hands were also greasy. This is a major quality reduction. I doubt I will order it again. Too bad as ordering online is so convenient.

column9: Soft and tasty but a little salty
column10: Turkey jerky is delicious because it's much softer than beef jerky. It's very more-ish, as the english say.
I enjoyed this product very much. It is seasoned just right not too salty either. It has the perfect texture and it is easy to chew. I will definitely purchase this product again!

This is delicious jerky. It's high in protein, softer and chewier than other brands, and it's relatively low in sodium for a jerky. It's easy to pack for snacks or lunches.  It keeps well so I buy it by the case and munch for a while. The Teriyaki flavor is a little bit greasier than the Original flavor, but that's only in the bag; once it's out, I don't notice. Excellent product for the whole family.

A popular product in my household for years has been the teriyaki turkey jerky from the local warehouse store, so I selected this as a natural, free range, no-chemicals alternative. I'm giving it a 4 star rating, because it's good, in fact it's very good, but it's a little bit drier, a little less consistent, and not quite as flavorful as the brand we are used to.

This was the worst jerky I have every had in my life.  The first package was okay, but the next couple of packages tasted a little 'off', almost stale. How can jerky taste stale? Well, apparently it can if it gets moldy.Now, I have eaten a lot of jerky in my life.  I've made jerky. Properly prepared, jerky should not get moldy. I have never, ever had turkey jerky get moldy in an unopened package. But we found mold on the next package we opened, and by the time we got to the next one, it was covered in mold. These were stored in a dark, cool, dry place. We ended up throwing away the rest.I am glad that neither my family nor I got food poisoning from this stuff. Do not buy!

column9: Best hot sauce on the planet
column10: Not too spicey but full of great flavor 'tio goes on everything. But it can also be hard to find at a reasonable price, so that is where amazon comes in. Buy a case and don't regret it!
Great stuff, what else to say! A case lasted me 4 months. Use it every morning on my eggs. Don't have to remind my wife to get it at the grocery store!

This is my favorite hot sauce hands down.  When we moved from NJ to MA, I stocked up.  Now I have had to order a case because we can't get it here.  It's a great sauce if you want just hot pepper and not a vinegar taste.

I purchased this tea honestly because I was looking for one more item to get up to the $25 so I could get free shipping.  I am a tea lover and I drink both loose teas and bag teas.  This looked almost too good to be true for the price, but I thought, "What the heck?"  I found that 1 bag will only steep one cup of tea.  You cannot get 2 cups like you can out of many other brands.  I also found that some bags did not want to steep at all.  Also, the string tends to come off easily.  The strings appear to be sealed into the bag and when they get into a boiling cup of water, they tend to come off and the top of the bag opens and the tea leaves come out.  Ok, but I wouldn't give it as a gift or anything.  I suggest sticking with a better brand for bagged teas like Lipton, Bigelow, or Celestial Seasonings.  For loose tea I recommend TeaSmith, Teavana, Davidson's, or Republic of Tea.  Also, check to see if your tea is Fair Trade Certified and/or Organic.

Not the REAL Ceylon Tea Company. Definately a knock off. Very embarassing to get this for my mom as a gift and have her tell me how aweful it is. I tried one of the strawberry (which was different from the one she told me was aweful) and it tasted like regular black tea. It didn't even smell like strawberry. At this point I am assuming that all of the differnt flavors are the same. The string came off of the tea bag and overall I can honestly say (right down to the packaging) that this tea is really cheap and no good. Don't waste your money. This company is a joke.
Great value for a set of teas.  The orange and strawberry teas are a little strange for me though. It's nothing fancy just good quality teas.
This is a very good bargain. I don't know how long these prices will last. But Ceylom teas are very potent and the variety is quite outstanding. I will be buying lots of it before the moth ends.

I ordered 3 boxes of these teas for gifts and also 1 box for me to try.  I thought they were a great idea because there was a variety, a good quantity and not expensive.  So many things wrong here ... where do I start. 1.) They all came in broken boxes 2.) There is no flavor to these teas.  Doesn't matter which one you drink they are all the same.  3.) I'm completely embarrassed that I had given these as gifts. Considering I threw mine away because they were just that tasteless.
There is very little tea in the bags.  It barely makes one cup of tea and the flavors are not very strong.

Bought these for a Mothers Day gift along with a "Vintage Classics 65821 Basket Tea Caddy by Vintage Classics".My neighbor was thrilled with both items !!She calls me just about every day to tell me what flavor is her current favorite !!Very Nice Price and Makes a Very Nice Gift !!

I bought this for my mother-in-law, who complains about everything. She said the tea bags fell out of the box during shipping and there were just too darned many of them. It sounds to me as if she liked it!

I bought two of these to give as a Christmas present.  Thankfully I live with the person I gave them to, because this tea as great quality.  Totally worth the price, and you can't beat it locally.  Well worth ordering!

What a great little box of Tea!  Great variety of flavors, enough to please just about everyone. All bags individually wrapped for freshness and in a see through gift box with a gift card attached, making it perfect for giving.

I purchased this product directly from the Blair's Site, as Blair himself touted that this product was made with spices that hit a 600,000 scoville!Being a chilli head I naturally wanted to try this. At best, I would get 1 or 2 of the chips that had any zing to it, but for the most part it tasted like a BBQ flavored chip. No distinct flavor of habenero.Now I bought the combination box which had 5 bags of these habenero chips in it, and they all tasted the same.
